The Surprising Salary Cap Cost of Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , though still unofficial, are trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens.
Brissett was benched this past weekend in favor for Gardner Minshew, who led the Cardinals to a comeback win over the Cowboys on Sunday and now has full control the team's starting position.
Brissett, demoted to Arizona's third emergency quarterback position, now finds himself on the way to Baltimore but likely won't play until next week, as the Ravens are on Thursday Night Football.
Things are still being finalized, though Brissett's departure opens a spot in the Cardinals' quarterback room.
Brissett's trade out of the desert comes at a cost for both this season and next.
By trading Brissett, the Cardinals will take on a dead cap hit of $9.6 million for the rest of the year while 2027 will see a $7.2 million dead cap hit according to Spotrac.
The Ravens, meanwhile, take on a mere $695,000.
Assuming the Jacoby Brissett trade is processed for Week 10, the #Ravens will be taking on a $650,000 salary for the rest of the 2026 season ($695k cap hit). The #Cardinals will take on dead cap hits of $9.6M for 2026, and another $7.2M in 2027.
For the moment, Arizona saves a total of $1.3 million for the rest of the 2026 season by trading Brissett. That places their running cap total at $11.5 million per Spotrac, which keeps them firmly at No. 11 for most cap space in the league.
This money can be rolled over into next offseason.
The Cardinals' total dead cap space does increase by $8.9 million immediately, seeing their total jump from $93.1 million to $102 million for 2026. Brissett now slots into the No. 2 spot for highest dead cap hit in Arizona, trailing No. 1 Kyler Murray ($46.5 million) and No. 3 Marvin Harrison Jr. ($8.8 million).
The Cardinals still rank No, 5 in total dead cap money for 2026, far behind the No. 1 ranked Miami Dolphins at $190 million.
For next offseason, 2027, Brissett's dead cap hit ties Murray ($7.2 million) for the highest in Arizona. After accounting for Brissett's hit, the Cardinals will be up to $20.4 million — though the number will surely increase as the organization makes more moves.
Brissett, scheduled to be a free agent next offseason, initially had a void year added by the Cardinals after he had his contract restructured at the start of training camp.
Arizona made a surprising decision to not absorb all of Brissett's salary this season, though it shouldn't have a massive impact on their total spending power in 2027.
Using OverTheCap's projections, the Cardinals have the second-most projected cap space next offseason at $104.2 million.

title: 25 Players Highlight Cardinals-Seahawks Week 9 Injury Report
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks have revealed their first injury report of Week 9, and it's a lengthy, star-studded list.
The Cardinals saw massive names such as Budda Baker and Josh Sweat — two players possibly being traded ahead of next week's trade deadline — on rest days while Walter Nolen returned to practice.
For Seattle, they're already down their starting quarterback in Sam Darnold for Week 9 while Leonard Williams, Quenton Nelson and others land on the list.
Arizona moves forward with Gardner Minshew under center for his first official start of 2026 after trading away Jacoby Brissett.
“I think he kind of showed all of us in terms of him going out there being the competitor that he is. Doesn’t shock me. The production was pretty wild in terms of the amount of points and just moving up and down the field, but he’s a competitor and he’s always prepared," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Minshew.
"He’s preparing like he’s the starter. He’s preparing like he’s going to be in there for whatever snap. He supported Jacoby at a high level too. He’s been a great backup for him. He’s been great for the room and (I) look forward to the challenge that we have this week with him.”
The Seahawks ruled out Darnold today, propping up Drew Lock for a second start against the Cardinals.
"We know what kind of challenges it's going to be. We're going into a hostile environment against arguably the best defense in football, an offense that we know firsthand can score points," LaFleur said of facing Seattle.
The Seahawks, 4-4, are trying to find their footing after losing their last three-of-four games.
Both sides face an uphill battle in terms of health this week.
Both teams will practice twice more this week on Thursday and Friday before labeling injured players as out, questionable or doubtful after Friday's practice.
On Saturday, the Cardinals and Seahawks can make up to two practice squad elevations. Based off who is listed on Friday's injury report, this could be key in identifying who the teams believe will be healthy or not.
Final inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday, where NFL teams must decide if any questionable players will be part of the 48-player gameday roster or not.
For Sunday's 2:25 PM MST kickoff in Seattle, that will be 12:55 PM MST.

title: 3 Cardinals Most Likely to Be Traded Next After Jacoby Brissett Move
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals , as promised, remain active ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
After dealing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans weeks ago, the Cardinals have now benched and successfully traded quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
Brissett, while still awaiting official word of completion, is heading to the Baltimore Ravens today.
While terms are unknown at this point in time, the Cardinals appear to be open for business.
With less than a week left to make moves, here are three Cardinals most likely next on the trade block:
This is the most obvious candidate, as Sweat has been rumored to be unhappy in Arizona since the early days of the offseason after the Cardinals fired Jonathan Gannon.
Sweat's production has picked up the pace in recent weeks, just in time for a potential deal to get done while maximizing his value.
The Cardinals are rumored to be in search of a second-round pick, though we'll see if the deadline can bring any desperate team looking for a playoff push to that price tag. It's likely we see a team package a third and a high Day 3 pick for Sweat, if he is traded.
Baker isn't quite knocking on the door to be traded like many believe Sweat is, though the reality is the star safety is getting another year older and he's not quite closer to winning a championship in the desert.
"I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here," he said to ESPN last week. "And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."
More than anything, this would be a move to place Baker at the forefront of competing on a playoff team, something he's only done once in his decade of service for the Cardinals.
This third spot is where things can get tricky, though after Harrison and Brissett were moved, there's not bountiful options for Arizona in terms of potential trade candidates.
We arrive to Conner, who hasn't played at all this season after being injured in Week 3 of last season with a foot/ankle injury. The veteran running back restructured his deal to remain in Arizona this past offseason, though the Cardinals' backfield (when healthy) is so crowded there's essentially no room for him.
Conner, much like Baker, is on the tail end of his career, and the organization just might do right by taking him off injured reserve and dealing him to a playoff team. He's on the final year of his contract and Arizona clearly wanted to get younger at the position this past offseason.

title: Cardinals-Ravens Trade For Jacoby Brissett is Major Win for Arizona
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are finally pulling off a trade involving quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
Brissett is reportedly being dealt to the Baltimore Ravens. While terms are not yet known, getting any sort of draft capital for Brissett is a massive win for Arizona, who recently demoted Brissett to No. 3 duties.
Trade: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, per @RapSheet and me. Deal is expected to be completed this weekend. The Ravens lost QB Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury, and his backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley to turf toe. pic.twitter.com/sGpFSxYc5u
Brissett was benched this past weekend while Gardner Minshew replaced him in the third quarter of Arizona's Week 8 matchup in Dallas, leading four straight scoring drives and ultimately an upset victory over the Cowboys.
From there, the writing was clearly on the wall for not only a demotion for Brissett, but a trade as well.
After holding out for a new contract and leading the Cardinals to a poor start in 2026, pressure mounted for Arizona to make a move to Minshew.
“That’s not easy. It’s not a fun phone call," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of benching Brissett ahead of Week 9.
"There’s no book for that. There’s a human element to it. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby, the person. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby, the player. Like I told you guys yesterday, it was not all on him. This was collective and starting with me, but the position that those guys sign up for, we know the deal. We needed a spark and obviously Gardner gave us one.”
Brissett will not make it in time for Baltimore's Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but a deal is expected to be done in the coming days. The Ravens have lost Lamar Jackson and Snoop Huntley due to injuries, seeing their quarterback room decimated nearly overnight.
That made the Cardinals and Ravens ideal trade partners in terms of opportunity for Baltimore and value for Arizona.
What exactly the Cardinals are getting in return for Brissett remains to be seen, though Arizona is expected to get a low Day 3 pick (rounds six or seven) for the veteran passer, which sees their trade deadline draft-pick haul expand after netting a second-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago.
While the Ravens get a veteran quarterback who has prior experience with their own quarterbacks coach in Israel Woolfork, Arizona also finds themselves as a massive winner here — clearing the path for rookie Carson Beck to earn eventual playing time while adding to their pool draft picks.
The Cardinals may not be done, either. Names such as Josh Sweat and Budda Baker have recently been involved in trade rumors.
The NFL's trade deadline is Nov. 10.

title: Cardinals-Seahawks Week 9 Battle Takes Major Twist
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals will not see Sam Darnold on Sunday.
The Seattle Seahawks are ruling Darnold out with a quad injury ahead of Week 9's meeting at Lumen Field. Drew Lock will start in his place.
Seahawks QB Sam Darnold will be out Sunday vs. Arizona due to quad injury, per HC  Mike Macdonald.
The Cardinals previously saw Lock in their Week 2 loss at State Farm Stadium, where Seattle's offense put up 381 total yards and 30+ points in a 31-7 blowout over Arizona.
Prior to that matchup, Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur gave a glowing review of Darnold.
"Sam's a great quarterback. Obviously, I'd say I know Sam a little bit better than Drew because I did have, I guess you could say, a month or so with him even though he wasn't in the building in New York. I've always really respected him dating back to USC. Understanding that he was a young quarterback going through it," said LaFleur back ahead of Week 2.
"Every situation's different by the quarterback and by the club, and he got himself in a very stable situation. I think starting in San Francisco, Minnesota, and then obviously in Seattle. It's not shocking that they got the result they did last year. They are, in my opinion, the best coached team in football. I think they have the best defense in football. In my opinion, they have a really, really good quarterback with it. Yeah, he's down this week, but again, like I just said with Drew, the moment's not too big for him. I think he's a good quarterback who's played a lot of good football."
Now, Lock is set for his third start of the season.
The Seahawks are 4-4 and are have lost their last three-of-four meetings entering Week 9. They're also playing on a short week after featuring on Monday Night Football.
When Lock started for Seattle, he orchestrated a fairly efficient game — going 19/26 passing for three touchdowns and no interceptions. He was also sacked only once by the Cardinals' defense.
Darnold has struggled in 2026, so this might not be a bad switch for the Seahawks' offense — especially if he can again take advantage of a Cardinals defense that's allowed five 30+ point outings in their last six games.
Arizona's fresh off a Week 8 upset over the Dallas Cowboys and are hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all regular season.
ESPN's football power index gives the Cardinals just a 17.9% chance to win against the Seahawks.

title: Jeremiyah Love Joins Troubling Cardinals Trend Among Recent Draft Picks
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without Jeremiyah Love moving into the foreseeable future after the organization placed him on injured reserve, ensuring he'll miss at minimum the next four weeks.
The Cardinals feel like they can't catch a break with the recent slew of injuries to younger players, and Love is just the latest of an unfortunate trend of recent first-round draft picks to miss time in their rookie season:
Love, first eligible to come off injured reserve in Week 13, will miss at least six games minimum in his rookie season thanks to three different ankle injuries suffered since preseason.
Love was hurt on the 14th and final touch of his preseason debut, which saw him miss the final two games. However, Love would return for the regular season ready to go.
Love didn't miss any of the first five weeks, though a different ankle injury hindered him – enough to make head coach Mike LaFleur sit the third overall pick for two consecutive weeks before returning in Week 8.
Love was hurt in the first half in Dallas with a high ankle sprain and now lands on injured reserve.
Ahead of 2025's training camp, the Cardinals announced Nolen would miss significant time due to a calf injury suffered while training at the team's facility.
The defensive lineman would miss the first seven games of the season before returning on Monday Night Football against the Dallas Cowboys, putting on a show and generating buzz within Arizona's fan base.
However, Nolen would only play six games before suffering a knee injury against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 16, putting him on injured reserve with what was later revealed to be a meniscus injury.
He made a full recovery and was ready to go for this year's version of training camp.
Robinson was hurt during a preseason practice, suffering a calf injury (many speculate Robinson specifically strained or tore his achilles tendon) and placing him on injured reserve before the regular season began.
He missed all but six games during his rookie year.
It is important to note the rookie defensive lineman also lost his mother before officially returning from his injury, which surely played some part in his delayed return to the field as well.
The Cardinals' injury woes extend past the first round of their draft classes.
Recently, 2026 second-round pick Chase Bisontis is set to miss his entire rookie year due to an MCL injury after looking impressive in preseason play. 2026 fourth-round pick Kaleb Proctor is also on injured reserve for the entire year with a meniscus injury.
2025 saw second-round pick Will Johnson miss five games while he's currently on injured reserve with a neck injury. Sixth-round pick from the class, Hayden Conner, began his rookie season on injured reserve after hurting his knee and played just five games for the Cardinals last season.
And for what it's worth, 2025 seventh-round pick Kitan Crawford did play most of his rookie season but went on injured reserve after 2026's season opener with an ankle injury.
2024 third-round pick Elijah Jones missed his entire rookie campaign due to an ankle injury. He played in just ten games for the Cardinals last season and now isn't even on the roster. Fifth-round pick Christian Jones had played a total of four games through his first two seasons due to ankle and knee issues before being cut this summer.

title: Cardinals RB Tyler Allgeier Wins Player of the Week Award
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier put the team on his back in Week 8's upset win over the Dallas Cowboys, rushing for 147 yards and one touchdown on 11 carries.
He also notched 44 receiving yards on five receptions and a touchdown through the air to pour in a performance worthy of NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
More info from the team's Media Relations Dept.:
"This is Allgeier’s first career selection as Player of the Week. He is also the third Cardinals player to earn Player of the Week honors this season after Chad Ryland (Week 6) and Simi Fehoko (Week 1) were each selected as NFC Special Teams Player of the Week. The Cardinals three Player of the Week selections are the most for the team in a single season since 2021 (seven).
"Allgeier finished Sunday’s win over the Cowboys with 147 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries (13.4 avg.) to go along with five receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown. He established career highs for rushing yards (147) and scrimmage yards (191), had his first career outing with both a rushing and receiving touchdown and had the two longest runs (63 and 52 yards) in his career. Allgeier’s 191 scrimmage yards led the NFL in Week 8 and his 63-yard touchdown run is the longest rushing touchdown in the NFL this season.
"He became just the fourth player in Cardinals franchise history to have 185+ scrimmage yards, 1+ rushing touchdown and 1+ touchdown reception in the same game, joining Ottis Anderson (11/4/1979 vs. Min), Wayne Morris (11/6/1977 @ Min) and Ollie Matson (twice - 10/20/1957 @ Was and 11/21/54 vs. Was).
"Allgeier totaled 184 yards (143 rushing; 41 receiving) and two touchdowns (1 rushing; 1 receiving) in the 2nd half of last Sunday’s game. He became the first player in franchise history to have 180+ yards from scrimmage, a rushing touchdown and a receiving touchdown all in the second half of a game. In the 3rd quarter, Allgeier started the Cardinals comeback with a career-long 63-yard run. On Arizona’s next possession, his next carry went for 52 yards. He became the first NFL player to gain 50+ yards on two straight carries within a game since Tampa Bay RB Doug Martin had TD runs of 67 and 70 yards on 11/4/12 at Oakland. Allgeier became the first Cardinals player to accomplish the feat since RB LeShon Johnson (touchdown runs of 56 and 70 yards) on 9/22/1996 at New Orleans."
Especially with Jeremiyah Love out for the foreseeable future, Arizona will lean on Allgeier heavily in the next few weeks.

title: Cardinals Eying These 3 Free Agents After Jeremiyah Love Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals officially placed running back Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve today, losing their star rookie for at least the next four weeks at a minimum.
It's a big blow for the Cardinals, though Arizona can't afford to stop their operation fresh off an upset win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.
While Tyler Allgeier is healthy and fresh off a monster performance, the Cardinals also may be without running back Bam Knight — who is in concussion protocol.
Needless to say, Arizona will need some fresh faces in their backfield.
As the team prepares for a road test against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9, the Cardinals tried out the following running backs according to the league's transaction wire:
Bentley played his college football at SMU (2019-21) and Ole Miss (2022-24) before declaring for the draft in 2025.
Bentley went undrafted in the 2025 NFL Draft and signed with the Indianapolis Colts as a free agent and appeared in one game for the organization last season, mostly owning practice squad duties.
Bentley was cut ahead of 2026 final roster dues and was picked up by the New Orleans Saints for two weeks before later being released.
He has logged just one NFL carry.
Jefferson has the most NFL experience out of the three running backs on this list, first approaching the league with the Detroit Lions as a seventh-round pick in 2021. He played in seven games during his rookie season.
He spent the next few seasons either injured or on Detroit's practice squad, not appearing in a single game for the Lions through the end of his tenure in 2024.
Jefferson inked a deal with the Tennessee Titans in training camp last season but was released ahead of final roster cuts. Just days later, he landed with the Cardinals — where he ultimately played in two games for Arizona. He did not re-sign with the team last offseason.
Jefferson spent brief moments with the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota this offseason before he was released from the Vikings with an injury designation on Aug. 30. His injury was not disclosed.
Jefferson has played in a total of 11 games with 96 yards on 21 rushes and two touchdowns.
Tau-Tolliver, undrafted this past offseason, played his first four college seasons at Sacramento State before transferring to Michigan State last year.
He signed with the Baltimore Ravens as a rookie free agent and was waived ahead of final roster cuts this August.

title: Breaking Down the Fallout for Cardinals, Jeremiyah Love After IR Move
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are reportedly placing Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve, ensuring the rookie running back will miss at least the next four games with a high ankle sprain.
It's a gut-punch for numerous reasons, as the third overall pick hasn't been fully healthy since preseason. Love's third ankle injury of his rookie season is now his most concerning.
How do the dominoes fall from here?
Love is first eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 13 against the Philadelphia Eagles. It's important to note Arizona has a bye week in Week 14, which may be tempting for the Cardinals to keep Love out for even more time to ensure he's properly healed.
After missing two prior games, Love's move to injured reserve makes him the third consecutive first-round pick by Arizona to miss at least six weeks of his rookie season, following in the footsteps of Darius Robinson (2024) and Walter Nolen III (2025).
Love was previously hindered by two different ankle injuries — one after playing a half of preseason and the next following him through the opening stages of the regular season, which caused him to be shut down for two weeks before returning on Sunday in Dallas .
Love still has an opportunity to return and finish his first season on a high note, though his inability to stay healthy largely suggests Arizona will be extra careful with his return, especially if the Cardinals are out of the playoff hunt when he is eligible to return.
His 2026 outlook, barring an eye-opening return full of highlight reel plays, will be overall disappointing. The third overall pick was expected to help take the Cardinals' offense to new levels, and while there's been small glimpses of his potential, nothing sustainable has been strung together to this point.
That begins to bleed into Love's outlook for the future, at least from an organization standpoint. By taking Love with the third pick, they instantly gave him the highest total of guaranteed money for any running back in the league. Part of the understanding is the Cardinals would use Love early and often to get the most bang for their buck, especially on his expensive rookie deal where he's still fresh.
It's fair to say Arizona hasn't gotten matched production for their value, for various reasons. While this won't lead to the Cardinals force-feeding Love 30 carries per game in the future, there is a financial component to his place in Arizona's offense.
The Cardinals, essentially, were hoping to have one of the league's best running backs early in his prime and paid the price to do so. The first of a four-year contract (with an option for a fifth season) hasn't paid out like they would have hoped.
And to be very clear, that's not on Love. He didn't choose to be taken so high with massive expectations placed immediately on his shoulders, nor was he hoping for such an injury-riddled season.
While it's been a forgettable start, Love should return at full health at some point before the end of the season, hopefully to build some momentum for a strong sophomore year in 2027.
Mike LaFleur currently has one healthy running back on his roster in Tyler Allgeier thanks to Love hitting injured reserve and Bam Knight currently in concussion protocol.
Allgeier, while impressing as a one-man show in the second half of the team's win against Dallas, shouldn't be relied on for similar production again within the next month of play. Knight's status for the foreseeable future is cloudy at best in this moment
Evan Hull and Jerome Ford exist as practice squad options for the Cardinals to elevate to the active roster.
The NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline is a week away, though it's unlikely the Cardinals give up anything significant after sinking so many resources into their running back room this offseason.
Arizona is likely to bring in some free agent running backs for visits or tryouts. At this point in the season, familiarity is often a big bonus for veterans to get acclimated as soon as possible.
Two potential names to watch here would be Raheem Mostert or Cam Akers — both previously spent time under LaFleur in his past stints with the 49ers (Mostert) or Akers (Rams) and would be fairly fluent in absorbing LaFleur's system and terminology.
That same logic applies to potentially poaching a player off another team's practice squad. Note, if Arizona does take that route, that player would have to be on the Cardinals' active roster for a minimum of three weeks.
Arizona would have to be extremely confident in doing so — one name to watch would be familiar face Michael Carter, who has bounced up and down on the Tennessee Titans' practice squad this season, though as of this moment he's on their active roster after being elevated.
The Cardinals do have two potential options on injured reserve with James Conner and Trey Benson, though it's not currently known if either is close to potentially returning. For what it's worth, Benson would have to reach an injury settlement before being released if he wants to play in 2026 while Conner does have a designation to return.

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love Will Miss More Time With Ankle Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals will be without Jeremiyah Love for the next four weeks, at minimum.
Love is hitting injured reserve, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, after suffering an ankle injury in the team's Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
"Sources: #AZCardinals RB Jeremiyah Love is headed to Injured Reserve because of a high-ankle sprain that knocks him out 4-5 weeks. Arizona’s first-round pick has previously been dealing with a different ankle sprain."
Love is eligible to return in Week 13 against the Philadelphia at the earliest, which will see him miss a total of six games at minimum to begin his NFL career.
This is now the third different ankle injury that has plagued Love in his rookie season. Love was hurt in preseason play but managed to recover ahead of the regular season before suffering an opposite ankle injury, one that hindered him playing before the Cardinals shut him down for two games.
Sunday was Love's return to action, though Arizona is now taking a precautious approach with their third overall pick.
Previously meeting with reporters on Monday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said he hadn't yet talked to Love about the injury as players had Monday off.
“This is new, so this is not the left ankle or the right. It’s a new portion of the ankle. I’ll keep it at that. I’m going to know a little bit more tomorrow. I haven’t talked to him yet, so out of respect of not talking to him yet, I’ll give you guys more on Wednesday," he said.
When asked if injured reserve was a possibility, LaFleur added:
“Hang with me on that one. I’ll talk to you guys’ Wednesday.”
Love was expected to bring a dynamic splash of playmaking to the Cardinals' offense as a first-round pick, and while flashes have pretty clearly shown he's a capable back, Love simply hasn't been able to shake injuries in his rookie campaign.
Fellow Cardinals running back Bam Knight is in concussion protocol after suffering a scary blow to the head against Dallas, leaving just Tyler Allgeier as the lone running back on Arizona's active roster. It's likely Evan Hull gets called up while the Cardinals may explore other avenues such as free agency or other NFL practice squads.
Arizona travels to face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9. LaFleur will meet with reporters on Wednesday.

title: Why Falcons’ Nightmare in Tampa Could Help Them Against Bengals in Madrid
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are in pretty unique territory.
After playing a monsoon of a road game in a history-making 16-0 road loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Atlanta has gone abroad .
On Sunday, the Falcons (3-5) face the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) in the NFL’s second-ever game in Madrid, Spain, for a Week 9 NFC versus AFC clash .
“The challenges week to week are so vastly different in this league,” said head coach Kevin Stefanski . “You have to be ready to adapt at any moment’s notice.”
Last Sunday, Nov. 1, Atlanta was on the receiving end of a shutout against the Bucs as a torrential downpour drenched the players in Raymond James Stadium.
The Falcons aren’t accustomed to rainy conditions. They play at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which features a retractable roof that opens only in response to Atlanta’s weather and seasonal conditions.
Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions, and Tampa became the first NFL team to win a game without a completed pass since 1974.
Want to know how bad of a stat that is? Passing the football in wasn’t as prominent in 1974 as it is now.
What an encore for the spooky Halloween holiday that happened a day before the Falcons-Bucs game.
It brought Atlanta back down to earth just a week after knocking off the undefeated San Francisco 49ers 29-20 . Talk about a roller coaster of a season.
“You spend time on the game last week, and you have honest conversations with each other,” Stefanski reflected. “Certainly feel like that experience will serve us well moving forward.”
After struggling to adjust to the elements in Tampa, the Falcons now have another opportunity to prove they can handle unfamiliar circumstances, this time with a six-hour time difference and an unconventional travel schedule.
In Madrid, adaptability is once again the name of the game.
The Falcons took the eight-hour flight from Atlanta to Madrid on Tuesday and landed on Wednesday morning. They immediately began walkthroughs to prepare for battle against the streaking Bengals, winners of three straight games.
For normal road games, the Falcons typically leave on the day before the Sunday kickoff.
So everything on the itinerary has been moved up significantly to allow adequate rest and training.
“Going into an international game, a little bit of a different schedule,” Stefanski said. “For us as coaches and players, we see that as a positive.”
Falcons-Bengals kicks off at 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time, which is 3:30 p.m. Madrid time. Atlanta is the designated home team.
Light showers are expected, but the game is at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, which has a retractable roof. NFL Network is set to televise the game.
Gerald Thomas, III, is a national award-winning reporter contributing to Atlanta Falcons On SI. He has several years of writing and editorial experience, including covering college athletics under the USA TODAY umbrella.

title: Where the Atlanta Falcons Stand in the NFC South Following Week 8
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are entering a critical stretch of their 2026 season, and their latest loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has made the NFC South even tighter.
Atlanta suffered a 16-0 shutout against Tampa Bay on Sunday, November 1, missing an opportunity to claim first place in the division. With the regular season approaching its halfway point, the Falcons have limited room for error as they attempt to overtake not one, but two division rivals.
Despite the disappointing result, Atlanta remains within striking distance of the division lead. Here is where each team stands following Week 8.
Carolina currently holds the top spot in the division despite having a losing record. The Panthers suffered a loss to the Green Bay Packers, allowing Tampa Bay and Atlanta to remain within reach.
The Buccaneers currently hold the tiebreaker over Atlanta thanks to their 2-0 divisional record. The Falcons, meanwhile, are 1-2 against NFC South opponents, making their remaining divisional matchups increasingly important.
New Orleans sits at the bottom of the standings at 2-5, one game behind Atlanta and Tampa Bay.
The good news for Atlanta is that the NFC South remains wide open. The Falcons are just half a game behind Carolina and have plenty of opportunities to improve their position over the remaining weeks.
However, their latest loss exposed some concerns that need to be addressed. Atlanta struggled offensively against Tampa Bay, failing to score a single point while allowing the Buccaneers to control the game on the ground.
The Falcons cannot afford many more performances like that, particularly against divisional opponents.
Their divisional record will also be something to monitor. With Tampa Bay already owning a head-to-head victory, Atlanta needs to find a way to even the playing field when these teams meet again.
The Falcons will turn their attention to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 9. Atlanta will travel to Madrid, Spain, for an international matchup that presents an opportunity to get back into the win column.
A victory would move Atlanta to 4-5 and keep the team firmly in the NFC South conversation. The Panthers are 2.5-point underdogs at home to the Denver Broncos, who are coming off an emotional win against the Kansas City Chiefs.  The Buccaneers are six-point underdogs at Chicago on Sunday. Night.
There's a very real scenario where a 3-5 team leads the division. However, there's also a very real scenario where the Falcons are in first place next week. And as ridiculous as it sounds, if the Saints beat the Browns, as the only team favored in the NFC South this week, and the rest lose, New Orleans moves into a tie for first place.
For Atlanta, the formula is simple. The Falcons need to start stacking wins, improve their divisional record and take advantage of the opportunities ahead.
The NFC South is still within reach, but after Sunday's shutout, Atlanta needs to respond quickly if it wants to make a serious push for the division title.

title: Falcons Get Encouraging Injury News Ahead of Bengals Matchup in Spain
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons received some much-needed injury news Wednesday as the team prepares for its Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain.
Atlanta has been dealing with several injuries over the past couple of weeks, particularly on defense. However, the Falcons' estimated injury report following Wednesday's walkthrough provided some optimism regarding the potential returns of three important contributors.
The biggest development was the return of defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. to full participation. Bowman, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, had missed the Falcons' previous two games but appears to be making progress toward returning to the lineup.
Linebacker Divine Deablo and running back Brian Robinson Jr. also provided encouraging updates. Deablo, who has been dealing with a forearm injury, was listed as a limited participant. Robinson, meanwhile, was also limited as he continues working his way back from a hamstring injury.
Having all three players show signs of progress is encouraging news for Atlanta, especially with a challenging international matchup against Cincinnati approaching.
Another notable development from Wednesday's walkthrough was the return of edge rusher James Pearce Jr.
Pearce missed the first eight games of the season while serving a suspension, but is now back with the team and working toward making his season debut against Cincinnati .
Head coach Kevin Stefanski expressed confidence in Pearce's football readiness, noting that the young pass rusher has spent the past month working with the Falcons' strength staff.
However, Atlanta will use the remainder of the week to determine how many snaps Pearce will receive against the Bengals.
His return could provide a significant boost to a Falcons defense that needs additional help generating pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
Here is Atlanta's estimated injury report following Wednesday's walkthrough:
It is important to note that Wednesday's report was an estimate because the Falcons held a walkthrough after arriving in Spain early Wednesday morning.
The Falcons still have some injury concerns heading into Sunday's matchup, but Wednesday brought several reasons for optimism.
Bowman's return to full participation is particularly encouraging, while Deablo and Robinson taking part in the walkthrough in a limited capacity gives Atlanta hope that they could be trending in the right direction.
Meanwhile, Pearce's return gives the defense another potential weapon as the Falcons look to get back on track following their disappointing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Atlanta will continue its preparation in Madrid throughout the week before facing Cincinnati on Sunday. The next injury updates will be important in determining which players will be available as the Falcons look to get back into the win column.

title: Should the Falcons Trade Tua Tagovailoa? The Case For and Against Moving QB
full_text:
As the trade deadline approaches in less than a week on Nov. 10, names have begun swirling about who will be on the move across the NFL.
From top stars like Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor to depth pieces for contenders, it’s always a fun part of the season.
One name that has ascended in trade talks is Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa . The seventh-year quarterback and former Pro Bowler has backed up Michael Penix Jr. this season after returning from an early-season oblique injury soon after being named the Week 1 starter.
He’s appeared in just one game for Atlanta, its 31-23 Week 5 loss to the Baltimore Ravens , where he threw the game-sealing overtime interception after Penix suffered a rib injury late in regulation. Tagovailoa has completed 2 of 3 pass attempts for 34 yards all year.
Tagovailoa arrived in Atlanta on a one-year deal worth $1.2 million after being released by the Miami Dolphins as a potential candidate to lead the Falcons’ (3-5) offense. Instead, he’s holding the clipboard on the sideline as the NFL reaches the halfway point of the season.
The question remains: Should Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham explore trade opportunities to move Tua?
Here’s the case for and against.
There’s a quarterback desperation in the NFL, especially in Baltimore. Wouldn’t it be wild to see Tagovailoa suit up for the team he recently gifted a win to, right?
But the Ravens are in quarterback purgatory right now. Two-time MVP Lamar Jackson has battled an ankle injury just about all season, and then injured his throwing-hand thumb while returning last week against the Buffalo Bills. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley suffered turf toe in the same game and is out for the season.
Now the Ravens turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to start moving forward. Sound familiar, Jack Strand fans?
The Ravens are currently last in the AFC North with a 4-4 record, but are two games behind No. 1 Pittsburgh Steelers. The division crown is very much still in play despite the quarterback injuries, and they're just one game behind for the seventh playoff spot.
Another team to watch is the Philadelphia Eagles after the debacle of handling Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation. But they may actually mail it in on the season and become sellers at the deadline, outside of running back Saquon Barkley.
But regardless, if any team wants Tagovailoa, he’ll be easily absorbed on a cheap contract.
After a season that started with a Rolodex of quarterbacks – Cooper Rush, Jack Strand – maybe the Falcons shouldn’t trade Tagovailoa.
Andy Dalton is now the Falcons’ emergency third-string quarterback.
Atlanta needs the depth under center.
As much as fans don’t want to speak it out loud – knock on wood before reading further – Michael Penix Jr. does have durability issues with three torn ACL injuries. The Falcons also held their breath when he hurt his ribs against Baltimore.
Love him or hate him, but Tagovailoa is the only other quarterback currently on the roster outside of Penix that would give Atlanta a shot to win games. Let’s not conveniently forget it wasn’t long ago he was leading the NFL in passer rating, yardage, and completion percentage. His passer rating last season in Miami was better than both Penix and Kirk Cousins' passer rating for the Falcons last season.
If the Falcons had benched Penix for tossing four interceptions , Tagovailoa may have come in to throw a couple more, but he’s the best option.
Plus, is the return that the team would get on the trade even worth it? Moving a quarterback getting paid for a little over a million probably won’t move the needle much. We’re talking like Day 3 NFL Draft picks here.
That’s not going to help the Falcons right now, in a year when they’ve been on a roller-coaster ride but are still in play for the NFC South division title.
Hear out offers and inquiries if they come.
But if it’s not a bona fide move or a heist that’ll upgrade the Falcons, like the Gervon Dexter Sr. trade , stand pat.
For those pro-Tua, he adds some insurance to a quarterback room that Atlanta could still very well be in the NFL Draft market for in 2027.
For the anti-Tuas, just wait on it. He’ll be off the team in a matter of months and searching for a new home.

title: Where Did the Falcons Fall After Dreadful Loss to Buccaneers?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons dropped an important NFC South matchup on Sunday, falling in humiliating fashion. Despite not completing a pass in a torrential downpour in Tampa, the Buccaneers smothered the Falcons 16-0.
Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions while the defense allowed 324 yards on the ground , and the Falcons will be eager to move on to next week. But Sunday brings another challenge, with the Falcons heading across the pond to face the high-flying Cincinnati Bengals in Week 9.
Joe Burrow leads the NFL’s top passing offense (288.4 yards per game) and the second-highest scoring unit (29.4 points per game). The Falcons, one of the NFL’s best offenses (Week 8 notwithstanding) since Penix returned in Week 3, will need to keep pace. James Pearce Jr.'s return could prove pivotal.
Elsewhere in the division, the Panthers lost a second straight game, and the Saints lost their fourth game in their last five. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from the national sites and put them all in one place for fans.
See below where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
The Falcons dropped three spots in Conor Orr’s power rankings, and the weather conditions had a lot to do with that. He said Atlanta “missed an opportunity” to let running back Bijan Robinson run the show, joking that the Falcons could have simply run the wildcat to better results.

title: Falcons Place Samson Ebukam on Injured Reserve, Make Additional Roster Move
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are making multiple roster moves as they prepare for Sunday’s matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain.
Atlanta has placed edge rusher Samson Ebukam on injured reserve following a hamstring injury suffered during Sunday’s 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The move means Ebukam will miss at least the next four games before becoming eligible to return.
The veteran defensive end was already expected to miss the Bengals matchup after head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Monday that Ebukam was dealing with a hamstring injury . The decision to place him on injured reserve indicates the Falcons will be without one of their key defensive contributors for an extended period.
Through seven appearances this season, Ebukam recorded 2.5 sacks, 11 combined tackles, two tackles for loss, and nine quarterback hits. His presence has been valuable to Atlanta’s defensive front, particularly as a pass rusher.
The Falcons will now have to find ways to replace his production while he recovers.
Atlanta also made a corresponding series of roster moves, signing defensive end Drake Jackson back to the practice squad after releasing him from the active roster Monday.
Jackson’s return provides the Falcons with additional defensive line depth as they navigate Ebukam’s absence. The former second-round pick has experience as an edge defender and gives Atlanta another option within its practice squad.
To make room for Jackson, the Falcons released offensive lineman Colby Sorsdal from the practice squad.
The moves came one day after the Falcons released Jackson and defensive lineman Jared Ivey from their active roster as the team prepared for the return of James Pearce Jr. from his league suspension.
Pearce’s reinstatement gives the Falcons another option along the defensive front, but losing Ebukam creates a significant hole in the rotation.
The Falcons enter Week 9 at 3-5, looking to turn things around after a disappointing shutout loss to Tampa Bay.
Atlanta travels to Madrid to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, with its defensive front facing another test as the team works through its latest personnel changes.
Ebukam’s absence will put additional pressure on the remaining defensive ends to generate consistent quarterback pressure and help Atlanta get back on track.

title: Updated Atlanta Falcons Draft Position, Top 3 Needs, and Mock Draft Selections
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had a chance to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South on Sunday and put a stake in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' chances of winning the division for the fifth time in six seasons.
Instead of becoming the only team with a .500 record and dropping Tampa Bay to 2-6, the Falcons find themselves sitting at 3-5 and looking up in the standings at both the Buccaneers (3-5) and the Carolina Panthers (3-4). Both teams have the tiebreaker over the Falcons via head-to-head record.
If there's a silver lining to this year's struggles, it's that the Falcons have a full allotment of draft picks after not having a first-round pick in 2026. New general manager Ian Cunningham's first class has been a success, with big-time contributions from linebackers Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr., selected in the fourth and sixth rounds, respectively.
Cornerback Avieon Terrell, the team's first selection, has struggled to get healthy, but has played well when available, and wide receiver Zachariah Branch has shown flashes. Atlanta lost sixth-round defensive tackle Anterio Thompson to a medical condition, and seventh-round offensive tackle Ethan Onianwa has been getting experience on special teams.
Looking towards next season, the Falcons currently sit with the No. 13 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The jury is still out on Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback as he uses this season to prove he can be the long-term answer for Atlanta and keep them out of the quarterback market in the offseason.
Sunday's game in the Tampa monsoon notwithstanding, he's played well enough for the Falcons to look in another direction in the first round, but he'll need to bounce back from Sunday's four-interception performance and stay healthy for 15 games.
Taking quarterback off the table, offensive tackle is the biggest need on this team early in the draft. Jake Matthews is 34 years old, and the iron man has shown signs of Father Time catching up to him this year. At right tackle, Jawaan Taylor is on a one-year contract and scheduled to be a free agent at the end of the season.
Cornerback is arguably the No. 2 need on this team. The Falcons selected Terrell at No. 48, but he's the first Day 1 or Day 2 cornerback the Falcons have taken since they drafted his brother in the first round in 2020. Injuries forced Mike Hughes into being the Falcons' No. 1 option at times this year, and he should be at best a No. 3 and probably best suited for a No. 4.
Nickel has been a problem too. Billy Bowman Jr. was drafted for the position in 2025, but he's only been available for 10 of 25 games the Falcons have played since being drafted in the fourth round out of Oklahoma. The Falcons have had to piece together the secondary from game to game, and they need another infusion of talent and depth.
Wide receiver comes in at No. 3 on the team's list of needs. Drake London is set at No. 1 for the foreseeable future. Jahan Dotson was signed as a free agent this offseason. However, he's better suited to a slot / No. 3 role, and he's getting paid like it. Branch is a nice addition, but the Falcons need more size, explosiveness, and depth.
Recent mock drafts have the Falcons addressing their biggest need at offensive tackle. On SI draft analyst Justin Melo has Atlanta taking Lance Heard from the surprising No. 7 Kentucky Wildcats.
"Atlanta Falcons offensive line coach Bill Callahan will have a say if the organization drafts an offensive tackle. He'll love Kentucky's Lance Heard, who fits his mold from a size and physicality perspective. This is all about getting a Jake Matthews replacement," Melo wrote On SI Draft.
Tankathon also has the Falcons going with an offensive tackle in Texas Longhorns product Trevor Goosby . Goosby is out for the remainder of the 2026 season after having surgery to repair a torn left patellar tendon. Early this season, he was considered a top-10 prospect, but his stock has fallen a bit with the injury.
If the Falcons are picking No. 13 in April, it equates to a 7-10 or 8-9 type of record. It's hard to picture this team going 7-10 if Michael Penix Jr. has an excellent second half of the season.
That brings up a couple of what-if scenarios that Cunningham will ponder during the draft process.
1. Can Penix establish himself as a franchise quarterback and the team still struggles this year? Recent history would say "no." When the Falcons have gotten good quarterback play, they've won. When they've gotten bad quarterback play, they've lost. A 7-10 season would likely mean Penix struggled in the second half.
2. If they're picking No. 13, is there a quarterback available that would be worth taking without reaching?
The Rams used the Falcons' No. 13 overall pick in the last draft to take quarterback Ty Simpson out of Alabama. That felt like a reach, and the Falcons got good value for their trade of that pick in James Pearce Jr.
But this is supposed to be a deeper draft class at quarterback, though that sentiment seems to be waning as the season rolls along.
Melo has Arch Manning in range, selected by the Arizona Cardinals at No. 12. There's a better-than-average chance he's not in the draft and returns to college football. The Cleveland Browns select Trinidad Chambliss at No. 16 out of Ole Miss, and he's the final quarterback taken in the first round.
There's a scenario where the Falcons would like to draft a quarterback, but there isn't one they like enough in the middle of the draft, and they find themselves stuck in purgatory again.
The best-case scenario for the Falcons is that Penix plays well for the remainder of the season, and Atlanta finds itself picking in the late teens or even early 20s. Then they can address one of their needs with the prospect they like best. Goosby is still on Melo's board at No. 24. Offensive tackle Zereoue of Utah is taken by the Panthers at No. 19.
Cornerbacks Ellis Robinson IV from Georgia and Kelley Jones of Mississippi State go to the Cowboys and Bengals at No. 20 and No. 23 respectively.
The game on Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals has a must-win feeling to it. Win and move to 4-5, and the Falcons will be right in the thick of the NFC South.
Lose and drop to 3-6, and these mock drafts start becoming a lot more interesting.

title: Falcons Get James Pearce Jr. Back, Release 2 Defenders
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are getting a key piece of their pass rush back while making adjustments to their defensive personnel ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain.
Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. has officially been reinstated by the NFL on Monday, making him eligible to return following his eight-game suspension .
Pearce’s reinstatement comes alongside two defensive roster moves. Atlanta waived defensive lineman Jared Ivey and released defensive end Drake Jackson, opening two spots on its 53-man roster as the team prepares for its international matchup, one of which will be filled by Pearce.
Pearce’s return could provide a significant boost to a Falcons defense looking to turn things around after Sunday’s disappointing 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The rookie led Atlanta with 10.5 sacks last season and emerged as one of the team’s most productive pass rushers. His ability to generate pressure could be particularly important as the Falcons look to improve their defensive production heading into the second half of the season against a team like the Bengals, who have an explosive passing game.
Ivey appeared in seven games for Atlanta this season after joining the organization through waivers following the NFL’s initial roster cutdowns in August. He recorded eight combined tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits.
Jackson joined Atlanta’s practice squad in September before being signed to the active roster on Oct. 24. He appeared in two games for the Falcons this season.
Although both defenders are now off the active roster, their time in Atlanta may not necessarily be over. Ivey and Jackson could potentially return to the Falcons’ practice squad if they clear waivers and the organization elects to bring them back.
The timing of the moves is notable, with Pearce officially back in the fold. Atlanta now has additional flexibility to adjust its defensive personnel while making room for the return of one of its most important pass-rushing contributors.
The Falcons enter Week 9 with a 3-5 record and will look to get back on track against Cincinnati. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 overtime win over 1-7 Tennessee Titans.  Sunday’s matchup in Madrid will provide an opportunity for Atlanta to get its defense back on track, with Pearce eligible to return.

title: Falcons Lose Two Key Contributors Ahead of Game in Spain
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will be without two important players when they travel to Madrid, Spain, to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski announced Monday that defensive end Samson Ebukam and rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch are dealing with hamstring injuries that will keep both players out of the Week 9 matchup.
“Samson Ebukam, Zachariah Branch have hamstring injuries,” Stefanski said to open his Monday press conference. “That’s going to keep them out of this game. Not sure, long term, how many games those types of injuries will be, but we’ll obviously treat those and then see how it goes over the next couple of weeks.”
The injuries leave Atlanta without contributors on both sides of the football as the team begins preparations for its international matchup against Cincinnati.
Ebukam has been a consistent presence in Atlanta’s defensive line rotation throughout his first season with the organization.
The veteran defensive end joined the Falcons this offseason after spending the previous two seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. His arrival also reunited him with defensive line coach Nate Ollie, whom he previously worked with in Indianapolis.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, Ebukam has recorded 2.5 sacks and 15 quarterback pressures, according to Next Gen Stats. His pressure total ranks fifth among Falcons defenders.
His absence creates another challenge for Atlanta’s pass rush, which will need additional production from the remaining defensive line rotation against a Cincinnati offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow.
The Falcons will likely need other defensive ends to take on expanded responsibilities while Ebukam recovers.
Branch’s absence will also be felt, particularly in Atlanta’s return game.
The Falcons selected the former USC wide receiver in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft to add another explosive element to their receiving corps while providing versatility as a return specialist.
Although Branch has primarily served as a complementary option in the passing game, recording 10 receptions for 64 yards, his contributions on special teams have been more substantial.
He has returned eight punts for 83 yards and 14 kickoffs for 360 yards this season.
Branch exited Sunday’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers early after returning a kickoff and did not return to the game. The hamstring injury will now sideline him against Cincinnati.
Losing Branch takes away an option who has provided Atlanta with opportunities to generate field position through the return game.
Atlanta will have to adjust its personnel heading into a matchup that carries importance as the team looks to get back on track following its loss to Tampa Bay.
The Falcons will face a Cincinnati team featuring one of the NFL’s most talented quarterback and wide receiver combinations. Having their defensive line depth and special teams personnel tested will make the upcoming matchup even more challenging.
Stefanski did not provide a definitive timetable for either player’s return, leaving open the possibility that their absences could extend beyond Sunday’s international game.
Atlanta will release its first official injury report Wednesday as preparations continue for the Week 9 matchup in Madrid.
For now, the Falcons know they will have to find answers without Ebukam and Branch as they attempt to get back into the win column against the Bengals.

title: What’s Going On With the Falcons’ Run Defense?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have a serious problem defending the run, and Sunday’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers exposed just how much the unit has regressed over the past month.
Atlanta entered Week 8 with one of the NFL’s top rushing defenses, ranked fourth in the league and allowing just 88.9 rushing yards per game. However, the Buccaneers completely dismantled that reputation, rushing for a franchise record 324 yards in a 16-0 victory at Raymond James Stadium.
The performance was particularly alarming because Tampa Bay completely abandoned its passing game. Baker Mayfield finished 0-for-3 passing, but the Buccaneers still controlled the afternoon by repeatedly attacking Atlanta on the ground.
Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards on 25 carries. Both running backs established career highs , and Tampa Bay averaged 5.8 yards per carry.
For a Falcons defense that had been one of the team’s biggest strengths early in the season, Sunday’s performance raised serious questions about what has changed.
The Buccaneers’ performance was not an isolated incident. Atlanta’s struggles defending the run have been building since its Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
The Falcons allowed 208 rushing yards to Baltimore, followed by 98 against Chicago and 123 against San Francisco. Tampa Bay then took things to another level with 324.
That is 753 rushing yards allowed across four games, an average of 188.3 per contest. The Dallas Cowboys are last in the NFL in rush defense at 152.8 yards-per-game.
The contrast with Atlanta’s early-season performance is significant. The Falcons entered their Week 8 matchup ranked fourth in rushing defense. Their season average now sits around 118 rushing yards allowed per game.
The numbers suggest Atlanta has gone from a defensive strength to a potential liability in a matter of weeks.
The most concerning part is that opponents have found success using similar concepts. Baltimore, Chicago, San Francisco and Tampa Bay have all been able to generate production on the ground, putting increased pressure on Atlanta’s defensive front and linebackers.
Following Sunday’s loss, safety Jessie Bates III acknowledged that Atlanta has to do a better job recognizing and defending the running schemes opposing offenses are using.
“We’re gonna see these same runs. We’re gonna see these same gap schemes. People are going to load the box. They feel like that’s going to be the answer to beat us,” Bates said.
The veteran safety also pushed back against the idea that Atlanta’s defense was completely ineffective.
“I thought we did a good job up until the fourth quarter. I think the first three quarters, I really thought we contained them.”
However, that containment eventually disappeared.
Bates acknowledged that Tampa Bay’s limited passing attack made the defensive assignment straightforward. The Falcons knew the Buccaneers wanted to run the football.
“You gotta bring your hard hat and be able to stop the run, and like I said, we didn’t do that,” Bates said.
This shows a larger issue with Atlanta’s defensive execution. Knowing what an opponent wants to do is one thing. Having the personnel and discipline to stop it is another.
The Falcons have an opportunity to respond when they travel to Madrid to face the Cincinnati Bengals.
However, the upcoming matchup presents another challenge for a defense that has struggled to contain opposing rushing attacks.
Bates believes the solution starts with preparation and execution.
“We just gotta be able to come in next week and be more prepared to stop the run and run the ball better,” Bates said.
Atlanta cannot afford to continue allowing opposing offenses to dictate the game through their ground attacks.
The Falcons entered the season with expectations of having a physical defense capable of controlling the line of scrimmage. Their early-season rushing defense suggested they were moving in that direction.
Now, four consecutive games of significant rushing production from opponents have changed the conversation.
The Buccaneers provided the clearest example of what happens when Atlanta cannot stop the run. Tampa Bay completed zero passes, scored 16 points and still won comfortably.
That should be a major wake-up call.
The Falcons need answers from their defensive front, better gap discipline from their linebackers and more consistent tackling from the entire unit.
Otherwise, opposing offenses will continue following the blueprint Tampa Bay just established.

title: The Ravens Anointed Trey Hendrickson As A $30M/Year Closer. Turns Out He's An Opener
full_text:
When the Ravens got embarrassed by the Bills on Sunday, their second-half defense, worst in the NFL, up to its usual antics, coaches and execs around the league took note.
The Ravens lack of pass protection and competent play calling had a role in three quarterbacks getting injured in about a 12-play span – highly unusual stuff – and once again they had been unable to stop an opponent from marching all over the field on them after halftime, the same collapsing, listless unit that has been torpedoing this franchise for years. All of that was supposed to change, of course, after firing a legion of respected coaches, hiring young defensive wizard Jesse Minter as head coach/defensive play caller and, after raising the ire of folks around the NFL with the shady way they withdrew from a blockbuster trade for Maxx Crosby then giving Trey Hendrickson $60M for two years to attack the quarterback.
Minter immediately coronated the 32-year-old his “closer” with a checkered recent injury history and an ugly end to his esteemed Bengals career with holdouts and hold-ins and not a lot of impact football lately. There were plenty of reasons Hendrickson’s market was soft, allowing Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta’s stunt withdraw from the trade over alleged health concerns, and then having the audacity to claim to his fans that he had plans to land both payers.
On Sunday night, after that 36-10 defeat with the Bills averaging 7.5 yards/play in the second half and with Josh Allen under no duress like so many opposing QBs before him, one NFL GM noted the Ravens might be getting what was coming to them. “Karma,” he noted from how they handled Crosby. A longtime NFL head coach who was watching, used the same word: “Karma is real,” he noted.
Whether karma or not, Year 1 with Hendrickson has been a disaster.
He has been a no-show in the fourth quarter all season, and by Week 9, that season is effectively over. Whatever he does from here on out – extended garbage time – is tainted. Rather than put games away, the Ravens have extended their pathetic run of getting DeCosta-ed – blowing double-digit leads in the second half to lose. Hendrickson has been the antithesis of an opener; like his rookie head coach he has been a no-show when it matters most.
The Raiders have to pry Crosby off the field; Hendrickson got hurt in his first game for Baltimore, his production tailed, he missed time with a surgical procedure, and he has as many sacks as Roquan Smith (two). He hasn’t has an impact moment, he was absolutely shutdown and invisible in his big “revenge’ game with the Bengals, and the Ravens better hope he isn’t aging fast, and has a resurgence next year, because, again, 2026 is a wrap (and DeCosta should he trading veterans).
We’ve been suggesting for weeks on “The Daily Flock Show” how the Ravens should handle this. Maybe they’ll start to adjust. You’d think allowing the most points of any team in the second half, and the second-highest passer rating, and second most big plays and ranking 30th in yards per play might prompt somebody there to try something else.
Here’s what they need to do:
Hendrickson is generating a pass-rush rate near 21% in the first half of games. In the fourth quarter, he has just five pressures on 43 pass rush reps, a woeful 12%. The Ravens have three fourth-quarter sacks as a team (Ethan Burke, undrafted free agent, safety Malaki Starks and Tavius Ronbinson, on IR but still leading the team in sacks.
It’s not like Hendrickson is taking games over early, but he is definitely effective. The injury is probably a big deal, so then get him on more of a pitch count, and be willing to blitz more to keep him fresh. His age was a serious concern for teams in free agency. He isn’t getting home late in games, and he isn’t opening things up for others; the Ravens rank 27th in pressure rate as a team in the fourth quarter.
They need to ration his pass-rushh reps better and accept that he'd probably a designated pass rusher, no matter how much they paid him.
DeCosta made a big reach in the second round for edge run-defender, Zion Young, rather than address his massive center need (he could have had his pick). He needs to have the guts to pay him on run downs or just early downs in general, and stop pretending Hendrickson is something he’s not. He’s never been good against the run.
Longtime Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale – very familiar with Hendrickson and the person who created the defense Minter is running, cut to the quick with what he sees on the film:
“Going against him when he was with the Bengals I think he is a very good pass rusher, and that's it,” Martindale told me on the show . “That's what he is. I think he's a third down, second-and-long type guy because he wants to get to the quarterback. The problem is, when they're playing in these games, especially with (backup) Snoop (Huntley) at quarterback, they've got the whole playbook that they're facing.
“They're not getting leads where people have to throw the ball to get back in the game. And when you get selfish, and you're rushing a passer on a run play, it exposes players. And that's what I'm seeing. That's what I'm seeing with him.”
Teams are going to start road grading the Ravens more and the Ravens aren’t going to win many games, so that closer stuff is basically out the door, anyway. They aren’t getting $10M out of Hendrickson this year, let alone $30M, and they are stuck with it all over again next season. Better find a way to make this age gracefully, while Crosby remains one of the unique every-down edge defenders in the NFL, and incredibly durable at that.
Turns out the Ravens started getting De Costa-ed even before the season began.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Things The Ravens Must Do To Upset The Jaguars Thursday
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are almost certain to lose Thursday night.
I’m not going to try to pretend otherwise. As best I can tell, since 2000, the Ravens have only bene an underdog of 10 points or more at home on three occasions – 2007 at the height of the Tom Brady Patriots dynasty, 2015 against the Legion of Boom Seahawks (with Jimmy Clausen at QB) and also that season against the Steelers (with Ryan Mallett at QB).
But they will play the game, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano making his first NFL start before anyone could have possibly thought imaginable, and crazy things can happen in professional sports and there is at least a case to be build that the Ravens pull ff a shocker against the second-best scoring defense in the NFL. It’s kinda flimsy, sure, but it wouldn’t be the most bizarre in the world (although I do feel compelled to acknowledge that the Ravens are 3-7 in their last 10 home games.
Perhaps this is Fagnano's only shot before journeyman Jacoby Brissett takes over. This also might be the last time the Ravens (4-4) sit at .500 for quite some time unless they break some tendencies and experiment with new concepts:
Dude needs to acknowledge what Wink Martindale and Marvin Lewis discussed with us – trying to get this bad roster with aging players on bloated contracts to take to his zone concepts and playing all that dime coverage, without getting DBs involved nearly enough in the pass rush, ain’t working. It’s failing, miserably.
If you are going to go down, go down fighting with a chance to impact the QB. Because Trey Hendrickson hasn’t been a “closer” by a long shot (0 sacks and 12% pressure rate in  fourth quarter) and this second half defense gets not nearly enough pressure and never gets its hands on the football. The Ravens have forced one second-half turnover all season, tied for worst in the NFL. Time to bring some heat and activate Kyle Hamilton and Marlon Humphrey from the slot and start attacking with Trenton Simpson from the second level and get out of the dime looks.
Trevor Lawrence will carve up the zone stuff. Check out these splits:
Lawrence vs Bitz : 44.3% Success Rate, 57.6% completions, 12% off target throws, 87.2 rating
Lawrence When Not Blitzed: 53.2 Success, 69.7% comp, 7.6% off target, 127.7 rating
At least die by the sword. Doing it Minter’s way still has the Ravens allowing the second most big plays of any NFL defense in the second half of games.
Have Fagnano drop back five straight times in this game like you did in Buffalo . I dare you. Against a better defense with a joke defensive line. The Jags are dealing with some defensive line injuries and the only chance the Ravens have is to play keep away and bleed the clock. There has to be volume in the run game and Doyle will have to go old school for this to work.
Jumbo packages, extra offensive linemen a ton of blocking tight end Nick Vannett. If they can keep it close that way, maybe the defense actually makes a play late. They aren’t going to bully the Jags at the line of scrimmage if they do not commit extra manpower to do it. The line has far more of a fighting chance picking up three yards on the ground than doing anything downfield.
Spare me the genius talk. Let’s have a fairy competent game plan for a change and some cogent adjustments and he should probably be on the sidelines after producing three points in the second half the last three weeks. What they have been trying with Derrick Henry has been an epic fail , and they need to commit to tackle eligible quite a bit.
The Ravens haven’t had any jam in the return game for a looooong time. Thursday would be a nice time to change that up. And Jake Moody gets what could be his last chance to show he can be an NFL kicker with Tyer Loop on IR. They’re going to make some long field goals in this goal with this QB situation, undoubtedly.
Jacksonville is feeling pretty good right now. Two weeks in London, bye week, running away with the AFC South, had to exert themselves for maybe 10 minutes in a 42-7 win over the Colts Sunday and now traveling on a short week for what everyone thinks will be a beatdown game.
Yeah, they might be a little flat and think they can just show up. Might be vulnerable to a punch in the face. We’ll see if the Ravens deliver it, but this could be a letdown spot and if it is Baltimore must seize the moment and use it to its advantage. There is no way they can play this game from behind and win.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Two Ravens Players Who Benefit Most From The Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
Jacoby Brissett is not going to save the Ravens lost season.
He might not even keep it afloat much longer. And, saddest of all, he might soon meet a similar outcome to what befell all three Ravens quarterbacks who had to drop back behind this offensive line on Sunday – immediate pain and, in two cases, the end of their season . Those IR stints for Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Snoop Huntley (toe) are what led to the minor trade for Brissett (the Ravens only assume $650,00 in cash and cap charges; something even they can withstand) who had been demoted to third string in Arizona after a fairly remarkable career resurgence in 2025.
Brissett, 33, is near the end of his career, he is not going to be able to do a ton outside the pocket and he lacks the running skill now needed to unlock a ground game that is threatening to be among the worst in the NFL in Derrick Henry’s age 32 season, where most careers died at that position and all would behind this OL ( they should trade him to a contender ). This isn’t going to open up a world of opportunity for alleged genius Declan Doyle, who is taking major lumps as a rookie play caller (he needs to get down to the sidelines , for starters), or anything like that.
Let’s be real – Brissett got benched against a terrible Dallas defense for Gardner Minshew despite the Cardinals putting up with his “hold-in” all offseason and giving him an incentivized contract to come back. He has not performed to 2025’s standard; he’s thrown seven picks already (8 in 14 games last year) and his yards per attempt was down to an anemic 5.6, with a QB rating of just 79.7.
But I also know this – he is a far more adroit passer of the football than Huntley, who has played most for this team at QB since Jackson first got hurt in Week 4. He will spray the ball around and attack all quadrants in ways Huntley just never would, and while I wouldn’t mind seeing Fagnano get a run in an already lost season in which they should sell at the deadline … but trying to get a half-season out of him is a bit much. (This team is going to lose more QBs behind this line; it’s inevitable).
But at the very least the Ravens have a chance to have a semblance of a downfield passing game with Brissett running the show – virtually certain to be Monday night in Week 10 – and look for two Ravens to benefit most from this transaction:
While his yard/attempt figures and air yard figures are not special, Brissett does things Huntley never dreamed of. In the last two years with the Ravens, Huntley has attempted a pass 15 yards or more downfield barely 18% of the team and over 20 yards downfield less than 6% of the team. Brissett, over the last three years as a starter, is pushing it at least 15 yards on 33% of his attempts and 10% of his throws go 20 yards or more.
And as we’ve known for years, only one guy shows up in this offense in that regard – Flowers. After getting shutout last week in Buffalo – and putting up bonkers numbers before Jackson got hurt – you cannot put too fine a point on getting him activated again.
During the last two years, Brissett did his most efficient work throwing on crossing routes, with a 113.5 rating, completing 67% of his attempts at 8.1/pass. Hmm. Anyone who has watched a functioning version of Baltimore’s offense since Flowers entered the league knows he feasts going across the face of the defense. And Brissett has attempted more passes on out routes than anything else while with the Cardinals, completing 79% of those throws with a rating of 103.9. Flowers has been targeted on outs more than any other route.
His speed and ability to win after the catch simply must become a part of whatever this offense looks like the rest of the way. The fifth-round pick was starting to click with Jackson and win downfield in the slot before Jackson got hurt, then Hibner got hurt and now the QB position is spiraling. But this kid has the ability to excel on deeper stuff and blocks better than I thought and Brissett is going to love him.
Brissett just force-fed elite tight end Trey McBride two years; that offense was a funnel to the point receiver Marvin Harrison Jr, a fourth-overall pick, got dealt away. Brissett will let it rip (he’s got the “no risk it; no biscuit” mentality later in his career) and he will throw jump balls and attack with go balls in the seam. Mark Andrews, honestly, should be inactive at this point and we know that will never happen, but he needs to be below Hibner on the depth chart (routes run and targets must be slashed).
We are getting 9 yards of YAC/reception on the rare occasions this kid is targeted. Over the last two seasons Brissett leads the NFL with 32.4% of his passes going to TEs (guess who is second at 30.8%  - yeah, Lamar). This is Brissett’s favorite way to attack, and ain’t no way Andrews is winning downfield against anybody and Hibner should be a fixture in the slot (with fellow rookie Josh Cuevas more of the in-line guy).
