title: Ravens Deal for a Veteran Passer After Losing Their Top Two Quarterbacks on Sunday
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens have found a solution to their quarterback problem, a few hours after reportedly learning that the team’s top backup Tyler Huntley would be missing the rest of the season due to a turf toe injury.
Starter Lamar Jackson is also sidelined with a thumb injury, and could also be lost for the rest of the season, prompting the Ravens to look elsewhere for help.
According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport, help is on the way, as Baltimore has agreed to acquire Jacoby Brissett via trade from the Arizona Cardinals.
Trade: the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, per @RapSheet and me. Deal is expected to be completed until this weekend. The Ravens lost QB Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury, and his backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley to turf… pic.twitter.com/BYEqcHA1jq
According to the insiders, the deal is expected to be finalized this weekend. No word yet on the compensation involved for the soon-to-be 34-year old veteran.
Over the course of his 11-year career, Brissett has played for the Patriots, Colts, Dolphins, Browns, Commanders and Cards. He was a third-round pick for New England in 2016 out of NC State.
Baltimore was desperate for a starter to potentially finish the regular season, after losing Jackson and Huntley in the span of a few plays last Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.
Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ended up playing for Baltimore in the 36-10 loss, but became somewhat of a question mark himself after being listed as limited for Monday’s walkthrough due to an ankle injury.
Fagnano is currently on track to start his first pro game on Thurssday night.
The Ravens are set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night, so finding viable passers on a short week became the team’s number one priority . Baltimore also signed free agent Austin Reed to the practices squad. Reed has spent some time with the Ravens during the summer, but did not survive final cuts before the season started. He last played for the Dallas Renegades of the UFL.
Bringing Brissett on board means the Ravens will have an experienced veteran under center in case Jackson can’t make it back before the regular season ends. Brissett's move comes on the heels of being demoted in Arizona after Gardner Minshew was named the starter going forward following an unlikely come from behind win in overtime, on the road, against the Cowboys on Sunday.
Brissett’s renegotiated contract with Arizona is set to expire at the end of the season, so he’s currently set to become a free agent next offseason. This means that his arrival in Baltimore should in no way impact Jackson’s contract negotiations with the Ravens.
Rafael brings over two decades of experience writing about all things football.

title: Tests Reveal Ravens QB Tyler Huntley Suffered Season-Ending Toe Injury
full_text:
As if losing two-time MVP starting quarterback Lamar Jackson to a potentially season-ending thumb injury on the first play of his first game back from a high ankle sprain in Week 8 wasn't bad enough; the Baltimore Ravens are slated to be without his primary backup for the remainder of the season as well.
Not too long after Jackson exited the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, Pro Bowl backup Tyler Huntley also left the game due to a toe injury and did not return. According to sources from ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , he won't be back at all this year after further tests revealed that his turf toe injury is of the season-ending variety and will require surgery to repair.
Sources: tests revealed that Ravens’ QB Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, Huntley’s season is over due to turf toe, and QB Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night vs. Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/Cok4gbSvH3
Huntley started three games in place of Jackson this season from Weeks 5-7 and went 1-2, leading a comeback win in overtime against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football on Oct. 11. The former underrated free agent has a record of 8-11 as a starter during his seven-year career, with 17 passing touchdowns, 11 interceptions and six rushing touchdowns.
With both Jackson and Huntley out indefinitely, undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano will be making his first career start Thursday night in primetime against the Jacksonville Jaguars to kick off Week 9.
Fagnano didn't escape the Bills' loss unscathed either, as he sustained an ankle injury that didn't cause him to leave the game. He did have to wear a bulky brace on his right ankle during Tuesday's practice, but he was still listed as a full participant.
The Ravens spent the 48 hours following Sunday's game scrambling to find depth at the sport's most important position because a hobbled, inexperienced rookie couldn't be their lone available quarterback on the roster when they face the  Jaguars. On Monday, they signed Kedon Slovis off the Green Bay Packers and brought back third-year pro Austin Reed. Combined with Fagnano, they have 23 career pass attempts, 45 offensive snaps and zero touchdown passes in three NFL games.
Reed has to appear in an NFL regular-season game since he entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2024. However, he spent part of training camp and the preseason with the Ravens, so he's familiar with the playbook. He appeared in all three preseason games and went 6-of-12 passes for 59 yards with one touchdown, one interception, and he also ran for a 14-yard touchdown. His connection with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle dates back to the summer they spent together in 2025 with the Chicago Bears.
"I feel pretty comfortable that I know how to prepare and get ready," Reed said. "I appreciate having an opportunity, but you never want it to be this way. I care for Lamar and Snoop, so it's tough to see them go down like that. But I'm excited to be here and to help Joe and this team any way I can."
Players and coaches alike have expressed their belief in Fagnano's ability to perform against the Jaguars in primetime. He dazzled in the preseason so much that he proved to be too good to cut and he also showed a lot of grit in the loss to the Bills.
"He's cool, calm and collected; [he] doesn't really get rattled, has a really good demeanor [and] played in a bunch of games in college," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I thought we operated really well when he was in there in the preseason, just from time on the play clock and penalties and substitutions. So, you certainly feel good about it."
Despite the two of them not being able to connect in his first time under center with the first team offense, two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers praised the rookie's knowledge of their playbook and expressed his belief in his ability to execute.
"He knows the playbook by heart," Flowers said. "He knows everything, so we are pretty confident in him calling the plays and going out and making the right decisions because we've seen him operate in the preseason. We think he'll do a good job. We just have to make some plays and help him out."
Even the defensive players have assured Fagnano that they have faith in him. He shared that future Hall of Fame defensive lineman Calais Campbell has come up to him numerous times to share as much.
"Having a guy like that that's been in the league for 18 years, his word means a lot," Fagnano said. "He's just saying, even in the middle of the game he's coming up to me, he's like, 'Hey, I've seen you work at practice, I've seen this, like, I know you can play.' Then, Derrick Henry [is] behind me telling me he's got my back."

title: 7 Winners and 7 Losers From Ravens' Crushing Loss To Bills
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens dropped their third straight game this season in Week 8 on Sunday because they weren't able to keep pace with the Buffalo Bills, who pulled away from them in the second half in a 36-10 road loss.
They came into this game as slight underdogs, but any chance they had of pulling off an upset was quickly extinguished after they were ravaged by injuries at the most important position in the sport in the first half.
With the loss, they fell to 4-4 and remain in last place in the division, where they rightfully belong given how they've played the past three weeks and how banged up they are.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
The four-time Pro Bowler was the only one of the Ravens' highly paid stars on defense who played at an elite level and left it all out on the field in this game, as he was flying around. Smith led the team in total tackles with 11, including six solos, had two pass breakups, made several crucial stops and finished as the Ravens' highest-graded player according to Pro Football Focus , with an overall grade of 91.1.
Before leaving the game to be evaluated for a concussion, the third-year pro was lights out in coverage on the right side of the field, so much so that he wasn't even targeted once.
At one point, the only play that was working for the Ravens' depleted offense was getting the ball into the eighth-year veteran out of the backfield on screens and checkdowns. Hill led the team in receptions with four and was second in receiving yards with 20, and he also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
In his first game back in action since being activated off injured reserve, the third-year pro made his presence felt on defense and special teams. He recorded three solo tackles, recovered the fumble that Smith forced and didn't allow a completion on the one time he was targeted in coverage.
The veteran depth piece came up with the Ravens' first turnover of the game and gave fans a glimmer of hope that they could play spoiler after falling behind 10-0. When he reeled in the tipped pass that bounced off the hands of a Bills tight end, it gave the offense the ball deep in Buffalo territory, and they made it a one-score game two plays later.
The 10th-year veteran played his second-most defensive snaps of the season with 43, and they didn't just start coming after Wiggins left the game. He only played three fewer than one of the biggest losers from this game, who will soon be revealed. Awuzie recorded a pair of tackles, including a solo, a pass breakup that was nearly an interception and was the second-highest-graded defender on the team behind Smith, with an overall grade of 81.2.
The journeyman veteran saw a significant uptick in playing time on defense with Jaylinn Hawkins out for a second week in a row, with a season-high 47 defensive snaps and tied for the fourth-most total tackles with a season-high six, including five solos. He was key in keeping the Bills' running game to 3.6 yards per rush by playing physically downhill.
The Ravens became the first team to have three different players at the position attempt a pass in the first half since the 2017 Dallas Cowboys. Two of them didn't return due to injury, and none of them came out of this game unscathed. Two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson went out after having his thumb hit on a follow-through during the Ravens' first offensive play from scrimmage. Primary backup and former Pro Bowl reserve Tyler Huntley didn't last much longer as he exited with toe injury after being sacked on his fifth dropback. The next-next man up was undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who entered the game in the second quarter and finished with an injured ankle.
While Jackson's potentially season-ending injury occurred on a fluky, occasional collision, it was the result of a lapse in pass protection, which went on to be a far too common theme throughout the game. It was the first of several pressures that right tackle Roger Rosengarten gave up to Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau. The rest of his linemates at the other four starting spots didn't fare much better as the Ravens allowed four sacks and a dozen quarterback hits. They failed to establish a consistent run game as they were held to under 100 rushing yards for the third week in a row, marking the team's longest stretch since Jackson's rookie year in 2018 before he was inserted into the starting lineup.
The four-time Pro Bowler continues to do himself no favors by being on the wrong end of big plays given up to the opposing team's top wide receivers. He allowed D.J. Moore to come down with a 49-yard jump ball on the Bills' first possession of the second half despite having great coverage on the play. Humphrey failed to dislodge the ball as they went to the ground but had a chance to redeem himself on the very next play when he made a great break on a quick slant to Moore. He didn't finish the play for what would've been a clutch drive-ending interception, and the Bills went back up by two scores on the very next play on a five-yard James Cook touchdown. Earlier in the game, he was called for a hold that negated what would've been a key third-down stop and forced a punt.
Despite being targeted five times, the second-most on the team, the two-time Pro Bowler was held without a catch for the first time in his entire four-year career. While the offensive line struggled to provide consistently clean pockets for the quarterbacks to deliver the ball to him when he got separation, he also had at least two drops.
In hindsight, the first-year play-caller should've just dialed up a Derrick Henry run on the first play of this game, but who's to say that Jackson still wouldn't have gotten hurt on his first dropback anyway. Nonetheless, Doyle made several questionable calls, with some pretty big shortcomings in this game. Flowers' drops aside, he didn't dial up enough plays to get the ball in his star receivers' hands. His decision to keep dialing up passing plays after Fagnano caught the Bills off guard with a pair of 10-plus-yard gains through the air that got the ball deep inside the red zone was truly baffling. The novice QB was sacked on his third dropback, and the drive short-circuited from there.
The second-year specialist's struggles continued to persist in this game as he went 1-of-2 on his field goal attempts, including his first career miss from under 40 yards, which came on a 34-yard chip shot at the end of Fagnano's first drive under center. Loop also had a bad habit from his rookie season rear it's ugly head when he got penalized for kicking the opening kickoff of the game out of bounds, giving the Bills the ball at their own 40-yard line. The Ravens placed him on injured reserve with a groin injury, and he will be replaced in the lineup by veteran Jake Moody .
The three-time Pro Bowler continues to look like a shell of his former self, offering no juice after the catch and is good for one or more concentration drop. Both traits were on display in this game as he caught three of his four targets for just 14 receiving yards, with a long of eight yards.

title: Josh Allen's History vs. Vikings' Defensive Coordinator Presents Clear Expectations
full_text:
Brian Flores is known for producing some of the best defenses in football, and on Monday Night Football , the Buffalo Bills and quarterback Josh Allen will face a Minnesota Vikings stop unit that ranks first in EPA per play and pressure rate .
Allen knows the Vikings' defensive coordinator very well from when he faced the Miami Dolphins from 2019 to 2021, when Flores was their head coach. If past results are any indication, Allen should have no problems picking up where he left off.
The Bills were 6-0 against the Dolphins in those three seasons, and they won those games by an average margin of about 18 points. Given how weak the Vikings' offense is (28th in EPA per play), Allen and Co. may not need to do much to reach that threshold.
Allen had yet to break out as a superstar in the league when he began facing Flores, and in his six games against him, he completed 64.4% of his passes for 1,525 yards and a 16-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. He added 200 yards and two more scores on the ground in those contests.
These stats do not account for Allen sitting the entire second half of Buffalo's meaningless Week 17 contest against Miami in 2020, so these stats technically span five and a half games.
Though Allen has had success against Flores in the past, there is plenty more talent for the defensive wizard to work with in Minnesota to try to befuddle Allen than he ever had in Miami.
Outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel is one player Allen will know well from his matchups against the Dolphins. He's a do-it-all defender for Flores, as he leads the Vikings with 6.5 sacks and 8.5 tackles for loss. In the four games he played under Flores against Allen, he registered 13 tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble.
Flores did not have another elite edge defender in Miami, but Dallas Turner, with six sacks and 8.5 TFLs, is blossoming in his third season as that piece. Both Van Ginkel and Turner rank in the top 10 in the NFL in sacks.
In the linebacking core, veteran Blake Cashman is another chess piece for Flores to use, as he leads the Vikings with 64 tackles and also has 4.5 sacks and five passes defensed.
Cornerback Xavien Howard was the only All-Pro Flores had in Miami, but Isaiah Rodgers, Byron Murphy and James Pierre have combined for six of the Vikings' eight interceptions this season, forming a trio that is hard to complete passes against.
Safety Joshua Metellus is another versatile piece, as he often plays in the box or in the slot to shut down opposing playmakers.
Despite such a talented group of defenders, Allen has a couple of advantages he'll need to emphasize if the Bills are to win their seventh game of the season.
#Skol #Vikings DC Brian Flores on #BillsMafia QB Josh Allen: "Josh is one of the best players in our league." Allen enters MNF with 20 total TD so far this season for the 6-1 Bills. pic.twitter.com/K6owGJUpvT
The Vikings blitz on 72.8% of defensive plays, by far the most in the NFL by about 30 percentage points. They also lead the league with an 11% sack rate. Fortunately for Buffalo, Allen doesn't take a nosedive against pressure. In fact, he's one of the league's better quarterbacks against extra rushers.
Allen has an overall rate of 0.22 EPA per play, fourth-best among quarterbacks with at least 100 snaps. His 0.11 EPA per play against the blitz is 10th in the league and -0.03 EPA per play against pressure is third-best.
For reference, the seven quarterbacks Minnesota has faced so far have combined for 0.15 EPA per play against the blitz and -2.72 EPA per play against pressure.
Allen can also lean on James Cook and the running game to settle down the pass rush and keep it honest. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries against Minnesota on Sunday, so Cook having a similar performance will help massively.
Going against Flores' defense is a tough task for any quarterback, but if anyone can overcome it, Allen can.

title: Three Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 9 vs. Vikings
full_text:
After knocking off the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, the Buffalo Bills will now turn their attention to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9 . It's a huge showdown for the Bills, who will travel to Minnesota for a Monday Night Football showdown.
The Vikings enter this one feeling the pressure after suffering their first loss of the season, falling to the Detroit Lions 19-15. They're a defensive powerhouse and will be focused on slowing down the high-scoring Bills' offense.
As for Buffalo, they have a chance to prove themselves against one of the top teams in the NFC. There will be plenty of pressure on them as well, but no one will be feeling as much heat as the following three players.
In Week 8, Te'Cory Couch snuck up on everyone. He was asked to step up with C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended and Dee Alford injured, and did exactly that. Filling in as a nickel corner, Couch was one of the highest-graded players on the team against the Ravens. His performance was solid enough that Buffalo felt confident in moving on from Gardner-Johnson once his suspension was officially over.
Now entering Week 9, Couch won't be able to sneak up on anyone. Initially signed as an undrafted free agent out of Miami in 2024, Couch has continued to develop for Buffalo and has earned a larger role on defense. Now, the pressure will be on as he needs to prove he can still get the job done even when big things are expected of him.
In all honesty, we could put the entire Buffalo offensive line on this list considering the task they're about to face. Minnesota boasts the No. 1 scoring defense in the NFL right now and that has a lot to do with the performance of its front seven. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has never been shy about bringing the blitz and that's led to 25 sacks in the first seven games for the Vikings.
While all five starters on the O-line will be under attack, Dawkins is the leader of the group and needs to set the tone. He will also find himself matched up with Dallas Turner, who is second on the team with six sacks, but is currently the 13th highest-rated pass-rusher among all qualified EDGE players, according to PFF. If Dawkins can slow him down one-on-one, the Bills can send help to the other side and potentially slow down the overall pass rush.
After a slow start to the season , Christian Benford has once again hit his stride. He was fantastic in Week 7 against Brock Bowers and helped shut down Zay Flowers who had zero receptions on five targets in Week 8. His confidence should be at an all-time high, and Buffalo is going to need his performance to match this week.
Benford will find himself lined up across from Justin Jefferson for much of the game and that should be one of the best matchups to watch all weekend. Jefferson is a route-running wizard who is unguardable when he's on top of his game. He's been slowed down this season by a subpar offense overall, but Jefferson can still light up the scoreboard without warning.
That's why Benford will be facing more pressure this weekend than anyone else on the Bills' roster. He's going to be asked to slow down the one player who can turn this game into a track meet. If he succeeds, Buffalo's chances of winning improve exponentially.

title: Which Bills' Safety Should Replace C.J. Gardner-Johnson in Starting Lineup?
full_text:
In a somewhat surprising move, the Buffalo Bills decided to shake the roster up on Tuesday evening by releasing veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson after just seven games of the 2026 campaign after originally bringing the boastful defender on board via a one-year deal in free agency on March 12 that was worth up to $6 million.
237 days later and fresh off a one-game suspension, Gardner-Johnson finds himself looking for a new NFL home and the Bills are in search of a new starting safety to pair with third-year defensive back Cole Bishop.
Last week against the Baltimore Ravens it was sixth-year veteran Damar Hamlin who earned the nod alongside Bishop, but fellow veteran safety Geno Stone also saw time on the field and played quite well in limited action.
So what is the best plan of attack moving forward for Buffalo’s first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard ?
Let’s scour through the candidates.
Damar Hamlin might not be flashy, but he’s the definition of consistent.
In spite of all of the hardship that he’s endured since that fateful day in Cincinnati, Ohio, at Paycor Stadium on Monday Night Football in January of 2023, Hamlin has never wavered in his return to the gridiron.
And, it’s led him to possibly once again regaining a starting defensive spot for a Bills’ squad currently sitting atop the AFC standings entering Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season.
In 2022 and 2024—the two seasons he previously started a majority of Buffalo’s games—Hamlin tallied 180 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, seven pass deflections, two interceptions, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery while starting in 17 of the 19 games he appeared in during the regular season.
As for this year, Hamlin has recorded 23 total tackles and one pass breakup while appearing in seven games with two starts.
And, after tallying 16 total tackles in a more prominent role over the past three weeks, the 28-year-old defensive back appears to be odds-on favorite to start the remainder of the season.
Veteran Geno Stone was an interesting addition to Buffalo’s roster earlier this offseason after joining the team almost immediately following the signing of the previously mentioned Gardner-Johnson in March.
The questions surrounding the addition weren’t due to a lack of experience or track record from Stone, but rather the repetitiveness of adding a second player at the safety position at the time.
Now, though, it seems as if it was a smart move by Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane to bring Stone on board.
After being called up from the practice squad on Sunday due to a “numbers game”, Stone wound up playing 19 defensive snaps against the Ravens and posted a team-high six tackles to go along with one tackle for loss and one pass deflection, which actually led to an easy tip-drill interception by rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun.
Does Stone have warts to his game? Sure. But, he seems dependable and was in the right place at the right time more often than not against the Ravens, which led to him being named the top-ranked defender for Buffalo in the matchup according to Pro Football Focus .
That type of reliability and innate ability to make a play on the ball—which is evidenced by his 14 career interceptions—is exactly what Jim Leonhard’s youthful defense needs right now on the backend.
Rookie safety Jalon Kilgore had a lot of fanfare amongst Bills Mafia after being selected by the team at pick No. 167 in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and for good reason.
The versatile defensive back had plenty of production for the South Carolina Gamecocks’ defense during his three collegiate seasons, and his stellar combination of size ( 6-foot-1, 210 lbs ), speed ( 4.40-second time in the 40-yard-dash ), and overall athleticism ( 10-foot-10-inch broad, 37-inch vertical ) is something that Buffalo could use more of in the secondary.
Eventually, Kilgore should take over as the long-term starter opposite Cole Bishop, but will that begin to take shape sometime this season?
Kilgore has only appeared in two games so far this regular season after struggling with injuries in the summer months, and he was just inactive once again for the matchup against Baltimore.
It’ll be interesting to see if the rookie starts seeing more opportunities now that Gardner-Johnson is out of the picture.
Out of all of the possible outcomes, this may be the least likely . . . but should it be?
A former UDFA signing of Bills following the 2024 NFL Draft, Couch has been on Buffalo’s practice squad over the past two seasons, but was recently signed to the active roster ahead of the game against the Ravens.
And, in the absence of the injured Dee Alford, Couch started in the slot at nickel cornerback for Buffalo, playing 71% of the team’s defensive snaps.
The 27-year-old performed admirably in the role , too, as he finished tied for second on the team in total tackles with a total of five while only allowing one reception in coverage according to PFF.
Given his recent performance in a starting role, it’s possible that Couch takes over that spot for Alford permanently as the calendar turns toward the middle of November, but the idea of shifting him back to safety—an area he experimented with in training camp and the preseason—is also intriguing.
Bills ON SI mentioned Couch as a player who earned the right to a 53-man roster spot before final cuts were made back in August, and that’s proving to be the case now in November.
Could Brandon Beane make a swing for some help in the secondary before next Tuesday’s trade deadline?
And, with that in mind, Bills ON SI has covered several options on the market leading up to November 10.
However, as it stands right now, Bills Mafia shouldn’t hold their collective breath for a move to be made.
“Big Baller Beane” may have permanently switched to "Bargain Bin Beane” at this juncture.
Ultimately, the direction that Buffalo decides to go in the absence of Gardner-Johnson could go several different ways: clearly.
But, at the moment, it would seem prudent for the Bills to stick with what worked against the Ravens .
Yes, the total defensive output may have been slightly skewed due to the quarterback the team ended up facing on Sunday, but the smoothness of the overall operation seemed to be much better than it had been prior to the bye week.
So, for that reason—as well as the ones mentioned above—some sort of platoon between Hamlin and Stone seems to be the recipe for success moving forward.

title: Ranking Bills' Toughest Potential Playoff Opponents With Field Already Taking Shape
full_text:
The AFC standings may show that 10 teams are at least .500 and that the Buffalo Bills are one of them. However, that's only scratching the surface. When you look deeper, seven teams, including the Bills, stand out from the rest as playoff teams.
The 5-3 Cleveland Browns were exposed on Sunday, falling 27-6 to the Pittsburgh Steelers, the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders had a four-game losing streak against quality opponents and the 4-4 Baltimore Ravens lost star quarterback Lamar Jackson for the season. And by the way, Baltimore's trade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett will not save them.
The AFC playoff race is about to get boring pic.twitter.com/d5QqvVHQBT
Buffalo and the other six teams in the AFC that are at least .500 will have at least a very high chance to make the postseason as long as they remain on their current trajectories, which means it's a good time to examine Buffalo's possible opponents for the playoffs.
This ranking from top to bottom will start with the opponent the Bills could dispatch the best and will go down to the team they would not want to face the most. Let's get started.
The Bills dismantled the Steelers 26-7 in Pittsburgh in 2025, and not much has changed besides Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin as head coach. The Steelers have run the ball well this season, ranking No. 1 in the NFL in rush EPA per play , but with Buffalo's improvements against the run, it will play right into the Bills' hands and allow them to tee off on Aaron Rodgers in his farewell tour.
On the other side of the ball, the Steelers did not sack Josh Allen despite the Bills starting two backup tackles, and with DJ Moore, they should have no issue moving the ball against Pittsburgh's defense.
This is an opponent that, if the Bills face them, the result may depend on where this game is played. Denver is 4-0 at home to start the year, and three of those games have been comeback wins. Conversely, they are 2-2 on the road with the two defeats coming convincingly at the hands of the Chiefs and 49ers.
We will get a good idea of what this matchup will look like at Mile High on Christmas Day, but Bills fans will hope this team does not have to go through more heartbreak like last season's playoff battle.
The Bills and Patriots know each other very well, so creating a game plan to go against New England is not the hardest thing in the world. The Bills lost at home to Mike Vrabel's Patriots in both 2025 and 2026, and stopping Drake Maye and the NFL's No. 2 offense in terms of EPA will be a challenge.
What will work for Buffalo is that the Patriots' defense is in the middle of the pack, which will allow Allen and James Cook to gain significant yardage and keep pace with Maye and New England's attack.
The Chiefs have been Buffalo's kryptonite in the postseason, with Josh Allen owning an 0-4 record against Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City in the playoffs. However, this Chiefs team has glaring flaws, like its inability to protect Patrick Mahomes and pressure opposing quarterbacks.
If the defense can make one stop in a critical moment, the Bills may just defeat Kansas City and make the Super Bowl, which Sean McDermott's teams could not.
The Bills and Jaguars went toe-to-toe in January, and the fact that it could have gone either way should leave Bills fans on their toes about possibly facing Jacksonville again, even in a stadium that's now a construction zone as it undergoes renovations.
There are no major holes on the Jags' roster, but the one thing Buffalo can take advantage of is Liam Coen's questionable game management, which cost him in Week 6 against the Texans in London.
Given how poorly Buffalo's defense has performed this season, Joe Burrow and this offense should give Bills fans nightmares, especially with the defeat Cincinnati handed them four seasons ago in the divisional round.
The Bengals' defense has improved slightly from last season, but it is still a unit that Allen, Joe Brady and Co. can exploit. However, the lack of a game-changer on Buffalo's defense may smack them in the face as Dexter Lawrence creates the turning point in a projected matchup.

title: Josh Allen 'So Proud Of' Spencer Brown Substitute Who Bailed Out Bills
full_text:
It was his second test in three weeks, and he aced it, according to multiple accounts.
Initially, it seemed odd that the Buffalo Bills were willing to let reliable swing tackle Ryan Van Demark leave for the Minnesota Vikings as a restricted free agent this offseason.
After seeing Tylan Grable's recent efforts, however, it's apparent why the Bills had enough trust in their 2024 sixth-round pick to comfortably part ways with a high-quality backup.
With Van Demark's role up for grabs, Grable won a training camp battle against fourth-round rookie Jude Bowry.
The Bills used him sparingly until starting right tackle Spencer Brown left after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up on October 12 against the Los Angeles Rams. Grable stepped up to get Buffalo through a 37-34 overtime victory.
Brown returned to take all reps against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, but he wound up experiencing issues coming out of the Week 7 bye. With Brown, who was ruled as questionable to play , ultimately being unavailable, Grable was back on duty in Week 8 against the Baltimore Ravens.
“The Rams game was huge for him and the confidence that he had going into the [Ravens] game," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady.
Keeping pressure off quarterback Josh Allen, who was sacked only once, for the most part, Grable manned the right tackle spot for all 82 possible snaps against the Ravens.
"I'm so proud of him," said the five-time NFL MVP finalist Allen following the 36-10 thumping on November 1. "He, again, throughout the week, not sure if he was going or not. [He] just decided, hey, I'm going to plan like I am. And I thought he played fantastic."
The Bills selected Grable out of Central Florida at No. 204 overall in 2024.
As a rookie, Grable was actually dressed over Van Demark for the first three weeks of the 2024 campaign until a groin injury landed the 6-foot-5 bookend on Injured Reserve until December . He was used sparingly as a sixth offensive lineman in heavy formations.
Grable never got off the ground in 2025 as a training camp head injury kept him sidelined until his season debut against the New York Jets in Week 18. Including this past Sunday's effort, he has three career starts under his belt.
The 27-year-old Grable has proven effective at both right and left tackle, giving the Bills a luxury of sorts off the bench.
Starting left guard Alec Anderson, who knows what it's like to be called in on short notice, claimed it was business as usual with Grable taking the first-team reps. The second-stringer reportedly fit in seamlessly.
"We go in there, all four of us [starting offensive linemen] have faith in our right tackle, and I think that that showed this week, because it was as if Spencer was out there. I didn't think nothing was happening. Josh wasn't getting pressured. We weren't sliding his way to help him," said Anderson (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio for the audio).
Meanwhile, former NFL offensive lineman Brian Baldinger, now known for his Baldy Breakdowns, gave Grable high marks in a social media post .
"Sure looks like he was ready for duty...Lots to like. Size; Power; Feet; and Attitude.  Bills can find em; and develop em," said Baldinger.

title: Will Bills Face Backup QB Again With Uncertainty Around Vikings' Kyler Murray?
full_text:
Last week, the Buffalo Bills’ caught an incredibly lucky break when the Baltimore Ravens had franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson and longtime veteran second-stringer Tyler Huntley go down during the first two quarters of Sunday’s critical AFC battle .
And, it paid dividends for Buffalo on the scoreboard and in the stat book.
Now, it appears that Bills’ first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s struggling unit might be receiving a second helping of that same luck entering Week 9 as it was announced after the recent game between the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions that Vikings’ veteran quarterback Kyler Murray sustained some stiffness in his hamstring during the Week 8 loss to the Lions.
And, with that being the case, his availability for Monday night’s upcoming interconference primetime meeting between Buffalo and Minnesota is in question.
"We're still in the process of evaluating," Vikings’ head coach Kevin O'Connell said to media members on Monday.
"We're going through a full (evaluation) of (Kyler’s hamstring) as we work through the day today. I'll be able to update you on that as we get into the work week.”
The news comes on the heels of the Vikings’ first loss of the season, which came at the hands of Detroit at Ford Field in Week 8, and there’s seemingly some rumblings about whether Murray should return to the lineup even if he’s healthy.
Despite O’Connell reiterating that the former 2019 No. 1 overall pick will remain the team’s starting quarterback when available, backup quarterback Carson Wentz has actually performed quite well in relief action so far this season.
Murray was removed from Minnesota’s season opener against the Green Bay Packers due to a concussion suffered in the first quarter of that game, and he subsequently missed Week 2, as well.
Kyler Murray is pretty easily playing the worst football of his career pic.twitter.com/Tmy2HoNKx2
In both outings, Wentz led the Vikings to victory while going a combined 23-of-39 passing for 276 yards and three touchdowns for a quarterback rating of 106.4.
Furthermore, Minnesota also scored the most points in a single game that it’s had so far this season with Wentz at the helm as the team put up 39 points against the Packers in Week 1, which is a far cry from the 18.4 points per game that the Vikings are averaging with Kyler Murray taking the snaps.
Needless to say, considering Murray is accounting for only 170.3 passing yards per game, 27.8 rushing yards per game, 0.8 total touchdowns per game, and 0.5 interceptions per game, the injury update for the former Arizona Cardinals’ franchise gunslinger might not be a bad thing, at least not for the Vikings.
And, adding in the fact that the aforementioned Wentz is actually 2-0 in his career against quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills , it makes the situation all the more interesting heading into the middle of the practice week.
In two games against Buffalo—one with Philadelphia in 2019 and one with Indianapolis in 2021—the North Dakota State product has a completion percentage of 63.6% ( 28-of-44 attempts ) for 278 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and no interceptions, while also adding 10 rushing attempts for 53 yards on the ground and an average of 5.3 yard per carry.
Wentz’s teams have also outscored the Bills 72-28 in both of those outings.
So, who should Bills Mafia be rooting for to be in the Vikings’ starting lineup on Monday Night Football in the coming days?
Well, given the history of Wentz’s success against the Western New York franchise—coupled with Murray’s continued struggles in 2026—maybe fans should hope for a speedy recovery from Minnesota’s preferred starter.
Ultimately, this will be an area to monitor all week long. Stay tuned to Bills ON SI .

title: Bills-Eagles Trade Proposal Would Land Buffalo Perfect Deadline Addition
full_text:
We are less than one week from the NFL trade deadline and some big moves have already happened. As of yet, however, the Buffalo Bills have been rather quiet .
Despite seeing contenders such as the San Francisco 49ers, Chicago Bears, and Seattle Seahawks all bolster their rosters, Buffalo general manager Brandon Beane hasn’t made any moves. That’s frustrating given the state of the defense, which is currently ranked 24th in points surrendered (and that number was helped tremendously by the fact that they faced a Baltimore Ravens team that had to rely on Joe Fagnano for most of the game).
If Beane did decide to look for defensive help, Cody Williams of FanSided has an intriguing name to keep an eye on. Williams says the perfect deadline target for Buffalo would be Zack Baun , a versatile linebacker who currently plays for the Philadelphia Eagles.
"At some point, we need to see the Buffalo Bills and general manager Brandon Beane give Josh Allen more help on the opposite side of the ball. Against the best teams on their schedule, the Bills are set up to need to put a huge number on the scoreboard," Williams wrote.
"They're capable, but the level of difficulty shouldn't be that high. The Eagles' huge downturn could make Zack Baun available, and the versatile linebacker is the all-angles presence that the Bills defense lacks in the middle right now."
Originally a third-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in 2020, Baun broke out with the Eagles in 2024 after signing a one-year deal in free agency. He made the Pro Bowl after recording 151 tackles, 3.5 sacks, and one interception. Baun then signed a three-year, $51 million deal in 2025 , keeping him under contract through the 2027 season.
There’s no denying that Baun would instantly improve the Buffalo defense. He’s currently the sixth-highest rated linebacker in the NFL, according to PFF, with an overall grade of 79.7 . He’s also incredibly well-rounded, proving to be capable against the run as well as in coverage.
The question is whether the Eagles really would be willing to make a move. Unfortunately, the answer is probably no.
While this is a lost season for the Eagles due to injuries, they know they have a championship-caliber team when healthy. Perhaps if Baun were a free agent in 2027 they would be willing to move on, but since he’s signed for another season, they’re far more likely to keep him around and hope they can contend next season when fully healthy.
That said, Beane would be doing his team a disservice if he didn’t look for an upgrade at linebacker and that should include at least seeing if the Eagles are open to a discussion.

title: Bills' Practice Squad Player Essentially Forced CJ Gardner-Johnson Out Door
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills apparently had enough of the Chauncey Gardner-Johnson experiment.
Much like he did with the Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans and Chicago Bears, all within the span of four seasons, Gardner-Johnson has worn out his welcome sooner than later in Orchard Park.
Required to make a roster move by Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET as Gardner-Johnson's one-game NFL-imposed suspension expired, the Bills chose not to tinker with the combination that performed so well in the combustible defensive back's absence.
Rather than cutting someone to open a roster spot for Gardner-Johnson, Buffalo sent the obnoxious, saliva-spewing safety packing .
Notably, the Bills decided to keep practice squad promotion Te'Cory Couch on their 53-man roster following his eye-opening performance against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1.
After appearing twice as a practice squad elevation this season, Couch signed to the active roster when Gardner-Johnson's suspension created a one-week vacancy.
There was an initial thought that Couch would serve only as a stop gap for the Week 8 home game against Baltimore. After providing nickel cornerback/safety insurance, Buffalo would release Couch with the hope of getting him back on the practice squad.
As it turns out, Couch isn't going anywhere. In fact, the 27-year-old versatile defensive back may have played his way into the Bills' long-term plans. At least, he's earned another chance to show what he can do.
While some of it has to do with the combustible Gardner-Johnson's subpar performance, particularly when it comes to on-field communication, Couch's opportunity is just as much a result of his progress in Jim Leonhard's defense.
"Te'Cory Couch had a great game," said Leonhard. "He went in there and executed really at a high level, communication and just winning some one-on-ones."
Seemingly acing his assignments, Couch totaled five tackles in the 36-10 win over Baltimore.
The Bills signed Couch as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Miami in 2024.
Following back-to-back seasons on Buffalo's practice squad , Couch finally made his NFL debut as a practice squad elevation against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3. He was active on game day again in Week 4, but subsequently missed practice time as a result of being banged up.
Couch, who saw only special teams snaps in his first two appearances, was needed on defense with the secondary missing Gardner-Johnson and injured starting slot cornerback Dee Alford .
“He's been injured. Now he's coming back. Hey, what's the Dee Alford situation going to be? Boom, you're up," said head coach Joe Brady. "Being able to make plays on the football, critical tackles, the involvement he has on special teams. And so it's going to be like that moving forward."
Couch appeared to come into his own this past summer during training camp. His willingness and ability to move around in Leonhard's defense helped him get noticed.
"TC, man, that's a dude who truly had to learn every position on this defense to get opportunities like today, and he did it, and he executed so well," said veteran Damar Hamlin , who started at safety in place of Gardner-Johnson .
Playing multiple roles during an August 22 preseason game against the Cleveland Browns, Couch made an interception as a safety. Playing in all three exhibition contest, he totaled six tackles on defense and added two more on special teams.
On Sunday against the Ravens, he played 71 percent of defensive snaps. His efforts were key to holding Ravens' wide receiver Zay Flowers without a catch.
"He was out there communicating. He was out there playing just lights out, if you ask me. So shoutout to him," said Hamlin. "He's been waiting on the opportunity for years, and it finally came his way, and I think he made the most of it."
The excellent communication represented a noticeable improvement over what Gardner-Johnson showed over the first six weeks.

title: Bills, Budda Baker Rumors Give Buffalo Hope for Deadline Trade With Cardinals
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' need at the safety position just became more dire when it was reported on Tuesday that the Bills are going to release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
The decision to cut ties with Gardner-Johnson comes following him serving a one-game suspension for spitting on a Las Vegas Raiders player. Despite that disgusting act, it's still at least a bit surprising the Bills are cutting him, as head coach Joe Brady previously said Gardner-Johnson wasn't going anywhere .
NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported that Gardner-Johnson's "inconsistency in play" was what led to his release and "not as much the spitting incident."
Nevertheless, adding to the safety position just became more important because the Bills don't have much they can rely on there.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler touched on Budda Baker's potential availability on Wednesday morning.
Fowler says Baker is on his radar as a trade candidate, and while Baker "would be hard to trade" because of his status as an Arizona Cardinals "lifer," he is also hearing that all of the losing in Arizona has "weighed on him."
In addition to all that, Fowler also said "teams such as Buffalo or Jacksonville could try to take advantage of that."
"Also on the Arizona front, safety Budda Baker remains on my radar, though he has been a Cardinals lifer and would be hard to trade. But my sense is the consistent losing has weighed on him, and teams such as Buffalo or Jacksonville could try to take advantage of that," Fowler said.
Fowler isn't the first one to surmise that Baker's career-long stint in Arizona might have him standing pat. ESPN's Adam Schefter recently said the same thing.
"That guy has been such a stud I don't know that Budda Baker is gonna be traded," Schefter said . "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from a guy that has meant so much to that franchise. (Baker) is such a baller."
It might be true that the Cardinals don't want to trade Baker, but if he wants to be moved because he is indeed sick of all the losing that isn't likely to end in the next few years with the Cardinals rebuilding, Arizona could oblige out of respect for him.
An eight-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro, Baker has been one of the better safeties in the NFL during his career.
The veteran is an excellent box safety who is both strong against the run and as a pass-rusher. Baker's 73.8 Pro Football Focus run defense grade ranks 33rd at the position, and he's top five in run stops, also. As a pass-rusher, Baker sports a 72.6 grade, ranked 14th, and he has 3.5 sacks in eight games.
The Bills could really use a boost in coverage given the fact that they have the third-worst pass defense in the league, and Baker has been strong in that area with a 48.1% completion rate surrendered and a passer rating against of 94.2.
When it comes to compensation, we could see Baker going for a fourth-round pick.
The Bills are well-stocked with draft capital to be able to afford that, and what makes this potential trade even better is that Baker's contract runs through 2027.
If Baker can be had, general manager Brandon Beane shouldn't hesitate to go get him.

title: Former NFL Player Questions Bills' Decision to Cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson
full_text:
On Tuesday, the Buffalo Bills decided to move on from C.J. Gardner-Johnson , releasing the veteran safety after he served his one-game suspension for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.
On the surface, it looks as though Buffalo made the right call. Gardner-Johnson joined the team with a questionable resume, which included being released by the Houston Texans after just three games last season.
What was worse is Gardner-Johnson showed no remorse whatsoever following the incident. He refused to admit he spit at Bowers , even making the ridiculous claim that it was a sign of his competitiveness.
Not everyone agrees, however, as former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho questioned the decision. Acho said the Bills might struggle to win without Gardner-Johnson, who he says was an enforcer on their defense.
"I don't know if I agree because you might need Chauncey to win. Like I think you need an enforcer. The Bills do not have an enforcer on that defense," Acho said.
BREAKING: Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was released by the Buffalo Bills 😳 My immediate reaction! Let me know if y’all agree— pic.twitter.com/wkSldUPdHk
"Terrell Bernard, good player, not an enforcer. Dorian Williams, good player, not an enforcer. You usually find your enforcers at linebacker. Um, sometimes Seattle Seahawks, you can find them outside at cornerback, but you need a freakazoid like Devin Witherspoon, but you don't have an enforcer up front, Ed Oliver is here today, gone tomorrow. Greg Rousseau having a phenomenal season. He's a good player, but he's not an enforcer."
Acho went on to say that without him being on the defense, he's torn. "The Bills, Where's your enforcer now on defense? ... The Bills lost their enforcer, so I'm torn."
Acho discussed some of the recent championship teams and pointed out the enforcers on their defense. He mentioned the Philadelphia Eagles who won a title in 2024 with Gardner-Johnson as their defensive enforcer.
There's truth to that after Gardner-Johnson recorded six interceptions for the Eagles that season, but that wasn't the same player Buffalo had in Gardner-Johnson. This season, he was a liability in the secondary, posting a 55.2 overall according to PFF . He also had nine missed tackles in just six games, two of which were in the first half against the Raiders before being ejected.
Gardner-Johnson might have been an enforcer at one point in his career, but he doesn't fall into that category now. Throw in the distraction he became with his antics and the decision to move on was one of the easiest the Bills have made in recent years.

title: Bryce Young's Reported Extension Update is Bad News for Panthers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers ' season through seven games has been a roller coaster . With that, so has Bryce Young's. Sitting at 3-4, there have been major highs and, more recently,  major lows. Young hasn't been the clear worst piece of Carolina's latest struggles , but he hasn't elevated Carolina to make up for roster deficiencies.
Through the first five games of the season, Young was playing as well as almost any QB in the league. Leading the league in passing yards per game, had an exceptional touchdown-to-interception ratio, and looked as poised as ever.
Young was the only QB throwing for over 300 yards per game, but after a two-game skid, that number has dropped. It was exactly how he needed to start the season because, as most football fans know, Young has a multi-year contract extension looming
Entering the 2026 season, Carolina opted not to extend Young and instead exercised his fifth-year option. That move by GM Dan Morgan and the Panthers' move signaled that Young would have to go out and earn a lucrative, multi-year deal to solidify him as the long-term QB1.
Now with almost half the season in the books, there is intel and updates on the status of Young's long-term future.
NBC Sports' Mike Florio gave updates on both Bryce Young and CJ Stroud. The top two picks in the 2023 NFL Draft, both of whom have had low moments in their careers, are awaiting new contracts.
When mentioning Young, Florio leans toward him getting an extension worth more than $50 million annually. It's a steep price tag, but thats where the QB market is if Young is going to be locked in long-term.
Florio even said that he "caught wind" of Carolina trending towards granting Young that huge contract
“As to Bryce Young, we’ve recently caught wind of chatter that the Panthers are “far down the road” toward signing him to a second deal in excess of $50 million per year” https://t.co/EIgSWogpw3
There are two sides to the argument over whether Young deserves a massive contract. This season has already shown both sides of that argument to a degree.
Young hasn't been nearly as efficient through the last two weeks, which has dropped his completion percentage for the season down to 58.7%, thats 29th in the NFL.
On the flip side, Young is still eighth in total passing yards, with 1921 through seven games. The argument against Young being the problem is that he's been pressured constantly behind a depleted offensive line.
Carolina's offensive line ranks 31st in pass-block win rate. Young has been pressured 64 times this season; that's the second most in the league. That said, there are certainly other problems than the QB himself.
However, over $50 million per year means that Young must be productive even in dire situations. The Panthers need a QB who can keep the offense steady despite injuries or poor offensive line play. So far, Young still has to show he can do that week to week.
Young is clearly a starting-level talent, but if Carolina commits to him long-term, it will hinder the roster's flexibility. By the end of this season, there should be no doubt that Young can carry a heavy burden.
Young has been solid this season and has clearly improved, but if this season continues to go in the wrong way, then there has to be a heavy evaluation of the QB first and foremost.
This isn't to say that Young and Carolina can't turn this around, but right now there should be no inclination one way or the other of what happens after this season.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: NFL Week 9 Expert Picks: Can the Panthers Turn It Around?
full_text:
It has been rough sledding for the Carolina Panthers over the last two weeks. They've been obliterated by two strong defenses that smelled blood in the water in Carolina's pass protection. Up next, the Denver Broncos. It's not ideal .
The Panthers were widely picked to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but after being trounced by them at home, almost no one had any faith in them to beat the Green Bay Packers. Has that sentiment changed back home vs. the Broncos?
CBS Sports' Pete Prisco picked the Panthers to lose every single time out until he picked them to beat the Buccaneers. He's back to picking them to lose, and it's hard to blame him. He predicts a 26-20 Broncos win.
"The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix. This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line," he wrote.
His CBS colleague John Breech thinks the Panthers lose by one, thus covering the spread. Mike Spector of Sportsbook Review believes the Panthers can cover the spread and potentially win outright.
"Denver is fortunate to be sitting at 6-2, as it has been outgained by 221-plus yards twice (and is 1-1 in those games), while going 2-0 in games it has also been outgained by 105 and 187 yards," he wrote. "This comes with risk, as the Broncos have tied an NFL record with 15 straight regular-season wins decided by one score. But I’m hoping for an even narrower Broncos win or a double-digit Panthers win."
Erich Richter of The New York Post thinks the Broncos win in a blowout. "The Broncos are rated No. 8 in defensive DVOA and they’re allowing just 4.9 yards per play in their last three games, eighth best in the NFL," he said. "The Panthers are 18th in total DVOA and I think they’re even worse on the field than that ranking suggest. Target the Broncos to win this one big."
Bill Bender of Sporting News predicts a 28-20 Broncos win. "Is this a trap spot for the Broncos after the comeback victory against Kansas City? It's a chance to turn up the heat on Carolina quarterback Bryce Young. Denver has 23 sacks, and running back Jonah Coleman is becoming a factor in the running game. The Broncos will extend their winning streak to five games."
His colleague, Vinnie Iyer , believes this is a potential trap game for the Broncos, but he still thinks it's a double-digit Broncos win because they've found the running game "just in time" to continue "pounding on the Panthers."
Surprisingly, not many believe this can be an actual trap game. The Broncos are coming off an emotional high and traveling across multiple time zones. They're also not as good as their record would suggest.
That's telling. The Panthers are getting no respect here, and it's quite hard to argue with that.

title: Monroe Freeling Gets Midseason Grade That Might Be Too High for Panthers Rookie
full_text:
Monroe Freeling has had a rough start with the Panthers. Carolina used its first-round pick on the former Georgia tackle, hoping he'd eventually become a big part of its offensive line. His first half of the season hasn't given the team much to feel good about.
CBS Sports gave Freeling a C- in its midseason rookie grades. That might seem a little generous based on his performance, although there are some reasons to give him the benefit of the doubt.
Freeling wasn't expected to start this early, and he's been dealing with a knee injury. Those circumstances deserve some consideration. Still, the Panthers used the 19th overall pick on him, and his performance has raised some concerns.
Freeling hasn't done a good job keeping defenders away from Bryce Young. He's been beaten around the edge too many times, and Carolina has paid for it.
The numbers aren't much better. Pro Football Focus had Freeling giving up at least four pressures in four of his first five starts. That's not what the Panthers wanted from their first-round pick.
Freeling spent most of his time at Georgia playing left tackle. Now he's on the right side, and it's been a rough adjustment. He's still learning, but the Panthers need him to figure things out.
Freeling has the size to play in this league. He wouldn't have been been a first-round pick if Carolina didn't see something it liked. But right now, he needs to do a better job keeping defenders away from Young.
Freeling still has time to get things straightened out. He's only a rookie, and the Panthers aren't ready to give up on him. But they need to start seeing some improvement.
The Green Bay game was a rough one. Freeling gave up four pressures and two sacks. It wasn't a good afternoon for Carolina's offensive line.
Freeling's knee has been bothering him, and he's had to play through it. At Georgia, he spent most of his time at left tackle. Carolina has him playing on the right, and he's still getting used to it.
CBS Sports gave him a C-. Considering the injury and everything else, that's understandable. But there have been too many bad plays to say he's had a good rookie season.
The Panthers drafted Freeling because they liked what they saw at Georgia. There's still a chance he becomes a good NFL tackle. He just has a lot to prove between now and the end of the season.

title: The Case For—and Against—the Panthers Trading for Donte Jackson
full_text:
When the Panthers traded Donte Jackson to Pittsburgh, I figured his days in Carolina were over . I certainly wasn't expecting to hear his name mentioned as somebody the Panthers might want back. But with all the problems they've had at cornerback, I guess I shouldn't be surprised.
The Panthers have been trying to get by without Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, and it hasn't always been pretty. They've had to rely on guys who probably weren't expected to play this much when the season started.
Jackson spent six seasons with the Panthers before they traded him. He's with the Chargers now, and with the November 10 trade deadline coming up, I wouldn't completely rule out Carolina making a call about him.
I wouldn't mind seeing Jackson back in a Panthers uniform. I just don't know how much sense it makes to give up something to get him, especially with the injury concerns that have followed him throughout his career.
Donte Jackson wasn't nearly as good as some made him out to be during his first stint in Carolina. He had his moments, but there were also plenty of times when his coverage left a lot to be desired. Still, bringing him back isn't the worst idea considering where the Panthers are right now.
Carolina has been forced to rely on cornerbacks who probably weren't expected to play this much. That's not where a team wants to be when it's trying to stay in the playoff race. Jackson isn't going to fix everything, but he would at least give the Panthers another experienced player to put on the field.
The price would have to be right, though. Giving up an early draft pick for Jackson wouldn't make much sense. A late-round selection would be a different conversation, especially if Carolina believes it can make a run over the final stretch of the season.
Jackson doesn't have to be the player some thought he was when Carolina drafted him. He just has to be better than what the Panthers are getting from the bottom of their cornerback depth chart. And given the injuries they've dealt with, that's an argument worth considering.
There's a reason the Panthers moved on from Jackson in the first place. He could make plays, but he also had a habit of giving up some big ones. His speed helped him recover when he got beat, but that didn't always make up for the mistakes.
The bigger concern now is his health. Jackson has dealt with injuries throughout his career, and he's had trouble staying on the field this season. Carolina already has enough injured cornerbacks. Trading for another one doesn't make much sense unless the Panthers are certain he can play.
Then there's the question of what Carolina would have to give up. Even a late-round draft pick has value, especially for a team that's still trying to build its roster. Giving away picks for a short-term fix can become a problem if those moves don't work out.
The Panthers need help at cornerback, but that doesn't mean they should make a trade just to say they did something. Jackson might be worth considering if he's healthy and the price is low. Otherwise, Carolina would be better off keeping its draft picks and looking elsewhere.

title: Monroe Freeling Looks Like a Misfire, So What Should Panthers Have Done?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers spent the 19th pick on Monroe Freeling, a move that came as a surprise to some but was praised by many. It hasn't panned out so far. Freeling has looked lost often.
From a depth perspective, tackle was unfortunately the only move they could've made . They couldn't foresee losing Taylor Moton and then losing him again seven quarters after he returned, but picking a backup for him proved to be prescient.
And in terms of immediate contributors in the rest of the first round, there aren't many. Dillon Thieneman might be the only better option, but the Panthers are probably thrilled with Zakee Wheatley instead.
So, if the Panthers did get a do-over, would they take Freeling? They would not, according to Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski, but they would still pick a tackle.
In Brent Sobleski's re-draft, the Panthers don't select Monroe Freeling, and it's not because he outplayed his draft slot (like Tetairoa McMillan in some 2025 re-drafts). It's because he hasn't remotely been worth it.
Freeling was always seen as a raw, developmental pick, and injuries have forced him into the lineup. Still, he honestly looks a good ways away from being an NFL player. The only reason he doesn't look worse is because his tackle teammate, Rasheed Walker, is among the worst linemen in the NFL.
Freeling didn't even get picked in the first round in Sobleski's do-over, which isn't surprising. So, who do the Panthers go with? According to the insider, they pick Max Iheanachor, who originally went a couple of picks later to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
"Carolina did sink this pick into an offensive tackle, Monroe Freeling, but Max Iheanachor was the better bet among the developmental options," Sobleski said.
He pointed out how Freeling was thrown into the lineup and has, at times, looked out of his depth. Meanwhile, Iheanachor did not make the starting lineup initially, but he has worked his way onto the field and become a starter.
"Iheanachor's presence has made a difference. The Steelers are now more athletic and nasty at the point of attack, which gives him the edge [here]," he concluded.
The Panthers obviously needed a tackle, but Freeling wasn't ready to play. Maybe one day he'll be the right pick, but for now, Carolina is suffering and might wish they could do it over.

title: 9 Players the Panthers Have to Call About Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline grows closer, we took a stab at some players the Carolina Panthers have to look into. They won't deal for most, if any, of these players, but they should at least get on the phone and find out what it would cost.
We covered earlier how Josh Downs is actually a good idea even if he's not a cornerback or an offensive lineman, and with his desire to be traded, the Panthers have leverage. They can't just ignore the option, especially with a firesale going on in Indianapolis.
The Panthers have suffered without Nic Scourton because he rushes the passer and sets the edge on the run. Josh Sweat can do that, too. He has a 64.7 run defense grade as an edge rusher. He'll be in high demand, but the Panthers have to at least check in.
The Panthers need bodies up front on defense. They have to be able to stop the run, and adding an interior defender like Grover Stewart makes a ton of sense. Have we mentioned that there's a firesale going on in Indianapolis?
Would the New Orleans Saints sell to the Panthers with a small gap between them in the standings? Probably not, but the Panthers badly need help on the offensive line. Robert Hunt has been abysmal, so calling about guard Cesar Ruiz is not a bad idea.
This year, cornerback is a massive need for the Panthers, but it will remain so in the future. Mike Jackson's contract is up, and can we trust Jaycee Horn and Will Lee to stay healthy for 17 games? Now, Sauce Gardner has his own injury history, but between the three of them, we like the chances of getting two full seasons.
The Philadelphia Eagles have already traded an offensive lineman and saw another retire. Why not just take this lost season as a chance to reset and keep selling pieces? Landon Dickerson can play guard and center, two positions the Panthers could stand to upgrade.
There are connections between Eagles CB Riq Woolen and the Panthers' coaching staff, so the fit makes sense. The need is obvious, too, and while Gardner is a long-term addition, Woolen would be much cheaper and a whole lot simpler to add right now.
It's as simple as the Panthers needing a cornerback and Jackson being familiar with this staff. He worked under new CB coach DeAngelo Hall in 2023. Plus, the Los Angeles Chargers should be interested in trading whoever they can.
The run defense has been shockingly bad this year, and that's with the Panthers running out fourth and fifth-string cornerbacks. If cornerback is the top priority, defensive lineman has to be up there, too. Adding Zach Sieler from the dead-end Miami Dolphins is a nice idea.

title: 7 Injuries to Monitor for Panthers: Good News on the Horizon?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have arguably been the most injured team all season. They've lost four cornerbacks, their top two edge rushers, both starting tackles, a starting guard, the second running back, the third wide receiver, their prized rookie wide receiver, and more. Those players are all out right now.
At times, they've been without Devin Lloyd, Bobby Okereke, Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, Bobby Brown, and Pat Jones. It has been a bloodbath, and one could reasonably argue that it has played a hand in their 3-4 record.
After a "mini-bye," so to speak, the Panthers are back in action this week ahead of an important matchup with the Denver Broncos . And fortunately, there are some positive rumblings in the injury world for once.
Through seven contests, the Panthers have honestly dropped like flies. Starting in Week 3, it seems like every single game costs a player a trip to the IR or at least a couple of games on the bench, unable to suit up.
That didn't end last week, with Will Lee III going down. He may avoid the IR, but he probably won't play this week. It's just been that kind of season, which is a shame given the talent this roster actually has when it's healthy.
Regardless, though, things may be beginning to turn in Carolina's favor. There are several injuries to monitor this week, and there is plenty of good news that seems to be on the horizon.
On Tuesday, Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks both got some work in on the side. So did Mike Jackson. The Panthers reportedly plan to open the 21-day return window for Brooks and Legette sooner rather than later.
Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks getting some work in. Mike Jackson also. pic.twitter.com/4h3HYFakKU
Joe Person reported that Jaelan Phillips and Jaycee Horn were also working off to the side. Horn hasn't played since Week 3, and Phillips has been out the last couple of weeks.
Dave Canales: Opening the 21-day window for OL Brady Christensen. Has to "get some football under his belt" to see where he can help the Panthers.
The Panthers officially opened the 21-day return window for Brady Christensen. They want him to get his feet under him first, but he could potentially be in the lineup sooner rather than later.
And perhaps the best update of all: Bryce Young hasn't missed any snaps, but he has clearly been hobbled by a knee injury, sapping his mobility. Young said he's "good," although he has never said it's been a problem.
Head coach Dave Canales said after practice that QB Bryce Young is "ready to rock" moving forward. Canales said there was a lot of energy at practice.
Dave Canales said it was hampering his quarterback, and on Tuesday, the coach said Young was "ready to rock," and reports suggest that Young's mobility is much improved. That could be the most significant update of all.

title: Week 9 NFL Odds Reveal Panthers' Chances of Righting Ship vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have endured back-to-back brutal losses. In both games, the offensive line collapsed to a level that made things untenable for virtually the entire offense. The defense wasn't in much better shape.
Despite getting a few extra days to prepare for Week 9, there is no reprieve . The Panthers are back home after a crushing trip to Green Bay, but the red-hot Denver Broncos are in town. They're coming off a huge win over the Kansas City Chiefs.
Unsurprisingly, the Panthers are home underdogs this week.
A win puts the Panthers at 4-4 and keeps them in first place in the NFC South. A loss drops them to 3-5 and puts them at risk of falling out of first place. This is a crucial game, and now that we're past the halfway point, all games carry a little bit of extra importance.
Unfortunately, oddsmakers don't think the Panthers are going to bounce back this week. On DraftKings , the Panthers are +120 to win on the moneyline. The Broncos are -142 to win outright.
The spread is 2.5 points, which is slightly down from where it began. The Panthers are -102 to cover, while the Broncos are -118 to cover the spread.
The over/under is set at 43.5 points. The over is -115, while the under is -105. Based on that, the final score is expected to be something along the lines of Broncos 24, Panthers 21. A close home defeat.
What does this tell us? It reveals that the Broncos are perhaps a little more vulnerable than we think. Their defense is absurdly good, and the Panthers have been crushed by good defenses two weeks in a row. But if the spread isn't that wide, then there's a path to victory.
The Broncos' offense is not absurdly good. In fact, it has been criticized plenty this season. Bo Nix is not playing good football. They have often won in spite of him. Could the Panthers' defense be motivated after Ejiro Evero's firing and take advantage of a lackluster offense?
Right now, the Panthers' defense is a movable object, and the Broncos' offense is a stoppable force. If the Carolina defense rises to the occasion, they might be able to gift the Panthers' offense a couple of possessions that could be key.
