title: 5 Cornerbacks the Panthers Have Been Urged to Target at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Panthers aren't just a little thin at cornerback anymore. They're running out of guys.
Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are already on injured reserve. Akayleb Evans joined them last week, and then Will Lee III went down against Green Bay with a hamstring injury. By the end of that game, Carolina was down to three healthy corners.
That's a tough way to make it through November.
CBS Sports recently named cornerback as the Panthers' biggest need at the trade deadlin e and came up with five players Carolina could look at: Riq Woolen, Donte Jackson, Alontae Taylor, Amik Robertson and Nahshon Wright.
Some of those names make a lot more sense to me than others.
Carolina doesn't need to make a trade just so it can say it did something. But with this many injuries at one position, Dan Morgan should at least be making calls.
So let's go through the five names CBS suggested and figure out which ones I'd actually want the Panthers to pursue.
Woolen is probably the first guy I'd call about.
I've liked his game for a while. He's 6-foot-4, has plenty of speed and has picked off 12 passes since coming into the league. Carolina could use all of that right now.
The only reason I'd hesitate is because he might not be here very long.
His contract is up after this season. Maybe the Panthers trade for him and two months later he's gone. I'm not crazy about that, but it wouldn't stop me either.
It really comes down to what Philadelphia wants.
If a fifth-round pick gets it done, I'd make the trade. If we're talking about a fourth, I'd have to think about it. Anything more than that and I'm out.
It doesn't need one badly enough to do something stupid.
Donte Jackson wouldn't need much of an introduction in Carolina.
We watched him play here for six years. There were good days and some frustrating ones, but Jackson started a lot of football games for the Panthers. If the Chargers aren't asking for much, I could see going back to someone Carolina already knows.
I'd have one question first. How healthy is he?
Jackson has only been on the field for four games this season because of a hamstring injury. Carolina already has enough injured corners. Before I'd give up anything for Jackson, I'd need to know he's ready to play.
Taylor is where I'd probably pass.
He can play outside or in the slot, and 40 pass breakups in four years with New Orleans isn't something I'd ignore. My problem isn't really with Taylor as a player.
Tennessee just signed him in March, and Carolina would be taking on $20.51 million guaranteed for next season. That's a lot different from grabbing Jackson for the rest of this year and seeing what happens.
Maybe Taylor would help. He probably would.
I just don't like the idea of solving an injury problem in November by taking on that much money for next season.
If I'm choosing between these two, give me Jackson at the cheaper price.
Amik Robertson might be the guy on this list I'm overlooking.
He's played seven games for Washington this season and already has eight passes defended. He's also been around long enough that Carolina should have a pretty good idea what it's getting. Robertson isn't the big swing Woolen would be, but maybe that's not what the Panthers need.
I'd have no problem calling Washington about him. Robertson has another year on his contract, but Carolina could get out of it after the season if things don't work.
Wright is the one I can't figure out.
Five interceptions last year. This year? Not one defensive snap for the Jets. He was hurt during training camp, lost the competition for a starting job and hasn't been able to get back into the mix. Wright has even admitted this season has been frustrating.
That makes me want to know what New York would take for him.
Carolina is desperate enough at corner to take a chance, and Wright shouldn't cost much considering he can't get on the field in New York.
Robertson would be the safer call. Wright would be the gamble.
At this point, I'd be willing to ask about both.
Woolen would be my first call.
This isn't a hard one for me. If I'm going to trade for a corner, give me the guy I think can help the most. I can worry about his contract when the season is over.
That doesn't mean Philadelphia gets whatever it asks for. There's a limit, and I'd be perfectly fine hanging up the phone if things got stupid.
Jackson would still interest me. I've seen him play enough football in a Panthers uniform to know exactly what comes with that deal.
I'm calling about Woolen first and going from there.
I'd rather take the shot on the best corner of these five and see what happens.

title: The Case For—and Against—the Panthers Trading for Jackson Powers-Johnson
full_text:
I've lost track of how many different offensive line combinations the Panthers have used this season. Injuries are part of it, but at some point you have to wonder how long Carolina can keep moving pieces around and hoping it works.
Jackson Powers-Johnson is an interesting name to consider.
Things haven't gone the way Powers-Johnson probably expected in Las Vegas. He was a second-round pick just two years ago, but he's already lost his spot in the starting lineup. If the Raiders are willing to move on this quickly, Carolina should at least find out what it would take.
I'm not looking at Powers-Johnson as some huge upgrade that suddenly fixes the offensive line. That's asking too much. What I like is that he's 23, he's played guard and center, and Carolina wouldn't be bringing in another veteran just to get through the next couple of months.
Especially after watching Bryce Young hit the ground six times against Green Bay.
There are reasons for Carolina to make the call.
There are also a few pretty good reasons to leave this one alone.
Powers-Johnson is a weird trade target. A year ago, I'm not sure the Raiders would've even listened. Now we're talking about whether a Day 3 pick could get it done.
He started 14 games as a rookie. Some came at left guard, others at center.
Losing his starting job bothers me. It should. I'd want to know why things changed so much from one season to the next before giving Las Vegas anything for him. But 14 starts as a rookie is enough for me to wonder if there's still something there.
There's no guarantee they can. That's why we're talking about a Day 3 pick instead of something much higher.
Maybe Carolina gets the rookie version of Powers-Johnson. If not, they move on and a late pick is gone. I can live with that.
I'd rather see the Panthers take that chance than keep moving the same pieces around up front.
This is where I get hung up. Trading for an offensive lineman sounds good right now. Trading for one who just lost his own starting job doesn't sound quite as good.
Powers-Johnson was playing right guard when the Raiders made a change. That's enough to make me wonder what Carolina would be getting. Maybe Las Vegas gave up on him too quickly. I'd still want an answer for why he isn't playing.
Then you have to figure out where he plays. Robert Hunt is at right guard. Powers-Johnson has experience at center, but he hasn't been playing there lately. If the Panthers trade for him, I'd want it to be because they have a spot in mind and not because they saw a former second-round pick available for cheap.
That's where I have a harder time talking myself into this one. Carolina doesn't need another offensive lineman to move around and figure out later.
They've done enough of that already.
For a Day 3 pick? Yeah, I would.
There's enough about Powers-Johnson that bothers me to understand why the Raiders might be ready to move on. I'm just not sure I'm ready to do the same with a 23-year-old offensive lineman who was starting games as a rookie.
I wouldn't get cute with the offer. If Las Vegas wants more than a late pick, they can keep him. Carolina has too many other things to fix to start throwing better picks at a player the Raiders just benched.
But a late pick is different. I'd send it and see if a new team can get something out of him.
If not, Dan Morgan moves on.
I think this one is worth finding out.

title: Bears Trade Rumor Could Lead to Deadline Deal With Eagles, Commanders or Jets
full_text:
All signs point to the Chicago Bears making a trade to improve the edge rushers room, but could general manager Ryan Poles have something else up his sleeve?
According to ESPN's Dan Graziano . not only is edge rusher on the table, but so is a move at cornerback, which is something fellow ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler also noted.
"The Bears made their big move for Simmons, but they're still poking around on potentially available cornerbacks, as are the Lions," Graziano wrote.
"The Bears have been linked to edge rushers such as Khalil Mack, but a few league evaluators told me what you heard -- that cornerback is becoming more of a need," Fowler said.
Chicago could use more depth at safety, but we don't see a dire issue there with Cam Lewis and Dillon Thieneman playing good football and Elijah Hicks backing them up. The Bears might get Coby Bryant back soon , also, although we can't say for sure.
The biggest issue is at cornerback, where Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson have been total liabilities. Johnson's issues have been especially shocking because the belief was he was going to rebound after a lackluster 2025 campaign in which Johnson was plagued by injury.
Rookie Malik Muhammad has been the Bears' best cornerback in 2026 and was able to transition from the slot to the outside after Kyler Gordon's return, which thankfully pushed Stevenson to a lesser role before Muhammad was ruled out for Week 8 after getting hurt in Week 7.
Unfortunately for the Bears, there is no such solution for Johnson with guys like Clark Phillips and Josh Blackwell serving as the other backups at cornerback.
If the Bears are serious about making an addition to cornerback, three names to keep an eye on are Riq Woolen of the Philadelphia Eagles, Mike Sainristil of the Washington Commanders and our old friend Nahshon Wright of the New York Jets.
The Eagles are in the midst of a disastrous 2-6 season and look primed to sell at the deadline. Woolen makes sense as a trade candidate because of his status as a 2027 free agent.
Woolen isn't having his best season, but his coverage numbers are still solid and better than those of both Stevenson and Johnson, and there's a realistic chance he plays better in Chicago.
Woolen thrives in man coverage and the Bears play the second-highest rate of man coverage in the NFL at 29.5%, which is over 12% more than the Eagles.
Sainristil is another player who is slated to be a free agent in 2027 and on a team that could sell at the deadline because of its putrid record.
The former second-round pick has struggled, but he does have superior numbers in completion rate and passer rating allowed than Johnson, and a better number in the latter than Stevenson.
Last but not least we have Wright, who would be a seamless fit in the Bears' defense given his experience in Dennis Allen's system.
Wright left the Jets in free agency, but for whatever reason has just not garnered a role at all. When he isn't a healthy scratch, Wright has only been playing on special teams.
Brendan Sugrue of Bears Wire reports that Wright is open to a reunion with Chicago, although he has not requested a trade. Wright replaced Stevenson last season and played well, so perhaps he could do the same in place of Johnson.
We would much rather see Chicago trade for Woolen or Wright, but the latter is a bit more realistic of an option because of his smalller contract and his cheaper price tag when it comes to compensation in a trade.

title: Jeffery Simmons Promises 'Good, Better, Best' Improvement for Next Bears Game
full_text:
Jeffery Simmons' debut with the Chicago Bears was almost perfect.
The star defensive tackle made an immediate impact for the Bears in his first game in Week 8 against the Jacksonville Jaguars and showed everyone exactly why general manager Ryan Poles was willing to give up a historic package for him.
The only hiccup for Simmons on Monday came after the contest, when head coach Ben Johnson was doing his "good, better, best" portion of his postgame speech and Simmons apparently wasn't familiar with it.
We know that because, in the video of the speech , Simmons was visible in the background and wasn't reciting it with the rest of the team. What was funnier was Montez Sweat trying to get him going.
On Wednesday, Simmons vowed to be better next time around. He even said he's going on YouTube to study up and make sure he gets it right, according to CHGO Bears .
"I've definitely been on YouTube trying to figure that out," he said with a smile. "Make sure I'm good for next game. So, next game, especially I'm on the camera like that, I'll know the words. I'll be ready."
We can envision Simmons now.
He'll have the playbook that he's still learning in one hand and Johnson's "good, better, best" on repeat.
Truth be told, nobody gives a damn about Simmons' "good, better, best" hiccup when he played the quality of football he did against Seattle.
Simmons was every bit of the menace the Bears hoped he would be. It took him just two drives to notch his first sack , and he had a team-high six tackles and two tackles for loss, a bunch of pressures, and even one pass defensed.
There are so many ways Simmons changes this defense.
Not only is he great as an interior pass-rusher and run defender, but Simmons also draws double teams that give his teammates more favorable matchups . And, there are even times when Simmons beats those double teams to make a play.
"Phenomenal player," defensive end Daniel Hardy said. "Really charged up the locker room. Definitely boosted up the DL. He took a ton of reps tonight and made them all count.  You gotta account for him. Give him a 1-on-1, it's not gonna end well. He frees stuff up for everybody just because he draws so much attention to him. So appreciate it, and we're all happy with the production."
"I definitely got my opportunities," defensive end Montez Sweat said. "I definitely got some 1-on-1s. I was looking forward to taking advantage of that, and I'm looking forward to doing that the rest of the year."
Simmons' presence has now become even more important with the Bears dealing with some injuries along the defensive line.
Chicago is likely to have lost Kentavius Street for the rest of the season, and Grady Jarrett's status for Week 9 is up in the air because of a groin injury.

title: Advancement in Bears Offense Now Obvious to Caleb Williams Himself
full_text:
Much like parents will chart the growth of a child with marks on a wall denoting their height at a specific age, there are ways of measuring the effect of time and the passing process on quarterback Caleb Williams .
Williams is sprouting up before the very eyes of Bears fans , and it's obvious from several things, especially the way he has learned to throw the shorter passes after going through his progression. He's learning to make the game easier.
“I would say I've grown in that area," Williams said late Wednesday at Halas Hall. "I think if you go back to high school, all I did was take shots. I went to college and scrambled around a little bit, I took a few checkdowns, very little. Then my first (NFL) year was very little. I got sacked a lot, all of that.
"Then this past year (2025), found a few more scrambles a little bit. Then this year it's just being a lot more comfortable with the playbook and understanding it and what we want to do with certain plays. Then from there, when they don't give us a specific coverage, just being able to check the ball down and keep the drive alive.”
Caleb Williams since returning from hamstring injury: 3-0 record 860 passing yards 4 TD, 0 INT 111.3 passer rating Bears haven’t trailed once over the last three weeks. https://t.co/nqIrrLUzvc pic.twitter.com/4OsJQvEtXU
Williams' average intended air yards on throws is longer than only five other starting quarterbacks and his air yards per completion is longer than only seven other starters. Last year he was in the top half of the league for both length of completion and intended distance.
No one wants to give up on the deeper throws and he has made those effectively when necessary, but more checkdowns than in the past helped the Bears establish some of the possession time which helped in their three straight wins.
The wild plays when he runs around in and out of the pocket have been occurred with less frequency, and this also brings down the downfield distance. He sees it as another growth sign.
TRENDING: Gamblers are calling for an INVESTIGATION into a play involving #Bears QB Caleb Williams and WR Kalif Raymond. Fans believe Williams threw a forward pass to Raymond, which would change how the play was officially recorded. WOW😳 pic.twitter.com/4FDiI2SpPO
“I had a couple of pretty cool scrambles, I'd say," he said of Monday night's win. "I still do all of that. I wouldn't say that I look different.
"I think I've just grown in certain aspects. I think I've tried to maintain the things that I've done well. Then the things that I haven't done well, just try and up those to the level of the other things that I have done well. So I wouldn't say different. I think part of it's just comfort with the offense also. I think that's a really big piece on my side. And then just finding ways to keep pushing myself and trying to be better for the guys.”
Cleaner pass plays to wide receivers are part of it, he said. In other words, the ball coming out in time and giving them the chance for yards after catch. Another is the way he directs things at the line of scrimmage for teammates before a play. This was very apparent in the noise at Seattle on Monday.
What’s crazy about Caleb Williams is that he’s a better “kid” and becoming a better leader than his football talent. He’s proven everyone wrong about being selfish and a diva. He’s the ultimate teammate. That should scare the NFL more than anything. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/VzbhoKWaG5
"The communication maybe seemed a little bit more emphasized, I would say, this past week overall," he said. "Just knowing the environment, playing in some loud games before in my career, I think that's what it showed.
"But we communicate. That's one of our biggest things as an offense is being able to communicate. It doesn't waver depending on home, away, crazy crowd or not."
The communication at the line is truly a sign of Williams advancing in Johnson's offense. It's the type of thing the better quarterbacks have done well over the years. Peyton Manning yelling "Omaha!" is an example of this type of thing.
What you are seeing with Caleb Williams is comfort with himself as a person, the game has slowed down for him, confidence in coaching & players around him = special.  Best QB play I’ve ever seen by @ChicagoBears
All of these things are examples of being doing the uncomfortable to become better. After all, Johnson said when hired that they all need to become comfortable with being uncomfortable.
"That's how you grow," Williams said. "That's how you get better. I think you get in season sometimes and you want to run things that maybe fit you a little bit more, then I will practice a few times. And I obviously trust Ben with it.
Never a fan of Caleb Williams #USC days, yet it must be @ChicagoBears coaching getting him better More red line work & touch passes, No.18 might be a bigger threat longstanding Has the targets, maybe add a RB, augment to the Defense secondary & #Bears unstoppable #NFL #Trade
"When he calls something and I don't like it, we go up in the office, we sit down, we talk about it, he shows me clips. And if I still don't like it, or I still don't see it, he won't call it because it's kind of butchering me out there. He's awesome with that. But a lot of times, we'll go up in the office, we'll talk about it. We'll watch multiple clips. Then at the end of it, I typically feel pretty good about it and where we want to go with the ball.”
This might all sound like assumed duties for any quarterback in any NFL city.
In Chicago, anything leading to an advanced state of quarterback play is foreign and even startling. It's not a place where quarterbacks have come to grow over the years.
Rome Odunze is one of the smoother route runners in the league. Let Rome and Caleb KEEP BUILDING CHEMISTRY https://t.co/jvQC1NhxX2 pic.twitter.com/tk7vaNftQR

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update, Another LT Issue & More From Bears' Wednesday Practice Report
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have put out their first (and estimated) injury report of the week ahead of the Week 9 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night.
Earlier in the day, we learned of the brutal news that the Bears will be without left tackle Braxton Jones for the remainder of the year after it was decided he needed surgery on his knee injury, which was diagnosed as a partially torn patellar tendon.
It also appears the Bears are going to be without defensive tackle Kentavius Street, who suffered a knee injury in Week 8. Head coach Ben Johnson said Street is likely done for 2026 .
Making matters worse, left tackle Theo Benedet and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett are both dealing with injuries and their statuses are up in the air. More on them in a bit.
There wasn't any good news on running back Kyle Monangai, either. Here's the full injury report and more.
Cornerback Malik Muhammad missed last week's game with a toe injury. His estimated limited practice is status quo from last week, when Muhammad logged three practices before not playing.
Grady Jarrett's injury will be one to monitor during the week. As we said, the Bears are already short-handed with Street on the shelf.
Adding to the running back woes, now Zavier Scott is hurt. Salvon Ahmed, who is on the practice squad, is the only other healthy running back behind D'Andre Swft and Roschon Johnson.
Once again an estimated non-participant, Monangai remains on track to sit out another game. If he doesn't practice on Thursday, it'll be a safe bet Monangai will miss a fifth game.
Head coach Ben Johnson said last week that this is not a case of Monangai's injury being worse than expected but rather just a case of not knowing "how a player will bounce back" from his injury.
“No, I think every time a player has an Injury, you don’t know how a player will bounce back from that. Obviously, we didn’t think it was warranted to put him on IR, and yet we’re hopeful we’ll get him back sooner rather than later," Johnson said .
Nicholas Moreano of Bears Roundtable reported after the game on Monday night that Benedet might have a separated shoulder, which could keep him out for an extended period of time.
"One observation from the Bears' locker room. I saw Theo Benedet leave with a Bears staff member before the media was allowed into the locker room," Moreano said. "When he came back, he sat at his locker, looking disappointed. As I was getting ready to record an interview, I heard him say separated shoulder."
If Benedet can't go on Sunday, the Bears are going to need a full game out of Ozzy Trapilo, but we're not sure if he's ready for that yet. Trapilo has only played limited snaps in two games this year while ramping up in his return from a torn patellar tendon.
After mixing in with Benedet in Weeks 6 and 7, playing 17 and 19 snaps, Trapilo didn't play against the Seahawks in Week 8.
In the event that Trapilo isn't ready for a full game in Week 9, the Bears could deploy Joe Thuney at left tackle and have Luke Newman take Thuney's spot.
The Bears also have Caden Barnett and Christian Jones on the practice squad, but Jones has just 70 career snaps in the NFL, with all of them coming at right tackle, and Barnett can play at tackle but he's also a rookie and has never played a regular-season snap.

title: Bears Coach Ben Johnson Reacts to Seahawks Win, Prepares for Buccaneers
full_text:
Coach Ben Johnson isn't pretending like there aren't problems with the Chicago Bears, despite a dominant 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football in Week 8.
On Wednesday, Johnson stressed that complacency isn't prevailing in the locker room after a dominant showing against the defending Super Bowl champions and the 12s at Lumen Field. There's a matchup with a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that just beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 without completing a single pass all game.
“We’ve gotta keep winning,” Johnson said on Wednesday . “We’ve gotta win each and every week. We gotta go 1-0 this week. That’s all we care about. That’s all we’ve talked about for the last year and a half in this building, and that doesn’t change, no matter what our record is and what’s happened previously. We’re gonna go right back to work. We’re gonna prepare just like we’ve been doing.”
“When you win, all the mistakes are minimized. And then when you lose, everything gets magnified to the nth degree. But they’re still there. Each and every game, there’s always things that we’ve got to clean up and get better at.”
With Jeffery Simmons' arrival working out as well as possible for Chicago in his debut in Seattle, and optimism about winning it all in February, the Bears could easily look past a team like the Bucs. Baker Mayfield's return from a thumb injury hardly inspired confidence on Tampa Bay's end.
After reinjuring Sam Darnold on Monday because of such a fearsome pass rush, Chicago cannot ease off the gas pedal against a more mobile quarterback and a truly dangerous Buccaneers ground game.
Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 310 rushing yards last weekend in the pouring rain. Running an offense similar to Army, Navy, and Air Force, Tampa Bay won an old school kind of game.
If the weather is bad on Sunday Night Football at Soldier Field, Johnson's squad is better-equipped than most. He thrives on bad weather. Even with Simmons giving the run defense a jolt, every level of the Bears' defense will be tested in Week 9.
Going from an injury-filled Seahawks running back room that just returned Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet to the Buccaneers will be drastic. Having too much confidence because of this past Monday's results would be a death knell.
Johnson has the attitude to avoid a letdown. We'll see if his team can execute on the field against Todd Bowles's team, given the 62-year-old head coach is playing for his job every week.

title: Bears Add Earnest Brown IV After Kentavius Street Injury Leaves DT Depth Thin
full_text:
The injury bug bit the Chicago Bears hard this week. Early on Wednesday afternoon, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reported that left tackle Braxton Jones will miss the rest of the season following surgery on his knee. Jones was placed on Injured Reserve (IR) on October 3 with the hope that he could return later in the season, but those hopes have been dashed.
Just hours after Jones' injury update, more injury news followed. The Bears announced that they had placed defensive tackle Kentavius Street on IR, and head coach Ben Johnson later said that it was "unlikely" that he would return this season, according to a report from Brad Biggs . This leaves the Bears dangerously thin along the defensive line, as Dayo Odeyingbo also remains on IR.
While Street is far from Chicago's top defender, they'll feel his loss. Street had been a dependable contributor to Dennis Allen's defense, earning a solid 70.6 impact grade from Pro Football Network. In training camp, Street had impressed Dennis Allen even more than rookie Jordan van den Berg , who had become a fan-favorite for his tenacious style of play.
Of course, the NFL is a 'next man up' league, and this rash of injuries to Chicago's defensive line opens the door for rookies to play a larger role than they previously had. Jordan van den Berg in particular stands to gain quite a bit should he see more snaps against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9. Plus, the Bears now know that they can simply lean on superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons after he dismantled the Seattle Seahawks in the Bears' statement primetime victory on Monday.
In light of these season-ending injuries to Street and Cole Kmet, the Bears made two roster moves on Wednesday to add to their depth. They signed tight end Stephen Carlson from the practice squad to the active roster, then added defensive tackle Earnest Brown IV to the practice squad, according to Brad Biggs .
Brown, a fifth-round pick in the 2021 NFL draft, has appeared in 15 regular season games between stints with the L.A. Rams and Buccaneers. In case the Bears continue to lose defensive tackles, he can step in and handle a small role, given his experience. As for Carlson, he's been with the Bears since 2023 but has only appeared in four regular season games, most recently against the Seahawks.

title: Braxton Jones Is Out for the Season, and the Bears Should Call a Former Ben Johnson Left Tackle
full_text:
The Bears' situation on the offensive line had been promising as Theo Benedet played well and Ozzy Trapilo continued working gradually back toward 100% with limited reps in games.
Now it all seems to be crashing down and perhaps instead of using any available salary cap money for another cornerback or edge rusher Khalil Mack, the Bears should be looking at left tackle.
A report by Brad Biggs of the Tribune on Wednesday said the starter to open this season, Braxton Jones, was going on season-ending IR for the second season in a row with a patellar tendon injury requiring surgery.
Hope had been Jones could eventually return and supply depth.
#Bears LT Braxton Jones will not return from IR this season. He underwent right knee surgery on Tuesday. 'I was really encouraged with his play. It was a big loss.' https://t.co/apoRcYTGaO
After Monday night's win, Bears reporter Nick Moreano posted Theo Benedet had suffered a possible shoulder separation in the win.
This would leave them relying on Trapilo. Normally this is no problem. Trapilo was a solid player as a rookie starter last year but his early return this year has not gone off without a hitch. Trapilo
Snap counts from last night’s Bears win pic.twitter.com/CNfGPv3CwB
Trapilo did not play Monday against Seattle even though he was not inactive. He was not on the injury report. He had played only 36 downs on offense in the wins over Atlanta and New England with what Pro Football Focus graded as marginal results. He had a solid run-blocking day against New England but struggled for 12 pass blocking attempts, and didn't do much better as a pass blocker for his nine reps against Atlanta in the passing game.
This view of Trapilo's play was supported by a report from CHGO's Adam Hoge. Prior to the start of the Seattle game Hoge quoted offensive line coach Dan Roushar saying Trapilo had "a couple rough ones." He added: "He knows it. He's gotta play better. We gotta have him play better to win."
Ahead of kickoff tonight, here are some #Bears offensive line nuggets from OL coach Dan Roushar: 🔹 On LT Theo Benedet: "Each of the last three games, his posture, his balance and his hands have all improved. I think he's gaining confidence. You see that in his play." (Added…
If Trapilo isn't physically up to playing at the level he displayed last year or just isn't playing well period, Jones is now out for the yearm and Benedet has a shoulder injury, it's leaving the Bears in a big lurch. At the very least, it's a depth problem and depending on the injuries it could be even be a starting issue.
Perhaps they could go to All-Pro left guard Joe Thuney at left tackle like they did in the playoff game with the Rams. There is another option available and it depends on cost.
Former Lions left tackle Taylor Decker remains an unsigned free agent. Detroit released him in March after contract discussions broke down. Washington was among teams reportedly interested in Decker. Because of his past relationship with coach Ben Johnson in Detroit, it would be an easy pickup with the offense and blocking scheme.
One observation from the Bears' locker room. I saw Theo Benedet leave with a Bears staff member before the media was allowed into the locker room. When he came back, he sat at his locker, looking disappointed. As I was getting ready to record an interview, I heard him say…
The problem is the Bears are down to less than $2 million in available cap space. They may need to start getting back cash via restructuring to do this, depending on the cost.
However, a team that has gone all in by trading two first-round picks and a fourth for Jeffery Simmons and has beaten the Super Bowl champion and loser in successive weeks, can't afford to be playing on offense with such difficult situation at left tackle.
Caleb Williams' blindside needs to be protected by someone and moving Thuney to do it doesn't help them at left guard. It might not even be a realistic move for Thuney, who turns 34 later this month.
The Bears need to revisit the Decker situation and solidify the left tackle position before they start worrying about spending some of their cap space on another pass rusher or a cornerback.
Taylor Decker has no ground to stand on, he was the highest paid OL on our team last season with both his blocking grades being under the top 50% pic.twitter.com/ndrYB1YuAn

title: Caleb Williams and Bears Can Enjoy Seeing Regressionists Eat Crow
full_text:
The Bears, at 6-2 and rising in numerous power rankings, look nothing like the team of many preseason predictions.
Those would be the regressionists.
ESPN's Bill Barnwell was the guy at the front of the parade, when he practically wrote a book on the reasons the Bears were tops for regression.
"I wouldn't be shocked if Williams takes another step forward and the offense follows in kind," Barnwell wrote. "With real concerns about the defense and a guarantee that the Bears won't be quite as lucky with turnovers and special teams work late in games, though, I'm not sure even an improved offense can get Chicago to 11 wins this season."
He also labeled the Broncos and Jaguars top regression candidates. Whoops.
"I want to make these fans extremely proud to be a Bears fan." Caleb Williams joins @notthefakeSVP and is welcomed by a crowd of Bears fans following their win on the road against the Seahawks 😤 pic.twitter.com/ntWXe10y2w
Even Yahoo Sports veteran Frank Schwab joined the dog pile, and when it all came down he used the excuse many others did and pointed at last year's turnover differential, along with the narrow Bears wins of 2025 and the tougher 2026 schedule.
"Williams still had accuracy issues last season, but showed significant growth and it's reasonable to think there's a big leap coming," Schwab wrote. "If he was an MVP candidate in his third season, it wouldn't be a surprise. But plenty of regression indicators are not kind to the Bears.
"Start with turnover differential. The Bears were +22 last season, five better than any other team and nine better than third place. That's likely unsustainable."
What the turnover truthers failed to realize, but many who have watched the NFL have, is you don't play last season over again. The team has changed. Other teams changed. They haven't had to stage miracle comebacks every week this season because they improved in Year 2 under Ben Johnson. This should have been expected.
Bears have not started 6-2 or better through eight games since 2012, when they started 7-1, finished 10-6 and missed the playoffs. #BearDown pic.twitter.com/JsyQuiagFX
Pro Football Focus usually finds a way to put all of its analytical numbers in the wrong category and they did with the Bears. Mark Chichester of PFF slated Williams one of the QBs who should take a step back in 2026 and sidekick Bradley Locker cited some other reasons many skipped over for calling the Bears regression candidates.
"At the same time, the Bears suffered a big loss up the middle when center Drew Dalman retired — and replacement Garrett Bradbury has never earned above a 68.0 overall PFF grade in any season," Locker wrote in an article naming the Bears one of three teams who'll take a step back. "Likewise, the team’s receiver room is counting heavily on inconsistent talents like Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond, who each earned a sub-73.0 PFF receiving grade last season."
Bears regression in 2026-27 is going to hit like a truck🤯 • 11 wins, but only a +26 point differential • Expected record was just 9.1–7.9 • NFL-best +22 turnover margin, even if they remain good at taking the ball away and get like a +10 thats still 12 less possessions… pic.twitter.com/LprPTILEsZ
Basing everything on PFF grading isn't advisable and besides that, he must not have been watching Dalman's play near the end of last season. It tailed off. Bradbury has been rock solid and even an upgrade over the way Dalman played from December on last season.  Odunze is now coming into his own, finally entirely healthy. Raymond has been a godsend.
They all should have been reading what Jonathan Jones wrote for The Athletic and considered this. He read and heard everything being said about regression. He did get the Panthers right, but let's face it, anyone could have told him they were only in the playoffs last year because the rest of the NFC South was rot.
"History does say that leading the league in takeaways in consecutive years is difficult," Jones wrote. "And repeating six fourth-quarter comeback victories (seven if you count the playoffs) probably isn’t realistic. But what if the Bears don’t put themselves in that position in the first place?"
Why would a better team need to stage such wild comebacks? The Bears clearly were and are better than last year. Jones found a Bears source who didn't want to be named and gave their take on the regression through turnover and schedule comments.
“I think it’s lazy,” this Bears source told him. “You see interceptions and say, ‘You can’t do that again.’ Fourth-quarter comebacks and say, ‘They can’t come back.’ And you’re ignoring all the space in between that can be improved.
“We use it for fuel more than anything.”
“If I was the Chicago Bears, I would take Jayden Daniels.” - Dan Orlovsky on February 29th 2024 pic.twitter.com/wGMnhl02ua
It's very apparent they are using it as fuel, as a 6-2 record going into the Tampa Bay game Sunday night says. Even frequent Williams critic Dan Orlovsky had to admit this week what's obvious.
"This is an incredibly scary football team right now,"  Orlovsky said.
He had ESPN cohort Mina Kimes saying maybe only Josh Allen is better than Williams now. And she based Allen's edge on mobility, even though she had to admit it's not exactly a Williams weakness,.
"This is an incredibly scary football team right now. ... I think it was a very clear message sent to the NFL." – @danorlovsky7 on Caleb Williams and the Bears 😤 pic.twitter.com/OOF3O58SqA
It was Orlovsky a week ago who was criticizing the Bears for not trading to get DeForest Buckner, who is 3 years older than Jeffery Simmons and doesn't stop the run anywhere near as well as he used to, let alone as well as Simmons does.
The Bears have taken names and remember what was said before the season. Williams even brought this up when he was interviewed by Scott Van Pelt on Monday night's ESPN postgame show.
"Oh yeah, we hear," Williams said about the negative turn predicted for the team before the season.
Here’s a FUN FACT When Dan Orlovsky rants about how you shouldn’t pair a first time Offensive HC like Ben Johnson with a young QB like Caleb in his Y2…. And how it seems most likely to fail (cherry picking his examples to make the argument) And how a defensive coach may be… pic.twitter.com/4bZlzV4HJt
Can they continue their roll now that the focus is going from regression to Super Bowl. He said the focus always has been not getting ahead of themselves.
"That's my focus each week," Williams told Van Pelt. "Being at my best focus on being where my feet are at and finding ways to make sure the team is there with me and we're not focused on what everybody says on the outside noise because we were supposedly the No. 1 regression team and now everybody is going to jump om the train to the other side."
There's room on their train for everyone, maybe even Barnwell if he wants. It's a train being fueled by a chip on their shoulder.
Dan Orlovsky Can’t Believe The Bears Didn’t Attempt To Trade For Deforest Buckner: “And then honestly, one of my big takeaways in how does Chicago not make this move?” pic.twitter.com/xCOAZfdGMC

title: Case Keenum Emerges as a Bears Trade Candidate With the Ravens Down to Their Third QB
full_text:
The Chicago Bears sit at 6-2 and are coming off the most convincing win in recent memory, a 34-17 beatdown of the defending Super Bowl champs on their own turf.
They're going all-in on a Super Bowl run after poaching Jeffery Simmons from the Titans last week. If anything, most believe they might add another asset ( specifically a cornerback or edge rusher ) ahead of the trade deadline.
However, their current roster isn't off limits. ESPN's Dan Graziano highlighted Case Keenum as someone who could be on the move if another (desperate) team comes calling.
"This is another team [the Bears] that I don't think would be moving players. But teams always need QB help, and Keenum showed a little something earlier this season in relief of Caleb Williams," Graziano wrote. "For the right offer, who knows?"
Barring a disaster, Keenum won't see the field again for Chicago this season. Hamstring injuries tend to linger, but Caleb Williams has seemingly put his in the rearview mirror.
Tyson Bagent also resumed his role as Williams' backup after returning from a concussion ( even after a disastrous performance against the Packers in Week 5 ). Bagent would be the next man up if the signal-caller goes down.
Still, Keenum's leadership makes him a valuable asset to Chicago's quarterback room. He's started 68 games (or 67 if you don't want to count his opening pitch/handoff against the Jets), and has a wealth of knowledge.
From a mentor perspective, he can offer advice to Williams that 26-year-old Bagent cannot. The Bears franchise quarterback has clearly found value in his presence, as well.
"Casey! Thank you!" Case Keenum told Caleb Williams what he was seeing, and QB1 executed it on the field 🗣️ @insidethenfl Week 7 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/t74Ql1MnJN
Would that mentorship be enough to make them hang onto him, regardless of what another team might offer? Personally, we think so.
With them packaging three draft picks to Tennessee for Simmons (while receiving a fifth-round selection in return), we understand there being a different perspective on the matter, though.
The Baltimore Ravens make the most sense as a potential suitor for Keenum (or Bagent, which might be the most logical candidate for both parties). They're far from out of the AFC playoff picture at 4-4, but they're staring down the barrel of QB3 Joe Fagnano starting the rest of the season after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both went down with injuries against the Bills on Sunday.
Jackson has yet to be ruled out for the year, but head coach Jesse Minter didn't sound optimistic speaking to reporters about his thumb injury after the contest. Huntley, meanwhile, was officially ruled out for the season with a turf toe injury this morning.
Keenum's ability to roll with the punches (as we saw in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3 ) and experience working with Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle make him a logical stopgap option to potentially save their season.
It's tough to find another trade partner for Keenum at this point. The Cardinals have a questionable quarterback situation, but Gardner Minshew feels like a younger version of Keenum, and they'll probably roll with him the rest of the way after he provided a huge spark on Sunday against Dallas.
However, if another starter goes down with an injury ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, he would then be a potential answer.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Chicago Bears Left Tackle Braxton Jones Set to Miss Rest of Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will not be getting left tackle Braxton Jones back this season.
According to The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs , Jones, who is on injured reserve due to a knee injury , suffered a partially torn patellar tendon that required season-ending surgery.
The initial plan was for Jones to rehabilitate the injury and make his way back, but that apparently did not work out.
"Chicago Bears left tackle Braxton Jones underwent surgery on his right knee Tuesday and won’t be an option to return from injured reserve this season," Biggs wrote.
"Jones suffered a partially torn patellar tendon, and the plan was for him to rehabilitate the injury before determining if it was feasible for him to return this season and delay surgery," he added. "After a little more than a month, it was decided to have the injury repaired, an NFL source said Wednesday."
This is the second significant injury Jones has suffered in the last three years. He saw his 2024 campaign cut short due to a broken left ankle, and he just didn't look like himself in his first season back in 2025, which led to him getting benched.
But Jones had rebounded in 2026 and was playing good football while serving as the replacement for Ozzy Trapilo, who was working his way back from his own torn patellar.
Unfortunately for the Bears, Jones' injury might not be the only one at the left tackle position.
According to Bears beat writer Nicholas Moreano of Bears Roundtable , it appears Theo Benedet might have suffered a shoulder injury in the Week 8 victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.
"One observation from the Bears' locker room. I saw Theo Benedet leave with a Bears staff member before the media was allowed into the locker room," Moreano said. "When he came back, he sat at his locker, looking disappointed. As I was getting ready to record an interview, I heard him say separated shoulder."
If Benedet is indeed dealing with a separated shoulder, he could miss significant time, in which case the Bears' depth at tackle is now in a very precarious spot.
Benedet had been playing the majority of the snaps at the position since Jones went down, with Ozzy Trapilo mixing in.
It goes without saying that now the Bears will have to rely on their second-round pick for more.
Chicago has been slowly ramping Trapilo up since he returned from his injury, but he has yet to take on a full workload in any game. He played 17 snaps in Week 6, 19 in Week 7, but then Trapilo didn't play any in Week 8.
If Benedet is indeed injured, the Bears are going to have to add another player at tackle, even if Trapilo is ready to be a full go.

title: Super Bowl Champion Labels Bengals as Contenders During 2026 Season
full_text:
After a 5-2 start, the Bengals have once again firmly established themselves among the best teams in the AFC. That said, the team still has plenty of flaws, but legends like Rob Gronkowski haven't stopped acknowledging them as a contender.
Gronkowski acknowledged the tackling issues and inability to run the football. However, he also clarified that Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins, Ja'Marr Chase, and the team's tight ends make the team a must-watch spectacle week in and week out.
"They're contenders, but they're also a little pretend a little bit because of the miscues, a lot of turnovers still, they can't run the ball, their defense can't tackle," Gronkowski said on the Gronk and Jules show. "But their offense is so fire, and we love watching them go, Tee Higgins, Ja'Marr Chase, Joe Burrow, they got a couple tight ends as well, you gotta tune in to the Cincinnati Bengals, they are a fireworks show basically every weekend."
Burrow set new career highs against the Titans in the team's 43-36 overtime win, totaling six touchdowns, while Higgins and Chase combined for 21 catches, 296 yards, and three touchdowns.
Both the defense and run game failed to impress against the lowly Titans, and neither has maintained the consistency that fans crave. However, the Bengals' offense can still beat any team in the league with its explosiveness.
Burrow and the team's other stars have consistently proven they can hold their own in shootouts over the last three years. The difference between now and those last three years, however, is the defense's ability to make a big play in a big moment. While the unit failed to make a play in key moments in the past, Dexter Lawrence changed that trend with a late-fourth-quarter sack of Cam Ward on Sunday to force overtime.
That moment, combined with a Boye Mafe strip-sack in the third quarter after Burrow threw an interception, shows this team can win high-scoring games after years of failure. Burrow himself confirmed this in his postgame press conference when he acknowledged that the Bengals win over the Titans has resulted in a loss in the past three seasons.
“We found a way to win today, we are 5-2, we lose that game the last three years.” Burrow said.
With the defense showing it can close out games on Sunday, the Bengals offense alone makes this team a true contender for the rest of the season.

title: Zac Taylor Comments on Team Health After Bengals Arrival in Spain
full_text:
Zac Taylor spoke to the media in Madrid, Spain, on Thursday morning, Cincinnati time.
The schedules are shifted in a big way for the Bengals, with all of their practices happening in the afternoon locally and in the morning on Eastern Standard Time.
Taylor gave the latest update on injuries to DJ Turner (heel) and Cedric Johnson (ankle).
According to The Enquirer's Kelsey Conway, Taylor noted a few players would be limited today but did not specify who. A good sign for Turner and Johnson's health that they weren't specificially ruled out.
Cincinnati is 5-2 this season in a close AFC North race with the Pittsburgh Steelers. They have had one of the best offenses in the NFL this season, and by far the best over the past month.
Taylor's unit is posting 0.216 EPA/play on offense since Week 5 began (first in the league by a wide margin). They are also first in success rate (58%).
Getting Turner and Johnson back on the field would be a boost for everyone, including that humming offense. Cornerback is a fluid position this week. Cincinnati still doesn't have Jalen Davis back from injured reserve yet.
"Thought he came in there and provided a lot of energy and competed and got Dax back outside," Taylor said about Josh Newton's repps in the game. "This time DJ is down, so now you got different grouping in there. And so that was a little bit of the plan going into the game, and then it evolves when you have an injury. But because those guys keep competing, and they're all ready when their numbers go on."
Cincinnati has practices today and tomorrow before the off day Saturday and show time on Sunday. Joe Burrow is healthy and ready to attack the Falcons as the most impactful passer in the league right now.
"We found a way to win today," Burrow said after beating the Titans. "We're 5-2. We've lost that game for the last three years. It's hard to win. You want to be great, snap in, snap out, but it's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That's what the NFL and getting better is. We'll continue to do that."
Cincinnati takes on the Falcons Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.

title: Multiple Outlets Believe Bengals Are Perfect Fit for Star Running Back Breece Hall
full_text:
It's a big weekend for the Cincinnati Bengals. Fresh off of their dramatic win over the Tennessee Titans, the Bengals are in Spain as they prepare for battle with the Atlanta Falcons.
A win over the Falcons on Sunday morning would put the Bengals in a prime position as the postseason race heats up. To compete with the rest of the top teams in the league, the Bengals could make a few additions to the roster prior to the trade deadline on November 10th.
There has been a lot of talk about this team adding a running back before the deadline, and a lot of fans are hoping that running back is Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor. However, the Bengals have now been linked to one of the more underrated backfield stars in the league.
B/R Gridiron has listed the Bengals as one of the next teams to make a potential blockbuster trade. The potential trade has the team landing New York Jets running back Breece Hall.
Hall has only appeared in three games this season, as he suffered a quad injury. However, NFL insider Ian Rapoport has revealed that Hall is good to go and should play this week.
There's no doubt that the veteran running back would elevate the backfield in Cincinnati. In his three games this season, Hall has rushed for 163 yards and one touchdown. Last season, the former second-round pick had his best season, rushing for over 1,000 yards for the first time in his career.
Bleacher report isn't the only one to mention the Bengals as a trade fit for Hall.
Jason Buechler of New York Jets On SI listed the Bengals as a trade fit for Hall.
"The Bengals have had one of the league's worst rushing attacks throughout Joe Burrow's career. They have trusted Chase Brown, but the fourth-year RB has managed only 340 rushing yards in seven games in 2027. Hall could be the perfect replacement for a Bengals team that has struggled to establish the run," Buechler wrote. "Hall makes an impact in both the rushing and passing game. That is exactly what Cincinnati needs. They are almost too dedicated to the pass, having had a bottom-five rushing offense over the past five years. Hall's ability to shine in both aspects of the offense may matter more to a team like Cincy than some think.
"Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals' offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals' second-round pick."
The Bengals would prefer to keep their second round pick. Would a third rounder get it done?
There shouldn't be any injury worries with Hall from an injury standpoint. He started at least 16 games for the Jets every single season.
Taylor is probably the dream addition still, and rightfully so, but if the Jets plan on moving players at the deadline, the Bengals shouldn't hesitate to reach out.
The biggest holdup in the Bengals making a move would have to be what the front office is willing to give up. If Taylor is the route they go, the Bengals may have to say goodbye to a second-round pick, and other assets. One would have to think the asking price for Hall would be lower.
Worrying about a discount shouldn't matter, but the front office has to take the future into account. This team can win with either running back discussed. As the trade deadline approaches, things are getting really interesting.

title: NFL Legends Make Case for Bengals to Trade for NFL All-Pro Before Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals are one of several teams "aggressively" pursuing Colts running back Jonathan Taylor according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. The Bengals should add Taylor for plenty of reasons, given his elite ability and their lack of run-game production. Future Hall of Famer and current CBS Sports announcer J.J. Watt chimed in on the fit for Taylor in Cincinnati and why it makes more sense than any other trade destination.
"I really do believe the Cincinnati Bengals make sense for a guy like him because of what their offense has in terms of the passing game and they just haven't been able to get going on the ground," Watt said on the CBS "Set Hut" show
Taylor has shined as one of the only bright spots of a subpar Colts roster in Indianapolis with 812 total yards and eight touchdowns on 169 touches. Meanwhile, Chase Brown and Samaje Perine have combined for 735 yards and three scores on 173 touches for the Bengals so far this season.
While those stats look similar, the difference is night and day in terms of who the bigger threat is on the field. Taylor is a threat to score every time he touches the ball as evidenced from his 40 touchdowns over the last three seasons.
Watt is not alone in believing the Bengals should target Taylor. Bengals legend Cris Collinsworth and his son Jac pointed out that the team is in a position to fix a glaring hole, similar to how the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons.
"With what Jeffery Simmons did in that game the other day for the Chicago Bears, who can match that, and can you do it with the guys that you currently have on your roster or are you now forced to do what the Bears did, which is to go out and fix that glaring hole on your football team," Collinsworth asked.
Collinsworth pointed to the Pro Football Focus grades of the Bengals' offensive line and the success of the new defensive additions as reasons to go all in and acquire Taylor.
"Dalton Risner is coming off an 80.0 grade, Amarius Mims coming off a 75.2 grade," Collinsworth said . "Now with the defense and Dexter Lawrence comes in and Boye Mafe comes in and the Bengals make moves that they've just never made, it's right now, it's this year, so go do it."
After sending the 10th overall pick to Dexter Lawrence this offseason and adding other pieces to the defense to complement the offense, the Bengals must now continue their all-in approach. Acquiring Taylor would potentially add another dynamic facet to the offense, similar to that of Colts Hall of Famer Edgerrin James.
James consistently created big plays for the Colts alongside Peyton Manning, Marvin Harrison, and Reggie Wayne in the early 2000s, helping field some of the greatest offenses the NFL has ever seen.
Taylor could create that same dynamic in Cincinnati in an offense featuring Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. The most important part of that dynamic is that the Bengals offense could efficiently run the ball and close out games down the stretch.
The trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10 at 4 pm ET.

title: Jessie Bates Admits He Still Thinks About Bengals Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals said goodbye to star safety Jessie Bate III for financial reasons a few years ago, and he still thinks about his opening stint in the NFL. Bates has been one of the best safeties to enter the league since 2010, and he sat down with FOX Sports' Jordan Schultz recently, touching on his time with the Bengals.
If the Falcons want to deal, maybe Bates can become a Bengal again via trade. Cincinnati could use another playmaker at the safety position.
He plays Cincinnati in Madrid on Nov. 9.
"I mean, heck yeah, man! They had to pay the offense, man. They had to get those playmakers, those one-in-a-lifetime type of talent," Bates said to Schultz about the what-if. "I love those dudes, and we had a great run. A couple times at the Super Bowl, and those times were some of the greatest times of my life. So I understood. That's part of the business. Sometimes you can't fit everybody in that cap number. That number is a little higher nowadays than it was back then around COVID, so it's all a blessing, man. It's part of the journey, and I was there for five years. That place has a special part in my heart for sure."
Since leaving the Bengals, Bates hasn't fallen off one bit; in fact, he's gotten better. The veteran is posting an 84.1 Pro Football Focus grade this season and has been at 80-plus in three of his four Falcons seasons.
The 2026 grade ranks second among qualified safeties (min. 280 snaps) to go along with three pass breakups, three forced fumbles and one interception not even midway through the season.
He would've more than lived up to a new deal with Cincinnati, and they could've made the money work, but things just didn't play out that way.
Eventually, they had to sign Bryan Cook this past offseason to finally bring that position to a potentially palatable level. Alas, Cook's regressed in 2026 due to nagging injury or other reasons.
He's posted a career-low 44.7 PFF grade so far in Cincinnati.
"If I could tell any other young guys that come in that building, it's definitely a business. And as much as the performance matters as well. The type of person you are, the character that you have in that locker room, the way you carry yourself definitely matters as well," Bates said.
Bates only has a $7.23 million cap hit on an expiring deal this season and could really help the Bengals in pursuit of another Super Bowl if Atlanta is willing to deal him.

title: Tee Higgins Picks Up First Career NFL Award Following Huge Outing Against Titans
full_text:
Tee Higgins' fantastic 2026 season continued with his first AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. The Bengals star had never won the honor until posting 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns this past weekend in a 43-36 win over Tennessee.
He's been one of the most efficient receivers in the NFL this season, ranking third among all qualified receivers in yards per route run behind Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Zay Flowers.
Higgins ranks second in the league with 726 receiving yards and 13th in touchdowns (four).
It marks the fourth Bengals player this season to earn a weekly recognition, following Evan McPherson (Special Teams, Week 1), Joe Burrow (Offensive, Week 7), a nd Ryan Rehkow (Special Teams, Week 7).
"Yeah, don't overthink it. Just keep throwing the ball and let those guys get some chunk plays," Zac Taylor said about feeding Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in the Titans shootout. "There were a lot of chunk plays, and you can feel a little bit when you have someone on your heels. We were starting to get a lot of momentum in the passing game. A lot of them were short throws, and those guys turned them into bigger plays."
Higgins was hyped about the performance in the Bengals' locker room.
"That just shows you what we've been preaching all season, all (training) camp. Never quit, always fight to the end, no matter what the outcome may be. Let's make sure we always fight to the end," Higgins said about the showing. "Big time players make big time plays in big time moments, and we were able to do that today. I say that about the three of us — big time players make those big time plays in big time moments. We were able to do that today."
The 27-year-old star has lived up to his contract extension and then some for the Bengals over the past year, and now he finally gets some hardware to show for it.
"Great team win. Most importantly, that was a great team win. Obviously, it didn't go how we wanted, but at the end of the day, we didn't have any quit in us and fought to the end and won," Higgins declared.
Cincinnati is hoping to get another (or multiple again) Player of the Week performance(s) from its roster on Sunday morning in the Spain battle against Atlanta.

title: Bengals' Trade Deadline Targets Could Include Veteran RB, Talented LB
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make some upgrades to their roster if they want to emerge as one of the best teams in the league. They need to add to a few spots on defense, but on offense, adding another running back would be a big move. They could target a huge player like Jonathan Taylor, but that seems more like a dream than reality.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently listed the Bengals as one of the best fits in a deal for Tampa Bay Buccaneers veteran running back Kenneth Gainwell.
"Gainwell left the Steelers in free agency to sign a two-year, $14 million deal with the Bucs. He has $3 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so an acquiring team would be committing some money next season," Popper wrote. "They could, in theory, cut Gainwell and just wear that as dead money. The Bucs would not take on any dead money in 2027 if they traded Gainwell, who is a very effective receiver and potential third-down back in a rotation."
Gainwell was tremendous for the Pittsburgh Steelers last season, but he hasn't been given the same opportunities in Tampa Bay. He would be a huge addition to a Bengals running back room that features Chase Brown without a clear No. 2 running back.
But they need to add talent to other places on their roster, including on the defensive side of the football. Popper also listed the Bengals as one of the best fits for outside linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson.
"Chaisson signed a one-year, $11 million deal with the Commanders in free agency. Through six weeks, he was tied for the team lead with 17 pressures," Popper wrote. "Chaisson is a capable pass rusher. He set a career high with 74 pressures last season for the Patriots. He is always going to be somewhat of a liability against the run. He is an option for a team looking for situational pass-rush juice."
This could help the Bengals quite a bit because Chaisson is a good option, but it's not the biggest need in the world. The Bengals have seen quite a bit of production from edge rushers like Cashius Howell and Boye Mafe, among others. Given the fact that Shemar Stewart was recently a healthy scratch, the Bengals could be looking to add a different edge rusher to their roster.
Chaisson has 2.5 sacks in six games this year. He had 7.5 sacks last season as a member of the New England Patriots defense.

title: Joe Burrow Rocks Fun Outfit As Bengals Arrive in Spain For International Battle Against Atlanta
full_text:
The Bengals flew to Madrid, Spain, on Wednesday as the team landed in town for their Sunday morning 9:30 a.m. EST game against the Atlanta Falcons.
Joe Burrow rocked a Pokémon Pikachu outfit onto the plane, and the travel seemingly went smoothly as the team hits the town for some fun today before normal practice schedules on Thursday and Friday.
"It speeds up the earlier part of your week, so that we can travel on Tuesday night. It changes your days a little bit," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the changes this week. "For the players, it doesn't make it more taxing. It's a little more taxing on the coaches. But it's like playing on a Monday night and having to turn around on a short week. Nothing we haven't had to do before — nothing to complain about. It just changes the structure of how you'll meet."
Cincinnati has already gone through the work it normally does on Wednesdays this week and now just needs to get adjusted to the new timings.
They are going through morning practice schedules on Cincinnati time, happening in the afternoon across the pond.
"Tomorrow we'll get a day ahead here," Taylor said on Monday. "So instead of doing a Wednesday practice, we'll do Tuesday afternoon practice. We're gonna be there Wednesday when we get there. It's just about acclimation for our players, and then Thursday and Friday will be normal, so we'll be practicing as normal. We'll follow a normal Thursday and Friday routine. Obviously, bus travel and stuff like that to the practice field changes a little bit of our timeline, but that's no big deal.
"And then Saturday we'll do a walk through the stadium. And walk-throughs at international stadiums, you're not usually allowed to be in the endzone with the logo paint, so it's a little bit of a half-speed walk-through. But Atlanta, they're the home team, so they get to go first."

title: Bengals Called Best Fit in Trade for Jets Disgruntled Pro Bowl CB
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals need to make one or two more additions to their defense if they want to emerge as one of the Super Bowl favorites this season. They have quite a bit of talent on that side of the ball, but they could still use some upgrades.
The Bengals need to add help at linebacker and at cornerback, though adding a cornerback might be the easier route, considering how many of them are expected to be available at the trade deadline.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently listed the Bengals as one of the best fits in a potential trade for New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright. Wright hasn't played for the Jets' defense this year after being named a Pro Bowler last season.
"The Jets signed Wright to a one-year deal in free agency, and he has yet to play a defensive snap this season for coach Aaron Glenn. Wright should be a trade candidate even if the Jets win games over the next three weeks," Popper wrote. "He had five picks playing for the Chicago Bears in 2025. Wright lacks some burst and change-of-direction ability. But his ball production last season was very impressive. At 6-foot-4, he has receiver-like skills in 50-50 situations."
Wright was a Pro Bowl cornerback with five interceptions a year ago. Now, he's not playing for the Jets. During this offseason, this seemed like a huge signing for New York, but it hasn't proven to be that way. Now it seems like Wright is disgruntled and wants out of New York.
This would be a risky deal for the Bengals, as there's likely a good reason or two that he isn't making an impact in New York. But it would likely only cost a Day 3 pick swap in the NFL Draft to bring him to Cincinnati. Could the Bengals afford to swap a sixth-round pick for a seventh-round pick and a cornerback like Wright? The answer to that question should be yes.
Still, if there are big concerns following Wright that the national media isn't aware of, the Bengals will likely stay away from him. Either way, he's a name to watch ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Why Shedeur Sanders' Expected Start Comes at the Perfect Time
full_text:
Two years ago, Shedeur Sanders expanded his skill set beyond the football field and released a song called “Perfect Timing.”
Now, as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol, the second-year quarterback is gearing up to make his first start of the 2026 season, and the timing couldn’t be more in his – and in the Browns’ – favor.
Here’s three reasons why Sanders getting the Week 9 nod comes at a pretty much the perfect time :
During his media availability on Wednesday afternoon , Sanders was asked what he’s seen from the Saints' defense.
“Um, yeah, I've seen a lot," he answered. "When I smile, just know that means… something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing.”
It seems Sanders doesn’t see Saints' defensive coordinator, Brandon Staley’s, unit as much of a threat.
And, the numbers don’t disagree with the quarterback’s (lack of) thoughts.
The Saints’ total defense ranks 28th overall in the league, giving up 372.7 yards per game and allowing 22 touchdowns so far this year. Its passing defense ranks 23rd overall, allowing 233.3 yards per game, and it doesn’t bring a lot of pressure up front.
New Orleans has also been pretty easy to score on this season. According to Pro Football Reference, 46.8% of the Saints’ defensive drives have ended in an offensive score, the second-highest among all 32 teams.
While the Saints aren’t the worst defense in the league, they’re far from the best – something that could make Sanders’ job a little easier on Sunday.
While it’s been reported that the Browns have no interest in trading Sanders by the November 10 deadline, it’s no secret there’s a lot of uncertainty in the future of Cleveland’s quarterback room.
When Watson was named the starter this offseason, it sent a clear message: Sanders is not the answer to the Browns’ struggles. At least not yet.
While Watson is doing just enough to keep the Browns a competitive team, he isn’t a top quarterback. During his time in Cleveland, he has yet to prove he’s the long-term solution. So who is?
Sanders has yet to prove it, either, despite flashes of his abilities when he took over under center last season.
Todd Monken, though, is excited to see what his young quarterback does with this week’s opportunity.
“He’s done his work,” Monken said. “All he’s done is be diligent and ask great questions. In every meeting, he’s dialed in.”
When it comes to the trade deadline, the Browns have some decisions to make.
This weekend could help solidify Sanders’ spot in the quarterback room, especially with Dillon Gabriel no longer on injured reserve.
After beating Pittsburgh in primetime the first time around, the Steelers got revenge on their home field to claim the top spot in the AFC North.
It was a tough outing for Watson, who was sacked eight times. He’s the most-sacked quarterback in the league so far this year.
The Browns need a morale boost, and it potentially coming from a different quarterback could be beneficial.
Cleveland has a stretch of winnable games ahead. After the Saints, the team hosts the 2-5 Texans, then the 4-4 Raiders after a bye week.
If Sanders wants to prove himself to his team and to Cleveland fans, starting with a win against New Orleans might just be the way to do that. Getting the Browns back on track after losing to their rival is the perfect opportunity to show he still has something to offer to the team that drafted him.
A Northeast Ohio native, Rachel grew up following all things Cleveland sports. She has experience in broadcast and digital media and graduated from West Virginia University with a degree in sports media.

title: Browns Have 4 Young Players Who Deserve More Playing Time as Season Hits Halfway Point
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns season hits the half way point and they sit as the eighth seed in the AFC at 5-3. They only play three more games against teams over .500 and have a chance to make a push for the playoffs. The team has arrived sooner than anyone thought because their roster is filled with rookies and second-year players.
Almost 30 percent of the game-day roster is composed of players from the last two draft classes. Eight such players are starters that have heavily contributed to winning. Carson Schwesinger was Defensive Rookie of the Year last season and KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston are competing for Offensive Rookie of the Year this season.
The young players have stepped up on both sides of the ball, but these non-starters need to get more playing time in the second half of the season to make the playoffs.
Sampson started the season as the backup running back to Quinshon Judkins, but got hurt in the first game. He returned in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans and showed off his speed by averaging 7.5 yards per rush and 10.7 yards per reception in the win. Sampson only got one carry for seven yards in last week’s blow-out loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The offense has struggled to run the ball all season and Sampson should be given more opportunities to find a spark. He can run on the outside and catch screen passes to keep the defense on its toes. The offense is night and day when he touches the ball.
The second-year receiver only has five catches this season for 86 yards. He got most of his playing time at the beginning of the season when Jerry Jeudy struggled and KC Concepcion left a game with a concussion. Jeudy improved and Concepcion did not miss any other time, so Bond got pushed to the sideline.
The speedster can take the top off of the defense and open up the middle of the field for Concepcion and Boston. He had a couple of bad drops in their loss against the New York Jets, but the weather conditions made things difficult. If Shedeur Sanders starts for the Browns , then Bond should get more playing time as they had chemistry last season and Sanders throws a better deep ball than Watson.
Huntington has gotten plenty of playing time and has played really well by stacking up 3.5 sacks. He anchored the middle of the defensive line when Mason Graham and Michael Hall Jr. were out with injury. Both players returned to the lineup and Huntington’s snaps will decrease.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. still look like they are playing injured and Huntington should start over Hall Jr. He has been providing pressure over the center and has gotten in the backfield to help stop the run. The defensive line needs him to help them slow down the rushing attack, which they have struggled to do this season.
The strong safety out of the University of Toledo was considered a “steal” in the second round of the NFL draft. His playing time has steadily been increasing and he has shown why. McNeil-Warren has laid some big hits on running backs and helped them stop the Titans at the goal line. He is behind Grand Delpit on the depth chart.
Ronnie Hickman has started at free safety and there have been a couple of communication breakdowns in the secondary. McNeil-Warren’s college film suggests he can play in the middle of the field and read the offense. He should get more opportunities to be a ball hawk in the secondary.
The young players are contributing up and down the roster and if the Browns wish to play their way into the playoffs, then these four players should be utilized more in the second half.
