title: Browns QB Trade Value Should Improve After Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
One by one, quarterbacks keep getting plucked off the trade block.
On Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Arizona Cardinals joined the fun by trading veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Brissett will look to bolster the Ravens' QB room following a wave of injuries to both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.
But while the move not only puts a band-aid on an AFC North squad that is still in contention to make a run for the top spot, it also puts the Cleveland Browns in a position to reevaluate the group they have on the roster.
With four quarterbacks on staff, a group that includes two second-year signal callers and a rookie, the Browns will be able to skew the market a bit as one of the last remaining teams left with depth at the position.
If any other team needs to add an extra arm to their roster at the deadline , Cleveland is going to likely be on the call list.
The Browns have rolled out controversial quarterback Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season.
However, in the early morning hours on Wednesday , that storyline hit a roadblock.
Second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders was thrust into the spotlight after Watson entered concussion protocol, with the 24-year-old now being projected to start Sunday's game for the Browns against the New Orleans Saints. This would be Watson's first missed game of the season.
With Sanders not expected to be the long-term starter, though, especially with this injury pretty much being a waiting game, Sunday could ultimately serve as a test to see if any teams in need of a quarterback could make Sanders their No. 1.
It would be surprising to not see any scouts in New Orleans, especially with the deadline approaching.
There's also an opportunity for both Gabriel's and Green's values to grow as well, even without taking the field this season. Both being so young and raw allows them to be molded into something that fits a specific team's system, particularly if they believe a 2026 playoff spot is a lost cause.
That same case can be made for Sanders; he just has a bit more experience on the gridiron under his belt than the other two.
Quarterbacks across the board, not just the Browns', probably saw a jump of roughly a pick's worth of trade value on Wednesday following the Brissett trade. For example, if Gabriel were valued as a fifth-round pick before the last few weeks, he has likely jumped up to fourth-round status, especially with very few quarterbacks still available on the open market.
With how many quarterbacks have been injured this season, including the likes of Seattle's Sam Darnold, the Eagles' Jalen Hurts, Jackson and many more, teams have to be readier than ever to embody that next-man-up mentality.
A season can't just fall off the rails completely after a quarterback goes down.
Over the next few days, it will be interesting to watch and see how the market continues to move, and values change with the trade deadline approaching.
And if one of Cleveland's four active quarterbacks on the 53-man roster is forced to put on a new jersey.

title: Shedeur Sanders Backs Deshaun Watson Ahead of Potential Start Against Saints
full_text:
Shedeur Sanders could have used Wednesday’s media session to explain how he might change the Cleveland Browns’ offense. Instead, he made a point of defending the quarterback he could replace this week.
With Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol and Sanders potentially in line to start against the New Orleans Saints, the second-year quarterback pushed back when asked how he could get Cleveland’s offense going earlier in games.
“Just my job. I don’t think it been bad . How many wins we got? It can’t be that bad, you know,” Sanders said. “I don’t want to just come in here and just try to discredit, you know, what Deshaun done and everything he done.”
The Browns enter the matchup at 5–3, and Sanders sees his responsibility as helping the team continue winning. He wasn’t interested in making his case at Watson’s expense, choosing instead to focus on the opportunity in front of him.
“That don’t make me feel good as a person,” Sanders said. “I think it’s just doing my job, not doing too much, doing what I have to do.”
According to the team’s injury statement, Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday’s game against Pittsburgh. He passed his initial evaluation and subsequent checks after the game and Monday morning before reporting Tuesday that symptoms began Monday night.
Head coach Todd Monken confirmed Watson’s placement in concussion protocol. Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported Wednesday that the expectation around Browns headquarters was that Sanders would start against New Orleans, although Monken had not ruled Watson out.
Sanders said he learned of the possibility at the same time reporters did. Asked about his preparation, he offered a straightforward response.
“The same way how I’ve been preparing every week. No different.”
Shedeur emphasized the relationships already established inside the locker room when asked about working with the offensive line. He suggested the adjustment appeared more complicated to people outside the building than it did to the players themselves.
“Deshaun led us this far and it’s unfortunate he wasn’t able to go out there, you know, but on my end, you know, I just got to step up for the quarterback room, for the team and do what I have to do,” Sanders said.
His description of what the offense needs from him was equally direct. "Just go out there and trust my teammates, trust the game plan and do everything I can...I ain’t really trying to ride the roller coaster life, you know, I like to keep everything even,” said Shedeur.

title: What This Browns Veteran Had To Say About Shedeur Sanders' Opportunity To Start Sunday
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns cannot escape the injury bug.
And ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the New Orleans Saints, the offense may look completely different.
On Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Browns announced a shocking update on quarterback Deshaun Watson, revealing the 31-year-old signal caller was in concussion protocol. He took a pretty nasty hit early in the Browns' loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers this past weekend, but cleared any concerns both during the game and on Monday.
"During the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit. The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a game-day concussion evaluation," the Browns' press release read. "Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns’ next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team’s medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times, he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared.
"On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol."
Fortunately, many of Cleveland's leaders spoke out in support of backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, whom the Browns may have to turn to for Sunday's road game against the New Orleans Saints.
Browns star cornerback Denzel Ward was one of the first players to Sanders' praise, speaking to media in the late morning hours on Wednesday.
Browns CB Denzel Ward on Shedeur Sanders possibly making his first start of the season: “I know he’s ready.” pic.twitter.com/LjFZIgTYN2
"We've got all the confidence in Shedeur," Ward began. "We know he will be ready to play once he is out there, so, you know, we always offer our support when needed, but we know he is ready."
Getting that extra confidence boost from a leader like Ward should go a long way for Sanders, especially if he is given the opportunity to make his first start of the 2026 season.
During his rookie campaign in 2025, the 24-year-old started seven games, throwing for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns on 212 passing attempts. He also rushed 21 times for 169 yards and one touchdown, adding a bit of versatility to his game.
While he seemingly did enough to earn the starting job in 2026, Watson's offseason surge pushed him to the top of the depth chart.
Fortunately, Sanders hasn't been completely out of the picture. He has still had the opportunity to serve as the No. 2, sitting and learning behind Watson , all while getting valuable reps in practice.
Such an experience has allowed him to welcome the challenge that sits ahead of him heading into this weekend.
"...Deshaun led us this far and it is unfortunate he wasn't able to go out there [this week]," Sanders said. "But on my end, I just got to step up for the quarterback room, for the team and do what I have to do."
With Ward's endorsement, the rest of the team rallying around him and a head full of confidence, Sanders has the perfect storm following him into his first potential start of the 2026 season.
For now, the focus will be on giving him first-team reps and preparing for a weekend without Watson.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury News Opens Door for Shedeur Sanders
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns dropped a bombshell on social media Wednesday morning. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol after a hit sustained during the first quarter of the Browns-Steelers game on Sunday:
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
Watson began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and reported them to the medical staff Tuesday morning, when he was placed in concussion protocol . An unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant cleared Watson to return during Sunday’s game. He also passed evaluations after the game and on Monday morning.
Watson has helped the Browns reach 5-3, engineering a game-winning drive in each of their five victories. He has 1,806 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions this season. This start, while unexpected, had many believing that Watson would remain the starter for the season, barring injury.
Unfortunately for Watson, that injury came.
Watson’s injury could open the door for backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders to show his capabilities once again. Sanders made seven starts as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.
some of Shedeur Sanders best throws vs. the Titans from the All-22 tape. #Browns The first ball to Fannin with a DE barreling down in his face is just silly... pic.twitter.com/zsZSNHxgbT
While it wasn’t all pretty, Sanders did show flashes of potential, specifically in the Browns’ matchup against the Titans in 2025. In that game, Sanders threw for 364 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding a rushing touchdown. Many assumed the Browns would continue to start Sanders into the 2026 season, but ultimately that was not the case.
The Browns held a highly publicized quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during training camp for the 2026 season. Sanders ultimately lost the battle to the veteran Watson, but a comment Browns head coach Todd Monken made during OTAs on June 3 still stands out today:
#Browns HC Todd Monken said he has not yet decided who will start at quarterback between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, nor has he finalized the offensive line heading into training camp. "I think both quarterbacks have played well enough. We really haven't been in pads,… pic.twitter.com/LFLUlv99mL
Todd Monken said, “But I’m fired up by the quarterbacks. I'll tell you, we got two starting-level quarterbacks. We really do.” Now, Sanders has the opportunity to prove his head coach right.
Sanders has not been confirmed as the starter against the Saints, as Watson could still clear concussion protocol before Sunday. Sanders will take the first-team practice reps Wednesday as Cleveland prepares for the possibility of playing without Watson.
The question now, if Sanders gets the start, is whether he can seize his opportunity. If Sanders performs better than Watson has to start the season, it may be difficult for the Browns to turn back to the veteran. However, Sanders must avoid holding the ball too long. That issue surfaced against Pittsburgh, contributing to two penalties for ineligible players downfield on screen passes.
If those struggles resurface, the Browns could quickly return to Watson, who has led five game-winning drives this season.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: A Blockbuster Trade the Browns Could Make to Completely Change the Franchise
full_text:
Rumors have begun to run wild around the NFL about the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.
After an unprecedented 0-7 start to the season, the Chargers may be enticed by the right offer to blow up the entire operation and go into rebuild mode.
With these rumors going around, some people, including ESPN Cleveland, have called for the Cleveland Browns to reach out and potentially make an offer for the former Oregon Duck.
Here are some of the pros and cons to a potential Justin Herbert trade.
. @BenjaminSolak lists the 3 teams that should try and trade for Justin Herbert: - Vikings - Jets - The Cleveland Browns 👀👀👀 Should the Browns explore a Herbert trade? pic.twitter.com/zpMT9W4yx9
In 2022, the Browns gave up pretty much their entire future to go out and trade for Deshaun Watson. We all know how that went before 2026 began.
Now, Watson is 31 years old and in the final year of his contract. If the Browns want to move on from Watson and go after Herbert, it would take another gigantic package.
While Herbert doesn't have legal issues off the field, his play on the field is still questionable. While some argue it's the poor system he's playing in, or the tough teams he's facing, Herbert still leads the NFL with 10 interceptions.
All in all, the move seems to be too risky for the Browns to make, especially with a potentially loaded 2027 rookie quarterback class.
While we are still looking back to the Deshaun Watson trade, let's not forget the slim amount of hope Cleveland fans had right when the trade went down.
If the Browns got Herbert, they would most likely have their best quarterback since Baker Mayfield. At times, it is easy to say Herbert is far better than Mayfield as well.
With the second-youngest team in the NFL, along with the back-to-back incredible draft classes, Herbert would come in surrounded by an incredibly talented team.
Before 2026, many argued that the Browns were a quarterback away from being a serious contender. Maybe Cleveland looks at Herbert as their "missing piece"?
While it is very unrealistic that the Browns will go make a move for Madison Beer's fiancé, there is another world of possibilities people are overlooking if the quarterback gets moved to another team.
Like I said, Moving Justin Herbert is the initial indicator that the Chargers are going into rebuild mode.
With that being said, the Browns' biggest need by far at the moment is help on that offensive line. Of course, it would be pricey, but if the Chargers are willing to move their quarterback, who's to say they wouldn't trade away guys like Joe Alt or Rashawn Slater?
If anything, the Browns should be hoping the Chargers are willing to trade Justin Herbert. Maybe then they could take a swing at a big trade, yet not for the guy you would have first thought of.

title: Browns' Loss to Steelers Confirms One Undeniable Truth About Deshaun Watson
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns came crashing back to Earth, courtesy of a 27-6 spanking by the Pittsburgh Steelers at Accrisure Stadium on Sunday, a few things became crystal clear regarding the club and its now 5-3 record start to the regular season.
The reasons for the team’s second loss in four weeks can be traced to many things. Among them, a multitude of flags iuncluding two taunting penalties while trailing by 21 points, a mesmerizing incapability to establish the run game, and a general lack of pressure on Pittsburgh's offense .
However, one thing really stood out above all else as the Browns now attempt to gather themselves for a third road trip in as many weeks: Deshaun Watson cannot be the team’s quarterback in 2027 and beyond.
Listen, everyone can reasonably accept that Cleveland’s latest rebuild endeavour might take more than one year after the club replaced head coach Kevin Stefanski with Todd Monken, even if the Browns have hit multiple home runs on two straight draft classes.
But one thing has become evident after Week 8’s disappointing outing , one that included eight sacks on Watson: the Browns will need another quarterback to complete this comeback.
Now, the offensive line was going to be a work in progress throughout the year. Watson wasn’t. At least that’s what the team has been telling us repeatedly since he was inserted into a two-way competition for the starting job, and then again when he was designated winner of said competition over Shedeur Sanders.
Watson’s experience would help mitigate some of the issues that naturally arise on a budding young team. And an offensive line with five new starters, including two rookies playing out of their most recent college spots was going to need all the help it could get.
It’s getting zilch out of Watson.
Because Watson plays the position in a similar way as he does his pressers, he lacks general awareness of what’s going on around him. That commonly leads to dropbacks out of the shotgun where Watson ends up with 11 to 13 yards of depth, which in turn leads to the tackles getting beat constantly.
Watch Tytus Howard throw up his arms several times out of frustration. Watson takes a 7-step drop out of the shotgun. At the top of his drop he is 13 yards from the line of scrimmage. It's impossible to block the edges when a QB does this. pic.twitter.com/uyZaBuMwL5
Out of Watson’s eight sacks on Sunday , at least five of them came on plays where Watson’s deep dropback contributed to the outcome. On at least three of those sacks, he had more than 2.5 seconds to get rid of the ball, and he didn’t.
Another consequence of Watson’s deep dropbacks is that tackles are then forced to hold defenders in order to avoid a hit on the passer. That happened at least a couple of times against Pittsburgh on Sunday.
And to make things worse, Watson’s tendency to drop back so deep is so easily detectable, that you could see the Steelers’ edge rushers pinning their ears back and targeting that range around 10 yards behind the line of scrimmage because they knew that’s where they would find the quarterback.
Watson didn’t actually trim his dropback and speed up his delivery until about six minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. Even so, he was still sacked a couple more times, with Watson feeling outside pressure and then stepping into the sack on the inside.
But Watson’s issues go further than just making life miserable for his tackles. He also had two grossly overthrown passes, two one-hoppers, and two passes batted down at the line of scrimmage as part of a performance that did, however, manage to cover up some of the blunders with plenty of garbage-time yards.
As much as Browns fans might want to see the team make a splash before the trade deadline, options aren’t really that great out there . Having said that, there are several names that could be had that are currently playing better than Watson, with Kirk Cousins at the top of that list.
Nonetheless, that’s not a long-term solution either, so there’s a good chance the Browns will ride 2026 out with Watson and his plethora of sacks, and then look to the draft to pick out a passer from a once very promising class that’s now shrinking on a weekly basis.
Cleveland wanted an experienced passer capable of bringing along all the young offensive talent on the roster slowly. Instead, Watson turned into a sack magnet. Now, the Browns should take a different approach, one where a young and talented quarterback gets to grow alongside the rest of the offensive pieces already in place.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Could Be Forced to Abandon Their Trade Deadline Plans After Steelers Loss
full_text:
Heading into their week eight matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers , the Cleveland Browns had in mind an idea for the upcoming trade deadline.
After finally having a winning season, Cleveland can finally be buyers at this stage of the season. Despite the loss, this status of "buyers" remains the same. However, the players they need to go after have dramatically changed.
Before facing their rivals, many rumors were swirling about the Browns going after another pass rusher to bolster the defensive line.
Guys like Khalil Mack and YaYa Diaby were being thrown around as potential targets.
Especially with the horrible start to Jared Verse's Browns career statistically, Cleveland really could still use a guy to help take some of that pressure off the 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year.
However, there is another stat that stands out far more than all the rest, and it shows why another position desperately needs more attention.
Quite literally doing a 180 to the other side of the ball, the Browns' offensive line has completely failed so far this season.
Even after going out and getting five new starters, finding potential great future options in the draft with Spencer Fano and Austin Barber, trading for Tytus Howard, and spending big bucks on Zion Johnson and Elgton Jenkins, the unit still needs a load of work.
The reason? Deshaun Watson has been sacked 33 times this season in eight games.
Last game alone, Pittsburgh was able to ruin the Browns' offense after dropping Watson eight times.
Not only does that 33 sacks allowed lead the entire NFL, but the Carolina Panthers, who rank 31st, have allowed 10 fewer sacks.
Clearly, Cleveland needs to spend some money to improve the guys up front. Who knows, maybe it wouldn't take too much to go after a guy like Landon Dickerson from Philadelphia.
Other wide receiver names continue to come up in connection to the trade deadline: Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., Indianapolis’ Josh Downs, Minnesota’s Jauan Jennings, Cleveland’s Jerry Jeudy, Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley. But the Jets won’t trade Wilson by next Tuesday. https://t.co/F2ONImsqPX
So the issue has been addressed, and we know what Cleveland needs to do. But how will they do it?
The Browns have 11 total picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. This includes multiple late-round picks, but also two that come in the first round.
Who is to say Cleveland doesn't go after a top lineman who is still in the early stages of his career? That way, if they do use a first-round pick, they can almost "draft early" with a guy who can help out this season and for years to come.
Now let's say Andrew Berry does not want to use a first-round pick to trade for a lineman. What else do the Browns have to offer?
If there's been a player whose name has been tossed around in trade talks since training camp, its been Jerry Jeudy.
Some teams that come to mind that are trying to potentially get wide receiver help for their quarterback are the Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams, and Washington Commanders.
Going forward, a change simply has to be made. Unfortunately for the Browns, it also doesn't look like that change will be able to be made internally.
If Cleveland seriously wants a chance to push for their first-ever AFC North title and first playoff appearance since 2023, they will need to make a move for at least one offensive lineman in the coming weeks.

title: Browns' Playoff Hopes Took a Major Hit, but Their Next Move Could Change Everything
full_text:
After the loss in Pittsburgh, the Cleveland Browns dropped to third in the AFC North and out of the playoff picture altogether in the conference. They sit at eighth in the AFC and have to get back on the winning track in order to keep pace. The Browns only play three games against teams over .500 the rest of the season.
The offense has been a black hole for the team in the first three quarters. Their ineffectiveness is driven by their i nability to run the ball and protect the quarterback . Watson leads the entire NFL in getting sacked and Quinshon Judkins is on pace for fewer yards than in his injury-shortened season last year.  Trading for help on the offense may be able to save their season.
The offensive line has struggled to both run and pass block . Harold Fannin Jr. has had to play closer to the line of scrimmage to help with blocking, which has resulted in fewer touches for him. In Pittsburgh, he had his best receiving game of the season and looked unstoppable as a pass catcher, but it came with a cost as Watson got sacked eight times and the running game was non-existent.
The Browns can save their offense by trading for a tight end that can block. Fannin Jr. can then be utilized to the best of his skill set, and the new tight end can play closer to the line of scrimmage to help the anemic line. There is a great fit at the position that could be on the trade block.
The 6’5, 260-pound tight end could be available, as the Colts have already traded away two major pieces and got throttled last week in Jacksonville. He is the Colts’ best blocking tight end and is on the last year of his contract. Trading for him would not cost any meaningful assets for the Browns and the transition should be smooth as his primary objective would be to block.
He was drafted in the sixth round out of Youngstown State. Ogletree only has three catches this season and 25 in his career. He has been the blocking tight end for star running back Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones has been sacked 11 fewer times than Watson.
On obvious passing downs, Fannin can line up on the outside and become a pure pass catcher. Ogletree can be used as a true blocking tight end. When Fannin has played downfield, the Browns have used running backs to try and provide extra protection. That strategy has not worked, and they need a bigger body to handle that duty.
Fannin is a key factor in the offense , as he can turn a short gain into a large one with his ability to break tackles. He is too fast and elusive to be covered by linebackers and too strong to be covered by a slot corner. Any other player trying to cover Fannin would benefit KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
Ogletree can also be used to slip out of the backfield on obvious passing downs. The Browns ran a play with Blake Whiteheart on their game-winning drive against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where the defense ignored him, thinking that he was only going to be used as a blocker, and he slipped out for an uncontested touchdown.
Although the Browns got defeated handedly in Pittsburgh, the offense is not too far off. The last half of the schedule lends them to be able to stack wins and save their playoff hopes. A non-consequential trade for Ogletree can help them fix their biggest problems down the stretch.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Dallas Cowboys vs. Indianapolis Colts: 3 Keys to Victory in Week 9
full_text:
After another disheartening loss , the Dallas Cowboys enter this weekend hoping to get back on track as they visit the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9.
Indianapolis is in full-on sale mode after trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, but as we saw in Week 8 , there’s no such thing as a sure win for this Cowboys team. For that reason, head coach Brian Schottenheimer needs to ensure his team comes into this game focused and ready, otherwise things could really get crazy in Big D.
That said, here’s a look at three key areas that Schottenheimer and the Cowboys must focus on to avoid another loss in Week 9.
With Alec Pierce out injured, the Colts don’t have a dominant passing game. That means they’re going to try and lean on their biggest strength, which is running the ball with Jonathan Taylor. Dallas enters the week with the worst run defense in the league , having just been carved up by the Cardinals. Arizona had 202 yards on the ground while averaging 7.5 yards per attempt.
Tyler Allgeier led the way with 147 yards on 11 attempts. If Dallas doesn’t clean up its tackling, Taylor is going to have a field day. That’s why the No. 1 focus on defense has to be slowing him down. If the Colts can beat them with the pass, so be it. But the Cowboys can’t make it easy on them by allowing Taylor to dictate the flow of the game.
Javonte Williams hasn’t been the same player we saw a year ago, entering Week 9 averaging just 3.9 yards per carry. He’s still shown flashes but defenses have clearly figured out how to slow him down. That’s why Dallas needs to switch things up and get Tyler Goodson involved as well against the Colts.
Indianapolis is surrendering 4.9 yards per rushing attempt and while it might be tempting to just feed Williams against them, Goodson offers a speed burst that Williams simply doesn’t possess. Forcing the Colts to worry about the bruising back while also sprinkling in someone who can break a long run is exactly the spark this offense needs. And this is the perfect week to get a solid timeshare figured out.
Easily the most confusing thing about Dallas this season (and there have been a lot of confusing things) is the complete inability to get George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb going at the same time. Brian Schottenheimer claims to be an elite play caller , yet he’s absolutely stumped when it comes to figuring out how to utilize two elite wide receivers. It’s gotten so bad that Brevyn Spann-Ford finished with more targets than Pickens in Week 8 while Ryan Flournoy had the same number of targets as Pickens.
Every play caller in the NFL dreams of having wideouts as talented as Dallas, and here we are entering Week 9 still saying Schottenheimer needs to get both involved. And once again, a key to victory for the Cowboys is getting Pickens involved early, which will open everything up for the entire offense.

title: Everything Dallas Cowboys Have to Fear About Indianapolis Colts in Week 9
full_text:
There are few teams in the NFL more eager to get back on the field in Week 9 than the Dallas Cowboys.
That's because Dallas is coming off a historically bad loss at the hands of the Arizona Cardinals, who mounted an incredible comeback before winning in overtime.
The Cowboys have the right opponent this week to get back on track against, as the Indianapolis Colts have lost four straight games and are in the midst of a fire sale.
But that doesn't mean the Cowboys don't have anything to fear against their upcoming opponent. Here are four things.
Trade rumors have been swirling around Taylor since the Colts' season started its downward spiral, and after Indy traded off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, those rumors have intensified.
But it doesn't look like Taylor is going to be dealt this week, so the Cowboys won't avoid him in what could be Taylor's last game with the Colts.
Taylor enters Week 9 ranked eighth in rushing yards, and that's despite being on a dead team and in an offense that has badly struggled.
Dallas' run defense can't stop a nosebleed, as evidenced by the Cowboys surrendering 152.8 rushing yards per game, the worst mark in the league by over six yards.
One of the best running backs in the sport, Taylor is capable of shredding this Cowboys unit en route to carrying his team to victory.
The Cowboys' defense needs every single inch of the football field with the way it has played this season, so the last thing the unit can afford is giving up long returns to set Indy's offense up.
Well, the Colts are one of the best return teams in the NFL, with Indy's kickoff return average of 27.8 ranking fourth. Two of the Colts' kick returners, Seth McGowan and Anthony Gould, rank inside the top 13 in return average.
Indy hasn't had as much success with punts, but Gould still ranks 14th in punt return average.
The Colts still don't have Alec Pierce, but they are equipped with a trio of talented pass-catchers in Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren.
Warren is one of the better athletes and pass-catchers at tight end in the NFL and creates matchup problems as a result.
Keenan Allen might not be the same player he once was, but he is still making an impact on the field. Downs is another talented pass-catcher who is capable of putting up a big number.
DaRon Bland has struggled this season and Caleb Downs is in the concussion protocol , so there'a a chance he might not play. There is absolutely a scenario where this trio could give Dallas fits on Sunday.
Wtih how bad the Cowboys have been this season, it's borderline insulting to the Colts to call this a trap game, but it still qualifies.
As we've seen over the last four weeks, the 2-6 Colts look like a team that has checked out and is playing out the string as they look to sell off pieces and transition to a new chapter in 2027.
Any motivated team should be able to go into Indianapolis and beat up on the Colts' corpse. The Cowboys are on life support , sure, but they still have a shot at the division, which should be providing the motivation needed to keep plugging along.
This is a game the Cowboys should win easily, but they simply can't think like that or else they're going to find themselves in another situation like the one we saw against Tampa bay and Arizona.

title: George Pickens Injury Update & More From Cowboys' Lengthy Wednesday Practice Report
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys released their first injury report of the week on Wednesday and it was quite lengthy.
In total, a whopping 16 players were listed, and of those 16, seven did not take part in practice, including safety Caleb Downs, tight end Jake Ferguson, safety P.J. Locke and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence.
All four players were injured in the dreadful Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, which was the first game back for Locke following his injured reserve stint.
Now, a full look at the injury report for the Cowboys, along with some more information on the walking wounded.
Downs and Locke are both in the concussion protocol , so they will have to be monitored during the week. Concussions can be tricky and neither one is guaranteed to play in Week 9.
With Jalen Thompson not likely to return from injured reserve this week, the Cowboys will need more from both Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell if Locke sits. Cobie Durant filled in for Downs following his exit in Week 8, so he's the replacement there.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed that Lawrence is going to be out a few weeks . ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Ferguson is dealing with a low-ankle sprain .
Luke Schoonmaker's limited session amounts to an upgrade for him after he didn't practice at all last week. The same goes for Dee Winters.
Pickens is still dealing with that shoulder injury. However, he did shed the hamstring issue he was listed with last week and based on that and the fact that he was limited Wednesday and played despite being limited throughout last week, there's no real concern about his status for Sunday.
Pickens has seen a downtick in targets and snaps the last two weeks, but the latter has everything to do with him playing hurt.
When it comes to the former issue, Brian Schottenheimer said he simply has to do a better job getting Pickens more involved.
"Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries," Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. "He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game."
"If I showed you the call sheet and you saw the targets for him, the targets for 88, it fills the entire back of my call sheet," Schottenheimer said.
"Again, when you have two of them, it's going to get spread around a little bit... CeeDee and George both having good years," Schotty added. "Ceedee's numbers are incredible, but, again, George is the guy that we're focused on knowing we got to get him going more and better, and that starts with me as the play-caller.
Having Lamb in the lineup more often this season has no doubt been one of the problems for Pickens' production. Last year, he didn't have to contend with Lamb as much for looks because Lamb struggled to stay healthy.
The other side of it is, as he said, Schottenheimer has to do a better job getting his No. 2 receiver more involved.

title: Dallas Cowboys Reunite With Practice Squad RB After Preseason Stint
full_text:
Although Javonte Williams has had impressive touchdown production, the Dallas Cowboys have struggled to find consistency in the running game during the 2026 season.
Dallas has the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (94.1) despite being tied for the NFL's third-most rushing touchdowns (10) headed into Week 9's matchup with the Indianapolis Colts.
A rushing unit that already struggles would be in deep water if Williams were to miss any time due to injury. Tyler Goodson has shown some promise but Dallas doesn't have any notable options behind him after parting ways with Emari Demercado.
So as a result, the Cowboys are bringing a familiar face back to the practice squad if running back depth becomes an issue moving forward.
The Cowboys have signed running back Jashaun Corbin to the practice squad, per reports from Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com.
Corbin spent some time with Dallas during training camp and appeared in the team's preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints when he tallied three carries for 14 yards. It's clear the coaching staff likes his potential, as they are now reuniting with him a little over two months later.
Corbin also spent time with the Atlanta Falcons during the 2025 preseason, finishing that three-game slate with 18 carries for 59 yards.
Corbin played college football at both Texas A&M and Florida State before going undrafted in 2022. He signed a deal with the New York Giants and appeared in six games with the team in 2023. He played mostly on special teams but posted one carry for one yard and three catches for 12 yards.
Corbin is the player Dallas decided to sign after working out two other running backs on Tuesday.
The Cowboys also hosted former Denver Broncos running back Blake Watson and former Green Bay Packers running back Damon Bankston, but the familiarity with Corbin won out.
The addition of Corbin obviously isn't going to move mountains for the Dallas offense but the team was in need of a third option in case of injury.
But in the meantime, Williams' individual play has been one of the lone bright spots for the Cowboys and he will remain the bell cow when healthy. Ideally, Corbin will never see the field for Dallas unless the coaching staff feels he can contribute on special teams in some capacity.

title: Dallas Cowboys Urged to Trade for Rising New York Jets Pass Rusher
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys need to make a seemingly infinite amount of changes if they want to somehow make the most out of the 2026 season.
While many fans feel that process starts with firing head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, Jerry Jones has made it clear that he's not thinking about making changes to the coaching staff anytime soon.
So in the meantime, the Cowboys have no choice but to pray that their current roster can miraculously turn things around, or more realistically, make improvements via trade.
All eyes have been on whether or not Dallas will make a deal to acquire Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat, but another name has now entered the fold.
ESPN's Aaron Schatz listed the Cowboys as a team that should trade for New York Jets edge rusher Kingsley Enagbare, who is on pace for a career-best season during his first year in East Rutherford.
It's no secret that Dallas needs pass-rushing help. The Cowboys are tied for the fifth-fewest sacks as a team (15) in the NFL ahead of Week 9, a concerning stat considering that Dallas has yet to have its bye week. Schatz also points out that Enagbare is third among all NFL edge rushers this season in run stop win rate.
Quinnen Williams has done his part with five sacks, but the edge rusher haven't produced at the level that the defense needs.
Enagbare, 26, could give Dallas an added boost while playing with something to prove. He's currently on a one-year deal with the Jets and would extra motivated as he looks to earn a new contract.
If he were to land with the Cowboys, Dallas' defense would be getting a player with a chip on his shoulder. So far this season, Enagbare has started all seven games for the Jets while tallying 24 total tackles, 2.5 sacks and one forced fumble.
The Cowboys have already traded for two former Green Bay Packers since last August, so why not make it one more?
Enagbare played his first four seasons in Green Bay after the Packers selected him in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. He spent multiple years alongside Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary. While with Green Bay, Enagbare played in 68 games (21 starts) while posting 146 total tackles (79 solo), 11.5 sacks and three forced fumbles.
Dallas is looking for anything positive to work with, so maybe that prior relationship can help bring a much-needed spark to the defense.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Explains George Pickens' Lack of Snaps, Targets in Recent Cowboys Games
full_text:
Over the last few weeks there has been a noticeable decline in the number of snaps George Pickens is playing for the Dallas Cowboys.
Over his first six games, Pickens didn't see fewer than 76.4% of snaps in any contest, and he has typically been north of 84% throughout the season.
However, in the last two games, Pickens has been on the field for 60.3% and 56.8% of the snaps, which is a pretty steep drop.
When asked about Pickens' snap counts on Wednesday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed it has to do with Pickens playing at less than 100%.
"Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries," Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. "He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game."
Schottenheimer added that it "would be poor coaching by me" to keep Pickens off the field for any reason.
That checks out because Pickens was added to the injury report in Week 7 due to a shoulder issue and he remained on it through last week. It's pretty hard to block effectively with a shoulder injury, so that's understandable.
Another issue with Pickens' usage is his number of targets. Pickens has seen just 10 the last two games combined after seeing 11 or more in three of the previous four games.
Schottenheimer addressed that, also.
"If I showed you the call sheet and you saw the targets for him, the targets for 88, it fills the entire back of my call sheet," Schottenheimer said.
"Again, when you have two of them, it's going to get spread around a little bit... CeeDee and George both having good years," Schotty added. "Ceedee's numbers are incredible, but, again, George is the guy that we're focused on knowing we got to get him going more and better, and that starts with me as the play-caller.
Schottenheimer isn't the only one in the Cowboys' building who says Pickens needs more. Owner Jerry Jones said that on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday.
“He needs the ball coming his way more," Jones said.
This is not to say the Cowboys can't do a better job of getting him involved, but it's not shocking at all to see Pickens' targets become less consistent this season.
Lamb has managed to stay healthy and has once again taken the mantle of the team's No. 1 wide receiver, which Pickens obviously took up in 2025 when Lamb missed time. That allowed for more targets and better production in his first season in Dallas.
Because his playing time and targets have decreased in recent weeks, and because the Cowboys look like a team that is going nowhere, there has been increased trade chatter surrounding Pickens.
However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport is hearing that Pickens isn't going anywhere.
"As of right now there's nothing there," Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday.
Would it make sense for the Cowboys to trade Pickens given their status as a sinking ship, and with Pickens set to be a free agent next offseason?
Sure, but clearly the Cowboys don't agree.

title: New Dallas Cowboys 2027 NFL Mock Draft Injects Versatility Into Secondary
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' embarrassing fourth-quarter collapse against the Arizona Cardinals reminded everyone of the overwhelming lack of talent on the team's defense, despite using several resources during the offseason in an attempt to revamp the unit.
Unfortunately, Christian Parker has appeared to be in over his head as defensive coordinator , and the team's lack of talent around the field continues to be a major problem. To make matters worse, the Cowboys will not have their highest of two first-round picks in the upcoming 2027 NFL draft , so they may miss out on an opportunity to add an elite player when the draft rolls around in the spring.
In a new 2027 NFL mock draft by Justin Melo of NFL Draft on SI . the Cowboys waste no time addressing the consistent issues with their pass defense by selecting Georgia Bulldogs standout Ellis Robinson IV at the end of Round 1.
Entering Week 9, the Cowboys have the league's worst total defense , giving up 385.4 total yards per game, while ranking No. 22 against the pass. Robinson could potentially step in as a Day 1 starter if the team decides to move on from former All-Pro DaRon Bland in the offseason.
A closer look at what Robinson could bring to the Cowboys' defensive backfield can be seen below.
"The Dallas Cowboys are still struggling on defense despite the injection of rookie talent," Melo wrote. "DaRon Bland has particularly struggled at cornerback. Georgia's Ellis Robinson IV is a supremely athletic cornerback who is versatile enough to thrive in both man and zone coverage."
Because of Bland's drastic fall off and the Cowboys' inability to get anything going on defense, any help the team can find through the draft or free agency will be welcomed additions.
This season, Robinson has recorded 15 combined tackles, five passes defensed. and two interceptions after recording a career-high four interceptions a season ago. He continues to rise up the draft boards and would be an intriguing pick for Dallas if they remain in the 20s when draft day rolls around.
The 2027 NFL Draft will be held from Thursday, April 29, through Saturday, May 1, at the National Mall outside of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

title: ESPN NFL Insider Pinpoints Cowboys Trade Candidate Not Named George Pickens
full_text:
There has been a lot of trade chatter surrounding George Pickens lately because of how down in the dumps the Dallas Cowboys are.
But all signs continue to point to the Cowboys not trading him , even though that might be the best course of action right now.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler was tasked with picking a Cowboys trade candidate and he named tight end Luke Schoonmaker.
"There are a lot of directions Dallas could go here," Fowler said. "But the struggling defense can't afford to move players on that side of the ball. Schoonmaker is the No. 3 tight end in the pecking order, and teams are looking for blocking tight ends. I just don't see Dallas moving key players at this point."
Schoonmaker had served as the Cowboys' No. 2 tight end in the past after being a second-round pick in 2023.
But Schoonmaker has not met expectations and he began losing his grip on the TE2 job last season, when Brevyn-Spann Ford began ascending.
And Spann-Ford's ascension was enough for the Cowboys to give him an extension, which was the first sign of trouble for Schoonmaker.
Eight weeks into the season and not only has Spann-Ford totally passed Schoonmaker on the depth chart, but the latter has also been completely irrelevant in the offense.
Schoonmaker has appeared for just 16% of the snaps and has three catches for 30 yards and no touchdowns on three targets. That continues his production decline after he went from 27/241 in 2024 to 14/132 in 2025.
Aside from his clear decline in the offense, Schoonmaker is also a free agent after this season and he has no future in Dallas. If there is a taker for his services, the Cowboys shouldn't hesitate to unload Schoonmaker before he leaves for nothing in 2027.
If that happens, the Cowboys could deploy practice squad tight end James Mitchell as their TE3, or they could even give rookie Michael Trigg a look.
There doesn't seem to be a lot of chatter about teams in the tight end market right now, but one team that makes sense for a trade for Schoonmaker is the Chicago Bears.
Chicago runs a lot of two- and three-tight end sets and recently lost its TE2, Cole Kmet, to a season-ending injury , which leaves the Bears depending on rookie Sam Roush, who has struggled, and a one-dimensional veteran in Stephen Carlson.
Schoonmaker is a serviceable blocker and pass-catcher and is probably a better option than Carlson, and he offers the experience the struggling Roush doesn't have.
If the Bears are willing to offer a seventh-round pick, the Cowboys should jump at the opportunity.

title: Stephen Jones Reveals Conditions for Cowboys to Make In-Season Coaching Change
full_text:
Brian Schottenheimer has a record of 10-14-1 as he enters Week 9 of his second season as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. His latest loss was a complete meltdown as Dallas surrendered a 14-point fourth quarter lead against the Arizona Cardinals.
Schottenheimer’s seat was already heating up before that game, but now it’s turned into a complete inferno . The calls for his job are coming from every corner and now Jerry and Stephen Jones find themselves fielding questions about making a coaching change in-season .
The Cowboys aren’t known for making such a drastic call, doing so just once since Jerry Jones bought the team. That happened in 2010 when Wade Phillips was fired following a 1-7 start. He was replaced by offensive coordinator Jason Garrett, who kept the job through the 2019 season. As of now, both Jerry and Stephen are backing Schottenheimer, although Stephen Jones recently revealed what would allow him to feel comfortable making a move during the season.
Jones didn't dive into what type of failure on the field would warrant a change, but instead focused on who they would have in line. While speaking on KRLD-FM on Monday, Jones said the Cowboys wouldn't hesitate to make a necessary change if they " had a succession plan in place .” Jones did reiterate, however, that they are still behind Schottenheimer.
Fans hoping that will change shouldn't hold their breath. According to Mac Engel of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, the Cowboys “ will not fire Schottenheimer during this season , but after it feels plausible.” Engel adds that Jerry Jones hates the idea of paying a coach who is not actively coaching the team.
That sentiment lines up with recent statements made by Jones, who delusionally said paying top dollar for coaches doesn't equate to success. That claim has no basis to it whatsoever, and just feels like Jones trying to gaslight a fan base that is tired of him being cheap when it comes to coaches.
That said, it gives us all the proof we need to know that Jones is not going to fire a coach in the middle of the season out of pure stubbornness. Sure, he did fire Phillips in 2010, but at that time he was looking for an excuse to promote Garrett. With no one on the staff being groomed to replace Schottenheimer, Jones will just play out the season before making any decisions, which means we are all in for quite a ride during the second half of the year.

title: Cowboys Linked to Underrated Steelers EDGE Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Jerry Jones continues to say the Dallas Cowboys will explore every opportunity to improve their roster ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
While Jones will be open to making moves, the Cowboys are limited in draft capital in 2027 , which could hurt their chances of pulling off a big move. That doesn’t mean they can’t still find someone who can help them this year, and beyond. John Owning recently revealed an intriguing option while appearing on 105.3 The Fan.
Owning said he doesn’t think the Cowboys will be “big buyers” at the deadline, but believes there’s one target worth keeping an eye on, saying Alex Highsmith of the Pittsburgh Steelers makes a lot of sense.
”Everyone talks about Maxx Crosby as kind of the golden goose that everyone wants to get. And I think obviously bringing him in would be a huge impact. He'd be a very valuable defender. But I just don't think that's very feasible given the draft picks that the Cowboys have, but I do think someone like I've talked to (Bryan) Broaddus about this a few times is Alex Highsmith from the Pittsburgh Steelers,” Owning said.
“I think he's someone who is young enough, he's impactful enough, and if you brought him in, he's someone who, even if this year is not your year, he can be impactful year two, year three, year four for you. So it's still, it legitimizes trading for him. So I think he's someone who can make an impact, not only in the pass rush department, but also defending the run on the edge. He would immediately walk into the team and be the number one edge defender.”
Should the Cowboys be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline? John Owning says they may not make a big splash, but that Alex Highsmith might be the "big move." pic.twitter.com/qgX0Z5uBXp
Highsmith has 18 tackles and 3.5 sacks this season, working in a rotation that includes T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig. Highsmith signed a four-year extension worth $68 million in 2023, keeping him under contract through the 2027 season .
This offseason, the Steelers signed Herbig to an extension as well, which led to us at Cowboys On SI asking if Highsmith could be a potential trade target for Dallas.
Seeing Dallas and Pittsburgh make a trade wouldn’t be surprising at all given their recent relationship.
The Cowboys have added George Pickens, Broderick Jones, and Joey Porter Jr. in trades with the Steelers over the past two seasons. So far, they’ve been satisfied with the results of those trades and it’s hard to see them regretting a move for someone as talented as Highsmith.

title: Jonathan Taylor's New Price Tag Just Changed Things for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are still being linked to the running back trade market ahead of November 10's NFL deadline.
The Broncos became the favorites to land Jonathan Taylor after Sunday's 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, but a significant obstacle could be in the way. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Indianapolis Colts have received at least one offer of a second-round pick plus additional compensation for Taylor, but they've yet to pull the trigger on a trade.
The Colts are holding out for a better offer — and they could be looking for a first-round pick. The Colts are now trying to send the signal that they want to hold onto Taylor as the cornerstone of their rebuild, but in an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport implied that Indy is looking for a first-round offer to part with their Pro Bowl back.
Would Taylor be worth a first-round pick to a team like the Broncos? That's the question.
As the Colts try to raise Taylor's value ahead of the deadline, the Broncos have to resist the temptation to overpay. As reliable and consistent as the veteran back is, he'll turn 28 in January, and he's rapidly approaching the dreaded 2,000-carry milestone.
Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension this summer, but his 2027 and 2028 salaries are $15 million and $9.46 million, respectively. His contract isn't prohibitive, especially for the caliber of back he is, but it's the cost to acquire him that could be the hitch in the Broncos' giddyup.
The Broncos have only made two first-round picks in the past five years, due to costly trades involving Russell Wilson, Sean Payton, and Jaylen Waddle. Nobody is questioning the compensation Denver gave to New Orleans to acquire Payton's rights — he's been worth every penny, so to speak — but the Wilson trade blew up in the Broncos' face, and the jury is still out on Waddle.
As the Broncos begin to age into one of the NFL's older rosters, keeping the draft pipeline flowing could become increasingly important. That's especially true as it pertains to a future Bo Nix contract, as that'll limit the number of salary-cap dollars available to pay veterans.
Giving up a second-round pick for Taylor, plus perhaps a couple of mid-round selections, would already be pushing the envelope for Denver. But if the Broncos believed he would be the missing piece to get them over the Super Bowl hump, it would quickly become a case of ' F(orget) them picks ' — a phrase the Los Angeles Rams have made famous.
I'm not convinced Taylor is worth a second-round pick, let alone a first-rounder, especially given the emergence of Jonah Coleman. Plus, the Broncos expect to get RJ Harvey back from injured reserve in a few weeks, and they still have J.K. Dobbins, whom Payton vociferously claimed on Wednesday is still a "huge part of what we're doing."
If the Broncos were to acquire Taylor, he'd be the de facto No. 1 running back, pushing everyone else, including Coleman, down the depth chart. Again, that's a collateral effect the Broncos could live with, if Taylor was the answer to unlocking this offense.
And he very well could be. The Broncos are the NFL's worst third-down offense halfway through the season, mainly because of their inefficiency on first and second down. Taylor could ostensibly help fix that in a hurry, moving the chains and giving Bo Nix much more favorable third-down situations.
I could see Taylor being an immediate difference-maker, but the idea that Denver would have to go another year without making a first-round selection... it would put a lot of pressure on Payton to win a Super Bowl this year.
Another option could be to trade for a guy who could simply fit into the Broncos' running back committee. Payton often laments the difficulty of feeding more than two running backs on game day, though a third back often gets some usage in the offense, like Harvey on third down and in the passing game.
This is much more of an issue for Denver now, only because Harvey is out of reach for the next three games. The Broncos' next three games are at the Carolina Panthers, home against the Las Vegas Raiders, and on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
If the Broncos believe they can weather that three-game storm without Harvey, with Coleman and Dobbins, they probably don't make a trade for a running back. But if they're worried about it, maybe they don't swing for the fences with Taylor and instead look at a more affordable option like Tennessee's Tony Pollard , who already has 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns in a terrible Titans offense.
It's a pickle. Since the Broncos have become competitive, we know GM George Paton has considered making trades ahead of the deadline as recently as last year (Waddle). But Paton has never actually pulled the in-season trigger.
At the same time, Paton never got close to a Lombardi Trophy until last year, and that, ladies and gentlemen, is why all bets are off. If the Colts stick to their guns, looking for a first-round value in exchange for Taylor, the Broncos may look elsewhere for help. They'll still be looking, though.
But if it's just a negotiating tactic, Taylor could end up going for much less, just as we saw when the Colts dealt away All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson (for a third- and a fifth-rounder) and veteran defensive lineman DeForest Buckner (a fourth-rounder). The Colts gave up both trenchmen for much less than was expected.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Addresses Trade Chatter
full_text:
Sean Payton wouldn't outright dismiss the idea of the 6-2, first-place Denver Broncos being "buyers" — acquiring star-level talent at a likely costly price — ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, as many within the fan base are hoping for.
But the veteran head coach did shoot down any speculation about the club being "sellers" — shipping off key pieces amid a potential championship run .
“Well, we’re a team that’s playing better, so we’re not looking to sell," Payton told reporters following Wednesday's practice.
The Broncos don't have a trade chip like the Colts do with running back Jonathan Taylor, whom Denver is the current betting favorite to land. Their highest-value commodities are players on expiring contracts.
That group includes wide receiver Marvin Mims, cornerbacks Riley Moss and Ja'Quan McMillian, safety Brandon Jones, offensive guard Ben Powers, tight end Evan Engram, and backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham.
A group that Payton isn't rushing to break up, realizing the landscape of today's NFL.
“I always think there’s buyers and sellers, right?" Payton said Wednesday. "It’s probably more noticeable in the last five years than maybe in our… Or at least I notice it more. Teams that are playing well are the potential buyers. The teams maybe that aren’t are the potential sellers.”
Taking Payton at his word, the Broncos rightfully have no business doing other teams any favors by giving away crucial pieces of their roster. Not when they're competing in a wide-open AFC. Not with their Super Bowl window wide open. Not here, not now.
Perhaps if Denver was 2-6, the "sellers" argument would be justified. But as of now, they hold the No. 2 seed in the conference, seemingly on track to capture the AFC West for the second consecutive year.
Trading Moss, a starting corner, for a hypothetical fourth-round pick isn't more valuable than simply retaining him for the remainder of the 2026 campaign. Ditto for Jones. Ditto for McMillian. Ditto for Mims. Each player is a significant contributor, if not a full-blown starter. Why fix what isn't broken?
Some fans don't want to hear this, but it'd actually be better if the Broncos maintained the status quo — did nothing — than suddenly face-lifted the lineups before Tuesday's deadline.
The options are on the table for Payton and his right-hand man, general manager George Paton, as the decision-making process remains fluid.
“We would meet and meet in the evening. The early part of it, all the GMs, they all talk with each other, but he and I’ll visit daily," Payton said. "So it’s not like it’s consuming two hours. His group is spending a lot of time separate from the time that I’m involved with our group. In other words, they’re doing their evaluation, we’re doing football, but he and I daily will visit about a bunch of things.”

title: Broncos Get Good News on Pat Bryant, Concerning Update on Talanoa Hufanga
full_text:
After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster.
That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina .
Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve.
Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown.
WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers.
What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday.
Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up.
Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming.
Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together.
Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season.
With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air.

title: Broncos-Panthers Matchups: Pat Surtain II vs. Tet McMillan Looms Large
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a nice four-game winning streak going, and they now sit atop the AFC West after beating the Kansas City Chiefs .
However, the Broncos must guard against riding the high of the win and dropping this coming game against the Carolina Panthers. The Broncos have to travel east for an early game, a trip that has historically challenged them, though that track record has significantly improved under Sean Payton.
To avoid a potential upset by the Panthers, which would be costly heading into the bye week, the Broncos will need to win two critical matchups. The biggest matchups come down to a wide receiver vs. a cornerback on both sides of the ball.
Let's dig into these matchups and why they're so important to the Broncos.
The Broncos have struggled to find consistency with Sutton and rekindle his connection with Bo Nix . Sutton has been the Broncos' second-most-targeted receiver, behind Jaylen Waddle, with 36 targets, but ranks third in receptions, with only 20.
Sutton has 221 yards with a single touchdown through eight games. His usual strength in contested catches hasn't been there, with only three contested catches on eight such targets, though he did come down with one last week against the Chiefs.
The Panthers' secondary isn't a good unit, and it's largely because of the injuries they've sustained. Denver should look at getting Sutton matched up on Lee, forcing Waddle to a different cornerback, which is a topic I'll dig into in a different article.
Before getting into Lee in coverage, one reason the Broncos should like this matchup is his tackling issues against bigger receivers. Denver needs Sutton to find his footing in that regard.
As for coverage, Lee has been targeted 42 times, allowing 27 catches. He plays aggressively in coverage and does have five pass break-ups this season, but that has also led to some big plays being relinquished, as his aggressiveness can burn him.
Lee has given up two plays over 40 yards and allowed 335 total receiving yards, the 11th-most among NFL cornerbacks. Denver needs to win this matchup to help out its other favorable matchup with Waddle.
This is the obvious one. The Panthers' offense runs through McMillan, who has the NFL's 12th-most targets, 12th-most receptions, and 11th-most yards among 33 qualifying receivers. He is the majority of the Panthers' offense, and if you can limit or eliminate him, you're setting yourself up for major success.
Denver must put its top corner on McMillan and let Surtain do his thing. It won't be easy, and Surtain isn't infallible, but he is one of the best corners in the NFL and is trustworthy.
The challenge comes in the routes McMillan runs the most. McMillan's main route-running hits correspond to the ones Surtain typically struggles against. Vance Joseph could make slight coverage adjustments to give Surtain a hand.
"He's a big receiver. He has great body control," Surtain said of McMillan on Wednesday. "He can run every route in the route tree, so I'm looking forward to that matchup."
If Surtain and the Broncos can't limit or eliminate McMillan, this game will be much harder to win, especially in front of the Panthers' home crowd. The Broncos could still win the game if McMillan has a day, because there's too much in football for one area to have that big an impact, outside of the quarterback.
It's about making the defense's job easier. Limiting McMillan would help Denver put some extra focus on stopping the Panthers' run game.

title: 3 Positions Broncos Should Target at Trade Deadline to Boost Super Bowl Hopes
full_text:
After beating the Kansas City Chiefs and moving into first place in the AFC West , there's the hope that the Denver Broncos might do more than win the division, but also clinch the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, just as they did last year.
The Broncos still have some tough games ahead, with the Pittsburgh Steelers sitting at 5-2 and awaiting them in Week 12, plus the Buffalo Bills and the New England Patriots in two of the final weeks. But most of Denver's remaining games are against opponents far from the NFL's top tiers.
With the Broncos in position to chase the No. 1 seed, a midseason trade makes sense — and finding an offensive playmaker would be the fastest upgrade.
Of course, the Broncos are rumored to be interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and are the new betting favorites to land him. But there are other running backs who might be available, along with tight ends and wide receivers, who could help the Broncos' offense.
With the NFL trade deadline now less than a week away (November 10), let's examine the positions to see what makes the most sense for Denver to acquire and which players might be available on the block.
Let's start with the position that may be getting the most attention. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on injured reserve for at least a few weeks, and J.K. Dobbins continues to underperform, so the Broncos could use some help here.
It makes the most sense to acquire a running back, but it may be best to find one for the short term rather than the long term. That's because Jonah Coleman has shown he could be a No. 1 back for the long term, and Harvey, while not a primary back, has shown he is a quality No. 2 option.
In this case, the Broncos may be better off with a short-term option who can replace Dobbins. That means that, as appealing as Taylor would be, he might not be the right option because he would be a long-term solution — and would push Coleman and Harvey down the depth chart.
Tennessee's Tony Pollard might actually be the best option. He's in the final year of his contract, and the Broncos might be able to include Dobbins in a deal. A possible deal could be the Broncos sending Dobbins and their fifth- and sixth-round picks to the Titans for Pollard and their sixth-rounder.
And if Lamar Jackson is going to miss the bulk of the season because of his thumb injury, the Baltimore Ravens could be talked into dealing Derrick Henry. A deal involving Dobbins, plus draft pick swaps, is possible here.
The Broncos would also get Henry on a cheap salary for 2026, and they could easily cut him next season with no dead money charges. Don't rule out Henry as a potential option.
This would be the position to pursue if Broncos fans want a player here for 2026 and beyond. With Evan Engram's deal expiring after the season and no other tight end on the roster standing out, it makes sense to find one.
However, the trade options aren't ideal if you're trying to get a long-term option. Trey McBride would be the dream scenario, but all indications are that the Arizona Cardinals are unwilling to trade him.
The Philadelphia Eagles are rumored to be ready to move players and could make Dallas Goedert available. Goedert would be a cheap player to acquire because of how the Eagles structured his deal.
However, Goedert would be a rental for the remainder of the season and not a long-term guy, as he's 31 this season. That doesn't mean the Broncos would have to dismiss Goedert as a possibility — only that they wouldn't be acquiring him for anything more than the short term.
In this case, the Broncos could find lots of options to add a playmaker. Among the names that have been mentioned are Calvin Ridley, Jerry Jeudy, Quentin Johnston, Brian Thomas Jr., and Josh Downs.
However, this is the least likely option among the offensive playmaker positions. The Broncos have a viable option who should be available after the bye week: Pat Bryant.
Bryant was placed on injured reserve after he sprained his ankle in Week 4 . He's eligible to come off injured reserve this week, though the Broncos could wait until after the Week 10 bye to give him more time to get healthy.
But once Bryant is back in the lineup, that should give the Broncos the receiving boost they need. The Broncos need not worry about seeking a trade here.
A running back to replace Dobbins for the rest of the season makes the most sense here. It would allow the Broncos to get help now in their pursuit of a Super Bowl and have a player who can provide help until Harvey returns from injury, but make it clear that Coleman is the top guy moving forward.
Doing so would mean the Broncos would have to part ways with some draft capital but not a lot — and while it's easy to say "forget them picks," Broncos fans must remember there are key players with expiring contracts or one year left after 2026 who need to be replaced.
It's easy to look at a trade like the Jeffery Simmons deal, but it's better to think about somebody like Rashid Shaheed, whom the Seattle Seahawks acquired last season for 2026 fourth- and fifth-round picks. Shaheed not only provided immediate help but was a key reason the Seahawks won the Super Bowl.
Sometimes the best trades to make are not of the blockbuster variety. It's often the under-the-radar deals involving Day 3 picks that turn out to be important for a deep playoff run.
It's my belief that the Broncos need to talk to the Titans about Pollard, while keeping an eye on the Ravens situation when it comes to Henry. A deal for Pollard or Henry might not be as sexy as Taylor, but it could do just as much to boost the Broncos' Super Bowl chances.
