title: If Bears Don’t Want to Play Ball on Khalil Mack Trade, Chargers Could Just Call Packers
full_text:
It feels like a matter of time before the Los Angeles Chargers trade away Khalil Mack at the deadline .
Barring Mack wanting to stay with the possibly soon-to-be 0-8 Chargers just one offseason removed from pondering retirement, it’s the right thing for the franchise to do. Get him to a contender and let him possibly finish his Hall of Fame career by getting a chance at a Lombardi Trophy.
It would also help the Chargers’ rebuild , because that’s where things are headed. No telling if Jim Harbaugh and his staff will actually be part of that next offseason, but every little bit of trade return helps.
For Mack, a reunion with the Chicago Bears still makes the most sense.
But if the Bears don’t want him, the Green Bay Packers are right there .
The Bears are all-in. Look at the Jeffery Simmons trade. A reunion with Khalil Mack is the next logical step, especially because the Chargers don’t exactly have any leverage to make it a costly deal.
There is a creative angle to consider, though: The Chargers could always leverage the competitive NFC North in Mack trade talks.
Somebody needs to break through and win that division.
And what do you know? The Packers are without Micah Parsons until at least Week 12, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . Oh, and hey, the Packers were one of the teams who were very hot after Mack before he originally went to the Bears.
Maybe there’s an angle there, where the Packers wouldn’t mind pairing Mack with Lukas Van Ness, then really beefing up the rotation with Parsons back in the mix later while they make a playoff push.
The threat of shipping Mack to a division rival who can inflict great harm on playoff chances during an all-in season might just give the Chargers some interesting leverage over the Bears in talks.
Sure, we’re talking minimal difference in draft compensation for Mack’s departure. And that’s even if he wishes to pack up and move one more time. But every little bit helps for what has quickly become the worst roster in the NFL looking at a possible complete coaching staff blowout.

title: Los Angeles Chargers Have a Real Chance to Be First 0-17 Team in NFL History
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are seven games into the 2026 season, and the conversation has already shifted from playoff expectations to a much uglier possibility.
After opening the year 0-7, the Bolts are staring at a situation nobody expected when the season began. They are not just trying to find their first win anymore. They are trying to avoid becoming the first team in NFL history to finish a 17-game season without winning once.
That is an unbelievable place for a team led by Jim Harbaugh to be in. Harbaugh was brought in to change the direction of this franchise, and there was a reason people believed the Chargers could be a serious team.
The offense has been a major concern . It is difficult to win consistently when a team is producing very little, and it becomes almost impossible when the offense cannot give the defense much room for error. Justin Herbert is the face of this team, but they need far more around him if they are going to change the direction of this season. Better play from the franchise quarterback would be nice as well.
The history makes this situation more interesting. The NFL has seen teams finish 0-16, with the Detroit Lions doing it in 2008 and the Cleveland Browns following in 2017. But neither team had to play 17 regular-season games. The league moved to a 17-game schedule in 2021, and no team has finished 0-17 since that change.
The last time the Bolts were this bad was over 25 years ago. LA Times columnist Mirjam Swanson noted that “They played like a team ready to accept another defeat and fell to 0-7 for the first time since 2000, when Harbaugh was their quarterback.”
The Chargers still have 10 games left, which means there is time to turn things around. Their remaining schedule includes matchups against the Texans, Ravens, Jets, Patriots, Buccaneers, Raiders, 49ers, Dolphins, Chiefs and Broncos. There are games in that group where the Bolts  should have a chance to compete, but that does not mean anything is guaranteed. At this point, even getting one win has become something this team has to prove it can do.
The problem is that the Chargers cannot keep treating every loss like an isolated bad afternoon. Seven games have produced the same result, and the offense has shown very little consistency. The team needs to find answers quickly, because the longer this continues, the more pressure builds on the coaching staff, the players and everyone involved in the organization. Could they become the first 0-17 team in NFL history? It is too early to say that is where this season is headed, but it is no longer an outrageous question. They are 0-7, they are scoring fewer points than anyone else, and there is not much evidence right now that things are about to change.
They do not need to start thinking about history just yet. They need to start thinking about winning a football game.

title: 3 Players Chargers Should Call About Before Trade Deadline to Keep Justin Herbert Alive
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are in the midst of a season collapse at 0-7 and with still little signs of life on offense. Chargers President of Foootball Operations and member of ownership John Spanos should greenlight general manager Joe Hortiz to begin looking to the future and trade assets that can bring back future draft capital.
The Chargers really have no business being buyers at the trade deadline. However, if they are building for the future and trying to protect franchise quarterback Justin Herbert and preserve his health and sanity, they could make a few minor moves with other teams who may be inclined to move a player or two before the deadline.
The Chargers offense has not been effective at all this season and it appears the run blocking from the entire team with the exception of the tackles has taken a nosedive off of a cliff and hit every rock on the way to bottom. The lack of run blocking and inefficiency in the run game has caused problems for the offense.
Los Angeles lost starting fullback Alec Ingold and replacement Scott Matlock struggled out of the bye week against the Rams. Cole Strange has been the worst guard on the entire team for most of the season, his blocking grades bare that out. The Chargers have rotated essentially every other offensive lineman on the roster at left guard and have yet to find the answer.
Let's dive in to a few names who could be low-cost options that the Chargers could target as a means to solve a short term problem but also with eyes to the future.
I have brought up Kieft before as a potential target and I just can't quit the idea of adding him to the offense. Kieft saw his snap counts drop to rookie tight end Bauer Sharp after suffering an elbow injury and Sharp has kept the job locked down. Kieft will be a free agent in 2027 and a move could be beneficial for his career and the Chargers could absolutely use him.
If the Chargers deploy a fullback in 2027 and beyond it might be worth to get one in the building before free agency to make a better judgement meanwhile protecting Justin Herbert. For some reason, the fullback position has been tasked with going one on one with edge rushers far too often in 2026, if this continues to be a trend, an upgrade could help keep Herbert upright.
Kieft has been able to handle defensive lineman one on one throughout his career and punishes defenders when used as a lead blocker. The Buccaneers have already found Kieft's replacement and the cost should be a simple flip of late round picks to bring a competent blocker into the building for the Chargers.
This trade target isn't about Justin Herbert and the offense. The Chargers are running out of corners and have been dialing up reclamation projects to fill out their depth. Kelee Ringo has not been a factor on defense this year for the Eagles, playing primarily special teams. The Chargers need special teams depth and cornerback depth this year and beyond.
Current Chargers special teams cornerback Deane Leonard has been dealing with a laundry list of injuries and is on an expiring contract. Ringo is a physical defensive back with plenty of traits to work with. His floor as a special teams player is worth looking into to help maintain the special teams rebound the Chargers are currently undertaking. Ringo's expiring contract and usage on the field should make for another late-round pick swap possible. If he works out, he could easily factor into the plans as cornerback and special teams depth going forward.
Capable depth offensive linemen do not usually get traded during the season. However, Rams backup interior offensive lineman Justin Dedich who can play all three spots has been languishing on injured reserve as the Rams roster has been completely full and they are choosing to use injured reserve activations on other players.
Dedich played an important role for the Rams last season but an injury suffered over the summer kept him out of training camp. The Chargers could use depth in the interior with experience. The true conundrum in this situation is the Chargers themselves are running out of IR activations. Players on injured reserve have been eligible to be traded since 2018 and the receiving team assumes the injury risk.
If the Chargers choose not to activate any of their own offensive lineman from injured reserve they could swing a late Day 3 pick swap with the Rams for a lineman who has been critical for them in the past but has been trapped on injured reserve this season.

title: Would Chargers Trade Tuli Tuipulotu to Desperate 49ers, Cowboys at NFL Deadline?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers will sell at the NFL trade deadline.
That feels like an obvious fact. Yet the way the Chargers have worked the trade phones so far, reports say other NFL teams are confused about how general manager Joe Hortiz and the club in Los Angeles have moved so far.
At 0-7 and counting, that should change. Justin Herbert trade packages probably won’t surface, or matter if they do. But guys like Khalil Mack, Donte Jackson and others could probably be had for the right price (and they owe it to Mack to send him to a contender if he wants).
There’s also the matter of Tuli Tuipulotu. It shouldn’t be a thing for the Chargers. But it just might be.
…if they want to move him.
Yes, it sounds ridiculous. The Chargers roster Tuipulotu, who has 29 sacks in 57 games and is just 24 years old. Why would they trade him away?
Well, for one, as The Athletic's Daniel Popper noted while listing Tuipulotu as the No. 2 overall trade candidate, big spenders like the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys would likely have interest.
“Tuipulotu took a big step as a player in 2025,” Popper wrote. “He has sustained that performance this season. Since the start of 2025, Tuipulotu ranks 12th in pressure rate among players with at least 250 pass-rush snaps.”
Tuipulotu is on the final year of his rookie contract and the team and player couldn't agree to an extension this past summer.
Two, there’s also the matter of this being the Chargers . Fans just watched the team trade for Odafe Oweh last year, get a breakout from him, then refuse to re-sign him despite approaching free agency with nearly $100 million in cap space. So they burned the trade asset for a half-season rental, then drafted Akheem Mesidor because he’s an “older” rookie while trying to replace Oweh’s production.
Which is to say, the Chargers don’t always make sense. And who knows? Maybe the Tuipulotu contract extension talks were worse than outsiders know. He’s going to come close to resetting the market. The Chargers still have roughly $26 million in free cap space right now but didn’t get something done.
One would think that Tuipulotu is a big building block and a nice one-two punch with Mesidor no matter what happens to the team and coaching staff next offseason. But the Chargers are in this hole in the first place because they don’t act like a normal, modern NFL franchise all the time.
So…don’t count out a good offer from a team like the 49ers or Cowboys suddenly causing some chaos over the next week before the deadline.

title: Chargers, Justin Herbert Trade Ideas Must Now Keep Jeffery Simmons, Bears Lessons in Mind
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers aren't going to trade Justin Herbert, but similar things were said before other NFL trade deadline blockbusters over the last week or so.
Sure, the Chargers are much more likely to trade Khalil Mack . No doubt the Chargers are getting calls from NFL teams around the league, even if those teams are leaving the phone calls more confused than anything else.
From an outsider’s view, the Chargers are much more likely to blow up the entire program before trading away Herbert. That means head coach Jim Harbaugh, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and even general manager Joe Hortiz, for starters.
But…these things were said before a different mega-trade happened last week, too.
Teams like the Minnesota Vikings could use a big swing for a star quarterback right now.
And teams like the Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears have shown that, sometimes, all it takes is the right offer to actually be put on the table.
That’s a point raised by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer this week, who fielded questions about a Herbert trade and pointed out that the Titans never actually moved star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons until another team actually made the right offer.
“It can’t hurt to make that phone call if you’re the Vikings,” Breer said. “Do I think Joe Hortiz is going to say ‘no way, we can’t trade a franchise quarterback,’ yeah, I think he’s going to say no way.”
Point is, all of this is just smoke and talk until a team actually puts a major offer on the table. Teams aren’t likely doing that for Herbert, so it’s all moot.
Breer added this: “I will just say this about Justin Herbert. I don’t think a lot of what’s happened this year is on him. I think if you go back to last year and you talk to people around the league, a lot of people felt he was playing at an MVP level in a near-impossible situation…it reminds me of the way people talked about Matthew Stafford in Detroit.”
Chargers fans are probably tired of hearing about the Herbert-Matthew Stafford comparison. But with how they keep blowing things up around him and failing to build back up properly around him again and again, it’s not an unfair one to make right now.
As things stand, the Chargers remain focused on trying to make sure Herbert becomes and stays a top-10 player within their franchise, not somewhere else.
But the reality hurts: The Chargers failed at roster building this offseason while bringing on Mike McDaniel. The combo has produced the worst play of Herbert’s career. They’re beelining toward another rebuild and blowing things up around Herbert again.
Herbert’s no-trade clause in his contract notwithstanding, what really happens if a team like the Vikings slaps three or more first-round picks on the table, officially? Do the Chargers make like the Titans with Simmons and jump, or stand still some more?
That’s the problem for the Chargers: There’s no easy answer when it comes to trades, or even what to really do with Harbaugh and his entire staff. Staying the course is just as risky as blowing everything up again.
Either way, Herbert’s name isn’t going to leave trade speculation discussions, even after the upcoming trade deadline, considering the Chargers’ season is already effectively over.

title: Obvious Khalil Mack, Bears Trade is a Formality for Chargers at This Point
full_text:
By far the best thing the Los Angeles Chargers have accomplished this season is their efforts to convince everyone that they won’t be blowing things up or selling anything at the NFL trade deadline.
Little on the field by the Chargers has qualified for the “best” qualifier, so that’s all they really have left.
It’s time for the Chargers to trade Khalil Mack .
The Chargers have even confused other NFL teams with their unwillingness to talk shop so far. But they just hit 0-7 out of the bye, turning in their worst offensive performance of the season so far, which should get Mike McDaniel fired in organizations that make any sense.
A Mack trade is a close second at this point.
This isn't about the Chargers getting quality future assets. It’s about doing right by Khalil Mack.
After all, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport has made it pretty clear that the Chicago Bears would be interested in the idea of a reunion with Mack.
Mack himself, at least, is trying to keep things civil and professional before the likely move.
“You’ve got to be where your feet are man, ultimately,” Mack said, according to Eric Williams of Fox Sports. “That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.”
Good on Mack, but where this is going is obvious. He had pondered retirement before agreeing to another one-year deal with the Chargers last offseason. If this is it, going out with this version of the Chargers would be unfortunate.
Mack is still playing great ball, too, hence the interest from contenders. Across 71 percent of the defense’s snaps, he’s ranked 23rd out of 110 EDGEs in total grade at PFF. He’s tallied 16 pressures, three sacks and five tackles for loss.
Mack’s expiring contract and the obvious lack of any leverage the Chargers hold in trade talks is going to be pretty appealing to contenders, too.
Sometimes the right move is the obvious one. The Chargers don’t seem to understand that fully yet. But once they do, letting Mack reunite with the Bears is a no-brainer, as is selling off almost anything else other teams might want before possibly blowing up the coaching staff next offseason.

title: Chargers Veteran Speaks Out About Growing Trade Speculation Following Sunday's Loss
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are finding themselves in a difficult position as the NFL season continues. Following Sunday’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams, veteran linebacker Khalil Mack addressed the growing speculation surrounding his future.
Per Eric Willaims of Fox Sports , Mack stated “That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all times. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.”
Mack is certainly a name that could generate attention around the league. However, the Chargers seem to be at the point where they do not want anything to do with trading players whatsoever.
Despite the outside discussion, Mack’s comments following Sunday’s game showed where his attention currently remains.
With trade speculation continuing to circulate, the veteran defender addressed the situation without allowing the conversation about his future to become the main focus. That approach is understandable for a player who has spent years dealing with the expectations that come with being one of the league’s established defensive veterans. Situations like this are part of the business, particularly around this time of the season.
The timing makes the situation interesting. The organization has to evaluate where its season is heading and whether keeping its current roster together makes the most sense. Staring at a winless record is what makes this all very complicated. Those decisions become even more important when the deadline is approaching and other teams are looking for opportunities to improve.
Pro Football Talk and NBC Sports writer Josh Alper also noted that Khalil Mack is “playing on a one-year deal and has the kind of history of success as a pass rusher that could be appealing to a number of teams”
Mack’s experience also makes him an important part of the conversation. Players with his background do not come around often by any means. So losing a veteran presence can have an impact beyond what shows up on the stat sheet. At the same time, the Chargers have to consider what makes the most sense for the organization moving forward. There is still plenty that can happen before the deadline arrives, and his future remains something worth monitoring. Sunday’s loss only added fuel to the fire, but the veteran linebacker has made it clear that the outside noise is not going to take his attention away from the game.
Whether he finishes the season in a Chargers uniform or becomes part of a larger deadline decision remains to be seen.
Khalil Mack on trade rumors: “You’ve got to be where your feet are man, ultimately. That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.”

title: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
full_text:
While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury.
The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers.
“The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.”
McDuffie was also a non-participant in practice with a back injury that he suffered at the end of Sunday’s game against the Chargers. He’ll be a player to monitor throughout the week. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), and safety Kam Curl (foot) also didn’t participate in practice. Parkinson missed last week’s game and he’ll be one to watch as well.
While the Rams got bad news with Watson, Wednesday marked the first time since Week 1 that Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald were on the practice field together . Garrett opened his 21-day practice window on Wednesday, leaving open the possibility that he could play against the Commanders.
“It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.”
The Rams are taking it day-by-day with Garrett. McVay made comparisons to the 2022 season with the number of injuries that the Rams have dealt with. They have erred on the side of caution with Garrett since training camp and that will likely continue.
In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams.  Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back).
Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury.
“It feels good. Full practice as I have been all year and hope to continue to be that way,” said Stafford. “Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”
On the Washington Commanders’ side, quarterback Jayden Daniels was listed as a full participant with a left elbow injury that he’s managed most of the season. Wide receiver Treylon Burks and Stefon Diggs didn’t practice. However, Diggs missed practice for rest purposes.
For every step forward that the Rams seem to take on the injury front, they continue to take another step back. Garrett and Ferguson returning to practice are certainly encouraging developments, but losing Watson for the season is a significant blow. With McDuffie now dealing with a back injury, the Rams will need to hope that their improving health along the defensive front can help offset some of the concerns in the secondary.

title: Why the Rams' 2026 Bye Week Is Causing Controversy
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are quickly approaching their bye week, which is set to take place in Week 11. However, it won’t be a typical bye week that most teams get. While most teams get a full week off, making it 14 days between games, the Rams are only getting 10 days . Essentially, the Rams’ bye week has been negated with a mini-bye.
On Tuesday, Kelly Stafford posted a story on Instagram, criticizing the NFL for its scheduling choice.
Kelly Stafford, wife of #Rams QB Matthew Stafford, calls out the NFL for the team's bye being only 10 days. Because the Rams host the Packers on Wednesday night (Thanksgiving Eve), their Week 11 bye is only 10 days between games instead of the usual 14. pic.twitter.com/jdrdjispll
“Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” wrote Stafford. “Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.”
Instead of a typical bye week, the Rams will have a shortened break because of their upcoming Wednesday matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Stafford mentioned that the Rams are the only team to have a shortened bye week, but it’s worth mentioning that the Packers will be in the same situation.
The NFL did the right thing by putting the Rams and Packers in the same situation with both teams playing on a Wednesday. At the same time, the Rams were just one of three teams with a negated bye week in 2026.
With that said, the Rams got more rest after Week 1 coming back from Australia. They’ll get 10 days off for their actual bye and then eight days off before playing the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams will then get a third-mini-bye before they play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 14.
When the NFL released its schedule, the Rams were a team with a significant rest disadvantage. The Rams were set to play five games with less rest than their opponen t. According to Warren Sharp ’s schedule analysis, the Rams were tied for 24th in net rest in 2026.
There is certainly reason for criticism for how the NFL came up with the Rams’ schedule. The lack of a true bye week is one of them.With that said, the Packers will be in the same situation.
That doesn’t mean that the NFL shouldn’t be criticized. Just because another team is in the same situation doesn’t make it right. Teams are given one bye week per season and the NFL has taken that away from two teams. With the NFL scheduling games on Thanksgiving Eve , it wouldn’t be surprising if two more teams faced the same situation next year.
Given that Kelly Stafford spoke out about the Rams’ lack of a true bye week, it’s fair to wonder if the players, especially Matthew Stafford, feel the same way. With the number of injuries that the Rams have had to manage this season, the extra four days would likely have been beneficial.

title: Rams May Be Better Equipped to Overcome Jaylen Watson Injury Than Expected
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got more bad injury news on Wednesday when it was reported that cornerback Jaylen Watson would undergo shoulder surgery , ending his 2026 season. It has been a consistent theme for the Rams in 2026, and just as they were set to get Myles Garrett back, Watson is now out for the year.
There’s no doubt that losing Watson will be a huge blow to the secondary. The Rams made Watson their top free agent target in the spring after trading for his teammate Trent McDuffie. After giving up 346 yards passing and three touchdowns to Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room and Watson was a big part of that.
Among qualifying cornerbacks, Watson’s 0.71 yards per coverage snap ranked 10th in the NFL. His 4.87 yards per target ranked sixth. The Rams signed Watson to give them a lengthy, physical outside cornerback to play on the boundary and he’s been able to provide that. Watson has nine pass breakups, which ranks fifth this season.
With Watson out, the Rams will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in his spot. While there is certainly a difference in being a rotational player and playing full time, the Rams have gotten good production out of Wallace and Forbes this season.
“I think those guys have done really well," said head coach Sean McVay. "Jimmy Lake has done such a great job really with those corners as a whole group. Josh has played a lot of snaps. I thought 'E-Forbes' really played well last week. Both of those guys have been tapped in. They've been ready to step up and it seems like there have been a lot of games that we've had our top corners get banged up and they've played a lot more."
Wallace ranks sixth in yards per coverage snap in 2026 and he’s played often. When Watson was hurt in Week 4, Wallace played 100 percent of the defensive snaps. He also played all of the defensive snaps in Weeks 6 and 7 with McDuffie out due to injury. Wallace may be a rotational player, but he’s played just five snaps fewer than Watson this season on defense and more snaps than McDuffie.
Additionally, Emmanuel Forbes has played well in 2026. Using Forbes less in a smaller, rotational role has benefited both the team and the player. The Rams have been able to be more selective about the situations he plays in.
Forbes’ 0.49 yards per coverage snap ranks seventh in the NFL and his 3.13 yards per target ranks fourth. Despite playing just 25 percent of the defensive snaps this season, Forbes has been credited with seven impact plays via Sumer Sports.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wallace and Forbes both rank among the top 12 cornerbacks in coverage grade. Forbes has a coverage grade of 79.9, which ranks seventh, and Wallace ranks 12 with a coverage grade of 76.4.
While it may have been disappointing when the Rams lost Aubrey Pleasant in the offseason, the impact that defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake has had on the cornerback room can’t go unnoticed. Under Lake, Wallace and Forbes have developed into reliable depth cornerbacks who have held their own when called upon. The Rams also signed Cam Lampkin to the active roster on Tuesday, who was a preseason and training camp standout.
Given that Wallace has played in a full-time role for much of the season, the moment shouldn’t be too big for him. Wallace has gotten grabby at times as he’s been called for three defensive pass interference penalties. However, for the most part, he’s exceeded expectations.
Again, losing Watson for the season is a significant blow to the defense. However, Wallace has stepped in well when his number has been called and Forbes has also played well. The Rams have spent much of the season overcoming injuries, and Watson's absence presents another challenge. With Watson out, the Rams’ depth will certainly be tested, but based on what Wallace and Forbes have shown, there’s reason for optimism.

title: Rams Suffer Another Major Injury Blow as Jaylen Watson Ruled Out for Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without cornerback Jaylen Watson for the rest of the season . After re-injuring his shoulder, Watson will undergo surgery, ending his 2026.
Rams CB Jaylen Watson is getting shoulder surgery and is out for the season.
Watson left in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers after aggravating a shoulder injury. He had previously dislocated his shoulder in Week 3 and was forced to miss one game. Watson had played the next two games without issues, but re-injured his shoulder on Sunday.
Head coach Sean McVay discussed Watson’s shoulder injury during his media availability on Monday and expressed optimism about his status. However, after further evaluation, it was decided that surgery was the best option.
“We'll see what his status looks like as the week progresses,” McVay said on Monday. “Came in, had some good strength, feeling good and optimistic. We'll take his status a day at a time and see where he's at by the time the game rolls around.”
Watson now heads on injured reserve and is set to miss the rest of the year. In Watson’s place, the Rams will likely rely on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes. Wallace has filled in for both Trent McDuffie and Watson this season. He has quietly developed into a reliable depth cornerback. Wallace has allowed 0.71 yards per coverage snap in 2026, ranking 20th in the NFL among qualifying cornerbacks. Forbes has also played well in a smaller role and will be relied on going forward as well.
Coming into the season, Watson was one of the Rams’ big offseason additions. After allowing Sam Darnold to throw for 346 yards and three touchdowns in the NFC Championship Game, the Rams made it a point to rebuild their cornerback room.Watson was the team’s big free-agent signing following its trade for McDuffie.
The Rams simply can’t seem to shake the injury bug this season. It has been one injury after another all year. Two weeks ago, the Rams had to place Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Davante Adams on injured reserve. Just when it seemed like they were going to get healthy and get Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson back , the Rams had to place Watson on injured reserve.
Losing Watson is another blow to the defense that the Rams will have to manage over the second half of the season. Wallace and Forbes have shown that they can step up when needed, but Watson being out for the year is still a significant loss for a secondary that had finally started to find its footing.

title: Rams Could Find Low-Cost, High-Reward Wide Receiver Solution in Brandon Aiyuk (But It's Complicated)
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams approach the NFL trade deadline, there’s no doubt that they are in need of a wide receiver . Without Davante Adams, the Rams have struggled with their receiver depth options outside of Puka Nacua.
It’s possible that the Rams could look into making a trade for a player like Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr. However, with the market as competitive as it is at wide receiver, Downs and Thomas may require more draft capital than the Rams would want to give up.
On Tuesday, another option potentially became available as San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk requested reinstatement from the NFL . Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus to be his agent, who said that the wide receiver is healthy and ready to get back on the field.
According to reports, Aiyuk is prepared to report to the team’s facility on Friday. Once he does, the 49ers can’t turn him away and the options would be to cut him or find a trade. With that said, it’s unlikely that a team would give up any draft capital for Aiyuk given the 49ers’ situation. If the 49ers are set on trading him,  it’s hard to see him getting  moved inside the division.
The move Brandon Aiyuk could’ve made months ago to force the #49ers ’ hand. Now finally headed to the facility. Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if Aiyuk was an option and he said no. So this will seemingly result in Aiyuk’s release. https://t.co/269oQTmYqd
On Wednesday, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan reiterated that he doesn’t have any expectations for Aiyuk and that he’s moved on from the situation mentally. As Shanahan noted in September, he said that Aiyuk is not an option for the team anymore.
After signing a four-year, $120 million extension, Aiyuk tore his ACL, MCL and meniscus and stopped showing up to the team facility. The 49ers voided $27 million in future guarantees owed to Aiyuk and placed him on the Reserve/Left Squad list last December.
Over the summer, Aiyuk went on social media, calling out Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, effectively burning that bridge. Despite some interest from the Washington Commanders in the offseason, Aiyuk’s actions turned off Washington’s front office.
It seems unlikely that the Rams would go after Aiyuk, but it may be something worth at least exploring, especially considering their current wide receiver situation. Aiyuk hasn’t played since 2024, but he would still be an upgrade over Konata Mumpfield. If the 49ers released him, the Rams would not be responsible for the remainder of his $120 million contract that he signed in 2024. If Aiyuk is cut, he enters the open market as a free agent.
The situation could be similar to how the Rams handled Odell Beckham Jr. in 2021. In 2021, Beckham signed with the Rams on a one-year contract with a base salary of the league minimum, which was $750,000 at the time. The Rams then added up to $4.25 million in performance and postseason incentives.
There is certainly some risk with Aiyuk considering his injury history and that he hasn’t played in two years. Given that he’s burned several bridges with his social media outbursts, that may be a distraction that a team doesn't want to take on midseason.
Still, when Aiyuk was healthy, he was a borderline top-10 wide receiver. He had 1,300 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023. Aiyuk had eight touchdowns the season prior. Until 2024, he had five or more touchdowns in each of his first four seasons.
In 2023, Aiyuk’s 3.02 yards per route run ranked third behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins. His 0.73 EPA per target also ranked second in the NFL.
The off-field stuff is certainly concerning. However, McVay and the Rams have dealt with that before. Jalen Ramsey was considered a locker room cancer before the Rams traded for him. Ramsey became one of the best leaders on defense. When the Rams added Odell Beckham Jr., he had the locker room cancer stigma as well. Beckham played a big role in the Rams’ Super Bowl run as Robert Woods got hurt.
McVay has managed big personalities in the past. Ndamukong Suh was another player that fit that description as well as Baker Mayfield in 2022. If Aiyuk is serious about getting back on the field and returning to play at a high level, it may be a situation to look into.
One of the biggest issues for the Rams at the trade deadline is weighing the potential reward against the cost. When McVay has talked about the possibility of a trade , he’s brought up the team’s lack of draft capital.
“Sometimes you have to really ask yourself what kind of resources are you willing to give up?” McVay said on Monday. “I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost? You have to have another person that's willing to do it and you have to have somebody that you feel like would add a lot of value to your roster, and then what are the resources that you would be willing to give up when you're looking at it as a whole?”
If the 49ers were to simply release Aiyuk, the Rams wouldn’t have to give up anything draft capital-wise. He’s a player that fills a need, wouldn’t cost a lot, and has experience in the system. It doesn’t hurt that he’d also get the opportunity to face the 49ers twice a year, especially if there is still animosity between the two sides.
Again, this isn’t to say that the Rams need to sign Aiyuk, but just that it’s something they should explore if he becomes available. Aiyuk comes with obvious baggage, but he also brings a level of talent that rarely becomes available at this point in the season. The Rams benefitted from a similar situation in 2021 with Beckham. If the Rams can add an upgrade at a position of need without sacrificing draft capital, it's an opportunity worth considering. Aiyuk could be a low-risk, high-reward opportunity that Les Snead and McVay can't afford to overlook.

title: Rams May Have Answer to Return Game Struggles in Preseason Standout
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams released punt returner and wide receiver Alex Bachman on Tuesday, leaving a need at the position. Since making the move, there has been a lot of uncertainty about who will take over the role.
Releasing Bachman was certainly needed as it was time for the Rams to raise the bar from “just catch the punt.” Bachman averaged 5.2 yards per punt return and 22.9 yards per kick return. Bachman offered more reliability than Xavier Smith, but it still wasn’t good enough.
While Konata Mumpfield is listed as the backup punt returner, it’s unlikely that he’ll take that role. Some have brought up Tutu Atwell, but that’s not something that he’s done throughout his career. Atwell returned 10 punts as a rookie in 2021 before getting hurt and then returned just four punts in three years at Louisville.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams could look into trading for Josh Downs or even Chimere Dike if he’s available. At the same time, Downs may cost draft capital that the Rams don’t want to part with and Dike hasn’t offered a lot as a receiver in his career.
Before the Rams make a move, they will likely move forward with players already in the building. One who makes the most sense is wide receiver Brennan Presley.
Presley was signed as an undrafted free agent last year and has had impressive moments in the preseason . Presley had 14 receptions for 125 yards in the preseason with a touchdown this year. During the 2025 preseason, Presley’s 164 receiving yards ranked fourth.
What a catch from Brennan Presley in the endzone! 🤲 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/8zZMy6r9Sa
However, where the Rams will likely utilize Presley is on special teams as a returner. At Oklahoma State, he earned second-team All-Big 12 honors as a kick returner in 2021 and was twice named the Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Week. In 2024, he became the only Power Conference player to record at least 760 receiving yards, 200 kickoff return yards, and 50 rushing yards in a season.
In five years at Oklahoma State , Presley returned 51 punts and 61 kickoffs. However, most of his impact was felt as a returner on kickoffs. His 100-yard kickoff return against Oklahoma in 2021 helped lead the Cowboys to a 37-33 win.
We got Brennan Presley just chillen on the practice squad btw pic.twitter.com/N25BAk2dcr
Presley has had limited return opportunities in the preseason with the Rams. During the 2025 preseason, he had a 38-yard return on a kickoff and then averaged 29.5 yards per kickoff return during the preseason this year. As a punt returner, Presley has just two punt returns the last two years, averaging 5.5 yards per return. It is worth noting that Presley had seven muffed punts at Oklahoma State.
While Presley hasn’t been on the active roster, he has spent the last two years on the practice squad. As the Rams continue to look to improve their special teams, Presley might be exactly what they need. The Rams are currently averaging just 23.5 yards per kickoff return, which ranks 29th in the NFL. While it’s been better over the last four weeks, there is still room for improvement.
The Rams have spent much of the season trying to find answers on special teams. After adding Joshua Karty to help the kickoff coverage last week, they are focusing on the return game this week. Releasing Bachman was another step in working to improve in that facet. Presley’s upside is certainly intriguing, and his experience and speed make him an option worth exploring. His performance in the preseason has at least earned him that opportunity.

title: Myles Garrett's Return to Practice Could Change Everything for Rams
full_text:
For much of the season, the Los Angeles Rams have been waiting to reap the rewards of the big trade they made this offseason when they acquired edge rusher Myles Garrett. After managing knee swelling in training camp and then not playing at 100 percent in Week 1, Garrett has been on injured reserve since. However, Garrett is finally set to return to practice this week .
To be clear, that doesn’t necessarily mean that Garrett will play on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, but it’s also the first good news that the Rams have gotten on him in two months. With that said, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that when Garrett gets on the field for practice, it should all happen quickly, leaving this week in play.
“I want to be careful to even set any sort of expectations. I think taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it,” said head coach Sean McVay on Monday. “That's the right thing for him and to see how he responds. I think it's a real positive that we're starting his clock.”
This is the moment that the Rams have been waiting for. During the offseason, Aaron Donald came out of retirement in large part because he wanted to play alongside Garrett. Those two have yet to play a snap together as Donald didn’t make the trip in Week 1 and Garrett was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 2.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams have been managing injuries to key players, Garrett being the first among them. The Rams have simply been trying to get by as they begin to get healthy and that is finally starting to happen.
Overall, the Rams’ depth has done well, all things considered. Josaiah Stewart was only expected to be a rotational player and has played 67.3 percent of the defensive snaps this season. Wesley Bailey was signed to the roster as an undrafted free agent and has played 30 percent of the defensive snaps, becoming a key part of the pass rush rotation.
Both players have two sacks on the year and Bailey forced a fumble last week against the los Angeles Chargers. However, Stewart’s 11.6 percent pressure rate ranks 70th out of 116 edge rushers. Bailey’s 8.5 percent pressure rate ranks 99th. Stewart and Bailey rank 61st and 78th in pass rush win rate.
The Rams have lacked consistent pressure off of the edge, and Garrett will certainly provide a huge boost to the defense and pass rush in that aspect if he’s healthy. While Jared Verse doesn’t have a sack this season for the Cleveland Browns, it’s fair to wonder what impact a healthy Verse could have had on the Rams’ defense.
Without Garrett, the Rams currently rank 21st in pressure rate, compared to second last year and 14th in 2024. The Rams were ninth in sack rate last year and 19th in 2024 and have dropped down to 27th this season. That’s despite going from the least-blitzing team to 16th. Chris Shula’s blitz rate has increased by nearly 10 percent to help the defense generate pressure on the quarterback.
Shula’s increased blitz rate has been a positive while Garrett has been out, and it will be interesting to see if that continues or if the defense goes back to what it has been the last few years when they’ve been comfortable getting pressure with four.
The Rams traded for Garrett in the offseason with the hope that he could take their defense and pass rush to the next level. Without Garrett, the Rams’ defense ranks sixth in EPA per play and their -0.15 EPA per pass ranks fourth. Garrett will be entering an already good situation without the pressure of having to do everything himself.
Still, this is what the Rams have been waiting for. The Super Bowl team that the Rams built this offseason is finally starting to come together as it gets healthy. They’ll still await the return of Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, and Terrance Ferguson, but having Garrett back in the lineup is a huge first step.
Without Garrett, the Rams have shown that they can play at a high level defensively. However, the Rams traded for Garrett so that the defense could take over games in JanuaryIf he returns healthy and can provide the consistent pressure that the Rams have been missing, this defense could become one of the NFL's most dangerous as they fight for a playoff spot. The Rams can finally start to look like the team they envisioned during the offseason. With Garrett set to return to practice, the Rams are one step closer to seeing that all come together.

title: Sean McVay Hints at Bigger Role for Rams Rookie CJ Daniels
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have not played many of their rookies this season. Their first-round pick has been the emergency quarterback every week and Keagen Trost is a key depth player on the offensive line, but was only just taken off of injured reserve in Week 6. Undrafted free agent Wesley Bailey has been the team’s most productive rookie.
It’s no surprise that the Rams have brought their rookies along slowly. That’s typically how the Rams have handled rookies under Sean McVay outside of a few exceptions. With that said, if last week showed anything, it’s that the rookies may be ready to contribute.
Against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Rams were without tight end Colby Parkinson. While the offense started with 11 personnel, they adjusted to more 13 personnel in the second half, which meant more snaps for Max Klare . Klare finished the game with 25 snaps, 20 of which came after halftime.
For the first 7.5 games, the Rams had deemed Klare not ready. However, Klare was the 12th-best run-blocking tight end in Week 8 and showed that he should have gotten snaps earlier.
With some of the Rams’ issues at wide receiver, it’s fair to wonder whether CJ Daniels is next to see an opportunity. Daniels was a standout in training camp and the preseason. However, he had been inactive for the first six weeks and has played just five snaps combined on offense over the last two games.
Still, on Monday, head coach Sean McVay hinted that Daniels could see more opportunities. “There's a guy in CJ Daniels  that's really done a hell of a job that you're going to see get more opportunities moving forward,” McVay said.
Daniels would fit exactly what the Rams need at wide receiver with Davante Adams out. It’s unrealistic to expect him to replace Adams or solve all of the Rams’ problems in the passing game. However, it could be worth giving him a run in the offense, especially if the Rams don't plan on trading for a wide receiver .
As the game progressed, you really saw Ty Simpson start to get comfortable. With be interested if Rams let him off the reigns a little bit next week. Tight coverage on CJ Daniels and Simpson throws an accurate ball. pic.twitter.com/ZPOUISGzac
He has more size than Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell and can play that “X” wide receiver role. Unlike Atwell, Daniels can win over the middle, and unlike Mumpfield, he provides a bigger target outside the numbers.
Those are things that Daniels showed throughout the offseason and then carried that into the preseason. Daniels had 0.36 targets per route run in the preseason, ranking 15th among wide receivers. He also used his size as he was credited with contested catches on three opportunities.
CJ Daniels with a very nice win on the deep out despite the CB aligning in off cov with outside leverage. Stetson Bennett with some excellent anticipation also. pic.twitter.com/FMk5qnYmiK
The Rams have had problems with their wide receiver depth, and it’s time for them to try something else. Mumpfield is averaging -0.32 EPA per target and has a targeted success rate of 38.1 percent. It simply has not been good enough at that spot.
At some point, the Rams need to find out whether Daniels can translate what he showed throughout the offseason into regular-season success. While they may have waited too long to get Klare involved when the opportunity came up, they shouldn’t make the same mistake with Daniels. The Rams have struggled to find consistent production from their depth receivers, and Daniels brings a different skill set to the offense. If Daniels can prove to be a reliable contributor,it would go a long way toward improving the passing game.

title: Rams Release Alex Bachman as Special Teams Overhaul Continues
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have made another change on special teams as they head into Week 9. On Tuesday, the Rams released wide receiver and kickoff/punt returner Alex Bachman. Over the past several weeks, the Rams have been working to make improvements to their special teams unit, and Bachman being released is the latest indication of that.
Earlier this season, the Rams turned to Bachman after they released wide receiver Xavier Smith from the same role. While Bachman fielded punts without issue, he didn’t offer much as a returner. Among players with at least five punt returns this season, Bachman averaged just 5.2 yards per return, which ranked 31st. At some point, the Rams needed to raise the bar from ‘just fielding punts’. Bachman averaged just 22.9 yards per kick return, ranking 62nd out of 75 qualifying returners.
Despite not giving up a long punt or kick return, the Rams lost 3.6 in special teams EPA on Sunday against the Chargers. Bachman gained zero yards on a punt return in which there looked to be space to head upfield.
Alex Bachman gained 0 yards on this play, and the ball is in his hands in this screenshot. How? pic.twitter.com/QYDnMGkvYq
It’s unclear where the Rams turn to next at returner. Jordan Whittington was the only other listed kick returner alongside Bachman, and the Rams just placed running back Dean Connors on injured reserve. At punt returner, Konata Mumpfield was technically the backup to Bachman. However, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams make a move this week for a returner.
Given the struggles on special teams this season, the Rams have made a conscious effort to improve. Last week, they signed Joshua Karty to help on kickoffs and also brought in Jon Rhattigan, who is a special teams player. Despite those changes, the Rams still lost 3.6 in special teams EPA without giving up a long return or missing any field goals last week.
Special Teams EPA through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/jkmVWblN8Z
In a corresponding move to releasing Bachman, the Rams signed cornerback Cam Lampkin from the practice squad to the active roster. After releasing Nyzier Fourqurean last week , the Rams have signed him back to the practice squad as well. The Rams also released linebacker Garrett Nelson from the practice squad.
Head coach Sean McVay has made it clear that the Rams aren’t satisfied with their special teams unit. The Rams have spent much of the season trying to find answers on special teams, and releasing Bachman is the latest attempt to raise the standard.

title: The Case For and Against the Rams' Top NFL Trade Deadline Targets
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is just a week away and there are several names that have been connected to the Los Angeles Rams. It’s still unclear whether the Rams will opt to make a move , and there are positives and negatives to each player they could consider. Let’s break down some top potential targets and make a case for why each would be a fit and why the Rams shouldn’t trade for them.
The Case For: There is no doubt that the Rams need help at wide receiver and Josh Downs would be a great fit . While he may not be the “X” that the Rams need with Davante Adams out, he would fit in perfectly alongside Adams and Puka Nacua. The Rams need a reliable target with speed and someone who can create underneath and find the soft spot in zones.Downs is a great separator, ranking fourth in first downs per route run on third and fourth down last season. His skillset is similar to Jamison Crowder, who had success in Sean McVay’s offense.
The Case Against: While Downs had a strong first and second season, he only had 566 yards last year and has 30 receptions for 330 yards this year. His size makes him less valuable as a blocker, which McVay does ask of his wide receivers. Despite having an opportunity, Downs has never been more than a WR3 in the Colts’ offense.
The Case For: Thomas is a former first-round pick and had over 1,200 yards as a rookie with 10 touchdowns. With Adams out, Thomas would slot right into the “X” receiver role and then would provide a bigger vertical threat once Adams does return. The Rams would have multiple years of team control remaining, including the ability to exercise his fifth-year option. He’d be someone the Rams could build the wide receiver room around alongside Nacua over the next few seasons.
The Case Against: While Thomas had over 1,200 yards as a rookie, he has just 824 yards since. He’s completely fallen out of favor and has struggled to get comfortable in a Liam Coen offense that is very similar to McVay’s. Thomas has struggled with drops and has had a low targeted success rate over the last two years. It’s possible that Thomas just needs a change of scenery, but the Rams might not be the right fit.
The Case For: It wouldn’t be a bad idea for the Rams to make a move for a nose tackle. Poona Ford is out for the season and the impact of his loss will be felt in the run game. Stewart would give the Rams exactly what they are missing without Ford: a run-stopping nose tackle in the middle of the defensive line.
The Case Against: Stewart would certainly fit a need, but the cost may simply be too high. A team would need to take on $6.7 million in salary to trade for Stewart. As it stands, the Rams only have $8,000 in cap space. They have some flexibility to open up some money, but $6.7 million would be a lot.
The Case For: There is no doubt that the Rams need special teams help and Chimere Dike is one of the best returners in the NFL. Dike is averaging 12.5 yards per punt return, which ranks 17th in the NFL. For reference, Alex Bachman averaged 5.2 yards per punt return. Dike kills two birds with one stone, adding wide receiver depth and providing a threat as a returner.
The Case Against: While Dike got more involved in the Tennessee Titans’ offense last week, he hasn’t provided much as a wide receiver consistently in his career. He had 423 yards total as a rookie and has just 124 yards this season. This isn’t like the Seattle Seahawks trading for Rashid Shaheed last year. If Dike offered more as a receiver, a trade could make sense. However, the Rams can’t afford to give up draft capital for strictly a returner.
The case For: The Rams have struggled getting to the quarterback this season. Their pass rush currently ranks 21st in pressure rate and 27th in sack rate. Josaiah Stewart hasn’t stepped up in the way that some expected and Wesley Bailey is still growing. Mack is a more experienced player and still had a 12.7 percent pressure rate this season, which is higher than Stewart and Bailey.
The Case Against: Mack would be an improvement over Stewart and Bailey, but once Myles Garrett returns from injury, he would be a rotational player. The Rams need a more productive pass rush, but it’s unlikely that Mack is the missing piece.

title: With Porter Injury, Raiders Could Get Extra Look at Promising Rookie
full_text:
This weekend, the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders travel back to the Bay Area to face the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers. It will be an emotional weekend for Raider Nation, especially those remaining in Oakland, as the team returns for the first time since their final game there nearly seven years ago.
As the Raiders prepare to face one of the best teams in the NFL after a bye week, they could be without No. 2 cornerback Darien Porter, who injured his groin early in their win over the New York Jets.
Porter did not practice on Wednesday, as head coach Klint Kubiak called him “day-to-day.”
“I think it's just we’re just taking it day to day, and he’s making progress,” Kubiak told reporters.
With Porter absent from practice and the possibility of him missing Sunday’s game, two rookie cornerbacks could get more opportunities to play opposite Eric Stokes.
Fifth-round rookie Hezekiah Masses has had an up-and-down rookie season, but the flashes have been encouraging when he has seen the field. It is hard to imagine him not having a major role in the defense in 2027. However, the Raiders need to begin viewing what they have in fourth-round selection Jermod McCoy as a unique case in these circumstances.
The former Tennessee Volunteer standout was once considered a top-15 prospect from this past spring’s NFL Draft. However, red flags around his major injury last January led to a shocking fall out of the first 100 picks, and the Raiders took an opportunity to bolster their defensive back room with a terrific talent who would need patience to get his feet under him.
McCoy played roughly 30 snaps against the Jets after Porter went down, and Kubiak said on Monday that it's all about getting better for McCoy, and I couldn’t agree more based on what I observed from Sunday’s game. However, there’s a sense that McCoy’s opportunity for more playing time could come this weekend at Levi’s Stadium.
While McCoy may get an extended look on Sunday, the focus for the rookie and the Raiders has not changed. Kubiak said as much on Wednesday, crediting defensive backs coach Joe Woods for being key in the growth of the young secondary pieces, including McCoy.
“Whether he was getting no reps or now getting more, it’s getting better at your position and being really intentional about your individual and being a factor on special teams, being great with your eyes and your keys and your technique, and those are things that make Joe Woods such a special coach, and we’re so happy to have Joe,” Kubiak said.
“And those DBs are so happy to have him as a mentor and as a coach. A guy with so much experience that helps him play.”
McCoy won’t yet be the star-studded talent he was as a sophomore in Knoxville, Tennessee. He is basically learning how to get comfortable on an active gridiron against live fire for the first time in almost two years. These things take time, but having a coaching staff that is disciplined in making sure young players have all the resources available to them is a key step in their development next week, the rest of the season, and the coming years.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Raiders' Matchup vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' Week 8 win over the New York Jets was just what they needed in between multiple games against the league's best teams. They are back to the grind as they prepare for another road challenge this week.
Las Vegas has already surpassed its win total from last season, but faces a three-game stretch that will leave little doubt about the direction of the season. Sunday's slate against San Francisco will be followed by games against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos.
The Raiders sit at 4-4, their best record this deep into the regular season in years. They look to build on their strong start by upsetting the 49ers this Sunday. Las Vegas will face a much more talented team this Sunday than they did last Sunday.
Still, if they perform well enough, there is always a chance the Raiders can leave San Francisco with a win. On the other hand, beating a team like the 49ers may take more than the Raiders currently have on their roster.
Sunday will be one of the Raiders' toughest games this season. However, not knowing which Raiders team will show up makes it a more interesting matchup than it may seem.
Below are the storylines I am watching the most in Las Vegas' Week 9 matchup against the 49ers.
The Raiders' defensive backfield has struggled over the past two weeks. After Matthew Stafford picked the unit apart, Geno Smith and the Jets' wide receivers did too. Las Vegas played man defense most of Sunday, which left veteran cornerback Eric Stokes on an island with the Jets' best receivers.
The Jets made the Raiders pay, targeting Stokes early and often. The veteran made several plays that helped the Raiders win, but his overall performance raised questions heading into Week 9. Stokes is the team's best cornerback. They need him to figure it out soon.
The Raiders may be without Darien Porter, which would add more to all of the defense's plate. Still, Stokes' performance will be the unit's most important on Sunday. Las Vegas will need all hands on deck against Brock Purdy and a well-coached 49ers team.
Against the Jets, Las Vegas largely used Washington to run the ball and Ashton Jeanty as the team's pass-catching option out of the backfield. It will be interesting to see if the Raiders take a similar approach to how they use their running backs on Sunday against San Francisco.
Washington's second half changed the game's trajectory for the Raiders, who trailed by almost double digits at halftime. One storyline I'll watch most closely is the Raiders' usage of Washington and Jeanty. How often Las Vegas hands off to Jeanty will be interesting to watch.
The Raiders may have made strides toward figuring out how to fix their ground game. However, their Week 9 game against the 49ers will give a better idea of whether or not that is the case. Las Vegas has yet to beat a team with a winning record. That could change this Sunday on the road.
Another storyline I will be watching is simply the fact that both teams have so much history individually and together, as the rivalry goes back decades. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak shared his memories of the Raiders from childhood, when his dad coached.
"I remember definitely just overall with the Raiders, every time, being in Denver, everybody’s walking around with Raider Hater shirts on, and the town has a buzz to it. And I remember one specific game. I think it was in the snow, but Jerry Rice and Tim Brown, and just as a young kid, getting to watch on the sideline, those are your heroes," Kubiak said on Wednesday.
"I just kind of remember the snow falling down in the stadium and watching those guys run on the field. And Tim Brown's got his finger tape rolled up, and then that week in my game, I’m rolling up my fingers. Tim Brown doesn’t need any gloves, neither do I. So, that really stands out, and I don’t remember your other question.”
Las Vegas looks to make it two in a row.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Upon Further Review: Grading Every Raiders Rookie Draft Pick
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.--The Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) face the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) this weekend.
But with the NFL season halfway over and the NFL trade deadline on the horizon, I decided to put the 2026 rookie class under the microscope, and I asked some of my NFL buddies to help me evaluate them.
I will never forget the first time I had a test that was graded on a curve. I had never seen that before, and I was in an advanced high school class, so I was grateful.
I had studied and was sure I had failed, only to find out my low, and, to be honest, terrible grade was higher, significantly higher because of a curve.
I learned an important lesson that day: the terms the grader uses matter as much as what they grade.
Several years ago, I asked four NFL executives to explain their paradigm for evaluating and grading rookies, and then combined them into my scale.
Let me break it down for you.
The reality is that not all NFL rookies are created equal, and whether you are picked and how much you're paid does matter. But you are always looking for the obscure player who becomes the unexpected dog.
First-round QBs are not the norm (explained later), and injuries can change things, as you will see with one Raiders rookie.
There are consistent sets of expectations that are tied to draft capital, that pretty consistently remain close or the same among all of the NFL franchises, and they break down into five distinct tiers:
• Top 10 Picks: These folks, fairly or not, have enormous immediate impact expectations. Expected to be immediate day-one starters and franchise cornerstones. The exception is quarterbacks, who are sometimes given time to sit if a veteran is in place.
• One NFL GM told me, “You fail here, and your franchise is set back for five years. You can’t fail. If you are picking here and you aren’t willing to bet your (private part) that you are correct, you trade out." • Rest of Round 1 (Picks 11–32): Expected to start by midseason or contribute heavily in key packages, eventually proving to be above-average starters. • Another GM said, “A first-round failure outside of the top ten still hurts. It is brutal. The first round is a place I never gamble. I’ve had success because I will not reach; I pick, move up, down, or out, but I never guess.” He has won big in the NFL. • Rounds 2–3 (Day 2): Expected to be core rotational contributors immediately and locked-in starters by year two. • An NFL GM described this group as, “Your bread and butter. I love the percentages of these guys that get second contracts, and the best teams make their living here.” He added, “There are so many bad drafting teams in our league now that these picks are like gold, and you get first-round guys every year here, if there is enough talent, to make a living.”
• Another GM said, “I would almost rather have more day two picks than day one. We have such a great NFL Draft team, and you get the guys who you win with, don’t have to pay too much, and they all are motivated because they think, and many know, they should have gone day one.” • Rounds 4–5 (Early Day 3): Expected to make the 53-man roster, play key special teams roles, and provide positional depth, though high-value positions like running back or interior offensive line can start earlier. • Per one GM, “Bad drafting in round one should be, and usually is, immediate grounds for getting fired. Great picks in rounds four and five is where you become a legend. The best organizations spend lots of money and find the guys here that bring big wins.” He added, “On our team we often say you can win praise in round one, but rounds four and five are where you build dynasties.”
• Rounds 6–7 (Late Day 3): Considered developmental projects or special teamers, where simply winning a roster spot over an undrafted free agent is a success. You hope these guys make the practice squad, and your coaches can turn them into something. • One GM said, “This is where the assistant position coaches, the young QC (quality control) kids get noticed. Getting picked here is basically a UDFA who does one thing really well, but not multiple so he moves up. Young coaches find their way here.”
The Indiana Hoosier has the Raiders brass more excited about him today than the day they picked him. He is impossible to grade, as he is sitting behind Kirk Cousins. But the young man that NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect of the last four years has met or exceeded every thought and hope, and as a man who covered Matthew Stafford in his rookie year, I can tell you he looks, acts, and performs like the superstar the Raiders think he can be.
Already a starter, he is way ahead of schedule. He has tremendous physical skills, but his ability to take expert coaching has set him apart.
The raw youngster showed some interesting skills, but was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August with an Achilles injury.
One of the smartest football players in a rookie class made up of smart football players, he has already started, and not because of an emergency with an injury. Can play all five offensive line positions and is the absolute real deal.
According to the grading criteria, he is right on target, and when you add his recovery from a major injury, the man everyone had as the best CB in the NFL Draft is on track.
Already a major contributor, Mike Washington Jr. (MWJ) may be the biggest steal of this draft class early and is a rising star who plays with no fear, other than what his size, speed, and power inflict when he comes at you in a downfield, north-south posture.
He made the 53-man roster and has shown brief flashes. He has impressed people with his ability to take coaching and to be coachable. He appears right on schedule, and based on the criteria, he is doing what is expected.
The young man isn’t a finished product and shouldn’t be. But he has started half of the Raiders' games and is a major contributor. He is far ahead of expectations, showing developing skill sets that speak highly of the coaching he is getting and his football acumen for taking it.
The sixth-rounder has played in seven regular-season games, is a key contributor, and, while not showing the flash we saw in the preseason, his presence and impact are evident. The growth needed to make the step into the starting lineup is clear. Still, nothing suggests anything other than top upside, but he has already overachieved based on the grading criteria.
The young man has shown some interesting flashes with his skill set, but as a seventh-round pick, he is on the practice squad, and the outlook for his future is very bright. Reps on the scout team are vital, but the hope and expectation are that he will take a significant step this offseason.

title: 3 Key Insights From NFL Sources on How Raiders Can Beat 49ers
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) are going back to the Bay this weekend, where they face their old Bay rival, who, like the Raiders, moved away to Santa Clara, to take on the San Francisco 49ers (6-1)
This game will bring a lot of emotion for the fans , as well as Klint Kubiak, who has family and friends in the 49ers organization.
Mike Shanahan had a major impact on Klint’s life, and the current 49ers head coach, Kyle, is not just a friend but a dear friend. Kubiak spoke of those relationships earlier today.
“Just really fortunate to grow up in that environment. I didn’t know it at the time, but I got to be exposed to a lot of football at a young age, and I’m very grateful for that, myself and my brothers.”
I have already told you the biggest story on the year that is being ignored, but a win on Sunday could top it for the head coach. Klint and 49ers OC Klay are not just brothers, but close friends. For the Raiders coach, his brother is the gold standard in life and football, and he wasn’t afraid to brag about his brother today.
“Yeah, I got to work with him side by side for an entire year. We were in college together and then we went our separate ways and got married, and it was just so great reconnecting with him and seeing the type of husband that he was and seeing how hard he worked and how smart he was, things that I already knew. But when you’re kind of in the fire with your brother every day, it definitely builds a closer bond.”
The reality is that both teams might be close and have deep ties, but once the ball is kicked off, they want to whip the other, and while the niceties are bigger than the game, the focus is the game.
The most important ingredient for a win in the NFL is one I have discussed many times and that a long-time coach shared with me.
You can’t ever forget the "Rule of Five." In the football world, a game is considered unwinnable if either team loses this key statistical battle. This rule involves sacks and turnovers. Two stats, while vastly different, are eerily similar in their impact on a football game.
For example, should the Raiders achieve two sacks of Brock Purdy while allowing one of Kirk Cousins, they have a net score of plus one. If they force three turnovers and allow only one, their score improves to plus three.
Thus, they would achieve a plus-three score for the day. The Raiders aim to accomplish a plus-five ratio in every game. On average, teams that attain the Rule of Five win 87% of their NFL games.
The 49ers are the best team the Raiders have faced all year, and I reached out to some NFL sources about what would be the epic upset of the first nine weeks of the NFL season, should the Raiders pull it off.
Each offered a different nugget on what the Raiders would need to do to win, based on their knowledge of both teams.
​Source No. 1: “The biggest key is that Raiders pass rush. Heavy pressure and blitzing in the second half have disrupted Brock Purdy's rhythm, forcing hasty decisions and throwing off the timing of the intermediate passing game.”
​Source No. 2: “The Niners opponents have capitalized on self-inflicted mistakes, taking advantage of costly turnovers and undisciplined defensive penalties that extend drives.”
​Source No. 3: “What stands out to be is how well coached, deep, and talented San Francisco is, and team’s like that aren’t going to just get beat, no matter who they play. The teams that stay patient on offense have succeeded by exploiting line-of-scrimmage injuries and making second-half adjustments, wearing down the defense late in games when key playmakers are banged up. So, it is an easy plan if you have the players, run the ball and pray.”
