title: DeeJay Dallas Decision Leaves Vikings With an Obvious Roster Cut to Make in Week 9
full_text:
The Vikings were in an interesting position when it comes to a player who has been a contributor at running back. DeeJay Dallas has been bounced around between the practice squad and the active roster since signing a one-year, $411,300 contract for the 2026 NFL season.
Dallas signed to the 53-man roster two weeks after joining the practice squad, but was surprisingly released in October and signed back to the practice squad. Since then, he has been elevated to the main roster every week .
However, the Vikings can no longer elevate him after doing so three times before Week 9. Minnesota needed to decide whether to leave him on the practice squad or sign him to the 53-man roster to continue using him on game day. On Wednesday, they made their decision by officially signing him to the main roster.
The #Vikings have signed RB DeeJay Dallas ( @DallasDeejay ) to the 53-man roster and T Corey Robinson II ( @coreyrobinson76 ) to the practice squad. pic.twitter.com/z340dwDyb5
After the Purple and Gold signed him to the 53-man roster, another player needs to be released, with one name standing out above the rest in Week 9: rookie RB Demond Claiborne.
Dallas has played in every Vikings game this season, so it would've been surprising if he wasn't signed to the 53-man roster at some point. He has played 63 offensive snaps and 123 special teams snaps, showing his value to the team in more ways than one.
There are some candidates to be let go now that Dallas's spot is secure. Players like safety Jakobe Thomas and defensive lineman Elijah Williams have been inactive all season , meaning they wouldn't change what has been happening on the field.
Still, neither as big a cut candidate as Claiborne, who has been inactive and has been losing offensive snaps to Dallas. That said, Minnesota is potentially worried he will be signed by another team before he can join the practice squad.
Nevertheless, Claiborne has six rushing attempts for 13 yards this season. He hasn't played since Week 5 and has played 18 offensive and four special teams snaps this season. He has not been a player who offers a lot of value on the 53-man roster, and the Vikings shouldn't be worried about losing him.
Holding on to Claiborne out of fear of losing him would be keeping a roster spot hostage. If he is signed to the practice squad, he could be elevated up to three times this season before he would need to be signed back to the 53.
Right now, the Vikings have several players who are regulars on the inactive list, but only Claiborne makes the most sense. He and Dallas play the same position, and Minnesota has already shown its preference between the two running backs this season.

title: Vikings' Uphill Battle for a Potential Kyler Murray Trade Solution Officially Steepens
full_text:
As Week 9 of the NFL season begins, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray continues to deal with a hamstring issue that could prevent him from suiting up against the Bills on Monday Night Football. But even if he can play, Murray has struggled as a quarterback this season, completing 64.9% of his passes while averaging only 170.3 passing yards per game. He has thrown five touchdowns to three interceptions while being sacked 15 times in six games played.
Whether it's due to his injury or inconsistent play, Murray has given the Vikings reason to consider outside arms.
If the Vikings are in the QB trade market, though, their lack of urgency could force the team to redirect their search after the news that the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Wednesday.
Trade: The #Ravens are finalizing a trade for former #AZCardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, per me and @AdamSchefter , filling the void left by the injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler “Snoop” Huntley. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend. pic.twitter.com/RWhT1LQ2fc
The Vikings probably don't feel bad about starting veteran backup Carson Wentz, but he isn't a quarterback who will provide a spark for Minnesota's offense. He may complete only 59% of his passes this year, but he has yet to throw an interception while throwing three touchdowns.
Wentz has a 3-3 record as a starter since joining the Vikings, but Minnesota could prove they are all-in on this season by making a trade for a quarterback who can ignite the offense and help put points on the scoreboard.
Brissett being off the market isn't a big deal, but it makes competing for other quarterbacks more challenging, whether that's Kirk Cousins, Justin Herbert or someone else. Now, the next wave of signal-callers to be traded will command a higher value based on how many teams need help at that position.
If nothing, the Vikings could use some help until Murray is ready to return to the field. If Minnesota doesn't acquire a quarterback soon, they could have to roll with Wentz as the starter and Max Brosmer as his backup, with no emergency third passer on the 53-man roster or practice squad.
The Vikings are 6-1 this season and on top of the NFC North. Every team in the division this year is playing good football and has a winning record heading into Week 9. The Purple and Gold need to give themselves the best chance to win every week, and that includes Monday night's game against the Bills.
If the Vikings are interested in acquiring a quarterback before the trade deadline, the team needs to act quickly and with purpose. The longer Minnesota waits, the more likely it becomes that it will overpay for a player who wasn't among its top options.

title: Vikings Week 9 Mailbag: Run Game Concerns, Trade Deadline Plans, Wes Phillips & More
full_text:
Only your beloved Vikings could be 6-1 while surrounded by a level of concern usually reserved for winless squads. The truth is, the Vikings’ defense is far too elite to be wasted by the kind of offensive performance we witnessed in Detroit this past Sunday, and the increase in pressure from the fanbase is more than warranted.
I asked you for your thoughts and questions on X, and as always, you did not disappoint. Let’s dive in.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
Another year, another letdown after an offseason hyping up a new and improved run game. Assistant head coach Frank Smith seemed like the man to fix it, implementing an outside zone scheme that should allow his backs to turn the corner for chunk yardage. The problem? It’s failing miserably.
The Vikings currently rank at the bottom of the league in advanced rushing analytics.
The Vikings' offense has many issues, but the run game remains problematic. The team talked about prioritizing it for the 4th straight offseason. Tons of changes over time: RBs, iOL, TE, OL coach, etc. Right now, they rank 31st in rushing success rate and 27th in EPA/play.
Two issues stand out more than most: inconsistent run blocking and the actual talent in the room.
Aaron Jones deserves a ton of respect for the effort he showed early this season, but he is simply not as explosive as he once was. Jordan Mason is very good in certain situations but is not an every-down back . Unfortunately, the team has built its current offensive identity around the run despite the lack of talent, and it doesn’t have a quarterback who makes the passing game a better alternative.
Minnesota’s decision to punt on a running back until late in the draft has proven to haunt them, with rookie Demond Claiborne a non-factor . A swing at Emmett Johnson or Mike Washington Jr. early on Day 3 could have provided the spark they needed.
This one is complicated because we don’t have a full understanding of everything Phillips is responsible for as the Vikings’ offensive coordinator. Kevin O’Connell has made it clear that he values Phillips as a key part of his game planning and decision-making process.
At the same time, he’s not the one calling the plays or making final personnel decisions. Getting rid of him may treat a symptom, but not the cause.
If the Vikings are to make a move at offensive coordinator next season, it would likely be with the understanding that O’Connell would give up play-calling duties, and I’m not sure I see that happening. It seems that KOC and his support staff may be attached at the hip, for better or worse.
This take is becoming increasingly popular, and there’s plenty of sound logic behind it.
The Vikings’ offense needs a ton of help if it is going to morph into a contender-level unit. Quarterback play is a massive concern, but there aren’t many upgrades easily available. The interior offensive line is inconsistent, to say the least, but the best available guard was already traded to Seattle last week . Then, there’s the running game, as we’ve discussed.
There’s a reason Jonathan Taylor has topped nearly every Vikes fan’s wishlist , but the biggest hurdles are still to come.
The Vikings enter next offseason with many of their key starters set to hit free agency. Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason, T.J. Hockenson, Andrew Van Ginkel, Blake Cashman, Isaiah Rodgers, and Jalen Redmond will all either need to be re-signed or replaced. The hard truth is that’s incredibly difficult to do after trading premium draft capital for a player with a heavy cap hit.
We have no idea what general manager Nolan Teasley thinks of this team long-term, so anything is on the table. Whatever he does, it needs to lead to results sooner rather than later. Vikings fans are sick of waiting.
Reminder that it’s been nearly SEVEN years since the Vikings won a playoff game and nearly FORTY years since they’ve won multiple playoff games in a single season. This fanbase deserves better.
The two positions that come with the highest upside are easily QB and RB.
The problem is, I’m not sure if addressing just one will actually solve the offensive inconsistencies. The dream scenario is for the Vikings to somehow land Jonathan Taylor and Kirk Cousins, but that outcome will likely remain a fantasy . The good news is the team seems to be exploring an upgrade at RB, but Taylor may be out of their price range.
My gut tells me we’ll either see a big move or nothing. A backup guard or blocking tight end doesn't really improve the chances of this offense playing at a championship level and only takes away future capital from Teasley’s first draft class. Now the new GM has a choice: go all in or plan for the future.

title: Vikings Suddenly Have a New Star RB Trade Target Who Isn't Jonathan Taylor in Week 9
full_text:
Fans are waiting for the Vikings to make a needle-moving deal before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline . The backfield is among general manager Nolan Teasley's biggest concerns, and many Vikings believers are dreaming of Colts star rusher Jonathan Taylor coming to the team. That said, Indianapolis won't deal Taylor unless the price is right , which could force teams like Minnesota to pivot.
That said, another running back might have recently become available.
A fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Braelon Allen has been impressive lately for the Jets . In three of his last four games, Allen has surpassed 100 rushing yards. He is averaging five yards per carry this season while also catching 17 of 22 targets for 81 yards.
The Jets' running back situation should interest the Vikings because Allen's breakout performance could make Breece Hall available through trade. He could be significantly less expensive to trade for than Taylor, while providing Minnesota with a legitimate starting threat.
The Jets are getting great production from a running back who is cheaper and younger than Hall. Allen is only 22 years old and is thriving in games where he plays more than 40 offensive snaps, which should force him to be on the field more often.
Allen has an excellent 82.4 Pro Football Focus grade this season that ranks him eighth out of 47 qualifying running backs. He has forced 26 missed tackles as a runner and averaged 3.6 yards after contact, making him one of the most effective running backs in the league.
Hall is still 25 years old and could be a great asset for a team like the Vikings. He played in the first three games of the season for the Jets before suffering a groin injury during practice that has kept him out of action since.
On Tuesday, Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich talked with the media, and The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported that he's "assuming" Hall will return as the starter when he is healthy . While that sounds good for Hall, it lacks the authority of a response that confirms his status in the offense.
Hall has a 63.9 PFF grade this season and is averaging 3.2 yards per carry. On paper, it seems obvious that the Jets should move forward with Allen and test the trade market to see what kind of compensation they can get for Hall. Still, it was only a year ago that Hall hit the 1,000-yard mark for the first time, giving the Vikings good reason to see if a fresh start can get him back to that level.
He could also help with the Vikings' passing struggles, as Hall has caught all 10 of his targets for 102 receiving yards this season. For reference, Minnesota's RBs have combined for 21 catches and 132 receiving yards as of Week 9.
Additionally, Hall would be more than a rental. According to Spotrac , he's under contract with cap hits of $14.5 million and $15.5 million in 2027 and 2028 , respectively, with his deal including a potential out between those seasons that would result in just $3 million of dead money.
Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley needs to start a conversation with Jets GM Darren Mougey, who is good friends with head coach Kevin O'Connell. Hall would be an excellent addition for the Purple and Gold this season and should be explored as soon as possible, especially if landing Taylor becomes more of a pipe dream.

title: 2 Season-Saving Vikings Trades Nolan Teasley Needs (And 2 More He Doesn't)
full_text:
Despite the tough loss to the Lions, the Vikings still figure to be buyers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline . How aggressive they'll be is another question, but the issues on offense aren't going away , and it may take a trade or two to fix them.
Here are two deals Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley should pull off and two more he needs to pump the brakes on.
The Vikings were reportedly in on guard Quenton Nelson—until they weren't—so it's reasonable to think they're still in the market for a guard ahead of the deadline. Eagles guard Landon Dickerson checks many of the boxes Nelson did (Pro Bowl resume, flexibility for long-term options) and is two years younger than the former Colt.
Left guard Joe Huber has filled in admirably for the injured Donovan Jackson, but adding one of the top guards in the NFL from a team clearly falling into disarray would be a huge boost for the lackluster Vikings offense. Right guard Will Fries has also played well below his contract and could be moved on from relatively easily in 2027, paving the way for a Jackson-Dickerson interior.
Dickerson's price, both in draft capital and contract cost, would be very palatable for the Vikings thanks to his low base salary in 2026 and their extra third-rounder from the Jonathan Greenard deal.
Clearly, Jonathan Taylor is the big fish in the running back pond , but it's feeling more and more likely that the Vikings aren't willing to meet the Colts' steep asking price. It's been reported that Indy is looking for first-round value for their star running back, but Teasley may not be willing to part with that for a running back on the wrong side of 27.
If Minnesota wants to add some juice to their backfield without breaking the bank, New England's TreVeyon Henderson fits the bill. Last year's second-round pick had nearly 1,000 yards on the ground but has since been relegated to RB3 after some poor play and a rash of health issues. If the Patriots decide he's no longer part of their future, they could look to move him for help elsewhere.
Henderson could be the home-run threat that the Vikings desperately need. He ripped off four rushes of over 40 yards in 2025 and would be the explosive runner to pair with chain movers Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. Minnesota already tried shopping Jauan Jennings to the 49ers , so shipping him off to New England—who currently has A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs all on ice—could be a win for both sides.
Hall has quickly become a popular consolation prize of the Taylor sweepstakes, but his fit and production don't really match what his asking price would be from New York. Assuming the Vikings find Taylor too pricey, they should feel similarly about Hall, who is younger but also doesn't boast the same impressive resume.
Despite their insistence that he isn't available, if teams start calling offering second-round value for Hall, it's going to be hard for the Jets to hang up the phone. But unlike Taylor, who is near the top of the leaderboards every season, Hall has just one 1,000-yard campaign to his name.
Most teams could probably connect the dots that sporting a jersey with J-E-T-S across the front probably has something to do with his lack of elite numbers. But at the same time, there have been few instances in which Hall has elevated a bad Jets team in the same way Taylor has carried the Colts for years.
If the Vikings are out on Taylor, Hall shouldn't be a conversation either.
The Vikings' quarterback play hasn't been good enough. Kyler Murray continues to miss receivers, take bad sacks and hasn't elevated the offense in any meaningful way. Despite his flaws, adding an outside hire at the deadline probably doesn't solve much either.
Cousins is familiar with the system and has been playing lights-out football in 2026. That's sort of a big problem, though, because it means the Raiders have little reason to deal him, especially for just a Day 3 pick. So would the Vikings really send, say, a third-round pick, for a 38-year old quarterback who still would likely need a few weeks to reacclimate to Kevin O'Connell's offense?
Trading for Cousins, or any quarterback, for that matter , just seems out of the question for an offense that can't afford to wait around a month while their new signal-caller learns the scheme. Cousins could certainly do it quicker, but the best option if Murray gets pulled is probably backup Carson Wentz.
He's not an elevator, but Wentz gets the ball out on time and accurately, and that's all fans are asking for at this point.

title: Ranking Vikings' Best QB Options If Kyler Murray Can't Face Bills in Week 9
full_text:
Playing quarterback for the Vikings is not for the faint of heart, and Kyler Murray’s short tenure with the team he grew up rooting for has been anything but easy so far.
Sure, he's playing quarterback for a 6-1 team, but on-field struggles and time lost to a concussion have only complicated matters. Now, Murray has a hamstring injury after a performance in Detroit that had many fans already asking for a QB swap.
If he can't play against the Bills on Monday, they may get their wish.
Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell spoke to the media on Monday and confirmed that Murray is still dealing with a sore hamstring , adding that they are going through a “full (evaluation),” and he will provide updates later in the week.
Kevin O'Connell provides updates on QB Kyler Murray, OT Christian Darrisaw, and S Theo Jackson. pic.twitter.com/hYX9lNT6fl
But what happens if Murray is unable to play?
Let’s break down the best paths the Vikings can take at the QB spot if they need to make a shift against the Bills.
I’ll start by saying that the likelihood of this happening is incredibly low, but since Brosmer's on the roster , we need to discuss it.
The former Gopher won over fans and the franchise alike with a surprising performance during training camp and preseason games in 2025, ultimately securing a roster spot. One thing definitely not in their forecast was Brosmer hitting the field in his rookie season. Unfortunately, injury luck had other plans, and Brosmer had to play before he was even close to ready.
ERNEST JONES 84-YARD PICK-SIX MINvsSEA on FOX/FOX One https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/VA6dvef6w6
Brosmer totaled 328 passing yards, four interceptions, a whopping 14 sacks taken, and zero touchdowns in seven appearances and two starts last season. His most noteworthy performance was a Christmas-night victory over the Lions, where Brosmer threw for three net passing yards.
O’Connell clearly wants to see what Brosmer has long-term, but there is no way the team can give him serious playing time this season.
I’d say this is the likeliest outcome we’ll see on Monday night if Murray is ruled out.
Wentz is a relatively steady hand who is familiar with the offense and, most importantly, feeds Justin Jefferson. The wideout’s lowest yardage total in seven games with Wentz was a 55-yard monsoon performance in Chicago in Week 2. Jefferson has already had fewer than 55 yards three times this season with Murray at QB; however, it's worth noting that Jefferson did leave the Week 3 win over the Bucs with an ankle injury in the first quarter.
JUSTIN JEFFERSON ON A FREE PLAY GBvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZKnmvwBDtR
If Wentz stays healthy, limits turnovers, and gets the ball to his playmakers, we may see a very different passing game on Monday night. Wentz may be an unlikely hero to rescue the Vikings’ sinking offense and carry it to the Lombardi, but they desperately need improvement at this point.
I don’t think the Raiders are in any rush to trade away Kirk Cousins with a 4-4 record, especially when he’s having quite the season, but having number-one pick Fernando Mendoza in the wings means it's worth a call. Cousins’ familiarity and success with O’Connell’s offense and Minnesota’s weapons make this an ideal fix for their 2026 QB woes.
Kirk Cousins has the Raiders back on top in a high-scoring game LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jQI5vkJ8Xb
I’d put the likelihood of this happening at around 5%, as the Raiders would be embracing the unknown by shifting to Mendoza this early. Minnesota is running out of time and options to fix their QB situation, with the Nov. 10 trade deadline quickly approaching .
If Minnesota is going to make a move, Cousins is the best fit, and now is the best time.

title: Vikings Week 9 Stock Report: James Pierre Among Risers, Brett Thorson Falls
full_text:
Like the Vikings' offense, this season is about to become an absolute roller coaster, with the Bills on deck in Week 9 and the trade deadline to follow . While some Vikings have helped to steady the ship, others are making progress harder.
The Lions handed the Vikings their first loss of the year, and there was plenty of blame to go around. From missed tackles to a dud of a day on offense, it just wasn't in the cards.
So, after the defeat, who is seeing their stock rise, and who might be in for a long season?
Pierre notched his second interception of the season last Sunday and handed Jared Goff his first of the year. After ranking as their No. 2 cornerback in 2025, Pierre is once again a Pro Football Focus darling in 2026. He has an impressive 75.9 grade this season, ranking him 12th out of 102 qualifying cornerbacks.
James Pierre picks it off! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XZ8sQnAqCx
With Isaiah Rodgers potentially dealing with an ankle injury that could force him to miss time, Pierre may see a spike in snaps this week against Buffalo. That's clearly not going to be an issue for the Vikings' defense, and Pierre has quietly become one of the best offseason additions for Minnesota.
Mason's second game back from injury was lacking, with just 20 yards on eight rushes, and he has yet to bring much juice to the backfield since recovering from a thumb injury. His 3.9 yards per carry and zero catches in the pass game this year are far from what the Vikings had wanted (and needed).
Mason is a solid RB2, but it's becoming clear the Vikings don't have a running back who moves the needle between him and Aaron Jones Sr. A sub-four yards per rush with essentially no impact in the passing game just isn't going to scare opposing defenses.
Van Ginkel will be 32 years old and a free agent next season. The Vikings could understandably be hesitant to offer him a new deal, but Gink just keeps making plays .
Van Ginkel notched another 2.5 sacks against Detroit, upping his season total to 6.5 and good enough for fifth in the NFL. He's got an interception and a forced fumble already as well, for good measure, and while it's reasonable to expect the drop-off to come, Van Ginkel just keeps defying the odds.
. @AndrewVanGinkel is having himself a day. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/SJjsbNH9H9
Despite plenty of other mouths to feed in 2027, it's just hard to see how the Vikings won't want to bring their star edge rusher back for another year.
Thorson beat out veteran Johnny Hekker for the job this offseason, but hasn't really done much to show he'll be the guy in 2027 and beyond.
Against Detroit, he badly shanked one punt, and his 44.1 punt average ranks 28th in the NFL this season. Hekker wasn't much better when filling in, so it's doubtful the Vikings make another in-season move, especially with the all-important job of holding for Will Reichard on the line.
Punter is clearly the least of the Vikings' worries this year, but expect some competition again in the spring.

title: Patriots Know They'll Need to Slow Down Packers QB Jordan Love
full_text:
It's a premier deep-ball matchup this week between the New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers. Drake Maye and Jordan Love are some of the best at launching it down the field this year and have combined for 4,229 passing yards through seven weeks.
It should be a fun game to watch — and the Patriots defense knows that they'll need to be ready for the passing attack.
"Jordan Love's ability to get the ball out fast," edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones said about challenges they'll face. "We'll see how it plays out."
The Patriots, coming off a win against the lowly Dolphins, will be able to use this week against a 5-3 Packers team as a good measuring stick. They're currently winless in two attempts against NFC teams this season and could use a good win against an opponent gunning for the postseason.
Part of what's made this Green Bay team good (they're averaging 21.7 points per game) is the growth of Love under center.
"Nobody's had more 20-yard pass plays. A quarterback that's wildly efficient. He has a few off days, but they're few and far between. They throw shots," Mike Vrabel said. "I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that's an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he's able to find (Matthew) Golden, (Christian) Watson or Tucker Kraft."
Love, a first round pick by Green Bay back in 2020, had the time to learn under Aaron Rodgers during his first few years in the NFL. Once the reigns were officially passed, he hit the ground running. A playoff team a year ago, the Packers have surrounded Love with plenty of talent on the offensive of the ball. He's taken advantage.
One area where he's shined is making adjustments at the line of scrimmage, something that's stood out to Vrabel.
"Whether he's sight adjusting and the ball's coming out quick, or he's changing the protection and making a call, communicating, I think I've seen that growth over the last couple years," Vrabel said. "Certainly, give him a lot of credit for the way that his career started: watching. I think that that's hard. It's hard to develop when you're not playing. But he certainly did. He probably learned a lot from what Aaron was doing and how Matt (LaFleur) was doing it with him."
This Patriots defense has had up-and-down performances against some of the NFL's top offenses. They limited the Seahawks in Week 1 (albeit down their starting quarterback in Sam Darnold) and beat Josh Allen and the Bills three weeks later. But they also gave up 30 points to Caleb Williams and the Bears, and trailed to the Miami Dolphins for most of the first half of an eventual win.
They'll need to be on their Ps and Qs against a Packers team hungry to get back into the mix of things in the NFC North.
"He's a talented player. He does a good job of finding his guys," Jones said. "The more comfortable he is in the pocket, the more accurate the ball is going to be. He's another prototypical quarterback, 6-(foot)-6, fast, can make any throw, so we got to do a good job of being smart."
"We all know he throws one of the prettiest deep balls in the league outside of Drake Maye, those moon balls that he throws up there," safety Kevin Byard said. "I think he's one of the most underrated quarterbacks in this league."

title: Patriots to Travel More That Almost Any Other Team Over Next 4 Games
full_text:
The New England Patriots enter the third quarter(ish) of their season on Sunday, as they take on the Green Bay Packers at home for their ninth contest of 2026.
After starting 2-2 in their first four games, which was the toughest start to a season in over 30 years, New England righted the ship and went 3-1 over the next four they played.
Now sitting at 5-3, the Patriots will be challenged with immense travel, a pair of playoff teams from a season ago, and some of the best teamms in the NFC. Here's what's on the Patriots plate from Weeks 9 through 13:
Sunday's 4:25 p.m. game against Green Bay could have momentum shifting effects on the next few games. While the Packers have been a powerhouse, winning four of their last five, traveling to Foxboro to face one of the best defenses in the league will be a challenge for coach Matt LaFleur and quarterback Jordan Love.
The Packers may potentially be without Micah Parsons, as he continues to rehab an ACL tear from last season — though he practiced for the first time all season on Wednesday. Green Bay has blocking miscues up front, which doesn't bode well for a team going against one of the top-ranked interior defensive lines in the NFL in Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, and Cory Durden.
Green Bay's 5-3 record is impressive, but they've yet to have an impressive win — notching victories over the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield, the Bears without Caleb Williams, and the Cowboys, Jets, and Panthers (those three teams have an 8-15 combined record). Green Bay is entering Sunday's match looking for a legitimacy proving win over the defending AFC Champions.
Following Sunday's game against Green Bay, the Patriots attend their first long road trip of the third quarter of their schedule, heading to Germany to take on the Detroit Lions.
The Lions, currently coming off a victory against the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings, have provided one of the most efficient and high-powered offenses in the league. With a defense that's sturggled heavily this season, the Lions completely contrast to the Patriots, who have been leveraged by their defense to create opportunities for their offense.
It'll be interesting to see how this game plays out for both sides, that match up fairly well to one another, and how the international status of this game will effect the outcoming.
The good news is, regardless of if the Patriots escape Munich with a win, they'll have plenty of time to work towards one, as they enter their bye week in Week 11.
After a restful Thanksgiving break, New England will board for another lengthy trip, heading to Los Angeles to face the Chargers.
Los Angeles is currently a staggering 0-7 and are driving like a truck without its brakes, wheels, or gas pedal. However, this AFC Wild Card round matchup from 2025 could be sneaky for the Patriots on Sunday Night Football. While this game is often forgotten when reliving New England's playoff run earlier this year, the Chargers kept this game close until Hunter Henry broke free for a touchdown in the fourth quarter.
The Chargers defense has been efficient this year and the real issues in Los Angeles lay with the offensive liabilities. Mike Vrabel took his first regular season loss after a bye last year, which will be something to watch this year as New England enters their Week 12 match for a potential trap game.
New England closes this five-week stretch of action and rest in a major way, facing the Buffalo Bills at home on the first Sunday of December.
In Week 4, the Patriots gave the Bills their first and only loss of the season. Since then Buffalo has been a wagon, toppling the Rams in overtime, outlasting the Raiders, and cruising past the Ravens.
Buffalo will visit New England one week after facing the Kansas City Chiefs, which could be advantageous for the Pats that would be looking to dominate game two of Buffalo's back-to-back matchup against recent AFC Champions.
However, if the Bills lose to Kansas City on Sunday Night Football in Week 12, Buffalo could also be looking at the Patriots game as an opportunity to get back in the win column. For New England, they have a massive opportunity to potenitally hand Buffalo their third loss of the season, sweep both games against the Bills, and put themselves in the drivers seat for the race to the AFC East title.
Another exciting feature of Week 13's game against the Bills is the storm blue rivalry uniforms returning to Gillette Stadium for the second time since their debut in 2025.

title: Patriots Week 9 Injury Report: Injured Vets Return, Offensive Stars Sit
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots got some good news and some bad news as they headed out to practice on Wednesday to prepare for the Green Bay Packers.
Speaking to reporters, head coach Mike Vrabel shared that wide receiver A.J. Brown, running back TreVeyon Henderson and defensive tackle Christian Barmore will all miss the session. But two players currently working their way back from injured reserve — wide receiver Mack Hollins and offensive guard Greg Van Roten — would begin their 21-day clocks to be activated .
Even with the trade deadline approaching , the Patriots aren't worried about any extracurriculars.
"We're focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay and make the corrections from the game," Vrabel said. "This is business as normal here."
Both Hollins and Van Roten were spotted during the media portion of the day and a few hours later, here's how the Patriots' first injury report looked:
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle/knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (foot)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
And in Wisconsin, the Packers announced their injury report, which included one of the NFL's best defensive players back in the fold:
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (concussion)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (shin)
Both Brown and Henderson missed last week's win in Miami with ailments. For Brown, he's been nursing an ankle injury suffered in Week 1 and a knee injury that's plagued him for years.
"My concern is about trying to prepare for the Packers," Vrabel said when asked about if he's concerned about Brown's knee. "That's really my only concern. ... Certainly the health of the team is critical, but we have to make sure that the guys that are practicing are preparing for Green Bay."
Henderson , on the other hand, has missed several days with an illness. This comes as the trade deadline looms and Henderson, who hasn't had that strong of a start to the season, has had his name thrown around in rumors. How serious is this illness?
"It's serious (enough) that he won't be available today," Vrabel said bluntly.
With Henderson sidelined, the Patriots relied on Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner, Lan Larison (who signed to the 53-man roster on Saturday) and Terrell Jennings ( who re-signed to the practice squad on Monday ).
The Patriots were also without starting tight end Hunter Henry, who suffered a foot injury against the Dolphins.
Each team is allowed to have eight players return off of IR during the regular season. Before Wednesday, the Patriots had only used a pair on Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant . Both Hollins and Van Roten were the next two designations and could come back as early as this week.
They both won't count towards the 53-man roster, but the Patriots have three weeks to fully activate them to the roster. If not, their seasons will be over. Right now, Vrabel is focused on getting them ready to go.
"We just want to get guys out there to practice," he said. "There's only so much that the trainers and strength coaches can do with them. So hopefully we can work those guys back in and see where they are here as we work through the week."
Hollins will be an easy fit into an offense that's had a number of wideouts banged up to this point . Last week in Miami, the Patriots had just four active wide receivers (and one of them was Ryan Miller, a temporary practice squad call-up). He'll become a starter the moment he gets back on the field.
"He's smart and ... he's easy to throw to and does a lot of things the right way," Drake Maye said of Hollins' return. "It's comforting, definitely, having 13 out there and looking forward to seeing whenever he gets a chance."
For Van Roten, his path is a bit cloudier. The Patriots have gotten good guard play out of Ben Brown and Matt Pryor, who both had to step up after Van Roten's injury in Week 3. If Van Roten comes back, he may push one of those guys back into a reserve role.

title: Patriots' Robert Kraft Among 5 HOF Contributor Candidates for 2027
full_text:
FOXBORO — Could this be the year that Robert Kraft finally gets inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame?
On Wednesday, the Pro Football Hall of Fame announced that the New England Patriots owner is one of five finalists for the Class of 2027 contributor category. Kraft was named alongside Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. These names were narrowed down from a larger group of 42 nominees by the contributor subcommittee.
Kraft, who bought the Patriots in 1994 and has helped usher in a new era of dynastic football, advanced in this process last year. Kraft was first nominated in 2013 and has eligible ever since. He wouldn't get inducted into Canton, along with former Patriots head coach Bill Belichick — who was the coaching nominee in 2026.
"I would just say that's unfortunate," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said last February after Kraft didn't earn induction . "In my experiences with Robert, he's more than deserving. He'll be in the Hall of Fame. I'm not in charge of deciding when that happens."
The Patriots have became a force in the NFL since Kr aft took over. During his time as owner, the Patriots have won 11 AFC titles and six Super Bowls. He also became the fastest NFL owner to reach 300 wins and has been a key member of several NFL ownership committees. In 2011, he was instrumental in helping to end the lockout ahead of that season.
It's a crowded group as it stands right now . Hay, who also reached this point a year ago, owned the Canton Bulldogs from 1918 to 1922 and was a key factor when it came to forming the NFL.
The late McCaskey was the principal owner of the Chicago Bears since 1983, and owned the team during their first Super Bowl over the Patriots in 1985. She was the daughter of Bears founder George Halas.
Williams played nine seasons in the NFL, winning Super Bowl MVP in 1987 and has spent the last 13 years in the Washington Commanders front office. He's also been a scout or front office executive in other years.
Wooten played offensive line for a decade before transitioning into scouting roles off the field. In 2003, he became chair of the Fritz Pollard Alliance, a group that hepps create opportunities for minorities in coaching and front office roles.
The Patriots have historically not been inducted into the Hall of Fame in recent years, despite having several people deserving of the honor. Last year, former kicker Adam Vinatieri was inducted as the first Patriots specialist to ever enter the halls of Canton.
The contributor category "recognizes individuals whose impact on professional football came through leadership, innovation and service to the game rather than on-field performance," according to the Hall of Fame. The voting committee will hold a meeting on Nov. 17 to narrow the group of five down to one.

title: Mack Hollins' Return Revitalizes a Broken Patriots WR Room
full_text:
On Wednesday, NFL Nework's Ian Rapaport reported that New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins would be returning to practice , beginning his 21-day window to be activated off the injured reserve.
In his second year with the Patriots, Hollins landed on injured reserve after sustaining a calf injury in the second half of New England's win over Buffalo in Week 4.
A big one for the #Patriots : WR Mack Hollins is set to return to practice today, sources say. Hollins, a glue guy for NE, has been on Injured Reserve with a calf injury and would help immensely vs the #Packers . pic.twitter.com/8uhIzxvxZ8
Through the first four weeks of the season, Hollins was the Patriots' leading receiver in yards and receptions, making his injury a major loss for the offense. Despite Hollins' absence, New England's passing game has been able to deliver, putting up 282.3 receiving yards per game from Weeks 5 to 8.
At the time of his injury, Hollins was the second Patriots receiver to land on IR this season, following A.J. Brown — who was injured in Week 1. Two weeks after Hollins came up gimpy on his right leg, Romeo Doubs was sidelined and sent to the injured reserve with a shoulder injury.
Brown returned in Week 6 and played only two games, missing Week 8's contest against Miami with a knee problem that arrived during last week's practice. Doubs isn't eligible to return off the injured reserve until Week 12. Drake Maye was left with just three receivers signed to the 53-man roster last Sunday against the Dolphins.
While New England's been able to make-do with the weakened wide recievers by utilizing tight ends and running backs in the passing game, those positions aren't exactly healthy either. TreVeyon Henderson didn't play in Week 8 due to an illness and is also still recovering a high ankle sprain sustained a couple games prior.
In the second half against Miami, tight end Hunter Henry injured his foot, leaving his status for Week 9's game against the Green Bay Packers up in the air. These considerations provide more value to Hollins' activation, who is looking to make an immediate impact in his return to play.
Hollins has played a major role in big situations for New England's passing attack. Maye often finds the 6-foot-4 receiver on third and fourth down plays. Since his injury, Henry has assumed that role, but with the tight end potentially missing some time, having Hollins back in the fold brings a much needed security blanket to last year's runner-up for MVP.
Part of the struggle for New England's wide receivers this year has been finding consistency, and the player that's been hurt the most by this is Brown. The superstar wide receiver has hauled in just nine of 20 passes thrown to him and has struggled to find meaningful production on offense.
Adding another perimeter threat in Hollins creates opportunities for Brown that he hasn't had due to defensive gameplans taking him out of the game (as well as uncharacteristically unreliable pass catching abilities). In the three quarters they played together in Week 1, Hollins' separation caused Seattle's defense to not overcommit on Brown. Maye took advantage of this adjustment, placing a deep pass to Brown that slipped off his fingers.
The Hollins effect can be seen through the sample size of games he missed last year with an abdomen injury. The wide receiver landed on injured reserve late last season, missing the final two weeks of the regular season and two playoff games. In those games, Maye threw for an average of 35 yards less than his season average passing yards per game. Returning to action in the AFC Championship game and the Super Bowl, Hollins was the leading receiver for New England in both contests.
The 33-year-old Hollins is in his 10th NFL season and is the most veteran receiver residing in Foxboro. While he's never been known to be a top wideout option, his voice and demeanor had a huge impact on a receiver room that many defenses looked past last season.
Hollins has extended his interest in this Patriots team far beyond the field. In both weeks the Patriots traveled while he was injured, Hollins made the trip with the players to Chicago and Miami — something that isn't required of players on IR.
Last week, New England's receivers had an average of 2.75 years of experience in the NFL. Activating the veteran Hollins and hopefully seeing Brown return to play on Sunday will bring a transformational impact to New England's offense and its high-caliber quarterback.

title: Patriots Make Key Roster Decision on WR Mack Hollins
full_text:
The New England Patriots, after weeks of injuries upon injuries, are one step closer to getting back a big piece of their offensive puzzle this week.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Patriots plan to have wide receiver Mack Hollins' 21-day window to return off of injury reserve begin Wednesday. Hollins has been on IR since Week 5 with a calf injury he suffered one week prior against the Buffalo Bills.
Hollins and the Patriots will have three weeks before a decision truly needs to be made on his return to the active roster, but because the team designated him to return, he's allowed to practice for those three weeks. This is the third of eight IR designations that the Patriots are allowed to use in the regular season, following wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant.
"Potentially, yeah," head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of both Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam returning this week. “Those guys are all working hard. We’ve got a long list of those guys, and I think (head athletic trainer) Jim (Whalen) and his staff, and obviously (director of sports performance) Frank (Piraino) and his staff are trying to do a great job with the return to play. We’ll see here where we come out from the game, where guys can help us and the spots that you have to make to get those guys back.
"So, there’s a lot of moving parts. We’ll try to make sure that the player is ready to return to practice. Then also, if they were to be available for the game, and then make the corresponding moves that would have to occur."
Hollins was a big part of New England's offense before he went down with the injury , recording a then-team high 15 receptions for 209 yards in the first four games of the season. He hasn't played in the last four games, but has been spotted on the team's road trips to both Chicago in Week 7 and Miami one week later.
The 6-foot-4 receiver has become a really trusted weapon for Drake Maye in this Patriots offense. Though his role in 2025 was limited in scope, after Brown's Week 1 injury this season, Hollins stepped up into a much bigger role — both as a pass catcher and as a leader for the younger wideouts.
The Patriots have gone through plenty banged-up receivers this season, with Brown dealing with both ankle and knee injuries and Romeo Doubs being placed on IR with a shoulder injury suffered in Week 6. Should Hollins return to the 53-man roster this week for the team's game against the Green Bay Packers, he'd join Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III in the wide receiver room. They also have Kyle Dixon, Chandler Brayboy and Ryan Miller on the practice squad.
After a myriad of moves to start the week, including Bryant's IR activation and the releasing of two defensive backs , the Patriots do have one open spot on their 53-man roster for Hollins to potentially fill. We will see if he ends up claiming that opening.
There are also several other players who are eligible to return from their stints on IR, including safety Dell Pettus (ankle), offensive guard Greg Van Roten (thigh), edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins (knee) and linebacker Khalil Jacobs (undisclosed).

title: 5 Edge Rushers Patriots Should Trade For After Gabe Jacas Injury
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than one week away, meaning movement is bound to happen across the league prior to November 10.
Teams have been identified as buyers or sellers ahead of the deadline with some organizations looking to upgrade their roster and others looking to trade valuable pieces for future draft capital.
The New England Patriots has been regarded as a buyer in this year's trade deadline conversation due to the pool of injuries that have plagued the Patriots roster. However, others argue that executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf and head coach Mike Vrabel are looking to make their team younger and acquire picks at the deadline.
If the Patriots were to buy-in, one position they'll certainly be inquiring about is edge rusher. The conversation around the Patriots needing an edge rusher has been loud over the past several years. This season, New England may have solved their EDGE issues with the emergence of Elijah Ponder and second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas.
ELITE: #PATRIOTS ROOKIE EDGE GABE JACAS HAS BEEN A STEAL. Through 8 games: • 3 sacks • 24 tackles • 4 TFLs • 1 INT • 11th in PFF grade • 12th in pass-rush grade • 9th in pass-rush win rate Jacas ranks FIRST among all rookies in the last three categories. WHAT A PICK. pic.twitter.com/vcyM4zSiMx
Jacas, who leads other rookies at his position in multiple statistics, went down in the second half of New England's victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Right now, his injury designation is listed as a knee issue, which leaves the severity of Jacas' injury up in the air.
While more information will be replaced on Wednesday, when the first injury report is released, the Patriots will need to find a suitable replacement if the injury sidelines the rookie for an extended period of time.
New England also rosters Dre'Mont Jones at defensive end, and they have a number of practice squad players who can play on the perimeter of the line (Jose Ramirez, Xavier Holmes). If the Pats decide to look out-of-house for an Jacas replacement, here's who they should target:
Diaby is a 6-foot-4, 270-pound linebacker for Tampa Bay, who is generating a lot of interest from teams looking for an outside linebacker.
The fourth-year player has been an essential piece to the Buccaneers defense, which has kept its offense in a lot of games that haven't swung their way. Diaby is on the final year of his rookie contract. which means a rental situation could make the price of him much lower than other names on this list.
Unfortunately, Diaby sustained a grade two MCL sprain during Tampa Bay's 16-0 win over Atlanta on Sunday, and is expected to miss several weeks because of it. This makes the rental value of Diaby significantly less, but would also mean the Patriots wouldn't have to give up much for him.
It's unlikely that the front office adds to the hospital waiting room-like lineup they already have by adding another injured player, but if Diaby's return time is sooner than Jacas', there's a chance he's included in a deal.
The 13-year veteran might not be as nimble as he was years ago, but his defensive impact is certainly still seen in the locker room and on the field. The 0-7 Chargers are looking to find value in their veteran pieces.
Mack is proving that his career isn't on a sharp decline, as he's registered three sacks and 21 tackles this year, and still finds himself on the field for 70% of defensive snaps.
Adding a veteran force in the 35-year-old Mack could make all the difference for this punishing Patriots defensive line. Mack's physical ability fits the mold that Vrabel seeks in his trench players on defense. The $4.4 million cap hit on Mack's contract for the remainder of this season fits well with the cap space New England has after recently restructuring Hunter Henry's contract .
Johnson II is a former Pro Bowl defensive end who's on the last year of his rookie contract. Similar to Diaby, Johnson might be a useful rental piece for the Patriots.
Johnson was an offseason trade acquisition for the Titans, coming from the New York Jets. He's emerged as one of the top defensive free agent prospects of the 2027 offseason. Vrabel's history with bringing people from Tennessee to New England could translate here, depsite the two never overlapping in Nashville.
As a member of the 1-7 Titans, Tennessee will also be a team to watch as they move on from their valuable pieces, like Jeffery Simmons, who they sent to Chicago in exchange for two first-round picks among other draft capital.
Johnson has three sacks and 20 tackles on the year, and is a valuable rental option to finish the season with New England before purusing a contract somewhere else.
It's rare for a trade within the division to happen so close to the deadline, especially with a player as talented as McDonald IV.
Between 2024 and 2025, McDonald registered 18.5 sacks, but his role has been downplayed this season due to the arrival of first-round pick David Bailey in New York.
McDonald has one year left on his rookie contract and may try to build a name for himself as a top defensive end before he becomes a free agent in 2028.
Should New England call the Chargers about a trade for a defensive end, it might not be Mack they inquire about, but instead Tuipulotu. The fourth-year player meets the theme of almost of every other name on this list by having an expiring contract.
Tuipulotu has three sacks and 30 tackles on the season while also forcing two fumbles. In 2025, he had 13 sacks and 20 tackles for losses en route to his first Pro Bowl appearance.
Similar to Johnson, it's unlikely the Patriots resign Tuipulotu if they acquire him, unless they were to move around other players. Christian Gonzalez's record-breaking contract extension ahead of Week 1, and Drake Maye's eventual record-breaking extension next offseason make long-term trade acquisitions difficult to come by for the Patriots in November.
While there are certainly better options out there for the Pats to pursue at defensive end, these five names make the most sense due to less financial commitment and smaller prices than players like Maxx Crosby or Josh Sweat.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: OT Marcus Bryant Activated, Depth Pieces Reshuffled
full_text:
As they continue to prep for the Green Bay Packers in Week 9, the New England Patriots made a myriad of moves to both their 53-man roster and their practice squad.
One of those moves finally allowed a second-year player to be activated off of injured reserve, while others reworked how the depth looks heading into the middle of this season.
Here's a look at all the transactions the Patriots announced on Tuesday and what they might mean for the 5-3 squad moving forward.
The Patriots are activating offensive tackle Marcus Bryant off of injured reserve onto the 53-man roster ahead of his 21-day return to play window expiring on Wednesday. Bryant, a seventh round pick a season ago, was on his way to making the team during training camp before an ankle injury landed him on IR .
Ahead of roster cuts in August, the Patriots designated him as a player to return off of IR during the season. Three weeks ago, he rejoined the team in practice and was given 21 days to be elevated to the roster. Bryant , who'll now join Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Caleb Lomu and Dametrious Crownover as the tackles on the team, will be likely used as a swing option on both sides of the line.
Last season as a rookie, the Missouri alum played in 12 games as a reserve — getting onto the field for 19 total offensive snaps and 56 total special teams snaps.
The Patriots had an open spot on the active roster before these moves took place, but also opened up another by releasing cornerback Kindle Vildor. A candidate to return on the practice squad, Vildor has bounced around between the 53-man roster and the practice squad in his first year with New England.
As a backup cornerback , the 29-year-old Vildor has played in five games this season and recorded six tackles, one pass breakup, a forced fumble and a special teams tackle. In recent weeks after the returns of both Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis from injury, Vildor was relegated to more of a special teams role. Against the Dolphins in Week 8, he played 13 snaps on special teams.
There is still one open spot on the 53-man roster, which could potentially go to either fullback Reggie Gilliam or wide receiver Mack Hollins. Both are eligible to return off of IR this week.
After linebacker K.J. Britt signed with the Detroit Lions , the Patriots had a spot to play with when it came to their practice squad. As first reported by ESPN's Mike Reiss, the team added linebacker Elias Neal, who spent the first few seasons of his NFL career with the Los Angeles Rams to fill that open 17th spot.
Neal has played in 10 total games and began this year on the Rams' practice squad. He was a game day elevation twice before being released on Oct. 27.
A few hours later, the team announced that they released wide receiver Cameron Dorner and offensive guard Jake Kubas from the practice squad, opening up two more spots on the practice-only unit. Dorner, who was one of the first UDFAs the team signed back in the spring, had a strong summer with the third-string offense . He was released from the roster after the preseason and returned on the practice squad.
Kubas, who played for the New York Giants this summer, signed to the team's initial practice squad and was one of the depth options on that unit alongside Andrew Rupcich, Xavier Newman-Johnson and Lorenz Metz. He wasn't called up once this year.
Reiss also reported that safety Elliott Davison , who was released Monday from the 53-man roster, will stick around and re-sign with the practice squad.
The Patriots currently have one open roster spot on the practice squad as they prepare for their first practice of the week tomorrow afternoon.

title: Patriots Week 8 Snap Count Analysis: WRs Rise to the Occasion
full_text:
The New England Patriots came into their Week 8 matchup with the Miami Dolphins down a lot of players. They were without their top three receivers, their starting guards and their second-best running back. They'd also lose their top tight end in the process. Still, they left Hard Rock Stadium happy.y
"I thought we started OK," Mike Vrabel said after the 24-19 win. "We got going, we had a field goal, and then didn't finish off drives, missed a field goal, defensively gave up some longer drives, some conversions. I give them a lot of credit, they competed. ... But also, I think we hurt ourselves. Again, we just have to try to stay out of our own way."
Here's a look at how the Patriots, who rode a strong second half to their fifth win of the year, divided up their snaps in all three phases of the game.
C Jared Wilson (60, 100%), OG Matt Pryor (60, 100%), OT Morgan Moses (60, 100%), OT Will Campbell (60, 100%), QB Drake Maye (60, 100%), TE Eli Raridon (55, 92%), WR Efton Chism III (53, 88%), WR Kyle Williams (50, 83%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (46, 77%), WR DeMario Douglas (39, 65%), OG Ben Brown (34, 57%), OG Walter Rouse (26, 43%), TE Tanner Arkin (16, 27%), RB Corey Kiner (11, 18%), TE Hunter Henry (8, 13%), TE Cameron Latu (7, 12%), RB Lan Larison (5, 8%), OT Caleb Lomu (5, 8%), WR Ryan Miller (5, 8%)
Without A.J. Brown, Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, the Patriots didn't have that deep of a wideout room on Sunday. They relied a lot of young Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III, DeMario Douglas and practice squad call-up Ryan Miller in the win, having them most of the snaps offensively. Both Williams and Douglas found the end zone in their larger roles. Eli Raridon, stepping up after Hunter Henry's foot injury in the second quarter , also played a career-high in snaps.
One major change happened halfway through the game, as the Patriots had Ben Brown replace Walter Rouse at left guard after a shaky first half. Brown, who missed the prior game with a knee injury, played really well in his return to the lineup.

While the offense managed with injuries pre-game, the defense suffered one that could come up big this week. Rookie edge rusher Gabe Jacas played just 19 snaps, tying his season low, and suffered a knee injury that forced him out of the game.
But they got some good snaps out of Cory Durden (who his first 1.5 sacks of the season) and Dre'Mont Jones (who also got banged up in the second half). Carlton Davis played all but two snaps in his return from a neck injury.

Ahead of this game, the Patriots signed Lan Larison to the active roster off of the practice squad , wiping away his two possible elevations. Larison, who returned some kicks in the season opener vs. Seattle, stepped up on special teams — recording a tackle on kickoff that limited a big return.

title: Patriots Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor for New England with 1 Week to Go
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline was pushed back a week this year, so the New England Patriots and 31 other teams will have until Nov. 10 to try and get deals done this season.
The Patriots , currently sitting at 4-3 and in second place in the AFC East, could end up being active on the market. Injuries across the board and potential depth issues at other places could led Eliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel to try and improve the team somehow, someway.
Aleady in this calendar year, the Patriots have made a few trades. Back in March, they shipped away Garrett Bradbury and Marte Mapu before acquiring A.J. Brown in a block buster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles three months later. During the summer, Kayshon Boutte was dealth to the Houston Texans and during roster cuts, the Patriots also sent draft picks for Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse.
So could they end up making a deal mid-season? Here's all the rumors, quotes and storylines that are surrounding the Patriots as the trade deadline looms.
The Patriots signed Carlton Davis last year to a three-year deal, but his name has now been thrown around in deals two years in. The veteran cornerback, who's missed several games with a neck injury, could be on the move — according to SI's Albert Breer.
"This is about the age of the team and if you look at the roster big picture," Breer said . "They’ve gotten older at a lot of key spots and they aren’t exactly flush with draft capital over the next couple of years. ... They’re going to have to find a way over the next, three, four, five years to make the roster younger particularly after they pay Drake Maye. They’re trying to creatively look at this."
Davis has been the Patriots' most physical cornerback when he's healthy, but the 29-year-old is one of the older players on the roster. The Patriots could try and offload both his playing abilities and his expensive contract for a chance to get younger in the secondary.
The Patriots have a lot of money tied up to the interior of their defense line, with Milton Williams ($28.5 million) and Christian Barmore ($17.1 million) being paid very well for this season. But Barmore, who's played just 41.9% of the snaps this season, hasn't been someone that's been a consistent player so far.
According to Breer , the defensive tackle "could be had" on the trade market after falling behind Cory Durden on the depth chart. Barmore has two more years after this season on his four-year, $84 million extension he signed in 2024 before hitting the open market.
This season, the 27-year-old has six total tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble.
Could the Patriots — the team with Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve — end up adding a wideout? ESPN reported that Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs requested a trade after a pair of his teammates were shipped away on Tuesday.
Downs spent two seasons with Drake Maye at North Carolina, scoring a career-high 11 touchdowns during the 2022 season. The Patriots only have four healthy wide receivers on the active roster right now, but adding Downs for what could be a cheap deal might help elevate the passing attack.
Seven games in, Downs has 26 receptions for 307 yards.
A few days after the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears , Vrabel spoke with reporters about how the team is stacking up prior to their Week 8 game with the Miami Dolphins. One of the questions posed was about if the Patriots will be active on the phones.
His answer left the door open for a deal being made, but the head coach also didn't officially dig a potential move into the sand. Like most coach-speak, Vrabel discussed how the Patriots would make moves to try and improve the overall roster in totality, and not try to single out a certain spot that needs upgrading.
"We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team," Vrabel said. "I don't know if we will or we won't. I would imagine that we'll try to do everything that we can to help us, within reason, and makes sense for us. I don't know how you want to interpret that, but I'm sure we'll listen and talk, just like everybody else does."
Some positions that the Patriots could end up attacking are running back, offensive guard (with a myriad of injuries hitting that group), interior defensive line and some backup cornerbacks.

title: Saints Get Major Injury Boost as Browns Face Quarterback Uncertainty
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints received encouraging injury updates Wednesday as left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
Meanwhile, Cleveland could be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , who entered the NFL's concussion protocol Wednesday after reporting symptoms following Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Watson initially passed concussion evaluations and finished the game but reported symptoms Monday night, putting his availability against New Orleans in question.
If Watson cannot play, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season.
Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards.
Watson has started all eight games for Cleveland this season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.
Despite his efficiency, the Browns have struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the NFL with just 17.4 points per game.
For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September .
The second-year left tackle has progressed considerably faster than initially expected, returning more than a month ahead of schedule.
The Saints now have a two-week window to activate Banks from injured reserve, potentially providing a significant boost to an offensive line that has struggled in his absence.
Backup left tackle Asim Richards has experienced difficulties adjusting to coach Kellen Moore's offensive scheme while filling in for Banks.
Initially expected to return in mid-December, Banks could reclaim his starting role once medically cleared, giving the Saints additional protection up front.
New Orleans also welcomed back Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State.
The rookie wide receiver participated on a limited basis Wednesday after missing the entire season to this point with a hamstring injury suffered during training camp .
Although his availability for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, Tyson's return represents another encouraging development for a Saints offense looking to improve its passing attack.
With Banks and Tyson progressing toward their respective returns and Cleveland potentially facing a quarterback change, Sunday's matchup could feature a considerably different outlook for both teams than initially anticipated.

title: Saints Make Coaching Staff Changes, but Mickey Loomis Shouldn't Escape Blame
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints have fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti following their Week 8 bye, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football.
The decision comes as head coach Kellen Moore attempts to fix one of the NFL's least productive rushing attacks, with New Orleans sitting at 2-5 through seven games.
The Saints have parted ways with run game coordinator TJ Paganetti, according to sources. Paganetti came from Philadelphia, where he helped architect the run game and was part of developing one of the league’s best offensive lines
The Saints are averaging just 86 rushing yards per game and 3.5 yards per carry, with their struggles reaching a low point in a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Oct. 25.
New Orleans had one of the most embarrassing rushing performances in franchise history, managing only 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts and averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Paganetti joined Moore's staff in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles , where he helped develop one of the NFL's most dominant rushing attacks.
During Philadelphia's Super Bowl-winning 2024 season, the Eagles rushed for a franchise-record 3,048 yards and averaged 179.3 yards per game, ranking second in the NFL.
However, that success never consistently translated to New Orleans.
While Paganetti deserves some responsibility, the Saints' problems extend beyond coaching.
While Moore is getting heat for the Saints’ offensive struggles, ultimately the biggest issue with the New Orleans Saints is the person who hired him: general manager Mickey Loomis .
Loomis is responsible for building the roster, including the backfield and the offensive line, the two weakest links on the Saints.
The running back room, featuring Alvin Kamara , Travis Etienne , Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson , hasn't delivered consistent production.
Etienne's placement on injured reserve has further complicated matters, especially when the Saints signed him on a four-year, $52 million deal.  Kamara, by contrast, hasn't shown the same explosiveness that made him one of the NFL's most dynamic playmakers.
The offensive line also remains a concern despite significant investments, including first-round selections Kelvin Banks Jr. , Taliese Fuaga and Cesar Ruiz along with the free agent signing of David Edwards for $76 million
New Orleans has struggled to consistently create running lanes, particularly along the interior, leaving its running backs with limited opportunities.
Paganetti arrived in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with Philadelphia, where he helped develop one of the NFL's most productive rushing attacks. However, the Eagles also had considerably better offensive line personnel.
Moore and Loomis must now share responsibility for determining whether the Saints' struggles stem from their offensive philosophy, player development or questionable roster construction.
Firing Paganetti sends a message that the current production is unacceptable, but changing coordinators won't automatically solve personnel deficiencies.

title: Saints Midseason Stock Report: 4 Bright Spots Amid a Disappointing Start
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter their bye week with a disappointing 2-5 record despite the hype around the Saints being contenders to possibly win the NFC South.
While the season has been anything but positive, the team still has bright spots on both offense and defense.
Here's a look at four players who have performed above and beyond as we reach the midseason point.
Tyler Shough hasn't been perfect, but the second-year quarterback continues to show encouraging signs of development under coach Kellen Moore .
Through seven games, Shough has completed 67% of his passes for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's also contributed 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
His pass yardage and touchdown totals are both in the top 10 as he is tied for seventh in passing touchdowns and ninth in passing yards, but for a majority of the season he was either No. 1 or No. 2 in passing yards.
Those numbers are impressive considering New Orleans' struggles establishing a consistent rushing attack and protecting its quarterback.
Despite occasional mistakes, Shough has demonstrated improved accuracy, pocket presence and command of Moore's offense.
If he continues developing and limits turnovers, the Saints should feel increasingly confident about their quarterback situation.
Wide receiver Chris Olave has shown why the Saints gave him a 4-year, $132 million extension.
Through seven games, the former first-round pick has caught 49 passes (fourth in the NFL) for 636 yards (third in the NFL) and two touchdowns, averaging 90.9 receiving yards per game.
He opened the season with four 100-yard performances in his first four games, including a dominant 182-yard outing against Detroit .
Chase Young has arguably been New Orleans' most impressive player on defense through seven games.
The former No. 2 overall pick has recorded seven sacks, establishing himself as one of the NFL's most productive pass rushers.
Out of 50 edge rushers with at least 125 pass rushes, Young ranked second with a 90.0 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade.
Young is on pace to record over 15 sacks, potentially putting him in the conversation for Pro Bowl recognition.
Though Young draws much of the spotlight, Carl Granderson is quietly putting together a standout year as well.
Across seven contests, the experienced defensive end has registered 25 tackles alongside 5.5 sacks, highlighted by a 1.5-sack effort versus Pittsburgh .
Granderson's current trajectory puts him on track for roughly 13 sacks, setting up a potential career mark.
Combined, Granderson and Young have racked up 12.5 sacks, forming one of the few reliable highlights for New Orleans' defense.
Even with the unit's broader difficulties, his growth paired with Young gives the Saints a high-caliber pass-rush duo for the future.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' 16-10 Loss to Steelers in Paris
full_text:
Hoping to build momentum ahead of their upcoming bye week after a major victory last week, the New Orleans Saints instead fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in Paris, exposing several recurring issues under coach Kellen Moore .
New Orleans' offensive struggles continued as missed scoring opportunities proved costly as the Saints fell to 2-5.
From an emerging young playmaker to a disastrous rushing performance, here is a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from the Saints' disappointing loss to Pittsburgh .
One of the few bright spots in New Orleans' disappointing loss was rookie wide receiver Barion Brown's emergence.
The sixth-round pick got a chance to show his explosiveness, finishing with three receptions for 57 yards and adding another 97 yards on four kickoff returns.
His biggest offensive play came in the first half when he caught a 49-yard pass from Tyler Shough , setting up Daniel Carlson 's 38-yard field goal.
Brown also returned a kickoff 42 yards in the second quarter, setting up a possession that ended with Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele .
Despite those contributions, Brown received just three targets.
That limited involvement raises questions about whether coach Kellen Moore is maximizing one of the offense's most explosive young playmakers.
With rookie Jordyn Tyson still sidelined by a hamstring injury, Brown has a chance to become a more consistent contributor alongside Chris Olave and Vele.
New Orleans gets a vital jolt on offense from Brown's explosive speed and big-play dynamism.
Following a sluggish 281-yard performance against Pittsburgh, integrating him must become a top priority for the Saints. To fully leverage the rookie's skill set, Moore ought to scheme designed touches, vertical routes and run-after-catch opportunities for him. Given how much he has delivered on minimal opportunities, Brown has earned a larger role.
In a narrow 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, kicker Daniel Carlson missed a crucial 52-yard field goal in the fourth quarter — his fourth failure in 11 attempts this season. This ongoing volatility in special teams poses a critical problem for the 2-5 Saints.
The fourth-quarter miss was particularly damaging because New Orleans had already wasted a promising red-zone opportunity earlier in the second half. Rather than positioning themselves to tie or take the lead with a field goal late in the game, the Saints remained trapped in a six-point deficit.
Carlson's 63.6% conversion rate stands in sharp contrast to Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who accounted for nine points by flawlessly making all three of his field goals (from 28, 47 and 39 yards).
With three one-score defeats recorded this year, New Orleans simply lacks the margin for error to withstand repeated scoring blunders in tight contests. Carlson's continuous field goal woes add to head coach Kellen Moore's list of bye-week priorities, as unreliable special teams only exacerbate the team's offensive stalls, defensive breakdowns and turnovers.
While much of the focus has centered on Tyler Shough's growth, an inept rushing attack still severely limits the Saints' offensive ceiling.
Sunday's outing represented a new low point for the ground game.
New Orleans generated a paltry 18 rushing yards across 17 carries, resulting in an abysmal 1.1 yards per carry.
The stat line is even more damning because Shough — a quarterback whose primary role isn't to lead the run game — was the team's top rusher with just 7 yards on three carries.
It is downright appalling that primary backs Alvin Kamara (six carries, five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries, six yards) both logged more rush attempts than total yards gained.
This embarrassing output highlights a backfield without a true lead option, further compounded by an offensive line that failed to establish leverage up front.
Such complete non-production is intolerable at any level of football—especially when relying on a developing quarterback to sustain drive after drive.
By stifling the run, Pittsburgh's defense put the burden entirely on Shough's shoulders.
Even with Shough connecting on nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans repeatedly stalled because it lacked offensive balance.
Unfortunately, this isn't merely a single bad afternoon.
The Saints' season-long inability to establish the run has made the offense predictable and easy for physical front sevens to counter.
