title: 3 Takeaways From Saints' Loss to Steelers: Same Problems, Different Country
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints traveled across the Atlantic Ocean hoping to build momentum heading into their bye week and salvage their season. Instead, they returned home with its fourth loss in five games and it just seems like another repeating nightmare for Who Dat Nation.
New Orleans fell 16-10 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in Paris, dropping to 2-5 through seven games under second-year coach Kellen Moore . It was the NFL's first regular-season game in France.
Despite another efficient passing performance from quarterback Tyler Shough , the Saints struggled to establish their rushing attack, failed to capitalize on scoring opportunities and couldn't get off the field defensively when it mattered most.
The loss marked New Orleans' third one-possession defeat this season, reinforcing concerns about the team's ability to execute in critical situations.
Here are three takeaways from another disappointing performance from the Saints performance.
For all the attention surrounding Shough's development, New Orleans' inability to run the football continues to undermine its offense.
Sunday's performance might have been its most concerning yet.
The Saints finished with just 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts, averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Even more alarming, Shough led the team with 7 rushing yards on three attempts. However, he is a quarterback and that is not his job.
But for Alvin Kamara (six carries for five yards) and Kendre Miller (eight carries for six yards) to have more carries than rushing yards is disgusting.
It shows the lack of life in a running back room without a primary option, compounded by an offensive line struggling to create leverage.
That level of production is unacceptable for any offense regardless of the level of play, especially one relying on a young quarterback to consistently move the ball.
Pittsburgh's defense shut down the run, forcing Shough to carry nearly the entire offensive load.
Although Shough completed nearly 79% of his passes, New Orleans could not consistently finish drives because it lacked balance.
The problems extend beyond one disappointing performance.
New Orleans has struggled to generate consistent production on the ground throughout the season, making the offense increasingly predictable against physical defensive fronts.
Because of the rushing problems, the Saints had to rely on Shough again.
Shough did everything you could ask of him, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and a touchdown. However, one costly mistake ultimately changed the game's complexion.
Trailing 13-10 at the start of the second half, New Orleans put together a 13-play drive that moved the offense inside Pittsburgh's 10-yard line as the Saints appeared positioned to take their first lead of the afternoon.
Instead, Shough threw a pass intended for Chris Olave , which Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson intercepted at the Pittsburgh 11-yard line.
The turnover erased a scoring opportunity and let Pittsburgh respond with a field goal, extending its lead to 16-10.
The interception proved costly, but it also highlighted the impossible position Shough has found himself in because of New Orleans' offensive struggles.
Despite completing nearly 79% of his passes, the quarterback could not afford even one mistake because the Saints had virtually no rushing attack to complement him.
That is an unrealistic expectation for any quarterback, much less one still developing at the NFL level.
Shough showed he could move the football against a Pittsburgh defense, distributing the ball effectively and keeping New Orleans competitive despite a one-dimensional offensive approach.
However, his play reinforced a troubling reality: when Shough plays well, the Saints can win; when he makes one mistake, the operation unravels.
Until Moore builds a credible run game and finishes drives, Shough bears an unreasonable load and New Orleans must create an offense where its quarterback does not need to be perfect to win.
Unless the Saints give Shough a credible rushing attack and adequate protection, they risk repeating a familiar chapter in franchise history: asking a talented young quarterback to overcome problems far beyond his control, much like Archie Manning decades ago.
Daniel Carlson 's fourth missed field goal in 11 attempts this season — a 52-yarder in the fourth quarter — kept New Orleans trailing in a 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh, highlighting a critical special teams weakness for the 2-5 Saints.
The missed 52-yard attempt came while the Saints trailed 16-10 in the fourth quarter, keeping Pittsburgh's lead at six points. Carlson's 63.6% success rate contrasts with Steelers kicker Chris Boswell , who converted all three attempts (28, 47 and 39 yards) for nine points.
The fourth-quarter miss was especially costly as New Orleans had already squandered a promising red-zone drive earlier in the second half. Instead of entering the final minutes needing only a field goal to tie or lead, the Saints remained six points behind.
Carlson's kicking struggles add to head coach Kellen Moore's bye-week concerns. For a team hampered by offensive inefficiency, defensive lapses and turnovers, unreliable special teams further shrink a narrow margin for error.
With three one-score losses this season, New Orleans cannot afford missed points. Sunday's loss highlights that the Saints lack the margin for error to overcome recurring scoring mistakes in tight games.

title: Greg Newsome II Bet on Himself, and It Paid Off With a $46 Million Extension
full_text:
There’s no safer bet in life than betting on yourself.
That’s exactly what New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II did. The 26-year-old signed a low-risk, high-reward one-year deal worth $8 million (including incentives) with Big Blue this offseason.
Seven games into that contract, Newsome has parlayed that “prove it” deal into a three-year, $46 million extension with $32 million guaranteed that he officially signed on Wednesday.
Not that Newsome ever doubted this was the direction things were heading.
“I knew the type of person I was, first and foremost. And I knew what type of player I was, and I knew that if I get to the right place, the money will take care of itself,” he said on Wednesday.
“I feel like when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted, you’re somewhere that you’re loved, everything else takes care of itself. So, I knew this would be the place.”
The Giants certainly wanted Newsome, a former first-round pick of the Browns whose up-and-down tenure in Cleveland ended when he was traded to Jacksonville midway through last season.
The trade proved a poor fit for Newsome’s strengths. He struggled in Jacksonville’s system, and the Jaguars showed little interest in bringing him back.
“Yeah, I definitely think it’s difficult. When you play in a primarily man-to-man, press scheme, getting traded midseason to a place where it’s a lot of zone, it’s a lot of reading different things and just learning your teammates, learning where you fit in that defense, learning everyone’s strengths, it’s definitely tough,” Newsome said.
“But God doesn’t make mistakes, and I feel like that helped me in the long run, just being able to adjust and get out of your comfort zone in a sense.”
With the Giants, Newsome has found that comfort zone. He has allowed a career-low 57% completion rate and has a 62.0 coverage rating.
Newsome has also not allowed a touchdown and has four pass breakups and one interception, matching what he did in 2023 with Cleveland, when he had his best season as a pro.
“(Defensive coordinator) Dennard (Wilson) has the perfect scheme for me,” he said. “Being able to challenge people, being aggressive and things like that. And just, man, just the ability to play with all 11 guys. We got some of the best players in the league, so they make my job a lot easier as well.”
Newsome is confident his best football is still ahead, but he recognized that the smart move was to strike while the financial iron was hot.
“You obviously could play it out, maybe make a few more millions, continue to play well. But for me, it’s not really about that,” he said.
“Once again, I chose (the Giants) because it just fits me. The coaches, my teammates — I love being around these guys.”
That love made accepting the Giants’ extension offer a no-brainer.
“It wasn’t, ‘how about I play it out and maybe make a few more millions?’ Obviously, it would be great to have a few more, but when you’re somewhere that you’re wanted and loved, the money, I’m getting good enough money that I’ll be secure for the rest of my life,” he said.
As the Giants prepare for their Week 9 showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles, Newsome will need to keep playing at a high level to help the team maintain its success. If New York hopes to earn its first trip to the playoffs since 2022, Newsome and the defense must meet the challenge every week.
The fans’ confidence and acceptance have not gone unnoticed by Newsome.
“Just seeing how passionate the fans are, just seeing how I come in and do the things that I want to do, and the fans are behind it,” Newsome said.
“They were behind me being here, and all that I can ask for is just to do my best for this fan base. And I’ll continue to see that as well. Obviously, they like winners. That’s what fans like, and we’re going to continue to do that.”

title: Giants Look to End 13-Game Losing Streak at Philadelphia
full_text:
The table has been set for the New York Giants — now all they have to do is cook the meal, and that means following a winning recipe one step at a time.
Head coach John Harbaugh has his team atop the NFC East at 4-2-1 as they come off their bye week with a visit to Philadelphia (2-6).
They have already beaten Dallas (3-5) and own a road tie against the Commanders (2-4-1). Yet he continues to tell his players to focus on the upcoming game, even though there’s little doubt they realize they’ve put themselves in good position to make a second-half run at the playoffs.
“I think they do keep it in mind,” Harbaugh said.
“It’s definitely always forefront because that’s the ultimate goal. We’ll bring it up every now and then, just answering the question in terms of how often, I don’t really know. Whenever it comes up or comes to mind, it probably gets mentioned. It’s more in context of what is the value of this game.
“What is the big picture value of this game? Why is this game so important? Why does this game matter? Why does this game require all of our attention? Because this game puts us in this position for what we’re trying to accomplish, ultimately. That’s really the context of it.”
The Giants have dropped 13 straight road games at Philadelphia since Josh Brown booted five field goals in a 15-7 victory on Oct. 27, 2013. Of course, none of their active players were on that roster, and that’s fine with Harbaugh, who knows you can only control the present.
“Our guys keep it in perspective, it really comes back to one play at a time. I know it’s a cliche, but it’s true,” he said.
“If you can do that and if you can lock in on one play, because it could be the play that makes a difference in the game, you have the best chance to be successful in that play. I think it all ties together, I guess is what I’m saying.”
Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen are always looking to improve the team, and the NFL’s trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.
It’s impossible to predict whether they will find the right price and the right trading partner to make a move. They have put themselves in a strong spot with the most difficult part of their schedule ahead.

title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice.
Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago.
At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.”
Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans.
Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury.
There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle.
If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game.
"I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray).
"So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll."
While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia.
If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night.
Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring.
Linebacker Abdul Carter, who missed Monday’s light practice due to illness, remained sidelined on Wednesday as he continues to recover.
Harbaugh, who said the lienbacker was home resting, "should be fine" for Sunday’s game against the Eagles.

title: Giants Will Reportedly Face QB Joe Milton III in Sunday's Clash Against Eagles
full_text:
Two days after Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee is their guy and “we are not making any changes there,” Sirianni has reportedly had a change of heart.
The Eagles, looking to snap a six-game losing streak, have reportedly decided to bench McKee and turn to quarterback Joe Milton III , whom they signed off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16, hoping to spark a turnaround when the New York Giants visit on Sunday.
Milton, 6-foot-5 and 236 pounds, has faced the Giants once before, in the 2025 regular-season finale on Jan. 4, a 34-17 Giants win.
Milton completed 7 of 13 passes for 73 yards and an interception in that game, and rushed once for four yards. Sunday’s game will be his first career start.
The Eagles, like the Giants, will have used three different starting quarterbacks. Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve after being diagnosed with blood clots. McKee has appeared in three games, all losses, and has completed 72 of 114 passes for 638 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions.
The Giants began the season with Jaxson Dart as their starting quarterback, but he was lost for the season after suffering a knee injury seven snaps into the team’s Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams.
The team then turned to backup Jameis Winston, whose contract they extended two years before the 2026 campaign began.
Winston posted a 2-1-1 record as a starter before Giants head coach John Harbaugh switched to J.J. McCarthy, whom the team acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Vikings last month.
McCarthy made his first start as a Giant in Week 7, leading them to a 27-21 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Before that, McCarthy played a handful of snaps in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints.
The Giants, 4-2-1, sit atop the NFC East with a chance to put even more space between themselves and their division foes.
The Cowboys (3-5) are next in the standings, followed by the Commanders (2-4-1) and the Eagles (2-6).

title: Giants’ Reported Trade Target Derrick Henry Appears Off the Market
full_text:
For those hoping for a reunion between running back Derrick Henry and head coach John Harbaugh with the New York Giants , that long-shot move now seems over.
The Ravens, 4-4 and last in the AFC North, face the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. Despite that, they are not out of contention for a postseason berth, which is why they are trying to salvage their 2026 season.
They have lost quarterback Lamar Jackson to a season-ending thumb injury and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley to turf toe .
Baltimore, which will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday, has reportedly acquired veteran signal-caller Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals to lead its offense the rest of the way.
With the Ravens taking such measures to stay afloat, any hope of the Giants, who are believed to be in the market for a bell-cow running back, working out a deal for Henry is likely over.
The 32-year-old Henry, signed through the 2027 season, has been mentioned as a possible fallback for the Giants, who have also reportedly been linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
Henry spent two seasons under Harbaugh in Baltimore and led the NFL in rushing touchdowns (16) in 2024. That familiarity and Henry’s contract made him a plausible alternative, especially since the Colts are reportedly seeking several draft picks for Taylor, who is 27, five years younger than Henry, and under contract through 2028.
Harbaugh, who said earlier this week that the Giants are open to taking calls from any team looking to make a deal, spoke about balancing the draft capital they’d give up against a player’s fit and cost.
“It’s got to be something that is a need, that fits your financial profile, that fits your price tag,” he said. “It’s not like we have a bunch of draft picks either. We’re not loaded with 12 or 13 draft picks, so we don’t have draft capital to burn. We don’t. So, we have to be smart shoppers that way.”
The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10.

title: Zaire Barnes Has Become a Quiet Difference-Maker for Giants’ Special Teams
full_text:
You won’t find New York Giants linebacker Zaire Barnes appearing in any TV commercials or ad campaigns.
Heck, you might not even recognize him if you passed him on the street.
But teammates and opponents know full well who he is: one of the faces of the Giants’ revamped special teams unit and a quiet difference-maker.
Barnes, who has played 79% of the Giants’ special teams snaps this season, currently leads the team with 11 special teams tackles (six solos) and also has a forced fumble, according to league stats.
His special teams tackle total with assists ranks second most in the league, behind Smael Mondon of the Eagles, who has 12 combined tackles.
Barnes, a converted college safety, seemed surprised when told where he ranked league-wide.
“I give a lot of credit to all the guys on the special teams unit, you know?” he told New York Giants On SI. “Especially on the punt team — (punter) Jordan (Stout) gives us great punts, which allows us to cover.
“And (assistant head coach/special teams coordinator) Coach Chris (Horton) allows us to get schemed down, while trusting his guys to get down there and make plays. So it’s definitely a collective group unit thing.”
As a key part of that group, Barnes, who also serves as depth at inside linebacker, has embraced what many view as the dirty work that comes with special teams. He first developed that mindset with the Jets, who drafted him in the sixth round out of Western Michigan in 2023.
“When I was first drafted over there, they saw me as a special teams guy,” Barnes recalled.
“Things obviously changed with the coaching staff situation, but at the same time, I learned a lot of great things, a lot of great techniques from Coach (Chris) Banjo, Coach Gobe (Michael Ghobrial), Coach (Brant) Boyer — all those guys. They taught me everything, and I wouldn’t be here without them.”
Then there were his teammates like Justin Hardy and Marcelino McCrary-Ball, two he credited in particular with mentoring him.
All of that, plus his own inner hunger and motivation from not being a high draft pick, has driven Barnes to put aside any ego about not playing on defense or not being one of the team’s A-listers.
And he wouldn’t have it any other way.
Having fun on the job is important, and Barnes said there is plenty of fun to be had playing special teams, something he discovered with the Jets.
Barnes, who likes to be challenged, said special teams offers that challenge — and it might not be for everyone.
“You kinda gotta be able to think on your feet pretty quickly just as you’re running down there,” he said.
“You don’t know where a block could be coming from. And just being able to slow down while running full speed and being able to make a tackle or a block — I think it’s definitely a different skill set you gotta embrace.”
It’s also a mindset that has helped many players who weren’t big contributors on their position units build long, productive NFL careers.
“It’s all about just taking pride in your role and just understanding that this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity even to wear the uniform on any given Sunday,” Barnes said.
“I definitely wanna make an impact, be a leader for this unit, and I appreciate those guys having confidence in me going in there week in and week out and allowing me to be me,” he said.

title: Ranking the Giants’ 5 Most Beatable Opponents in the Race for the NFC East
full_text:
The New York Giants enjoyed a much-needed bye week, but as they return from the break, it's full steam ahead as they fight to maintain their lead and capture their first NFC East title since 2011, when they went on a deep, historic run to Super Bowl XLVI.
Head coach John Harbaugh's Giants earned some extra space between them and the two rival teams beneath them in the division standings, the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles, who each lost their Week 8 matchups to the Cardinals and Commanders while Big Blue watched from the couch.
With the 2026 season one of the most unpredictable ever, the reality is that getting over the finish line means the Giants must charge forth and handle their business in a select few games during the second half of their schedule that should lean in their favor.
One thing that Harbaugh's first year in charge has proven is that the Giants can compete with almost anybody with the gritty style of football they've displayed almost every week so far.
With their 4-2-1 start and momentum building as the calendar turns to November, anything can happen the rest of the way. But in looking at the rest of the Giants' opponents, there are five teams — one of which the Giants will see twice in the coming weeks — that New York should be able to record a “W” against, ranked in order of most challenging to easiest.
While the NFC East has failed to impress many outsiders, the NFC North is arguably the league's best division this season.
The group's four teams are all in the race for the postseason entering Week 9, including the Detroit Lions, who will host the Giants at Ford Field in Week 16, for the second time in as many years.
Last season, the two franchises played an offensive thriller in which the Giants built an early 17-7 lead behind the leadership of Jameis Winston, who started in place of Jaxson Dart.
The Giants' run defense was ultimately their biggest weakness in slowing down Jahmyr Gibbs and Detroit's backfield in the second half and overtime, leading to a tough 34-27 loss in extra time.
The story hasn't changed much for the Lions' offense led by quarterback Jared Goff, which sits among the top three in total production after seven games.
Still, their defense is what leaves hope for teams like the Giants, whose offense is newly functional, to contend in another potential shootout.
Detroit has struggled to protect the end zone, ranking 28th in opponent red zone scoring percentage (74.1%) and allowing at least 21 points in five of seven contests.
They could also trouble the Giants' desire to lead off with the ground game by allowing an average of 96.6 rushing yards per game.
Still, in the passing realm, they have been picked apart at the highest rate in the NFL, including allowing the most passing touchdowns (18) as their red zone efforts have plummeted.
The Giants' aerial attack hasn't flashed much beyond the talents of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely, who have combined for 1,000 of the team's 1,700 receiving yards and 7 of 11 receiving touchdowns through seven games.
The way the group carved up the Texans defense in Week 7 behind the heroics of J.J. McCarthy suggests he could be the difference-maker in helping New York get over the top of the Lions this time around.
The Cleveland Browns might have been one of the biggest surprises early in the season, but what has held them back is their inability to put together a complete effort on both sides of the ball every Sunday.
Despite sitting at 5-3 and one game out of first place in the AFC North, the Browns share a similar lack of belief with the Giants because of who they've beaten.
The Browns opened the 2026 campaign with a 4-1 start behind three consecutive scratch-and-claw wins over the Buccaneers, Panthers, and Steelers.
Since Week 5, they've lost to the Jets with under 200 yards of total offense and two turnovers before barely etching out wins against the Titans and Ravens, and most recently getting blown out by Pittsburgh in the second meeting last Sunday.
Many outsiders doubted Cleveland because their quarterback situation seemed largely undecided at the start of the season. Deshaun Watson returned and reclaimed the reins from Shedeur Sanders, but the veteran's presence hasn't consistently reignited their offense.
As a result, the Browns have the league's fourth-worst scoring offense, which struggles to sustain long drives and chokes inside opponents' 20-yard line (48.0% red zone scoring rate).
Their best target is a second-year tight end in Harold Fannin Jr., and their backfield hasn't seen one back command the No. 1 role while averaging under four yards per carry.
Their calling card is the defense, which has limited opposing offenses to the sixth-fewest total yards and the fifth-lowest yards per pass attempt.
Both factors spell what could be a rock fight for the Giants, but the catalyst could be New York's RPO-style offense, in which the threat of McCarthy taking off could open up chances to gash the Browns on the ground.
If the Giants can strike a few blows in positive territory early and then control the flow of the game with their running back room, this matchup could turn into another one of the outings like the one against Tennessee, where Harbaugh and company dominate the clock and leave Watson few chances to make a push down the stretch.
Depending on how the next few weeks unfold for both rival franchises, the winner of the NFC East could be decided in the Giants' second meeting with the Dallas Cowboys in Week 17.
Harbaugh's tenure as Giants head coach got off to an impressive start as his team finally upended the Cowboys, 28-20, on the primetime stage behind nearly 400 yards of total offense and a pass rush that finally got pressure on quarterback Dak Prescott.
A lot will be different for Big Blue when they travel to Arlington to face Prescott and company again. They won't have Jaxson Dart under center or Brian Burns leading the outside linebacker room, and questions remain as to how healthy the Giants' roster will be at that point in a long season.
Based on what J.J. McCarthy has shown in his two recent outings, there shouldn't be much of a decline in what the Giants can achieve, as they'll likely have to trade punches with the Cowboys' offense, which is building its fifth top-10 season in the last six years.
Piling up points has been an imperative for Dallas given that its defense has been marred by injuries and its porous secondary has been the main culprit in allowing the NFL's highest average of 385.4 total yards per contest through eight games.
If the Cowboys' defensive woes show no signs of improvement as the second half progresses (they have matchups with the 49ers, Seahawks, Rams, and Jaguars remaining), the penultimate game against the Giants could be meaningless for Dallas if they rack up a few more losses in those tougher contests.
With the Giants at 4-2-1 and also set to face some of those same opponents in the next month, there is no guarantee the Cowboys won't take advantage of chances to catch up to their rivals and force an intriguing revenge game as the playoff picture comes into focus.
What we do know is they have the pieces to gash the Cowboys a second time, and if the pass rush can get home to Prescott a few more times, New York's fourth-quarter grit could be the key to sweeping their division foe.
The Giants will get their first chance to spar with the Philadelphia Eagles on the road in Week 9, but for the first time in almost two decades, Big Blue has a real shot to sweep the Birds.
Philadelphia will welcome the Giants to The Linc with an ugly 2-6 record and riding the second-longest active losing streak behind the winless Chargers.
Injuries to key pieces on both sides have largely steered their downfall from being a perennial contender for the NFC East and the Super Bowl, including the loss of starting quarterback Jalen Hurts to blood clots and multiple offensive weapons dealing with nagging ailments.

title: Eagles Are Down, Giants Are Rising: Why Week 9 Could Break the Philly Curse
full_text:
As New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh’s father, legendary college coach Jack Harbaugh, likes to say, “Who’s got it better than us?”
No phrase could more precisely describe the feeling in East Rutherford as the Giants return from their bye week having won without playing a snap.
While the Giants were watching from their living rooms, results around the NFC East fell perfectly in their favor.
The Dallas Cowboys suffered a crushing overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals after Jacoby Brissett was benched and kicker Chad Ryland missed an extra point that would have won it in regulation.
Several hours later, the Giants also got some help from the Washington Commanders, who trounced the struggling Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football , leaving the other three division members with at least four losses. Meanwhile, New York sits pretty at 4-2-1 coming off the bye.
Harbaugh’s Giants are returning with growing belief in their chances to win the division and potentially make some noise in the postseason, but that all starts in Week 9 as they visit the Philadelphia Eagles for an important rivalry game with some sour history for the franchise.
And as the team returns with fresh legs and the trade deadline looms, SI’s Conor Orr continues to ride high on the Giants, lifting them two more spots to No. 15 in his latest MMQB NFL power rankings poll .
It’s no bold statement to say Philadelphia hasn’t been a friendly place for the Giants in one of their biggest rivalries.
Not only have the Birds dominated the regular-season series for much of the past decade, winning 13 of 17 meetings dating back to the start of the 2016 season, but they’ve also held down the fort at Lincoln Financial Field, winning every contest against the Giants since 2013.
Granted, the Eagles have been in the midst of a successful run in that timeframe, including five first-place finishes in the NFC East, eight playoff berths, and three Super Bowl appearances, two of which ended in championships.
That Philadelphia team hasn’t been seen this season, though. The Eagles got off to a hot start at 2-0 but have since lost six straight games, falling into the division’s last-place hole as mounting injuries have taken away key players on both sides of the ball.
The most notable absence is quarterback Jalen Hurts, whose season ended after Week 5, when blood clots were discovered during an evaluation of a cleat injury suffered the week before against the Rams.
Without Hurts running the show, the Eagles have struggled to keep up with their opponents in recent weeks. Philadelphia’s offense has dropped to 30th in points scored and 32nd in total yardage, both their worst rankings since 2020, the last time they finished last in the NFC East.
It hasn’t just been the quarterback situation that has led to their downfall. Running back Saquon Barkley has also been dealing with a hamstring issue that is limiting him in games, and the Eagles’ offensive line lost some serious strength when right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired.
The Giants won’t feel any lost love for the Eagles when they head down I-95 to battle their heated rivals and seek their second division victory of the season. With a weakened Eagles offense compared to a rising offense led by J.J. McCarthy, it’s fair to call this New York’s best chance in years to break the curse in Philadelphia.
Just over a year ago, the Giants hung close with the Eagles behind the talents of then-rookies Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo, whose rushing kept Philadelphia’s defense honest as the Giants led 14-10 late in the second quarter.
Not long after, the contest went south as Skattebo suffered a horrific season-ending ankle injury, and the vibes were sucked out of the Giants in what finished as a 38-20 rout that hastened the end of Brian Daboll’s tenure as head coach.
The Giants will return without a few key pieces, including Dart, who is out with a season-ending knee injury, and a potentially thin backfield, as they look to shake their little-brother status in this division series.
What they do have now is the right coaching in Harbaugh and a more capable quarterback in McCarthy, who proved to be the right starter two weeks ago in the win over Houston.

title: NFL Insider: Missing Draft Picks Are Complicating Giants’ Trade Efforts
full_text:
The New York Giants have made no secret of their desire to be involved in the trade market, as head coach John Harbaugh publicly invited teams interested in doing business with Big Blue to call.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Giants have been making calls of their own. Schultz reported that the Giants have been among the most active in reaching out to other teams about trades.
However, the Giants, who have been heavily linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor as trade talks heat up, have hit an obstacle in pursuing any acquisition: draft assets.
"The difficult part, teams have told me, is that the Giants don’t have a 4th- or 5th-round pick in 2027," Schultz reported.
Because Big Blue lacks fourth- and fifth-round picks in 2027 after using them in other trades, their efforts to make a deal have reportedly been complicated, as those picks are believed to be essential to making any sort of deal for Taylor.
While Tankathon projects a fourth-round comp pick being awarded to the Giants in the 2027 draft, that pick cannot be traded until it’s officially awarded, which won’t happen until next March.
Harbaugh, who said he is open to adding players before the trade deadline, acknowledged that it would probably be an uphill battle.
“It’s got to be something that is a need, that fits your financial profile, that fits your price tag,” the Giants head coach said.
“It’s not like we have a bunch of draft picks either. We’re not loaded with 12 or 13 draft picks, so we don’t have draft capital to burn. So, we have to be smart shoppers that way.”
Harbaugh didn’t rule out the possibility of dipping into the team’s 2028 draft class, telling reporters on Monday, “Yeah, it’s easier to put it on the credit card.”
Schultz’s report seems to back that possibility as coming to fruition, saying that the Giants may be willing to spend premium picks from the 2027 and/or 2028 drafts for the right player.
“From the sound of things, they’re pushing for bigger names who would require higher picks — and seem open to doing that,” Schultz said.
That would make sense, especially if the Giants hope to trade one of their quarterbacks (Jaxson Dart or J.J. McCarthy) next winter for premium picks in return.
The NFL trade deadline is 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. In addition to a running back, the Giants are thought to be looking for a defensive tackle to add to their defensive line.

title: Giants Reward Greg Newsome II’s Breakout Season With a Big Extension
full_text:
The New York Giants ’ cornerbacks room just locked in a key piece for the next three years.
Cornerback Greg Newsome II, who signed a one-year deal worth $8 million, including incentives, has agreed to terms with Big Blue on a three-year, $46 million extension that includes $32 million guaranteed, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .
Newsome, a first-round pick by the Browns in 2021, was traded to the Jaguars midseason in 2025.
The Giants were looking to replace Cor’Dale Flott, who went to the Tennessee Titans in free agency. They brought Newsome in to compete with Deonte Banks, Paulson Adebo, and, eventually, rookie second-round pick Colton Hood for a starting role.
Newsome grabbed a starting job early and has been a steady performer, enjoying the best season of his career, aside from a concussion that kept him out of the team’s Week 7 game.
He is currently allowing a 57.7% completion rate when targeted, which is a career low. He has also allowed just 52 yards after the catch, another career low, has yet to surrender a touchdown, and has four pass breakups and an interception for a career-best 62.0 coverage rating.
He has played 90% of the defensive snaps this season.
Extending Newsome gives the Giants flexibility to release Adebo next offseason, a move that would save $14 million against a $6.317 million dead money hit.
That money could be used to extend Deonte Banks, who is also in a contract year and has played well this season.

title: Kenyon Sadiq’s Quiet Stretch Raises a bigger Questions About the Jets
full_text:
Following his breakout in Week 3, it seemed like New York Jets first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq was on the precipice of stardom.
Seven catches, 105 yards and a touchdown had left the Detroit Lions flummoxed about how to defend him, and the Jets thrilled with what he could bring to the offense.
Since then, though, Sadiq has been quiet. Horrifically quiet. After his dominant performance in September, he has been targeted 13 times, has caught five passes, with just 43 yards to boot. All of the success found earlier in the season has seemed to go away.
It's left some Jets fans worried. What has caused Sadiq's quiet stat sheet over the last several weeks? Is he not as good as many fans may have hoped?
In reality, there should be no concern about Sadiq's standing. It just highlights the true failing of the team's coaching staff.
Rookie seasons for tight ends are always a crapshoot. Young players have to learn how to both block and operate the route tree for NFL offenses. There should be no fan that is concerned over what Sadiq can do on the field. The fact he had one breakout game is enough to show his upside.
The reason why he hasn't gotten the ball is the same reason Garrett Wilson and other top targets have had uneven target share seasons: there are so many weapons to get the ball to.
"It's only one ball, and Garrett [Wilson] has to get it, Braelon [Allen] has to get it, Sadiq has to get it, Mason [Taylor] has to get it," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said last week .
In fairness to the team, it's a great problem to have. With so many weapons, the offense can target specific matchups against their opponents to get the ball to their best players. There is a reason why the group has seemingly turned a corner as a collective group.
Sadiq will be a part of that. And his breakouts will come in time.
"He's uncoverable, the way I see it," Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson said after his breakout in Week 3. "You can put safeties on him and stuff, but he's just a tough cover. You got a guy that runs that well, that can catch the ball ... Not to mention he's confident. He's a great dude to be around. It's awesome to have him here."
Despite all the positive future thoughts, though, the reality is this coaching staff is unable to make the most of the unit they have.
The true reality of Sadiq's statistical fallout over the last month has only highlighted how much offensive coordinator Frank Reich has failed this group. When the team first drafted Sadiq, they understood they had to come up with a plan to find success with the rookie and second-year tight end Mason Taylor.
Reich pointed to his past experience with two tight ends, and the fact he had a plan to get Sadiq going as an offensive weapon.
Through eight games, it's clear there is no plan. The offensive game plan is not creative enough to scheme players open or have people stand out in matchups. New York runs its offense the exact way they always do.
They are unable and unwilling to adapt.

title: Projected Breece Hall-Broncos Trade Nets Jets Realistic Return as New Era Begins
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, playoff contenders are looking to strengthen their rosters for the postseason, whereas teams near the bottom of the standings are beginning to sell veteran players for future draft capital.
That’s been the Jets’ strategy for most of the last 15 years, and it’ll likely continue this year with Gang Green sitting at 2-6.
New York traded away cornerstone players Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams for multiple first-round selections last year, and while we shouldn’t expect New York to do another fire sale, the team could move on from star running back Breece Hall.
With Braelon Allen breaking out during Hall’s five-game absence , rushing for 504 yards and three touchdowns, a backfield controversy has emerged that could ultimately lead to the Jets trading Hall.
One team in desperate need of a running back is the Broncos, who placed Tyler Badie and R.J. Harvey on injured reserve over the last couple weeks. With Denver currently sitting second in the AFC standings at 6-2, the Broncos have plenty of incentive to pursue a trade for Hall as they look to strengthen their backfield for a playoff run.
A potential deal between the two teams could give New York more valuable draft capital while providing Denver with much-needed help in the backfield.
While head coach Aaron Glenn said that the five-year veteran isn’t going anywhere, per ESPN’s Rich Cimini , his word may not carry as much weight as it once did. Since Glenn took over coaching duties in 2025, the Jets have posted a 5-20 record and are 0-8 against the AFC East.
His tenure has been highlighted by poor coaching decisions and a lack of improvement despite a major overhaul to the roster this past offseason. It’s unlikely Glenn will keep his job beyond 2026, and the team’s best interest should be setting the next era of Gang Green football up for success.
Darren Mougey will play a large role in doing so.
Over his two seasons as New York’s general manager, he’s built a strong foundation of valuable draft capital by trading Gardner and Williams. He’s also had early success in his draft classes, with Armand Membou and David Bailey among his most notable selections.
Trading Hall would add to this.
Although a third-round pick isn’t the greatest asset, it’s a valuable return, and it would add to New York’s massive stockpile of draft capital.
The pick would put the Jets at 10 picks for the 2027 draft, six of them coming in the first three rounds. That would give the Jets plenty of flexibility to address multiple areas or trade for an immediate starter.
Running back trades are tricky.
Years ago, teams spent high-value draft picks on running backs, but since the Trent Richardson trade in 2013, the market for the position has changed significantly. The Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022 was by far the biggest one, as the 49ers gave up 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round pick plus a 2024 fifth-round pick.
Remember, McCaffrey was a top-three player at the position who was just entering his prime years. While Hall isn’t on the level of McCaffrey, he’s coming off the best season of his career and is still just 25 years old.
The Jets reportedly turned down a fourth-round offer from the Chiefs for Hall last season, with Mougey insisting on receiving a third-round pick in return. With Hall’s best years ahead of him, a third-round pick is a reasonable deal for both sides.
With Hall under contract through 2028, Denver would strengthen its chances throughout the next several years of its Super Bowl window.
For New York, it provides more valuable draft capital to build their team for next season while allowing Allen to take over as the team’s starting running back.
We’ve seen that the Jets aren’t close to competing for a championship; however, they are a few pieces away from being a playoff-caliber team. Trading Hall to Denver for a third-round pick would be a step towards ending the 15-year playoff drought.

title: 3 Most Realistic Jets' Trade Candidates Entering Final Week Before Deadline
full_text:
We're under a week away from the NFL trade deadline and it appears the New York Jets are ready to be silent. Last season, they gave away Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in mega-deals.
It's clear the team won't be dealing with something similar this year.
Still, there are three players who could find themselves in a new home away from Florham Park. Let's go through the three most likely candidates to be moved going into next week.
Early in the year, Brownlee was New York's best player in the secondary. A dip in production, coupled with an in-season benching and struggles in Week 8 has made Brownlee expendable. More importantly, the team has D'Angelo Ponds waiting in the wings to get reps across the board.
Brownlee may not get a lot on the market, but his role for the team simply doesn't match where the team is currently. New York would be best served moving on from him and allowing Ponds to play.
McDonald is a player that will arguably carry the most return for the franchise if they actually end up being sellers. He has three sacks this season, but over 21 in his first three years in the NFL. He's someone who can get to the quarterback in bunches.
There will be Super Bowl contenders who look at that skill as an absolute need. If the Jets can get an early Day Three pick (a fourth rounder) it may be enough to entice the team to restart the rebuild of their defensive line.
Wright has barely seen the field this year due to losing the cornerback position battle against AZ Thomas in training camp. The fact Wright is coming off a year where he led all cornerbacks in interceptions, and the Jets only have one recorded this season, is irrelevant to the coaching staff.
Wright isn't a fit for what the Jets want to do defensively at corner. Because of that, it makes more sense than anything to simply move on from Wright at this point for a late-round pick swap. Either that, or he'll be released for a chance to play with a contender.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has been clear: the team wants to keep Hall on the roster. Since he's missed the last five games, it's hard to envision a team giving New York a trade deal they are willing to listen to.
Remember, though, the team didn't have a dream in mind of moving on from Sauce Gardner from last season. Indianapolis simply gave them an offer they couldn't refuse.
Will another team do the same for Hall? Is a third-round pick something the team can't refuse? Most likely not. It seems Hall is here to stay at this point.

title: Garrett Wilson Injury Will Test if New Jets' Optimism is Deserved
full_text:
Garrett Wilson is the best player on the New York Jets. That has been the case over the last several years now.
Whenever the former Ohio State star is off the field, New York is worse for it. So when head coach Aaron Glenn announced Wilson entered concussion protocol before practice on Wednesday, most fans wouldn't be wrong to feel even worse going into Sunday's contest against the Kansas City Chiefs. New York is already 2-6 and needs everyone on deck to be able to thwart the playoff contender.
But what if I told you the Jets, for the first time since Wilson was brought to the team in 2022, aren't going to miss Wilson as much as before? What if the offense won't miss a beat?
And it has everything to do with the system and personnel at their disposal.
Sometimes, an injury to a WR1 doesn't have the kind of debilitating effect on an offense that you might expect. Part of that reason is due to the depth around the top receiver. If Wilson does not pass concussion protocol in time for Sunday's game, the Jets will be perfectly fine.
And it's due to the depth on the roster.
At receiver, Adonai Mitchell and rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. have shown their own breakout capabilities over the last few weeks. In Week 6 and 7, Cooper was the first rookie receiver with back-to-back 100-yard games since Al Toon in 1985. Just last week, Mitchell recorded a seven-catch, 142-yard game as the most productive player in the offense. Without Wilson, players like Cooper will be in the spotlight, and he appears ready for it.
“What he did is showcase who he is," Geno Smith said after Week 6 of Cooper.  "He’s a playmaker. He finds ways to make catches, the tough catches … he makes them look easy.”
And what about Smith himself? Many times a top receiver leaves a game, the quarterback normally struggles immediately after. Only true veterans with years of experience are able to keep an offense afloat. Smith is among the latter quarterbacks mentioned.
So far this season, he has recorded 1,913 yards passing with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions. He has been everything the team has hoped for at the position and more. It's another reason why the team should be perfectly fine without Wilson.
"He's really commanding that offense the way you want a quarterback to do that, so the drop back game he's doing a hell of a job," Glenn said of Smith.
Remember, we haven't even brought up the fact that Braelon Allen is on a historic five-game pace, and Breece Hall could be in line to return to the team after missing the last five contests. New York having a successful rushing attack changes the desperate need for a top receiver, especially with quality other wideouts on the roster.
Losing Wilson is never easy for the Jets offense. But unlike prior years, the team is better prepared for his absence. They might even remain a unit that's able to put up plenty of points without him.

title: 3 Logical Breece Hall Trade Destinations to Give Jets the Best Return
full_text:
Breece Hall's last snap for the Jets was on Sept. 27, and Gang Green has gone 1-4 since the injury. However, that has not been because of the running back room. Braelon Allen has taken over the backfield, leaving New York with an interesting conundrum.
In the five games Hall has missed, Allen has 504 rushing yards and is averaging 5.4 yards per carry. This has put Hall's future with the Jets in question.
Hall is no stranger to trade rumors. The running back was one of the names in rumor mills when the Jets were selling in 2025. Hall ultimately stayed with the Jets and signed a three-year, $45.75 million contract with New York. The former Iowa State Cyclone looks to be on the trading block again as the Jets look like sellers before the deadline.
So if Hall is on his way out, what teams would be willing to give New York the best return for the fifth-year veteran?
The Broncos' run game has been less than stellar in 2026. Denver has averaged just 92.6 rushing yards per game this season. Denver is in the conversation for teams looking for running back help at the trade deadline.
Denver holds nine draft picks for the 2027 draft. The Broncos have two fourth-round picks, which opens the door for negotiations. Breece Hall won't fetch as high a return as Jonathan Taylor, but the Jets can still get value from trading the running back.
The Jets could snag the Broncos' third-round pick as Denver has two in the fourth. If New York gets a third for Hall, that would give them six picks in the first three rounds. Denver needs help in the run game, and it may be a perfect trade for both teams.
The Packers are another team that could be a good trade partner for Hall.
Green Bay's rushing attack has been abysmal, ranking dead last in the NFL. Josh Jacobs has returned from his stint on the Commissioner's List to a paltry 2.3 yards per carry and may miss more games due to his ongoing investigations .
The Packers are 5-3 despite a poor rushing attack, so Green Bay may be willing to trade for a talent like Hall. The Packers don't have a first-round pick in 2027, but they hold two fourth-round picks. The Jets could benefit more from the Packers' draft capital if they trade Hall.
New York should look for the third-round pick from the Packers if Green Bay wants Hall. That doesn't mean the Jets can't snag a second-round pick for the running back. The Packers are desperate to contend, and an answer to their running-game woes might be worth a late second if Green Bay is to have two picks in the third.
The Bengals have had one of the league's worst rushing attacks throughout Joe Burrow's career. They have trusted Chase Brown, but the fourth-year RB has managed only 340 rushing yards in seven games in 2027. Hall could be the perfect replacement for a Bengals team that has struggled to establish the run.
Hall makes an impact in both the rushing and passing game. That is exactly what Cincinnati needs. They are almost too dedicated to the pass, having had a bottom-five rushing offense over the past five years. Hall's ability to shine in both aspects of the offense may matter more to a team like Cincy than some think .
Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals' offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals' second-round pick.
The Jets set a precedent that Hall will not go for less than a third-round pick during last year's trade deadline. With these teams, the Jets will have a chance to get that caliber of return and maybe more. If they want to move on from Hall, they should want, at least, Day 2 picks in return.

title: Jets Desperately Need Omar Cooper Jr. to Bounce Back Even More Amid Garrett Wilson Concussion Concerns
full_text:
Coming off a 38-33 loss to the Raiders last Sunday and falling to 2-6 on the season, the Jets are in deep trouble with a challenging road trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the Chiefs in Week 9.
While Braelon Allen has been sensational on the ground and the offensive line continues to show some positive signs, it was a disaster for the special teams unit, the defense and a coaching staff that cannot seem to make the appropriate adjustments from week to week and over the course of a game.
For the last two weeks, though, the Jets have slowly started to get a little healthier, especially in the wide receiver room as rookie Omar Cooper Jr. (high ankle sprain) and Adonai Mitchell (finger) made their return from their respective injuries.
While that has given the Jets their top-three wideouts the last two weeks, that may not be the case on Sunday after ESPN 's Rich Cimini confirmed on Wednesday that WR1 Garrett Wilson "is in concussion protocol," per head coach Aaron Glenn.
WR Garrett Wilson is in concussion protocol, per Aaron Glenn. #Jets
That means he would have to pass the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol and could be unable to play on Sunday. If that is the case, that could present the opportunity Cooper needs to respond after receiving zero targets in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
Sure, Mitchell led the team with seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Wilson was targeted a team-high 12 times against Las Vegas. That said, Cooper had back-to-back 100-yard receiving games prior to that dud last Sunday and could benefit the most if Wilson is unable to play as the Jets take a three-game losing streak into Kansas City .
Wilson may not have been on the injury report earlier this week , but the fact that his status is in doubt speaks to the potential opportunity that could exist for Cooper, who has already demonstrated first-round talent and shown why he is one of the top targets on this team.
If Wilson is not on the field or is limited in some capacity, the Jets need Cooper to take on a larger target share alongside Mitchell and create some consistent separation. It is no secret that the Jets will not be given much of a chance against the Chiefs, so it is crucial for Cooper to take advantage of slants and quick-hitting routes to rack up yards after the catch.
It might be easy to overreact to Cooper's lack of impact and usage in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders, but let's not forget how frustrated Wilson has been with his limited targets and the additional attention that Mitchell receives in the passing attack when he is healthy. It was also just one game and likely a small blip on the radar for Cooper if the two weeks beforehand were any indication.
With the attention mostly focused on Mitchell and tight end Mason Taylor, who broke out for two receiving TDs in Week 7, Cooper could be instrumental in keeping the chains moving and preventing the offense from stalling out, which has become an issue at times throughout the season.
Considering seven of Cooper's 12 catches this season have been over the middle of the field, everything could be lining up for him to bounce back in Week 9. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , the Chiefs gave up six completions on eight middle-of-the-field attempts against the Broncos in Week 8, so this could be a favorable opportunity for him against a formidable opponent.
Regardless of how Cooper performs on Sunday, though, his disappearing act against the Raiders should not be too concerning for the Jets . That said, even though his workload should see an increase, there is still a boom-or-bust nature when you consider the inconsistency from this coaching staff and the targets that were coming Mitchell's way last week.
If Cooper can break free and create an explosive play or two, it may not matter how many times quarterback Geno Smith looks his way. With that in mind, expect Cooper to have an expanded volume and usage as the uncertainty surrounding Wilson potentially leads to more opportunities for the rookie.

title: 3 Jets Face More Pressure After Garrett Wilson Concussion News Creates New Obstacle in Week 9
full_text:
The Jets will look to avoid a season-worst fourth consecutive loss when they visit the Chiefs for some Sunday afternoon action in Week 9 . Beating Patrick Mahomes & Co. was never going to be easy, especially with how inconsistent Gang Green's performances have been this season, but a potential upset in Kansas City will be even tougher to pull off if the Jets are without star wide receiver Garrett Wilson.
On Wednesday afternoon, New York head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that Wilson has been placed in concussion protocol and will be "day-to-day."
WR Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol Full injury update from Coach Glenn ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/la6Lq13a1G
Given that Wilson must clear the NFL's five-step protocol to get back into the lineup, there's a good chance that the Jets won't have him when they take on the Chiefs this weekend. As such, New York needs this trio to step up if it hopes to keep Sunday's clash competitive.
Alongside rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell is another Jets playmaker who needs to take things to another level if Wilson misses time. Fortunately, he proved he could do exactly that last week.
Even though his team didn't win, last week's loss to the Raiders was a career day for Mitchell, who converted nine targets into seven catches, 142 receiving yards and a touchdown. Considering how he had a 9-123-0 stat line in three games before that (mostly due to a nagging finger injury), it's safe to say that the former Georgia/Texas product is more than capable of being the Jets' lead pass-catcher.
An incredible 48-yard catch by Adonai Mitchell! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/a7pOlkJn27
The Chiefs have a fairly middle-of-the-road pass defense this season, ranking 18th in passing yards allowed per game (222.9) and T-16th when it comes to yards per completion (10.2). With a career-high average depth of target of 18.2 yards this season , per Pro Football Focus , Mitchell has what it takes to take advantage of any potential miscues in Kansas City's secondary.
The Jets' passing attack hasn't been consistent this season, but another huge performance from Mitchell (sans Wilson) would boost optimism about the unit's outlook.
It's safe to say that Kenyon Sadiq's big seven-catch, 105-yard performance in Week 3 is nothing but a distant memory at this point. The rookie tight end has been nearly invisible since then, catching just five balls on 13 targets (38.5%) for 43 receiving yards without a touchdown in the last five games. Even though it's only his rookie season, that's pretty disappointing for someone drafted 16th overall in April .
All slumps eventually end, though, especially when a player is as talented as Sadiq. Despite the Jets being underdogs this weekend ( by 10 points, per DraftKings Sportsbook ), a clash with the Chiefs might be exactly what the doctor ordered.
As previously mentioned, Kansas City's pass defense hasn't been great, and that's even truer when it comes to stopping tight ends. Heading into Week 9, when it comes to TEs, the Chiefs have allowed:
In other words, it's a great opportunity for Sadiq (and Mason Taylor) to step up if Wilson is stuck in concussion protocol.
With Wilson's immediate outlook uncertain, a potential Breece Hall return in Week 9 would be huge for the Jets. The stud running back hasn't played since Week 3 due to a quad injury, but head coach Aaron Glenn revealed on Wednesday that Hall's situation is "trending in the right direction," per ESPN 's Rich Cimini.
Breece Hall is "trending in the right direction," Glenn says. https://t.co/O4Rn1Q6iOy
Hall's job is to run the ball, but that doesn't take away from the fact that his presence is a key part of the Jets' passing game. The Iowa State product has amassed 198 catches for 1,744 receiving yards (8.8 yards per reception) and nine touchdowns in 59 career games, which includes catching all 10 of his targets for 102 yards this season.
For comparison, New York's other two running backs—Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis—have combined for just 149 yards on 22 receptions this season. That's just 6.8 yards per reception compared to Hall's 10.2.
Besides, having Hall available in pass-catching situations would allow the Jets to keep Allen on the field, looking to keep taking advantage of his ongoing breakout .
Assuming he can finally play for the first time since September, Hall's looming return certainly looks a lot more important for the Jets.

title: How Soon Could the Jets Start Cade Klubnik Over Geno Smith This Season?
full_text:
The Jets are 2-6 so far this season. One question is looming as New York continues to lose. Quarterback play hasn't been the most glaring issue for the team, but Geno Smith is 36 years old. The veteran quarterback is on a one-year deal, and the Jets have a rookie sitting on the bench.
The Jets look likely to miss the playoffs for a 16th consecutive season. If the team is even considering the QB position in the 2027 draft , they must see what they have in rookie Cade Klubnik. The fourth-round pick should get some playing time this season, but how soon could that happen?
The Jets drafted Cade Klubnik with the 110th overall pick in the 2026 draft from Clemson. Klubnik joined the Jets after an underwhelming last season as a Tiger, but some viewed him as a top-five pick before his last season in South Carolina. He showed some of that talent in the preseason and should get some run at some point this season.
Klubnik finished his first NFL preseason with a total stat line of 21-of-34 passing for 190 yards and an interception. He did not record a passing touchdown, but looked good on some touchdown drives. The former Clemson Tiger also started two of the three preseason games, showing he has the talent to run with the first-team offense.
Klubnik also matches the mold of a successful quarterback in today's game. Klubnik is 6'2" and has mobility that the Jets' offense lacks right now. If the Jets keep losing, calls for the rookie to start will only get louder.
Smith has been far from the biggest problem on the Jets this season. Through eight games, Smith has 1,913 yards, 12 touchdowns and only three interceptions. The veteran quarterback also comes off a game where he helped lead the Jets to 33 points (the second-most they've scored in the Aaron Glenn era).
What a throw from Geno Smith and what a catch by AD Mitchell 😱 LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cxPa0KclpY
Smith doesn't deserve to be benched in a season where the Jets' offense has been more than competent. However, the season seems to be slipping away . The Jets are unlikely to see Geno as their quarterback beyond this season, as he enters the twilight of his career.
So when will they bench the veteran for the rookie?
Barring injury, Smith will start as long as the Jets still have any playoff hope. He seems to be the best chance to win right now. He is having his best season since he made the Pro Bowl as a Seahawk, and the Jets have been in almost every game this season. Klubnik is waiting in the wings, but a QB switch doesn't seem close.
Klubnik could realistically start as early as Week 11 against the Chargers.
If New York drops the next two and Smith looks terrible, Klubnik may get a chance against the struggling Los Angeles team. However, that would put the Jets at 2-8, still possible to make the playoffs, though extremely unlikely. The team will most likely stick with Smith as long as the playoffs are still possible.
That said, Jets fans will most likely see Klubnik start in Week 15 against the Cardinals. New York will likely be out of the playoff race by then unless they make a run soon. This will let Klubnik start against a team that has struggled much like the Jets this season .
Klubnik would avoid playing the Denver defense by a week, but still get to finish his season against some playoff hopefuls. While the road to Klubnik starting looks far away, the rookie will have his chance to prove the Jets don't need to use any of their three first-round picks at QB.

title: Making Sense of Jets' D'Angelo Ponds Plans as Questions Brew in Week 9
full_text:
Among the chief positive points surrounding the 2026 Jets season has been their dominant rookie class . All three first-round picks have stood out in some way and have received rookie of the week honors from the NFL.
Even fourth-round defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. has enjoyed a positive start to his NFL career .
There's one member of the class, though, that has yet to stand out.
Second-round cornerback D'Angelo Ponds missed all of training camp and the first quarter of the season with an injury. After battling back, he received his first NFL start in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
Despite the positive tape, Ponds was sent to the bench last week in New York's loss to Las Vegas . So what gives? What will it take for the Jets to turn to Ponds going forward?
Against the Dolphins in Week 7, Ponds was targeted three times and gave up one reception for five yards. He was, however, called for a pass interference penalty in the end zone that gave the Dolphins an inevitable score.
But by and large, the first start of Ponds's career was a good one. It showed he could be a quality player in the slot. With more reps, the belief was that the Indiana product would be even better.
Ponds was effectively benched by the Jets in their loss to the Raiders and played just a single defensive snap. In his stead, Jarvis Brownlee Jr. got the start in the slot and was penalized twice while also giving up three catches on four targets, a touchdown, and a near-perfect passer rating.
So what gives? Why would the Jets move back to Brownlee in a clear lost season at 2-6? The reality is that the team still wants to win for their coaching staff and head coach Aaron Glenn believes that Brownlee gives them the best chance to be successful on the field.
Never mind the fact that Brownlee acknowledged he was late to multiple meetings and was benched in Week 7; this is only about what he can do on the field.
But now, with the team at 2-6 and needing to see what they have in their young talent, change may be coming.
Don't be surprised if the Jets look to move off of Brownlee in some capacity as the trade deadline gets closer. Ponds will eventually see the field more and more, but Brownlee is seen as a stopgap to that chance.
Once the team is firmly out of any hope of a .500 season ( something that would keep Glenn's job at any rate ), the focus must shift back to getting their rookie class as many reps as possible. That includes putting Ponds both in the slot and in the boundary—where he made his living as one of the best corners in college despite his small frame.
Ponds will eventually be a starter for the Jets. The longer the team waits, though, the more worrisome it is that they might have wasted a top second-round selection. They are better off playing him and moving on from Brownlee altogether.

title: 5 Best 2027 Draft Prospects Jets Need on Their Radar as Colts Sink Further Into Basement
full_text:
At 2-6, it's clear the Jets aren't going to be booking their tickets to the postseason for a 16th straight season. The good news is that they are well within striking distance of collecting two of the top five overall selections in the 2027 NFL Draft.
They have the Colts to thank for that. By trading Sauce Gardner to Indy for two first-round picks, and with the Colts at an abysmal 2-6 mark, the Jets could very well come away with two top picks to rebuild the roster.
Projected team as of Week 9
Should that happen as expected, there are several players the team should be focused on.
With that said, let's look at the five prospects that make the most sense for the Jets to start thinking about now that April is only five months away.
What a ride for Mestemaker. The Oklahoma State quarterback didn't start a game at quarterback in varsity during high school. He's grown to be the top quarterback of the 2027 class, with a lightning-quick release and the arm strength to win downfield.
He's not the perfect prospect. Mestemaker is still raw in his footwork, but this is the kind of athlete and player that teams will line up for, giving him the chance to grow into a franchise quarterback.
Going into the 2027 offseason, New York's chief focus should be the quarterback position and along its defensive line. While Geno Smith has played well this season, he is not the long-term answer at the position for the franchise.
If the Jets bring in Mestemaker, they will have him sit behind a veteran to start his career. The benefit is that they can get the top quarterback of the class, and one with the skill set to be an excellent starter in the NFL.
Mestemaker is going to be the top quarterback taken in the 2027 draft. That seems to be a foregone conclusion. But people shouldn't be overlooking what Carr has done over his college career at Notre Dame.
This season, Carr has thrown for 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception through eight games. He has an NFL-ready release, is very good from the pocket, and can make all throws. His issue comes in the differences between modern NFL quarterbacks.
Unlike players like Josh Allen or other quarterbacks who can make things happen when the offensive line breaks down, Carr isn't quite known for that. He isn't the greatest athlete in the world. In the Fighting Irish's loss to BYU this season, he did manage to escape many sacks, but things will be different in the NFL.
I expect him to be the second quarterback taken off the board, and someone the Jets seem very comfortable with, having visited Notre Dame games four times this season.
Is it a bad look that the Jets had Quinnen Williams on the roster and they traded him... only to pick his replacement in the hopes that he becomes Williams? Maybe.
But the Jets' defensive line was poor with Williams on the field to start the year. They need to refocus their efforts on bringing in players who can rush the passer along the interior line. Enter Echoles. The defensive tackle from Ole Miss has been excellent throughout his career. Echoles is known as one of the better run defenders in the country but also adds an excellent array of pass-rushing moves.
He appears to be a perferct fit for what the Jets need along their line.
David Bailey is not enough to fix the Jets' pass-rushing woes. They need more help, and from players who can both play the run and get after the quarterback. There will be people debating who the better edge rusher is between Stewart and Colin Simmons.
At this moment, attitude aside, I think Stewart is the player who offers the most upside moving forward. He can play the run better than Bailey and has the explosiveness needed for an edge rusher in the NFL.
Dylan Stewart is too ELITE to not go top 5 Athletic traits like his are exceedingly rare https://t.co/EcmZUyR5hM pic.twitter.com/TSeMmz6IZ1
There will be health and character questions that follow him, but the Jets need ballplayers right now. Not nice guys. Stewart would fundamentally shift what the defense can look like in 2027.
I see Simmons in a similar way to Bailey for the Jets.
The Texas product has a long history of getting to the passer and has caused plenty of turnovers on his own. But he does have an injury history and can be overwhelmed by bigger tackles. He's still a great enough prospect to be a lock for the top five, but I think the Jets should focus on Stewart's upside over Simmons at this point.
Either pick would be celebrated, though.

title: 3 Pending Eagles Free Agents Who Should Be Used as Trade Deadline Bait
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away, which means there could be some major moves coming for the Eagles in the very near future. The Eagles could look to recoup some value for several players prior to the deadline, especially players without a long-term future in Philadelphia.
Here's a look at three pending free agents who the Eagles should use as trade deadline bait.
A plethora of teams in the contender conversation could use some added depth at the linebacker position. Meanwhile, the Eagles aren't in the contender conversation, but they're deep enough at linebacker to get by if one is traded away.
So, the Eagles should do what they can to move on from veteran A.J. Epenesa. Not necessarily because he can't play, but because he doesn't appear to have a future with the franchise.
It seems unlikely that the Birds would bring him back in free agency over the offseason, so they should try to recoup some value while they can. Granted, they probably wouldn't get much more than a late-round pick in a potential deal, but something is better than nothing.
The Browns were interested in Epenesa over the offseason, and even signed him initially before opting out of the deal following concerns about his physical. Perhaps they'll revisit that interest now that he has shown that he's healthy enough to play. On the season, Epenesa has appeared in six games and tallied seven combined tackles and one pass defended.
This one is obvious. Brown has no future in Philly beyond the current campaign , but there are plenty of teams out there who would be interested in adding an extra weapon for a potential playoff push.
Just last season, Brown caught 49 passes for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Kansas City Chiefs. Perhaps a reunion with the Chiefs is in the cards? Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes certainly wouldn't be upset about the addition of another viable option to throw to.
If not the Chiefs, other contenders, including the Rams, Bills and 49ers, could possibly be interested in a veteran receiver like Brown. Given his lack of action with the Eagles (4 total receptions), Brown would likely welcome a change of scenery.
As a young defensive lineman with plenty of promise, there is ample interest around the NFL in Moro Ojomo, including from the Jaguars , according to a report from ESPN . As opposed to the first two players listed above, Ojomo would likely fetch a nice return for the Eagles in a potential trade if they use him as bait prior to the deadline , which they should.
The Eagles already have a ton of money tied up in the defensive line moving forward thanks to the massive contracts of Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, so there's a real chance that they won't be able to pay Ojomo market value over the offseason. It's also fair to wonder whether they'd want to pay him a ton, as opposed to allocating that money to a different position.
If the Eagles were contending this season, there would be a real argument for holding onto Ojomo, even without the uncertainty about his long-term future with the franchise. But since that isn't the case, they should try to recoup as much value as possible.
