title: Seahawks Injury Report Updates on Drew Lock, Uchenna Nwosu, More
full_text:
It took much longer than typical, but the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals finally released injury reports after practicing later than usual. Both lists are quite long, so perhaps putting the information together took some time. Neither team is likely thrilled with the current state of their rosters, so let’s run it down bit by bit and then watch for improvement.
It wasn’t a real practice today in Seattle, since the team just played on Monday, so take this for what it is right now. In any case, Nick Emmanwori (shoulder) , Tory Horton (hand), and Tyrice Knight (thigh) all checked in with what seem to be new injuries (Knight’s prior listing was not for a thigh), but all were listed as full participants and should be perfectly fine.
Limited included Anthony Bradford (knee), Velus Jones (hamstring), Drew Lock (right elbow), Quenton Nelson (knee), and Uchenna Nwosu (ankle). The big one to watch right now is, of course, Drew Lock , and you’d figure he needs to have a full practice at some point to play a game. Nwosu progressing to partial progress, however, is a great sign.
The DNPs of the day are pretty substantial, although most are anticipated. Charles Cross (ankle) , Sam Darnold (quadricep, ribs), Connor O’Toole (foot), Brandon Pili (back), Rashid Shaheed (knee), and Leonard Williams (stinger). We already know Darnold is out this week, but the rest have what seems to be a chance to play this weekend. And we may need them.
In terms of the actual injury report, the Cardinals look to be in decent shape. They do have a lot of DNPs, but most of them are for rest days. Budda Baker, Hjalte Froholdt, Isaac Seumalo, and Josh Sweat got the day off for that purpose, and Jacoby Brissett is on ice because of the imminent trade. Reggie Virgil (back) was a full participant, so a minor issue there.
They do have some very significant players in the limited participation pool, but their status as limited today is promising for their availability. Isaiah Adams (ankle), Walter Nolen (ankle), and Michael Wilson (ribs) among them. Wilson is particularly interesting, as he has two broken ribs but seems adamant on playing. We’ll see which way it goes this week.
The DNPs include Bam Knight (concussion), Jon Gaines (ankle), and Jayden Williams (knee), three players I would anticipate sit on Sunday. But remember, this comes on top of the numerous long-term injuries to players like Kendrick Bourne, Paris Johnson Jr, Will Johnson, Jeremiyah Love, and even James Conner and Tip Reiman. It’s a beat up squad.

title: How Seahawks' Drew Lock Could Become a Full-Time Starter
full_text:
It feels like Deja Vu as the Seattle Seahawks (4-4) prepare for the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) with Drew Lock as the starting quarterback. The Seahawks ruled starting quarterback Sam Darnold out with a quad injury. Head coach Mike Macdonald didn’t initially reveal that Darnold suffered any injury during the 34-17 Week 8 home loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football.
​The Seahawks are looking to get back on track after the loss to the Bears . The coaching staff trusts Lock to start Week 9 versus the Cardinals. There might be an opportunity for him to be the Seahawks’ most trusted quarterback for the rest of the season.
​The Seahawks haven’t seen consistency from Darnold this season. Between his turnovers, his early-season injury, facing the constant pressure from opposing defenses and the poor communication from offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, Darnold has struggled significantly . He needs a lot of things on the offense to go right. Darnold is 2-4 this season, not counting the Week 1 win over the New England Patriots, where he was injured in the first series.
​Lock, on the other hand, managed to help the Seahawks win in Week 1 and then led the team to a 31-7 road win over the Cardinals. Through two or three weeks into the season, Lock was among the league’s top leaders in quarterback rating. Lock had the third-best quarterback rating in Week 2 with 139.1. Lock completed 19-of-26 for 235 yards, three touchdowns and only one sack in the win over Arizona.
​Through seven quarters with the Seahawks’ offense, Lock has looked more comfortable and made better decisions. At this point of the season, he might have recovered from his elbow injury. Darnold, however, may have the quad injury and the broken rib for a portion of the season. This might be what affects him for the remainder of the season. The Seahawks are already in eighth place in the NFC standings and they’ll need the healthiest quarterback possible.
​This was the season for the Seahawks’ front office to decide if Darnold would be the franchise quarterback moving forward. After a difficult set of playing and adapting to the offensive changes, he isn’t making his case that he will return in 2027 as the starter. It doesn’t help that he is suffering another set of injuries this season.
​There is a real chance that Lock could get the first shot at starting quarterback for next season based on how well he plays. Lock has been the quarterback to adapt to the new changes the most; he still has a great feel for reading the field and he possesses solid arm strength. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith accounted for four touchdowns this season with Lock throwing him the ball.
Lock could play well against the Cardinals in Week 9 and at the Oakland Raiders in Week 10. If he does, he needs a chance to prepare as the starting quarterback during the bye week to prepare for the road game at the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12. Lock is already a fan favorite, but if he turns the team around offensively and helps the team secure a Wild Card spot or shock the league by winning the NFC West Division, then he might have earned the role.
​The biggest question will be Darnold’s contract. He is set to earn $41.9 million in his final year next season. If he is cut or traded, the Seahawks would take a $19.2 million dead cap hit , but the front office would save $22.7 million. Those savings could be given to Lock for a new contract.

title: Sam Darnold Declared out for Week 9 vs. Cardinals
full_text:
We may have our answer as to why Sam Darnold was so frustratingly inaccurate on Monday Night against the Chicago Bears. Per Mike Macdonald, Sam sustained a broken rib on the second play of the game, and combined with the quad injury he suffered late, he has already been ruled out for this weekend.
Per Mike Macdonald, Drew Lock will start in Darnold's place this weekend. This is significant, as Lock has been limited in practice the last two weeks and was inactive for both games, with reporters indicating that Lock was limited in his ability to throw during practice. We'll find out later today if those limitations persist, but the implication is he’s available.
Many Seattle Seahawk fans have been clamoring for Lock over the last month amid poor play from Sam, so there will be a lot of excitement in the fanbase to see if Lock can perform. Drew obviously played quite well earlier this season, particularly against the Arizona Cardinals , who he will be facing this weekend. It’s certainly a defense that can be had.
Sam Darnold had already been playing his way out of a lucrative extension , and quite possibly being in Seattle at all. Now that he's had the second half of his season derailed by injury, it becomes all the more likely that this is the end of the line for Sam. If Drew plays well, it's possible he doesn't even get his starting job back now, given how shaky things were.
There’s also the possibility that he won’t be able to get his starting job back at all by virtue of the fact that the injury is serious enough to sideline him for a while. The Seahawks play the Raiders after the Cardinals, and then have their bye week, so I imagine there is strong incentive to at least hold Sam out until then. Given how fast they scratched him this week, maybe more.
The offense of the Seahawks has been so poor in recent times, it’s hard to suggest that this makes things much worse. This defense is still among the best in the NFL, so they can win games. It’s also an opportunity to take an extended look at Lock and decide if he is the quarterback you want to bring back for the 2027 season instead of Darnold.
It’s also a chance to evaluate Brian Fleury with a different quarterback, and if things go significantly better then perhaps the problem isn’t with Brian. I won’t pretend that Drew Lock is an elite quarterback, but he’s proven capable, and if Fleury isn’t able to put up decent results with him then it’s probably safe to assume that he’s just not the guy.

title: Seahawks-Jonathan Taylor Trade Proposal Named Perfect Deadline Move
full_text:
We are less than a week away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline and the Seattle Seahawks already pulled off one blockbuster move. Ahead of their Week 8 showdown with the Chicago Bears , the Seahawks added guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts .
Nelson addressed one of their biggest concerns, but the offense still left a lot to be desired during the loss to Chicago. That's why there's a continued push for the Seahawks to continue their aggressive approach and Cody Williams of FanSided identified a player he says would be the perfect deadline addition.
After watching their ground game struggle this weekend, Williams says the Seahawks should be willing to make another move with the Colts and add running back Jonathan Taylor.
"John Schneider and the Seahawks already got one blockbuster done with the Colts in the Quenton Nelson trade, so let's make it a perfect pair. Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned in Week 8, but the Seattle rushing attack still came up lacking," Williams wrote.
"Maybe that improves as those guys get back into the flow, but Jonathan Taylor is an upgrade no matter how you slice it. Sam Darnold and this offense desperately need to get the ground game back in a more respectable spot and Taylor might be the missing piece to accomplish that."
Indianapolis is in full rebuild mode, having traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. They could also move wide receiver Josh Downs, who requested a trade. For what it's worth, Taylor has not asked to be dealt, but he remains a hot name on the rumor mill and could be exaclty what Seattle's offense needs.
Taylor enters Week 9 with 610 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. He's added an additional 202 yards on 21 receptions. Those numbers are impressive, but they're down from a year ago when he had 1,585 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns.
In Seattle, Taylor would likely find much more success than he has in Indianapolis, where their offense is struggling to find any rhythm. He would also be able to run behind Nelson once again, a combination that's led to plenty of yards for Taylor throughout his career.
The big question for Seattle would be whether they would be comfortable paying for Taylor. They balked at the idea of paying Kenneth Walker following their Super Bowl win, and Taylor has a richer contract. Ahead of the season, he signed a two-year, $44 million extension which has him under contract through 2028, although his cap hit is more than $21 million over the next two seasons.

title: One Stunning Number Sums Up Seahawks’ Lopsided Loss to Bears
full_text:
A clash of reigning division champions turned one-sided on Monday night in the Pacific Northwest. The Chicago Bears marched 80 yards in 17 plays for a touchdown on the opening possession of their clash with the Seattle Seahawks. Ben Johnson’s team took a 7-0 lead that they would never relinquish on the way to a decisive 34-17 triumph over the Seattle Seahawks.
It was the worst loss by Mike Macdonald’s squad since a 30-13 home prime time setback to the Green Bay Packers i n Week 15 of 2024. And eight weeks into 2026, the defending Super Bowl champions have already dropped one more games than it did all of last season, when they concluded a 17-3 overall campaign by hosting a Lombardi Trophy.
How truly stunning was the 17-point setback? As the sideline leader of the Seahawks, Macdonald owns a 31-14 overall record, which includes the team’s three-game postseason run in 2025, and it was just the fifth time the team lost a game by double digits.
And just how odd was it that the club lost by such a margin? Go back to 2025 and the team’s only three defeats that season were to the San Francisco 49ers (17-13), Tampa Bay Buccaneers (38-35), and Los Angeles Rams (21-19). Entering last Monday night’s battle with Johnson’s team, there were losses at the hands of the Washington Commanders (33-31), the 49ers (32-29) , and a Thursday night overtime setback to the Denver Broncos (17-14) in Week 6 this season.
3 FOR D'ANDRE SWIFT 🎩 #NFL #Bears #DaBears #Seahawks #GoHawks #CHIvsSEA pic.twitter.com/OMkHpCPdfM
This is easy math. Combine the margin of defeat in those six losses and it adds up to 17 points—equaling the surprising result on Monday evening at Lumen Field. Spooky stuff, indeed, post Halloween.
Coincidence aside, it was indeed a disturbing Monday night for Macdonald and company. The visiting Bears won the total yardage battle (363-252) and owned time of possession, 35:03-24:57. Chicago totaled 35 running plays for 126 yards. D'Andre Swift ran for 69 of those yards and three touchdowns.
Sam Darnold's pass is deflected and intercepted by Chicago! That Bears front has been relentless all night. Darnold didn't even realize it was picked off and started slowly jogging off the field. pic.twitter.com/9GQP5gNVkS
And while turnovers were a big part of Seattle’s regular-season showing in 2025, quarterback Sam Darnold finds himself in unchartered personal territory. In 2026, his completion percentage is a shaky 60.2 percent. He’s thrown for 10 scores opposed to nine interceptions. Darnold has been picked off at least once in six straight games, the longest-such streak of his nine-year NFL career.
Obviously, there’s a chance to rebound on Sunday against the division-rival Cardinals, who the Seahawks have defeated 10 straight times. But Monday night’s uncharacteristic lopsided loss by the Macdonald’s team was certainly an eye-opener.

title: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Has a Request Ahead of Cardinals Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are 1-3 in their last four games , but things could be looking up as they take on the last-place Arizona Cardinals in their Week 9 matchup.
The Seahawks have already beaten the Cardinals this season, and it was arguably their most dominant performance of the year to date. The Seahawks scored 31 points and held the Cardinals to just a touchdown and 151 total yards throughout the game. Head coach Mike Macdonald hopes that version of the Seahawks comes to the field against the Cardinals.
"We have to focus on recapturing us and making sure that we're us when we turn the tape on. There were too many times throughout that game where that wasn't us in terms of just our style of ball. That's where we need to get better," Macdonald said.
The mindset of the Seahawks remains the same as it was at the beginning of the season. They want to do whatever it takes to win every game and hoist the Lombardi Trophy at the end of the season. They are doing it one step at a time, but are encountering challenges they didn't face last season.
The loss against the Chicago Bears in Week 8 marked their fourth of the season. Last year, the Seahawks only lost three games throughout the entire year. Macdonald knows his team is trying, but their poor execution is why they aren't succeeding.
"They want to play that way too. It's the same thing, we come together and we go forward and we tell each other the truth on the tape and where we can improve on what's us and what's not and how we fix it, and we find those solutions and we go. That's what we do. That's part of our process here, we're always going to do it that way. But it definitely stings, for sure it stings," Macdonald said.
Simply put, there's a target on the Seahawks' back this season after winning the Super Bowl last year. Teams are preparing for them a little differently and are attacking some weaknesses that may not have been discovered over the last year. Teams are getting stronger and smarter against them, and it's leading to Seattle's struggles.
It's very hard to beat a team twice in one year, and the Cardinals are going to come up with a new game plan to try and dethrone the defending champs. It's up to the Seahawks to play their game and execute the plans that have built them up over the last year or so.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Cardinals vs. Seahawks in Week 9
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field.
While the Seahawks beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2, anything can happen in a divisional game, especially when it comes to Arizona. The Cardinals stormed back from down 14 points in the fourth quarter in Week 8 to beat the Dallas Cowboys on the road. All three of Arizona's wins so far this season have come away from Glendale.
Here's a look at three possible scenarios for the game this weekend.
The Seahawks have won their last 10 meetings against the Cardinals, dating back to the rematch in the 2021 season. The Seahawks are coming off a loss, and they know they need to make a big effort to come back with vengeance.
Their spot in the playoffs is teetering, and they need to figure out how to fix their offense before the season gets away from them. A game like this against the Cardinals should be treated as a get-back game, and with the 12s in their corner, Seattle might be able to blow them out like they did in Week 2.
The Seahawks have shown a bit of a regression over the past couple of weeks, and it could bite them this week with the Cardinals coming to town. They have a lot of momentum from their offensive rejuvenation in the fourth quarter, when they replaced Jacoby Brissett with Gardner Minshew, who has been named the starter for the game against the Seahawks.
If Arizona can find that same offensive rhythm throughout the game against Seattle while Sam Darnold continues to put up subpar performances, the Cardinals might be able to walk away from this one with a win, stunning the Seahawks.
While the Cardinals were able to come back against the Cowboys, their poorest defense does not compare to what Seattle has in store. On top of that, the Seahawks are coming off one of their worst defensive performances of the season, giving up 34 points to the Chicago Bears.
The Seahawks' defense is going to play a lot more focused this week, and having them go up against a quarterback in his first start of the year is a recipe for a Seattle victory by multiple scores.

title: The One Word Mike Macdonald Used to Describe Seahawks Loss vs. Bears
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are picking up the pieces after falling to the Chicago Bears 34-17 in Week 8's edition of Monday Night Football.
The Seahawks started out 2-0, but they have lost four of their last six games, and this defeat was the worst of them all. It's the first loss the Seahawks have had by multiple scores this season, and Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald shared his thoughts on the loss.
"Frustrating's a good way to put it," Macdonald said on Seattle Sports 710AM Tuesday morning. "Like I said after the game, we lost the game, it was a three-phase Seahawk loss, and that's a tough pill to swallow. That's something where you're disappointed."
The Seahawks' loss put them on the outside looking in for the NFC playoff picture. They need to win their final two games before the bye against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders.
They will be eager to return to practice this week to correct some of the errors that they have made over the last couple of weeks. However, Macdonald and the coaching staff aren't looking at this situation like the sky is falling.
"Let's stay the course, let's go back to work. There are things that we need to improve on and we need to get better at that are in our control, and that's all you can do. That's where our focus needs to be," Macdonald said.
With the Cardinals on deck, the Seahawks know they cannot underestimate their NFC West rival. While the Seahawks beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2, the Cardinals have a flare for the dramatics.
They managed to complete a two-touchdown comeback in the fourth quarter last week against the Dallas Cowboys, with Gardner Minshew as their backup quarterback entering the game. Minshew is expected to start for the Cardinals against the Seahawks this week as a result of his success, so the Seahawks need to be ready for an Arizona team with a lot of momentum.
Kickoff between the Cardinals and Seahawks is scheduled for 1:25 pm PT on Sunday at Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the Fox One app.

title: Seahawks Week 8 Snap Counts: Running Back Split Surprises
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks suffered arguably their worst loss since the 2024 season on Monday night at home against the Chicago Bears. Almost everything went wrong in all three phases , and Seattle’s place in the NFC playoff picture is growing bleak at the midseason point.
Seattle had both running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price return after extended absences, and they also had major shakeups on the offensive line with the addition of Quenton Nelson at left guard.
Here’s a look at how the Seahawks’ offensive and defensive snap counts shook out from their loss to the Bears.
* All snap count statistics are courtesy of Pro Football Reference
RG Grey Zabel (63; 100%), RT Abraham Lucas (63; 100%), LT Josh Jones (63; 100%), LG Quenton Nelson (63; 100%), QB Sam Darnold (63; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (62; 98%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (61; 97%), TE AJ Barner (60; 95%), WR Cooper Kupp (5; 92%), WR Tory Horton (43; 68%), RB Jadarian Price (30; 48%), RB Zach Charbonnet (23; 37%), TE Eric Saubert (15; 24%), RB George Holani (11; 17%), FB Brady Russell (10; 16%), TE Nick Kallerup (4; 6%), C Olu Oluwatimi (1; 2%)
Unsurprisingly, Nelson played every snap in his first game with the Seahawks. Zabel also played every snap in his first NFL game at right guard. Sundell exited with an injury, but he only missed one snap, and that’s why Oluwatimi logged a play. The offensive line performance left a lot to be desired, with three players in new positions.
Smith-Njigba has averaged about 55 snaps per game, so his usage went up in this game. That was likely to make up for Rashid Shaheed’s absence, but Horton also saw a healthy dose of snaps after Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.
Price saw more usage at running back, and that translated to the box score. Charbonnet logged nine touches for 29 yards in his first game this season, and Price totaled 12 touches for 37 yards. Neither was efficient on a bad day for the offense.
LB Ernest Jones IV (70; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (70; 100%), S Ty Okada (70; 100%), CB Josh Jobe (69; 99%), S Julian Love (66; 94%), LB/DB Nick Emmanwori (64; 91%), LB Drake Thomas (59; 84%), DL Byron Murphy II (54; 77%), LB Derick Hall (51; 73%), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (45; 64%), DL Leonard Williams (41; 59%), DL Jarran Reed (33; 47%), DL Mike Morris (26; 37%), DL Rylie Mills (23; 33%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (13; 19%), LB Dante Fowler Jr. (8; 11%), S Rodney Thomas II (4; 6%), LB Connor O’Toole (4; 6%)
Williams was lower on the defensive line rotation only due to suffering a stinger in the second half. That increased snap counts for Morris and Mills, who overall filled in well. Even on a bad day for the defense, the Seahawks’ run defense held up and proved that their depth up front remains quite good.
Jones, Witherspoon, Okada, Jobe and Love are still the mainstays of the defense who rarely come off the field. Emmanwori is getting to that point, but he still plays somewhat of a specialist role. Head coach Mike Macdonald is starting to find a role for him on every play, however.
The main deficiency was at edge rusher. Without Uchenna Nwosu, the rotation remained largely reliant on Hall and Lawrence, and they didn’t get much pressure. Seattle’s defense relies on Nwosu’s presence more than many realized.

title: 49ers Have Easy Decision to Make on Mike Evans Against Raiders
full_text:
Mike Evans didn't take part in the 49ers’ first Week 9 practice against the Raiders . He’s been dealing with Achilles tendinitis since playing the Seahawks in Week 5.
Evans aggravated his Achilles in Week 6 against the Commanders, forcing him to exit in the final minutes of the first half. He’s been out ever since. On Wednesday, Kyle Shanahan shared an update on Evans.
“I think we've made a lot of progress. I think he's going in the right direction,” Shanahan said. “It's something we’ve definitely got to be smart with, but we're not going to like overly do it. We just want to wait until he's healthy and he's still working his way to get there.”
It’s good to hear that Evans is making progress, and that they’re being cautious with him ramping it up. That said, the 49ers have an easy decision to make on Evans against the Raiders on Sunday.
Don’t play him. Don’t even think about it.
Resting Evans is the best course of action for the 49ers to take. Rather, it’s the only decision to make. They made the mistake of letting him play against the Commanders despite missing the entire week of practice for that game.
That should’ve convinced the 49ers to hold Evans out. Yet they allowed him to make the call. Instead of protecting the player from himself, they let Evans worsen his injury and miss time .
They must avoid making the same mistake. Achilles tendinitis is no joke. The 49ers know that injury all too well when Christian McCaffrey had it in 2024, and that was bilateral Achilles tendinitis.
Every step they take with Evans must be taken with extreme caution. He’s a critical part of their team . He’s the difference between the 49ers making and winning the Super Bowl or not.
Luckily, the 49ers are facing the pitiful Raiders. Don’t let their 4-4 record fool you. They may be better than the dumpster fire that they usually are, but they’re not a good team.
Their defense is their Achilles' heel (no pun intended). The 49ers will be able to move the ball against them at will and put up a bunch of points without Evans.
Brock Purdy should have no issue throwing for over 300 yards and a few touchdowns. He doesn’t need Evans against the Raiders. Let him rest so he can overcome Achilles tendinitis for good.

title: Why the 49ers Might Be Done Trading for Players
full_text:
Trading for DeForest Buckner was incredible move made by the San Francisco 49ers .
They reunited with a player who was integral to their first Super Bowl appearance under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch in 2019 at a crucial position.
Plus, the 49ers didn't have to give up much to acquire Buckner. A fourth-round pick did the trick, which means the 49ers still have quality draft capital to make another move.
A wide receiver or an edge rusher (preferably) would be the positions they should target. They've already shown their hand by wanting to add a receiver after Jauan Jennings denied them .
Another move is likely on the horizon. However, the 49ers might be done trading for players. It's a reality 49ers fans should start to accept.
Let's start with trading for a wide receiver, since the 49ers want to do that. They went after Jennings. That move can indicate a few things.
The 49ers wanted another familiar player to help them (shocker). Jennings isn't a significantly impactful player, but he does improve the offense, especially since he'd need little time to integrate.
It also wasn't going to cost the 49ers much to acquire Jennings had he been okay with the trade. They probably aren't looking at big-time receivers because of the cost and acclimation.
Not to mention that there isn't a premier receiver to go after. Garrett Wilson, who has been discussed a bunch by fans and pundits, isn't a legitimate trade option.
I think it's safe to say they're looking for value options, not difference-makers. That's going to be rough for them since several teams are desperate for a wide receiver.
That will only drive up the cost to acquire one, meaning the 49ers need to overpay.  Speaking of overpaying, that's what they'll need to do for Khalil Mack .
The Los Angeles Chargers have given zero indication they wanna move him, or any one for that matter, despite being a dumpster fire.
Any time a team is digging in its heels on a player, a significant trade package is required to get them. Again, I don't think the 49ers are into that.
Once you get beyond Mack, who else is there to trade for?  That's assuming the 49ers even view an edge rusher as a need.
Now that they have Buckner, they might believe he's the key to unlocking their defensive front. Plus, they're banking on Nick Bosa returning at some point.
Bosa and Buckner will free up Romello Height, and he was already flashing in the last few games. He was always best suited as a complementary player, not a lead.
Height is their acquired edge rusher since Buckner and Bosa will free him up tremendously. That's how they can view it instead of forcing a trade.
The same goes for the wide receiver position. Instead of overpaying or trading the farm for someone like Wilson, they can wait for their injured players to return.
The moment they went after Jennings, they proved they weren't going after a top-notch receiver. They just wanted depth.
The 49ers have the right attitude about trying to make another trade, but it's clear that a blockbuster is unlikely and that they won't force one. The market isn't great.
There's no 2023 Chase Young trade to make, nor a 2019 Emmanuel Sanders one. Trading for Buckner might end up being their only move.

title: 49ers Provide Encouraging Injury Update on Nick Bosa
full_text:
After being out for the last six weeks with a calf injury, the San Francisco 49ers will have Nick Bosa on hand in a limited capacity for their first Week 9 practice.
Kyle Shanahan provided an encouraging injury update today that Bosa has made enough progress with his calf to allow him to return to practice.
This is the first major positive step for Bosa since he suffered his injury while warming up in practice for Week 3. Initially, Bosa thought he would be ready to play in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons.
Unfortunately, he jumped the gun. With the 49ers coming off their Bye, he's now ready. By participating in Wednesday's practice, Bosa is trending toward playing Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Having Bosa back will be a tremendous boost to the 49ers' defense, especially their pass rush. They couldn't muster any pressure on Michael Penix Jr. in their loss to the Falcons.
With Bosa back, that will never be the case. The 49ers have a fairly strong defensive front. They just needed a premier pass rusher to lead the way and draw the offense's attention.
But now the 49ers have added DeForest Buckner. These two have shown before how lethal they are when paired together.
However, that was back in 2019 when Bosa was a rookie. He's dramatically improved since then. Meanwhile, Buckner is still a force to be reckoned with.
He's recorded four sacks (tied for second-most defensive tackles), 15 pressures (tied for 16th), six quick pressures (tied for 9th), and eight quarterback hits (tied for 4th) through the first seven weeks of the season, despite being double-teamed 83 times as a pass rusher, tied for seventh-most among defensive tackles.
It doesn't get much better than that. Bosa and Buckner are going to be a menace together. Not to mention, Osa Odighizuwa is a lethal player in his own right.
The 49ers' pass rush will go from being obsolete to incredible. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has to be thrilled with the talent he has at his disposal.
The 49ers' defense was already playing at a high level without Bosa and Buckner. Now they are going to overwhelm offenses with their physicality.
However, Bosa will be under a magnifying glass for the rest of the season. He's an injury-prone player, so the odds are he will get hurt again.
If he manages to stay healthy for the rest of the season, the 49ers' defense will be one of the best in the NFL.

title: Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey Miss 49ers' First Week 9 Practice
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers won't have two of their star players, Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey, on hand for their first Week 9 practice vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. They were two of four players held out.
Evans has been dealing with an Achilles injury since Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. He worsened the injury the following week against the Washington Commanders.
The 49ers held him out of Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons after revealing he has Achilles tendinitis. Evans has taken two weeks off, so it's concerning that he's still being hampered. That led a reporter to ask Kyle Shanahan how Evans' recovery is coming along.
"I think we've made a lot of progress," Shanahan said. "I think he's going in the right direction. It's definitely something we've got to be smart with, but we're not going to overly do it. We want to wait until he's healthy, and he's still working his way to get there."
Not a whole lot of insight there, but Achilles tendinitis is pretty straightforward. Evans needs rest and must slowly ramp up as he continues to make progress.
At this time, I doubt Evans will play against the Raiders. In fact, they should already rule him out in their minds. They don't need him to beat them.
You can say the same thing about McCaffrey, who is still hampered by a hamstring injury he suffered against the Falcons. McCaffrey exited the game early in the first half before returning.
I wouldn't be worried about him missing Wednesday's practice. McCaffrey always misses the first practice of the week. This is normal for him.
The only reason the 49ers are listing him with a hamstring is because they have to, even if he's 90% healthy. McCaffrey could miss Thursday's practice as well, and it wouldn't be a concern.
All the 49ers need is for him to practice on Friday before giving him the green light. But if his hamstring isn't right, they should sit him.
They can beat the Raiders without Evans and McCaffrey. The Raiders are one of the worst defenses in the league. Brock Purdy should have no problem carving them up.
As for the other two 49ers who missed practice: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Siran Neal (knee, foot).

title: The 49ers have Three Extremely Tough Matchups Looming After the Bye
full_text:
The second half of the season begins this week for the San Francisco 49ers when they host the Las Vegas Raiders. Winning that game shouldn't be that difficult for them.
In fact, it's one of the easiest games left on their schedule . The real test and challenge arrive after them. Let's dive into the three toughest matchups for the 49ers after the Bye.
The Minnesota Vikings were the fakest undefeated team in the NFL in recent memory. Their offense is pitiful. Justin Jefferson is barely a threat because of how awful Kyler Murray is.
However, their defense is insane. They're the reason the Vikings started the season 6-0. The 49ers are all too familiar with the Vikings' defense led by Brian Flores.
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy always struggle against him. I doubt Week 11 in Mexico City will be the game where they finally have the last laugh.
I think the 49ers will lose this game unless Murray becomes a turnover machine. Thankfully, the 49ers are battle-tested after playing two of the tougher defenses, the Denver Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks
Everyone is going to be down on the Seattle Seahawks after they suffered a brutal loss to the Chicago Bears , but they're still a really good team. The Bears aren't slouches.
It's not like they lost to a weak team. Seattle is still a matchup nightmare for the 49ers because of their defense. The 49ers' offense struggled to move the ball against them for the majority of the game.
If it weren't for a plethora of turnovers caused by the defense, they probably wouldn't have won in Week 5. I'd say it's unlikely the 49ers' defense can replicate that performance.
The 49ers' offense will need to be better if they want the game to go a lot more smoothly in the second matchup. In any case, it's a divisional matchup between two strong teams. That'll always be a tough game.
The last tough matchup the 49ers will face in the regular season will be when they fly to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs.
I know the Chiefs haven't looked as fierce in recent weeks, but the reality is they own the 49ers. It doesn't matter what shape the Chiefs are in.
They will always be a tough outing for the 49ers because of Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid, and Steve Spagnuolo. Shanahan and Purdy can't crack the code against them.
And while the Chiefs aren't as great as they were in the past, they are still a pretty solid team. Not to mention that when the 49ers play them, it will most likely be freezing at Arrowhead.
This can easily be a tight game the 49ers drop. I'd love to say I think they won't have too tough a time, but a cold December game and their track record against the Chiefs say otherwise.

title: 2 Tempting Trades the 49ers Must Avoid Making
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have all the motivation in the world to make another trade after Week 8 .
Most importantly, they have the draft capital for it. However, just because they have the capital, it doesn't mean they should wildly overpay for a player. That said, here are two trades the 49ers must not make a reality.
It's not a bad idea for the 49ers to add a wide receiver, but there isn't a blockbuster one available to make. Yet for some reason, some fans and pundits bring up Brian Thomas Jr. as a savior.
It confuses me because Thomas isn't good. He has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns this season. He's not the player that he was in his rookie season, when he reeled in 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.
That player is probably gone. Now, you can say a change of scenery will help him, especially playing for Kyle Shanahan. The issue with that is that he can't even excel playing for Liam Coen, who is one of the best offensive coaches in the NFL.
Not to mention that Trevor Lawrence has been playing really well this year. He's easily been a top-10 quarterback this season. If Thomas isn't thriving, it's because of him.
A fifth-round pick for him would be fine, but it won't get it done. The Jaguars are intent on keeping him, so unless it's a high pick, Thomas is staying put, as he should. Anything higher than a fifth would be an insanely bad trade.
The market has changed for Khalil Mack after the Chicago Bears acquired Jeffrey Simmons from the Tennessee Titans for two first-round picks.
Simmons is 29, at the peak of his powers, and is under contract for the foreseeable future. That plunders Mack's value. A first-round pick for him would be an overpay. The 49ers mustn't offer that.
A second-round pick might even be one too. Originally, I advocated for that, but the market has been set, making a first or second round pick trade for Mack an extreme overpay.
The fact that the Chargers have been unwilling to move him or any other player means his cost is driven up further. It's not a good business move at all.
However, you can make the case that it isn't that bad. The 49ers have a poor track record of drafting in the first round, so why not help your chances of a Super Bowl in 2026? At least that'll be more beneficial than most of their first-round selections.

title: Only One Wide Receiver Trade Makes Sense for the 49ers
full_text:
Trading for a wide receiver has been hot topic surrounding the San Francisco 49ers .
With all the injuries at the position, it's caused a ton of knee-jerk reactions from fans advocating for the 49ers to acquire a receiver . I don't believe the receiver position is that pressing an issue .
Most of the injured receivers will be back in the next week or two. Plus, there isn't a blockbuster trade for the 49ers to make. Garrrett Wilson is the only possible one, but the New York Jets aren't budging.
Still, the 49ers would like to add a receiver. Otherwise, they wouldn't have checked in with the Minnesota Vikings for Jauan Jennings. That leaves only one wide receiver trade that makes sense for the 49ers.
Trading for Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts is the only one that makes sense. For starters, he would be a solid fit for the 49ers, providing them with the vertical threat that they're missing.
Downs can take the top off the defense and open things up for everyone else underneath. The best part is that defensive backs won't be too worried about Downs because of Mike Evans.
Are they going to let Downs run by them down the field? Or will they suffer with Evans gashing on intermediate routes? It's a pickle for defenses to deal with.
Not to mention there's George Kittle, Deebo Samuel, Christian McCaffrey, and Demarcus Robinson to worry about. The 49ers' offense will stress defenses with Downs.
He may not be a premier receiver, but he has enough skill to make an impact for the 49ers. Plus, the 49ers already made a deal with the Colts last week when they reunited with DeForest Buckner.
They have a connection with the Colts, so they can easily call them up and check on Downs. Indianapolis is having a fire sale up until the trade deadline on Nov. 10.
Along with Buckner, they traded All-Pro offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. Even star running back Jonathan Taylor might be on the move.
A fifth-round pick should do the trick to pry Downs from them. It's also the highest the 49ers should go, since Downs is playing in the final year of his rookie contract.
Adding Downs hits all of the markers for the 49ers. He's a fit, plays for a team in the dumps, and his face value is very affordable.
The biggest issue with trading for Downs, any wide receiver, really, is that several teams need one. If other teams are calling the Colts for him, his cost will drive up.
If the 49ers are going to overpay, they might as well do it for an edge rusher, not a receiver. It's an overblown issue that can be masked, especially if they can add another pass rusher.

title: Brandon Aiyuk has Filed for Reinstatement and will Report to the 49ers on Friday
full_text:
Brandon Aiyuk has the most incredible timing.
We haven't heard from this guy in months. He tried so hard to force the 49ers to release him all offseason, and then he went silent. It seemed like he had given up on playing football entirely.
Now, less than a week before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, he has hired mega-agent Drew Rosenhaus, filed for reinstatement with the NFL, and intends to report to the 49ers facility this Friday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .
Suddenly, Aiyuk is moving extremely fast, and it's unclear what he ultimately wants now that Rosenhaus is representing him. Does Aiyuk want to play for the 49ers again, or does he think he can get them finally to trade him? Or cut him?
Unless the 49ers have been in contact with Aiyuk, they're probably confused as well. They have to figure out what they're going to do when he shows up.
Option 1: Call the police. Technically, there's a warrant out for Aiyuk's arrest because he filmed himself driving past Levi's Stadium while going more than 100 miles per hour. This was an error in judgment.
Pros: Aiyuk would get arrested and humiliated in front of his teammates.
Cons: He would bail out of jail in five minutes and come right back to the facility, so this would just delay the confrontation.
Option 2: Remove Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list and try to find some team that's willing to trade a conditional seventh-round pick for him if the 49ers pay part of his salary. If no such team exists, cut him.
Pros: The 49ers never would have to deal with Aiyuk again.
Cons: A former All-Pro wide receiver who's 28 could go to a contender such as the Chiefs, the Bills, Rams, or the Seahawks. And if he plays well, the 49ers would look incompetent because they need a wide receiver like Aiyuk, and someone might get fired.
Option 3: Let Aiyuk return to the team as if nothing happened, provided he addresses his teammates and coaches and reconciles face-to-face with them.
Pros: The 49ers might get a former All-Pro wide receiver who's 28 and healthy and hungry to prove that he deserves a big contract this offseason. This version of Aiyuk could carry the 49ers to their first Super Bowl victory since 1995, assuming Mike Evans returns at some point this season and stays relatively healthy.
Cons: Aiyuk could come back for one day, pull his calf on the practice field like Nick Bosa and Dante Pettis did, sign an injury settlement and never play for the 49ers again.
I couldn't tell you what the right thing to do is. I hope the 49ers and Aiyuk reconcile. That would be a wonderful, heartwarming ending to a bizarre story.
I like a heartwarming ending.

title: 3 Trade Deadline Targets for 49ers Who Fit Raheem Morris's Scheme
full_text:
When you think of the San Francisco 49ers edge rushers, you typically think of a long-armed, strong run defender who can slide inside on pass-rushing downs. Mykel Williams and Keion White tend to fit that mold. They were additions when the team ran their old scheme, though.
With Raheem Morris, they are more multiple . They lean on speed rushers and players who can drop into coverage more. That is why they drafted Romello Height, who plays the same position as Williams, but is more than 2 inches shorter, 21 pounds lighter, and has arms that are inches shorter based on their combine measurements.
With that in mind, Daniel Popper of The Athletic listed three speed rushers as options for the 49ers at the trade deadline. While a 49ers team of the past would never add these options, the Morris version would see them as fits.
McDonald is similar in height and weight to Romello Height, but he has longer arms and more proven pass rush production in the NFL. He could be a one-year rental, so he would not stall the development of Height in the long term. Still, with 18.5 sacks in the past two years combined and three sacks already this year, he would be a great addition.
Smith is a former first-round pick in the fourth year of his rookie contract. So the acquiring team could add Smith this year and have him on the fifth-year option next year. Smith is a Super Bowl winner and starter on the Eagles' defense. His game is based on speed, but he could be a strong mentor for Height and would fit this defense more than units in the past. Smith already has four sacks this season.
Chaisson is another former first-round pick. He is a bit older than Smith and McDonald, but he is still just 27 years old. Chaisson is not much of a run defender, which is why he has bounced around the NFL. Still, he has 3.5 sacks this year and had 7.5 sacks on the Patriots last year. He also added three sacks in the Patriots' playoff run last year. He has proven playoff experience and would be a good fit for a rental.

title: Buccaneers’ Vita Vea Addresses NFL Trade Rumors
full_text:
We are less than a week away from the NFL trade deadline, and the phones are starting to ring.
Just a few weeks ago, we were discussing whether the Tampa Bay Buccaneers would be sellers at the deadline given their disastrous start to the season, but they have since won back-to-back divisional games to put them right back in the hunt for the NFC South crown.
Even though the Bucs might not see themselves as sellers now that they are just a half-game back of the Carolina Panthers in the NFC South, it doesn't mean that they aren't willing to make moves.
In fact, a recent report suggested that the New York Giants are possibly interested in obtaining the services of Vita Vea after striking out on Jeffrey Simmons.
However, Vea was quick to shut things down when asked how he felt about being linked to a potential trade.
“I didn't know until you brought it up, honestly. Shoot, I just come in here to do my job," Vea said during player availability following Wednesday's practice.
The 31-year-old Vea has served as the Buccaneers' run stopper up the middle for nine years, and despite his lack of stats, he constantly impacts the game thanks to being double-teamed for the majority of snaps he plays.
Through eight games, he has 16 total tackles, including a tackle for loss, a sack and two passes defended.
It's an interesting quote from Vea, given that he publicly requested a trade this offseason with the hopes of getting the Bucs to budge on a contract extension that would pay him like one of the elite interior defensive linemen in the league.
Vea ultimately got what he wanted, signing a one-year, $30 million extension that locks him in with the Bucs through the 2027 season.
While it doesn't seem as though general manager Jason Licht and the front office have any intention of trading him, they could decide to do so given his slow start to the season, capitalizing on his peak trade value as he continues to age as well as saving them some headaches when it comes to salary cap impact.
Even though it would make sense to try and get some high draft capital for Vea, it's highly unlikely that Tampa Bay makes that trade — or any trade at all.

title: 3 Ways the Buccaneers Upset the Bears on Sunday Night Football
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough, tough task on Sunday Night Football. They're set to duel against the Chicago Bears, who just defeated the defending Super Bowl champions and are looking like Super Bowl contenders themselves this year.
The Bucs haven't been slouches themselves in recent weeks either, though. They've won three of their last four games, and they currently boast one of the best running offenses and one of the best overall defenses in football.
The Bears will be favored to win this one on home turf against a Bucs team that has struggled this year, and they definitely should be. But the Bucs will try their hardest to get the upset done on the road to move to 4-5 and, potentially, the NFC South lead.
Here's how the Bucs can defeat the Bears on Sunday:
This one shouldn't be too hard for the Bucs — they're really, really good at it, and Chicago is middling at running the football.
Chicago's rushing success rate is 40.6% and their EPA/play on the ground is -0.096. The Bucs have been excellent against the run, allowing a rush EPA/play of -0.208, and they allow just a 35.3% success rate. The Bucs allow the second-fewest yards per game on the ground (80).
Despite their overall lack of advanced metrics in their favor, the Bears still tend to produce on the ground in raw numbers. They're second in the NFL in rushing yards per game behind Tampa Bay's offense (150.8) and they run the ball quite often, the fourth-highest rate in the league (48.87%).
If the Bucs are going to stop the Bears, it starts right here. The Bears have high production but run inefficiently, so limiting explosive plays from running backs like D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai (if he plays) will be key.
Tampa Bay has done a good job of that so far this season, but they can't just be tough against the run in Chicago — they have to bury it.
The Buccaneers are going to have to throw the football sometime. This would be a great game to start.
The Bucs have thrown just 14 passes in their last two games for 64 yards. The Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons were almost entirely unable to handle Tampa Bay's run game, and as a result, the Bucs had no need to throw as they ran for hundreds of yards and easily won both matchups.
That will not be the same environment that Tampa Bay walks into on Sunday. New defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons will ensure that the middle is sufficiently blocked, so Tampa Bay simply must be able to pass with a passing game that has been largely ineffective under Zac Robinson.
Robinson will have to dial up some strong concepts to combat Dennis Allen's defense in Chicago. Additionally, quarterback Baker Mayfield must play well as he recovers from his injured thumb and the receiving corps — potentially without Emeka Egbuka — has to get some separation.
Caleb Williams may very well be the most talented quarterback in football. He's had some consistency issues, but ever since returning from a hamstring injury, he's been simply excellent.
Williams thrives off-platform and is very comfortable outside the pocket. Recently, however, he's been very good at standing and delivering the football inside the pocket, too, and there isn't a throw he cannot make. The key for Tampa Bay will be to get pressure on Williams from the interior and get him down quickly with Calijah Kancey and A'Shawn Robinson — they're in for a long night if they don't.
The Bucs could also utilize some man coverage against Williams, too. He has a +0.048 dropback EPA/play against man coverage and a +0.294 dropback EPA/play against zone, so getting Tampa Bay's excellent secondary a little closer to the football may help them.
Williams will get his. The Bucs just have to make sure it isn't often.

title: Emeka Egbuka Injury Update: Latest on Bucs WR After Missing Another Practice
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough task ahead of them. They're set to face off against one of the best teams in the NFC, the Chicago Bears, on the road in prime time on Sunday Night Football in Week 9.
Tampa Bay hasn't thrown the ball all that much the last two weeks — just 14 times — but it'll probably need to if it wants to beat the Bears. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is recovering from a thumb injury, and while he'll need to throw the football well, his receiving corps will need to step up, too.
The big question heading into Wednesday was whether or not wideout Emeka Egbuka, who has missed the last two games, would be able to play on Sunday night. After Wednesday's practice, the answer to that question remains up in the air.
Egbuka has been dealing with both a concussion and a foot injury over the past two weeks. Head coach Todd Bowles revealed last Friday that Egbuka is out of concussion protocol — his foot issue, however, still remains.
Egbuka practiced on Thursday and Friday last week, but he did not participate in practice on Wednesday. Instead, he was working off to the side with a trainer, so he'll likely be a non-participant in Wednesday's practice when the injury report comes out later tonight.
When asked about Egbuka on Monday, Bowles said he was "50-50" last week, so his lack of participation is definitely something to watch as the week goes on.
"I don't know. He was kinda 50-50 last week," Bowles said Monday. "We'll see how he progresses."
So far this season, Egbuka has netted 28 receptions for 240 yards and two touchdowns. He also has a rushing touchdown on the ground.
In Egbuka's stead — and without Jalen McMillan — wideouts Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst have taken on some work. The Bucs also just got wideout David Sills back from injured reserve, so he's another receiver who could step up in Egbuka's absence, should he not be able to go.
There is still a chance that he could, however. And if he does, Tampa Bay will need to use him against a Bears defense that has only gotten more formidable in recent weeks with the addition of star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons. Egbuka will have two days to try and play, so Thursday's practice could be crucial.
The Bucs will play the Bears at 8:20 p.m. on Sunday night.

title: Buccaneers Star Vita Vea on NFC East Team's 'Radar' Ahead of Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching very fast. There's one week of NFL play left before it hits on Nov. 10, and naturally, teams are calling all around the league to try to make their squads better before that time.
There was a time when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers could have become sellers at that trade deadline had things not gone according to plan. It was sure looking that way — the Bucs lost their first four games of the season and were 2-5 heading into Week 8 — but now, the Bucs are 3-5, half a game out of the NFC South lead and very much in the mix.
That would seem to indicate the Bucs aren't really going to be sellers anymore. But if they got the right offer, anything could be appealing — and according to an NFL insider, one NFC East team could be looking to trade for one of Tampa Bay's star players on defense.
ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reported that the New York Giants are keeping tabs on Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea ahead of the deadline, but that the Bucs don't plan to trade him at the moment.
"Another player on the Giants' radar is Tampa Bay's Vita Vea. (The Bucs are not expected to move him.) It would be a mild surprise if New York doesn't walk away with some help up front," Fowler wrote .
Vea's case is an interesting one. Vea held out of training camp for a significant portion of the year and even requested a trade for a new deal, and the Bucs gave it to him by giving him a one-year contract extension worth $30 million. He hasn't lit up the stat sheet since signing that contract and has clearly declined, so the Bucs may be wise to move on from him this season.
That being said, his ability as a space eater is still very valuable, and he remains a stalwart of a defensive unit that is currently top-three in the NFL by most advanced metrics. If head coach Todd Bowles still wants Vea in that unit, the Bucs will keep him around.
Tampa Bay plays a very tough Chicago Bears team on Sunday night. If the Bucs win, trading Vea feels out of the question — they'd be 4-5 with a shot to lead the NFC South entirely.
If the Bucs lose, though? Perhaps general manager Jason Licht picks up the phone, and perhaps the New York Giants can get some help on the defensive interior.

title: Buccaneers Not Worried About Lack of Passing Game
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won their last two games against NFC South opponents. They've done so in quite an unusual way.
The Bucs have thrown just 14 passes in their last two games for 64 yards — quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't complete a pass at all in a 16-0 win against the Atlanta Falcons. Mayfield is recovering from a thumb injury, but over the past two weeks, he hasn't had to test it at all.
Now, the Bucs are facing off against the 6-2 Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football. The Bears just traded for one of the best defensive tackles in football in Jeffrey Simmons and knocked off the defending Super Bowl champions the Seattle Seahawks. It's probably safe to say that the Bucs won't be able to win on the run game alone for the third week in a row.
So, are the Bucs confident that their quarterback can throw the ball if needed? Head coach Todd Bowles certainly seems to be.
Bowles spoke to the media on Monday, and during his time, he stressed that the conditions are mainly what caused the Bucs to abandon the pass entirely.
"I've seen it in practice. Like you said, the conditions [didn’t require it]," Bowles said. "Carolina just got away in the second quarter, and we kind of got ahead. Yesterday, it was kind of impossible to throw, especially early on. In the last part of the ballgame, we had the lead and we really didn't have to throw the ball. You saw what happened when they threw the football."
Despite that, though, Bowles is confident that the Bucs can pass the ball if they need to. Mayfield may be recovering from a thumb injury, but Bowles believes his recent practices have shown he can accurately throw the ball when it's necessary.
"But we see it every day in practice, [I am] very confident. I thought Baker [Mayfield] had a great week of practice throwing the football, but we knew what the conditions were going to be," Bowles said. "Obviously, as they turned out, it was pretty much a monsoon most of the ballgame, so we didn't have to throw it. We kind of [grinded] it out, but [I'm] very confident our passing game will be fine."
The Bucs will likely have to throw against the Bears, who are looking more like a Super Bowl contender every week. It will be cold, but conditions will be much more favorable to throwing the football on Sunday night.
The Bucs play the Bears at 8:20 on Nov. 8. When they do, it might be time for Mayfield to put his thumb to the test.

title: Week 8 NFC South Standings: What Are the Buccaneers' Playoff Chances?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a big win against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, winning 16-0 (without throwing a pass!).
That win makes the Buccaneers, currently 3-5, 2-0 in the NFC South. It went a long way to putting them closer to the division lead — and it increased their chances to make the playoffs in a big way.
Here's what the NFC South currently looks like, and where the Buccaneers' playoff chances lie after eight weeks of football:
The Buccaneers beat the Falcons to move to three wins on the year. Tampa Bay has won three of its last four games, and now it has the same number of wins as the Panthers and Falcons do. The Bucs have beaten both of those teams, but because the Panthers have played one less game, Carolina is just a half-game out of the division lead. The Bucs will play the Chicago Bears next on Sunday Night Football.
The Panthers lost their game to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football. They'll play the Denver Broncos next on Sunday, another game they could potentially drop at home to give the Bucs an edge.
The Falcons will play the Cincinnati Bengals, who beat the Buccaneers during the first week of the regular season. The Bengals are 5-2, so that will be another tough matchup for the Falcons as they try to match pace with the Buccaneers.
The New Orleans Saints are coming off their bye week, and they'll also play a winning team. The Saints will face off against the Cleveland Browns at home on Sunday.
The Athletic's playoff predictor currently has the Bucs with a 41% chance to make the playoffs at 3-5.
If the Bucs beat the Chicago Bears — a very tough task — that number will jump to 54%. If all of their NFC South opponents were to lose on Sunday, that number would jump to 62%. If all NFC South teams lose and the Bucs also lose, the number is 43%, and if the Bucs lose and either the Panthers or Falcons win, it falls to 35%. A Saints win with a Bucs loss and a Panthers and Falcons loss puts their odds at 39%.
The Bucs' greatest threat is each team within the division, and the Bucs will play four more games against those teams for the remainder of the season. They'll be focused on winning those games, but they'll have to pick up some wins in between, too — and they have their first chance to do so on Sunday night against the Bears.

title: Buccaneers' Biggest Strength Is Finally Becoming Their Biggest Weapon
full_text:
Entering the 2026 season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offensive line was forecasted to be one of the best in the league.
Much of that came from the fact that they would finally be a healthy unit again, getting that much-needed continuity back after injuries decimated the group over the past couple of seasons.
It was the best of starts to the season for the unit, as they struggled to find that cohesion, particularly in the middle of the line.
However, the Bucs' front has seen a drastic turnaround that is showing brightly after putting together back-to-back performances for the ages.
After leading the way for the rushing attack led by Bucky Irving for over 250 yards against the Carolina Panthers, the offensive line showed their strength once again, this time moving the Atlanta Falcons' defensive front seven around for over 300 yards on the ground.
The middle of the unit — Cody Mauch, Ben Bredeson and Graham Barton — have had their ups and downs, but have since been the anchors of helping the run game.
With the inside starting to match the level of play of Tristan Wirfs and Luke Goedeke, it's starting to look much like we thought it would heading into the year.
Remaining healthy has been a huge aspect of that, and with everyone playing on the same page and understanding what is being asked of them, they have helped the Bucs become the league's top rushing attack at 168.6 yards per game.
The explosive run game has been noticeable with Zac Robinson opening up his zone-blocking schemes for the line, creating leverage that has led to wide-open holes for the backs to run through. The use of counter schemes has also been noted as something that has been a tremendous spark to the offense.
The Bucs' tight end production of Cade Otton, Payne Durham and rookie Bauer Sharp in the run game has also been an amazing result.
While the offensive line has been fantastic in the run game, they could use some polishing in protecting the quarterback when it comes to passing downs.
They currently aren't the best against the pass rush, but if they are able to take their confidence from running the ball effectively and use it when working in pass protection, the unit will undoubtedly help lead the Bucs to victories.

title: Bucs' Baker Mayfield Reveals Why He Didn't Complete a Single Pass
full_text:
It was an interesting game, to say the least, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' 16-0 Week 8 defeat of the Atlanta Falcons brought them just half a game out of the NFC South lead.
The field and weather conditions made for a sloppy game overall, and ultimately led to both quarterbacks not throwing the ball or not being effective in throwing it.
That led to a huge game on the ground for the Bucs, who set multiple records in the process. However, with Baker Mayfield not completing a single pass on the day, it became the first time a team went on to win a game in that fashion in 52 years (the 1974 Buffalo Bills).
Following the win, Mayfield spoke about not completing a single pass.
“It’s winning – that’s the way I think about it. We won. [It’s] getting our guys lined up, making sure we are running the right run plays," Mayfield said. "Obviously, ball security [is crucial] in these conditions – we had some early ones. We decided to go to the shotgun and pistol sets – it’s just easier to receive the snaps instead of it coming back through your hands under center."
"So, going from there and just trying to manage the game. [It’s] time management and just trying to bleed the clock as much as possible. Just get everybody on the same page and go from there. That’s my job in these conditions and, listen, I will do whatever it takes to win. That’s all that matters to me.”
Mayfield nailed it on the head in his postgame press conference.
It's clear that the game script was going to demand Tampa Bay run the ball, and after doing so effectively against the Carolina Panthers just a week before, the Falcons knew it was coming.
That didn't matter, as the Falcons gave up over 300 yards rushing, with career highs on the ground by both Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.
It didn't matter to Mayfield whether or not the ball would be put in his hands. It was all about winning, and that is exactly what they did.
Whether the Bucs can continue this type of play and still continue to stack wins remains to be seen, and at some point, Mayfield will have to throw the ball to help.
But for the time being, they should continue to lean on their strengths, which will undoubtedly be tested this upcoming week against a Chicago Bears' defense that ranks fourth in the league against the run.

title: One Big Concern Remains After Buccaneers' Back-to-Back Wins
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off of fantastic wins against the division rival Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons and find themselves only half a game back from first place in the NFC South after a terrible start to the season.
The main boon for this team has been their ability to run the football and play lights-out defense as one of the best units in the league in recent weeks.
One major question is on many Bucs fans' minds, and a growing concern is where the pass game has been in recent weeks this season.
Over the past two weeks, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has thrown the ball 14 times for 64 yards and a touchdown, and that includes him throwing just three passes in a monsoon against the Falcons.
The weather is typically attributed as the biggest reason as to why the team ran the ball as much as they did against Atlanta, but there are many who worry that Mayfield isn't fully healthy and the team simply can't throw the football with his thumb injury.
It is important to remember, though, that Todd Bowles and offensive coordinator Zach Robinson want to be a running football team.
"Everything we talked about – controlling time of possession, running the football, getting turnovers on defense, making plays on special teams, the things we had to do to win the ball game – that's what we talked about right before kickoff in the locker room," Bowles said. "So, it came to fruition. I didn't think it would come to fruition that close, but it came pretty close."
Time will tell whether or not the Bucs want to open up the passing attack more going forward with the 2026 offense. However, it is also important to note that right now, the Bucs don't need to pass the football much, considering the great level of success they have running the ball under Zach Robinson.
While it might not be the game plan many wanted the Buccaneers to have on offense to reach success, the plan the team has in place is working well.

title: Todd Bowles Gives Injury Update on Buccaneers Defensive Starter
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are on a bit of a hot streak. They've won three of their last four games, and now, they're just a half game out of the NFC South lead.
They'll want to keep that going, and to do that, they'll need as many starting players as they can to contribute. But one key defensive starter could be out for some time after Sunday's 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons — but it might not be too long.
Todd Bowles spoke to media on Monday, and he gave an update on edge rusher Yaya Diaby and whether or not he could miss some time.
Todd Bowles told the media Monday that Diaby sprained his MCL in the win over the Falcons. It corroborates an earlier Monday report by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Rapoport reported that it was a Grade 2 sprain and that Diaby could miss a little time, but that he wouldn't miss significant time.
#Bucs outside linebacker YaYa Diaby, who exited Sunday’s win early, is believed to have suffered an MCL sprain, source says. He’ll have an MRI this morning, but the hope is the injury is not one to cause him to miss extended time. pic.twitter.com/r1nJQnwxix
Bowles confirmed on Monday that Diaby has a sprain and that the hope is that he won't be put on injured reserve.
"He has an MCL sprain. Not sure how much he'll miss," Bowles said. We'll see how the week progresses and we'll go from there."
Diaby is in a contract year in 2026, and while he was slow to get going this season, he's made up for lost time in recent weeks.
Diaby had a hat trick of sacks against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, boosting his total to three. So far this year, he has 11 solo tackles, three sacks and an interception, the latter of which he got against the Dallas Cowboys in a win on Thursday Night Football.
If Diaby misses some time, the Bucs will likely turn to players like David Walker, Al-Quadin Muhammad and Anthony Nelson to fill in for him on his side. Walker has been a standout edge rusher this season for Tampa Bay and is earning more snaps there, while both Muhammad and Nelson have been strong rotational pieces so far this year.
If Diaby does have to miss some time, he has at least one thing going for him. The Bucs will have a bye week in Week 10, so he could use that as a buffer to recover and miss fewer games than he normally would.
